spots.name: Sekumpul Waterfall
spots.desc: Sekumpul Waterfall is widely regarded as one of Bali’s most spectacular waterfalls, hidden deep within a lush jungle valley in the island’s mountainous north. The site actually consists of several waterfalls cascading side by side through dense tropical vegetation, creating a dramatic and photogenic landscape. Reaching the falls requires a moderately challenging trek involving steep stairs, river…

spots.name: Bandung Indah Plaza
spots.desc: Typical Indonesian city mall with an Empire XXI cinema, a family karaoke (KTV), large supermarket, department store, and a range of middle class shops and reasonably priced cafés and restaurants.

spots.name: Paris Van Java
spots.desc: Open-air style shopping mall, buildings designed in a European colonial style, hence its name. Wide alleyways and boulevards filled with middle to upper class apparels with a plethora of food outlets, as well as a Blitz cinema that sometimes airs non-Hollywood blockbusters as well as a number of Indonesian movies.

spots.name: Tomb of King Silalahi
spots.desc: A grave of Batak King Silalahi, contains well-preserved Batak traditional house.

spots.name: Aek Rangat hot springs
spots.desc: There are several establishments at hot springs, most of which also offer accommodations and restaurants. If you stay or eat at the establishment, the entry fee may be free. The water is hot. Locals usually use their hands to get some water out of the pool. Standing in the pool is possible, but you probably won't be able to swim.

spots.name: Vihara Sejahtera Sakti
spots.desc: This Chinese temple was built in 1868. Take your time to look at the temple drawings such as "Story of Devotion to the state of children and parents.".

spots.name: Petruk Cave
spots.desc: Still natural (not crowded). You must be accompanied by an official guide. There is no lighting so bring a flashlight. The return journey into the cave can take up to two hours. Your feet will get wet because there is water on the cave floor. Inside the cave, there are various stalagmites and a waterfall.

spots.name: Telaga Warna
spots.desc: Beautiful green-coloured lake set in a landscape of rain forest, and near the tea plantations. You can just enjoy the view, or go around the lake by boat or pedalo.

spots.name: BTC Fashion Mall
spots.desc: Shopping mall with a large number of small shops selling cheap clothing. There are also various other shops, restaurants, cafés, and a cinema.

spots.name: Saluopa Waterfall
spots.desc: By all accounts the Saluopa Waterfall - while a little tough to reach, about 12 km out of town - is one of the best available, notable for the lack of other tourists and businesses. There are approximately 10 drops, each of which you can bathe in. A nice relief from the heat of Sulawesi, and worth if considering if you have time. Toilets and restaurants at site.

spots.name: Simarjarunjung hill
spots.desc: Aside from the green pine forest and surrounding hills, tourists can enjoy the beauty of Lake Toba from this place. Although it does not seem so close, Lake Toba still looks beautiful when viewed from this point. Another spot to view the eastern side of Lake Toba.

spots.name: Ponot Falls
spots.desc: A 3-step waterfall, one of the highest in Indonesia, around 200 m.

spots.name: Sigura-gura Falls & Dam
spots.desc: Said to be the highest waterfall in Indonesia at 250 m, the Sigura-Gura Falls and the nearby dam are part of the Sigura-Gura hydro power plant complex that powers most of North Sumatra. It is operated by the state-owned PT Inalum. The dam is said to be the 2nd largest in Indonesia. Access is limited, but there's a lookout from the main street to view the falls, the dam and the power plant complex.

spots.name: Istana Plaza
spots.desc: Typical Indonesian mall with middle-class shops and cafés.

spots.name: Aua Sarumpun
spots.desc: A hill offering views of Lake Maninjau from a height.

spots.name: West Java People's Struggle Monument
spots.desc: Monument established in 1995.

spots.name: Central Sulawesi State Museum
spots.desc: Ethnological museum of the region, including about the megalithicum stones of Bada Valley and Kaili tribal culture.
spots.price: kids Rp1,500, adults Rp3,000. foreigner Rp10,000
spots.addr: Jl. Kemiri No.23, Kamonji, West Palu

spots.name: Fatmawati House
spots.desc: A museum to commemorate Sukarno's wife. The house was built in Bengkulunese vernacular architecture style which is getting rare as people favours more modern style.

spots.name: Sungai Suci Beach
spots.desc: The beach is located just outside the city border. You'll need a private vehicle since it settles quite far from the major road. The beach features cliffs and a large offshore rock that makes it distinct from any other beaches in Bengkulu. The rock is connected to the mainland by rope bridges.
spots.price: Entry fee Rp5,000 per person, another Rp5,000 if you want to cross the bridges

spots.name: Delipark Mall & Rivapark
spots.desc: The largest upscale mall, part of Podomoro City Deli Medan. Their tenants include Sogo Dept Store, Marks & Spencer, Pull & Bear, Uniqlo, Tumi, Swarovski, Transmart Supermarket, Ace Hardware, Starbucks and many more.
spots.addr: Jl. Putri Hijau / Guru Patimpus No 1, Medan

spots.name: Idrus Tintin (MTQ) Building
spots.desc: A great building with Malay and modern architecture. One of the city's landmark. Some great events held here from Musabaqah Tilawatil Qur'an (MTQ) to Indonesian Film Festival.

spots.name: Sidik Jari Museum
spots.local: Museum Lukisan Sidik Jari Ngurah Gede Pemecutan
spots.desc: Small, private fine art museum established and owned by I Gusti Ngurah Gede Pemecutan and which exhibits his own work as well as that of other artists. Also has facilities for public dance and other performances.

spots.name: Paragon City Mall
spots.desc: At the G floor, you can buy beauty products at L'Occitane and the Body Shop. Some of the well-known tenants include Adidas, Giordano, Levi’s, Hush Puppies, and Wakai. Food options include BreadTalk, J.CO Donuts, dan Starbucks.

spots.name: Malioboro Mall
spots.desc: Yogyakarta's premier shopping mall for shopping in hassle-free, air-con comfort. Features a large Matahari department store, a Hero supermarket (B1F), a Periplus book store with a good English selection (B1F), and all the usual suspects of Western and Indonesian fast food (McDonald's, Pizza Hut, KFC, EsTeler 77, etc.) Home to the largest Dagadu outlet.

spots.name: Gudeg Wijilan Yu Djum
spots.desc: A more lavish variety of Gudeg, served with thicker sauce, and more expensive as well.
spots.addr: Jl. Wijilan 31, Kraton & Jalan Kaliurang km 4.5, Karangasem CT III/22

spots.name: Jodipan Colorful Village
spots.desc: This village has all houses in it painted colorfully. The village has two areas, Jodipan and Tridi, which are connected by the Ngalam Indonesia Glass Bridge over the Brantas River, the first glass bridge in Indonesia.

spots.name: Museum Kesehatan dr. Adhyatma, MPH
spots.desc: A museum built in the 1990s oriented towards the history of health & medicinal treatment in Indonesia, from the depiction of health in traditional cultures to the evolution of remedy methods.

spots.name: Museum TNI AL Loka Jala Çrana
spots.desc: Established in 1969, the museum contains various displays related to the Indonesian Navy since the revolution era, including ships and amphibious tanks and a planetarium.
spots.hours: Mon-Thu 08:00-14:00, Fri 08:00-15:00, closed on Sat Sun and public holidays
spots.addr: Candradimuka Kompleks Pendidikan TNI AL Bumimoro

spots.name: Surabaya Town Square
spots.desc: Anchored by Foodmart. A shopping mall with the largest cinema studio in Surabaya. Open until midnight.

spots.name: Botani Square
spots.desc: Food court, convention centre, meeting point. A prestigious shopping mall in Bogor. Easy to access via public transportation. Located next to Terminal (Bus Station) Baranangsiang. 24 hr ATM. It is also recommended for city check-in, with an airport bus to take you directly to Jakarta's CGK International Airport. Located also next to Botanical Garden and Bogor Agriculture Institute.

spots.name: Bukit Bangkirai
spots.desc: The main attraction is the Canopy Bridge, which is famous in East Borneo. It was built for the biological study of the ecosystem in the canopy of the tropical rainforest. It is now popular for the public to view the beauty of the rainforest from 30 m (90 ft) above the ground. It's also a very nice place to enjoy nature or to camp and watch the stars.
spots.price: Entrance Rp 22,000 domestic or foreigner, Canopy domestic Rp 25,000, Canopy foreigner Rp 75,000

spots.name: Mal Jayapura
spots.desc: The largest in the metro area and the only mall in the city center. Though it's no different than any metropolitan shopping malls, this is the most chic place you can find to shop for everything you need.

spots.name: Saga Mall
spots.desc: A basic mall at another district. Not as much anchor tenants as Mal Jayapura other than the first KFC in the city that made the locals hyped.

spots.name: Manado Town Square
spots.desc: Opened in 2006, the biggest shopping centre in Manado. You can find various western stuff here.

spots.name: MTC Karebosi
spots.desc: IT Centre (electronic, mobile, and computer), Carrefour Express, local shops, cafés, playground, CFC, etc.
spots.addr: Jl. Jend. Sudirman No.1, Pattunuang, Wajo, Kota Makassar, Sulawesi Selatan 90113

spots.name: Mall Ratu Indah
spots.desc: Matahari Dept. Store, Gramedia bookstore, Hero supermarket, XXI Cineplex, Breadtalk, Excelso, J.Co, McDonald, Pizza Hut, KFC, Playground, Some cafes and boutique, etc.
spots.addr: Jl. Dr. Ratulangi No.35, Mamajang Luar, Mamajang, Kota Makassar, Sulawesi Selatan 90114

spots.name: Mall Panakkukang
spots.desc: Mall Panakkukang: Matahari Dept Store, Rimo Dept. Store, Hypermart, Diamond Hypermarket, 21 Cineplex, Excelso, Gramedia, Disctarra, Breadtalk, AW, Sport Shop, Dunkin Donuts, Pizza Hut, Rotiboy, Jco, some cafes, boutiques, playgrounds, etc.

spots.name: Panjang Beach
spots.desc: Pantai Panjang means long beach, as it stretches for 7 kilometres. Not only noted for its length, the beach itself extends for 500 metres during the low tide. You'll find numerous huts that sell foods and drinks. Some also provides benches to lounge around. The city government continually tries to expropriate the lands since they are deemed to pollute the beach and encourage questionable…

spots.name: Lampung Museum
spots.desc: Gallery hall of exhibits on the history and culture of Bandar Lampung and Lampung, including bronze work, ceramics, representative Sumatran dwellings, fauna dioramas, and weaponry.

spots.name: Pantai Mutun
spots.desc: Water park attached to the beach on the Sunda Strait/Lampung Bay. Banana boat rentals, etc. Clear water.

spots.name: Grand Palladium Mall
spots.desc: No longer grand, this out-of-fashion mall is adjacent to Hotel Aryaduta in the city center. Used to be popular, but most outlets have now closed, as happens to malls in fickle Medan. All the large stores have left, but there are still a few small shops selling things like gems and CDs, and a few good restaurants. Be sure to try Tiong Sim Noodle & Hong Kong BBQ (open until 02:00 daily!): Their…

spots.name: Mall Pekanbaru
spots.desc: Mega Dept. Store, Lucky Mart, Gramedia Book Store, Handphone Centre, Solaria, Bakso Lapangan Tembak, Ikan Bakar Cianjur, KFC, Bread Boutique, MP Night Club.

spots.name: People's Struggle Monument
spots.local: Museum Monumen Perjuangan Rakyat Sumatera Bagian Selatan
spots.desc: Located opposite the Grand Mosque, it was inaugurated in 1988 to commemorate the struggle for Indonesia's independence in Palembang. Inside this brutalist-style building, there is a museum displaying various artifacts and historical photos related to the Five-Day and Five-Night Battle in Palembang (1947). There is also a dancing fountain in the monument's courtyard.
spots.addr: Jl. Merdeka no.1, 19 Ilir, Bukit Kecil 30113

spots.name: Bayt Al-Qur'an Al-Akbar
spots.desc: Claimed to house the largest wood-carved copy of the Quran in the world, displayed page by page on the 15-metre high galleries. Reviews are mixed, with many travellers saying it is a must visit on a trip to Palembang and others complaining about a long drive on bad roads to a rural area and poor access for disabled people.
spots.addr: Pondok Pesantren IGM Al Ihsaniyah, Jl. M. Amin Fauzi, Soak Bujang, Gandus 30149

spots.name: Basko Grand Mall
spots.desc: KFC, Pizza Hut, J.CO, Bread Talk, Matahari, Solaria, Foodmart, etc.

spots.name: Semarang Bridge Fountain
spots.desc: Dancing fountain show in the evening.

spots.name: Mount Meja Natural Tourism Park
spots.local: Taman Wisata Alam Gunung Meja Manokwari

spots.name: City of Tomorrow
spots.desc: Anchored by Matahari and Hypermart.

spots.name: Situ Gede
spots.desc: Small natural lake at the edge of the city.

spots.name: Ambon Plaza
spots.desc: Fashion tenants and cinema.

spots.name: Maluku CIty Mall
spots.desc: Fashion tenants and culinary tenants.

spots.name: Pantai Talise
spots.desc: Crowded beach where steps lead into the water.

spots.name: Palu Grand Mall
spots.desc: features: KFC, Hypermart, The Body Shop, etc.

spots.name: Plaza Senapelan
spots.desc: Suzuya Dept. Store, D'cost Seafood Restaurant, A&W.

spots.name: Kanto Lampo Waterfall
spots.desc: Unlike most waterfalls, Kanto Lampo flows over a series of stepped rock terraces, creating one of Bali's most photographed natural attractions. Be prepared to get wet if climbing onto the rocks.

spots.name: Tibumana Waterfall
spots.desc: Set within a forested valley east of Ubud, Tibumana Waterfall is a graceful single-drop cascade flowing into a calm swimming pool. The easy walk through bamboo groves and tropical vegetation makes it one of the area's most relaxing waterfalls.

spots.name: Ubud Market
spots.desc: This is a double storey warren of stalls bursting at the seams with wood carvings, batik shirts, sarongs, and all manner of other souvenirs aimed specifically at tourists. The merchants here haggle with tourists for a living, and think nothing of asking for ten times the going price, so try to establish a baseline before you go in to buy. Most of the merchants downstairs will lose interest if you…

spots.name: OHD Museum
spots.desc: The private collection of modern Indonesian art of Oei Hong Djien. There are two parts to the collection. This museum hosts the changing exhibitions. The permanent collection is housed in a separate building attached to his home, also in Magelang. It may be possible to see the permanent collection by asking at the museum.
spots.hours: Wed-Mon 10:00–17:00. Last entry 16:00. Closed on public holidays
spots.price: Indonesian ID card holders: Rp50,000 (adults), Rp25,000 (students); non-Indonesian ID card holders: Rp100,000 (adults)…

spots.name: Bukit Cinta
spots.desc: Offers a view of the Rawa Pening lake. This place is often visited by young couples, hence the name. There is a playground for children, and you can ride a boat around the lake for Rp30,000 per half an hour.

spots.name: Museum Probolinggo
spots.desc: Historical tourist attractions that store relics of Probolinggo's past such as artifacts, Probolinggo banknotes, replica statues, heirlooms to some photos of Probolinggo in the past.

spots.name: Diponegoro Museum
spots.desc: Featuring Prince Diponegoro, a national hero.

spots.name: BSD Junction
spots.desc: Shopping mall in the centre of BSD City.

spots.name: Bali Bomb Memorial
spots.desc: This is a memorial to the 202 victims who died when bombs were detonated on 12 October 2002. It can be found on Jl Legian opposite the corner of Poppies II. This is the former site of the old Paddy's Bar, and opposite the former site of the Sari Club, which is still an empty space, next to the Billabong shop. Every year on the anniversary date there is a ceremony mourning those killed or wounded…

spots.name: Waterbom Park
spots.desc: This is one of the biggest water theme parks in Asia and is within easy walking distance from Kuta beach.
spots.price: Adults Rp520,000, under-12s Rp370,000, good value 2-day passes available

spots.name: Pasir Panjang Beach
spots.desc: A 3-km-long beach. This beach could be reached within 20-30 minutes if you are from singkawang city by car.

spots.name: Dharmayana Temple
spots.desc: Dharmayana Temple a vibrant Chinese Buddhist temple tucked away in central Kuta, just a short walk from the beach and the area’s bustling tourist streets. Dating back to 1876, it is one of the oldest and most active temples in Bali, serving the local Chinese Balinese community. The temple’s bright red walls, ornately carved dragons, and aromatic incense coils create a serene and atmospheric…

spots.name: Mal Bali Galleria
spots.desc: Galleria is home to number of well-known brand stores, a food court, Planet Hollywood and a great cinema. There is a large duty free shopping centre which is aimed primarily at Japanese, Korean and Taiwanese tourists. You can buy luxury items tax free, and they are collected upon departure at the airport.

spots.name: Makam dan Masjid Kuno Taman
spots.desc: The mosque was built by Kyai Ageng Misbach or Kyai Donopuro in 1754. It is surrounded by the grave of the regents of Madiun.
spots.addr: Jl. Kemiri No.46, Taman, Kec. Taman

spots.name: Harry Darsono
spots.desc: Harry Darsono PhD is a famous, multi talented designer. His famous designs include fashion, batik, and furniture. He is also a lecturer at universities, amateur musician, and wine connosieur. Collection: fashion, textile, batik, antique piano.

spots.name: Raya Pasi Nature Reserve
spots.desc: Hike Mount Poteng, exploring the dense rain forest of Borneo, if you are lucky you can spot Rafflesia tuan-mudae Flower (The largest flower species in the world which can grow up 95 cm in diameter).

spots.name: Sinka Island Park
spots.desc: Ride dog-cart, swimming, or enjoy local F&B.

spots.name: Sikidang Crater
spots.desc: A volcanic crater. A nearby small hill provides a good viewpoint.

spots.name: General Soedirman
spots.desc: The statue stands on the avenue named for his namesake. Sudirman (old spelling: Soedirman) was the leader of the Indonesian forces in the guerrilla war against the Dutch in Yogyakarta (1948-1949).

spots.name: Mall Taman Palem
spots.desc: An old mall with plenty of food tenants. Usually not so crowded, even at the weekend. There is a functional hall at the 5th floor.
spots.addr: Jl. Kamal Raya No.13, RT.13/RW.10, Cengkareng Timur

spots.name: Sukamade
spots.desc: Four different species of sea turtle lay eggs on the beach here and every night of the year there are turtles to see. If there is a preferred time to visit it would be at a full moon and the attendant high tide. To watch a turtle laying her eggs here is a once in a lifetime experience. Don't forget to visit the hatchery facility. Young turtles of all four species are incubate here and released…

spots.name: Ngembag Tourism Park
spots.desc: Used to be an abandoned spring, now this park has a playground and a children's pool.

spots.name: Mount Mananggel
spots.desc: Mount Manangel is the mountain that is closest to the town of Cianjur - about 7 km from the town. It is 1200 m above sea level. Starting at the edges of the town, you can walk across the flowing paddy fields, through villages to the foot of the mountain until you reach a waterfall that will get you refreshed if you fancy taking a swim at Cibodas’ waterfalls. Hike for 2½ hours then you’ll see a…
spots.addr: Jln. Cibeureum Desa. Mekar Jaya Kec. Mande Cianjur

spots.name: Pasar Tanah Abang
spots.desc: This is the prime place for garments in Jakarta or even Indonesia. The biggest in Southeast Asia and usually export to Africa and Middle East, arrangement delivery in all countries in the world. Groceries and semi retail (minimum 3 pieces) sale. All types of fashion are abundant. Haggling is not too necessary, mainly if you buy in bulk to get a large discount, the prices can be the cheapest you…

spots.name: Lubang Buaya
spots.desc: Marks the site where an alleged failed coup d'état by the Partai Komunis Indonesia (Indonesian Communist Party) met its end in 1965, alongside the bodies of several high-ranking generals who are believed to have been tortured to death.

spots.name: ITC Mangga Dua
spots.desc: This is the cheapest place in Jakarta when it comes to clothing, but haggling is still the norm. Thousands of independent clothing lines in line with counterfeit brands. Very crowded on the weekends, watch out for pickpockets.

spots.name: Paisu Pok Lake
spots.desc: Likely the reason why you heard about Banggai in the first place. A lake famed on social media for its lush setting surrounded by palm trees and especially its extremely transparent water. Rental of gazebos (30,000 rupiah), stand-up paddles (100,000), boats (30,000), snorkelling equipment and even drones and experienced underwater photographers are available, to make sure influencers can get the…
spots.hours: Accessible 24/7, best in the morning before local tourists arrive
spots.price: 5,000 rupiah entrance fee, late afternoon the fee is not collected anymore

spots.name: Mandaragiri Semeru Agung
spots.desc: Hindu temple in sub-district Senduro.

spots.name: Bakoel Koffie
spots.desc: The oldest coffee roaster in Jakarta since 1878.
spots.addr: Jl. Cikini Raya No.25, RT.16/RW.1, Cikini

spots.name: Mall Graha Cijantung
spots.addr: Jalan. Pendidikan No. 1, Jl. Raya Bogor Km 24. Cijantung

spots.name: Seasons City
spots.desc: A budget shopping center.

spots.name: Telaga Biru Maima
spots.desc: A turquoise water lake.

spots.name: Melasti Beach
spots.desc: A broad white-sand beach reached by a spectacular switchback road cut through high limestone cliffs. Once relatively isolated, Melasti is now a popular, developed beach with beach clubs, food options and good road access, but the cliff scenery remains exceptional. It is a strong choice for swimming when conditions are calm; check tides and surf before entering the water.

spots.name: Mount Sawal
spots.desc: A volcano that set as a wildlife sanctuary . Animal species in the area include the critically endangered Javan leopard. The volcano is about 1,750 metres high, and relatively easy to climb. From the summit you can see other volcanoes, such as the Mount Ciremai.

spots.name: Medicinal Herb Garden
spots.desc: A garden that displays a collection of medicinal plants, roughly 400 species. You can also buy medicinal plant at relatively affordable prices as souvenir.

spots.name: Toran Bay
spots.desc: A turquoise water bay. There is some karst which overgrown with the majority of Papuan orchids.

spots.name: Pungkruk Beach
spots.desc: This beach has a characteristic, namely the contours of a flat beach and interesting spots along the coastline. You can also relax and enjoy the panoramic sunset in peace from the available gazebo. On one side of the beach, you can visit the mangrove forest area which has a cooler and more beautiful climate.
spots.addr: Rw. 01, Mororejo, Kec. Mlonggo, Kabupaten Jepara, Jawa Tengah, Indonesia

spots.name: Lawang Ombo
spots.desc: An old house built in the 1860s was used as an opium warehouse during the Dutch colonial period.
spots.addr: Jl. Sunan Bonang No.70, Pereng, Soditan

spots.name: Rembang Great Mosque
spots.desc: This mosque was built in 1814. There is a cemetery of the dukes of Rembang at the west side of the mosque.

spots.name: R.A. Kartini Museum
spots.desc: R.A. Kartini was an Indonesian women's rights activist from Jepara and wife of the Regent of Rembang. The museum was the house of the Regent of Rembang. It contains Kartini's original writings and a painting of Kartini by his only son RM Susalit.

spots.name: Trio Mall Kebumen
spots.desc: The first lifestyle shopping mall in Kebumen. It is combined with 4 stars hotel.

spots.name: Candi Gana
spots.desc: Rich in statues, bas-reliefs and sculpted stones. Frequent representations of children or dwarfs with raised hands. In the middle of housing complex. Under restoration since 1997.

spots.name: Prambanan Jazz Festival
spots.desc: The annual jazz music festival that is usually held around July, where local and international musicians play.

spots.name: Palagan Ambarawa Monument
spots.desc: A monument to commemorate the Battle of Ambarawa, in which the Indonesian army defeated the British and Dutch troops in 1945. It houses several weapons and vehicles used during the National Revolution Period.

spots.name: Ranu Segaran Lake
spots.desc: Near the lake, there is also a natural hot spring Air Panas Segaran. You may bathe there.

spots.name: Non-alignment Nations Friendship Monument
spots.desc: Built to commemorate the spirit of the 10th Summit of the Non-Aligned Movement. The shape of the monument is a globe, supported by a fountain decorated with 5 doves in the middle. Nearby, 108 trees are the embodiment of friendship, and the trees consist of various types to symbolise the 108 countries that are part of the non-aligned countries.

spots.name: Golden Snail Legend Garden
spots.desc: This place is an expansion of what used to be a flower garden. Attractions in this complex are as follows: Petualangan Dinosaurus, Mata Legenda, Ulat Selur, Bajak Laut, Mobil Tanjak, Kereta Beos, Baby Dino, Perang Galaksi, and Nirwata Kisar.
spots.hours: Mon to Fri 10:00 to 17:00; weekend & holiday 10:00 to 18:00
spots.price: Monday to Friday Rp 20,000; weekend & holiday Rp 30,000

spots.name: Mina Lake
spots.desc: Go fishing. Sometimes, there is a fishing competition event.

spots.name: Candi Jiwa
spots.desc: The Candi Jiwa temple is located in the middle of rice fields. It is one of the temples that has been researched the most, and has been partly restored. It measures 19 by 19 metres, and is 4.7 metres high. In the middle of the temple, there is a circular structure, which could have been a stupa such as found in the Borobudur temple.

spots.name: Batam City Square (BCS)
spots.desc: One of the more crowded malls in Batam. You can watch a movie there for Rp20,000. The mall also has karaoke, lounge, Timezone arcade, bowling and slot machines.

spots.name: Wayob Beach
spots.desc: A white sand beach.

spots.name: Mall Karawang Central Plaza
spots.desc: Largest shopping centre in Karawang.

spots.name: Kitikiti Waterfall
spots.desc: A waterfall by the sea.

spots.name: Taman Safari Indonesia
spots.desc: Zoo, with car safari trail that allows cars and tourist buses to see and/or feed elephants, zebras, goats, hippos and more, hiking trails, petting zoo. Buy carrots from the many vendors by the side of the road leading up to the zoo before your get there to feed to the animals. Inside the zoo there are more animals to see, shows to view such as the 'Wild-Wild West' the Lion show and the Sea-Lion…
spots.price: The entrance ticket fee to the complex for domestic tourist is Rp85,000 for adults and Rp70,000 for children under 6…

spots.name: SMP Negeri 5
spots.desc: The main junior high school in colonial Bandung, built in 1920. The building is still in use as junior highschool (SMP).

spots.name: Sibea-bea Hill
spots.desc: possibly the highest statue of Jesus Christ in the world, with a reported height of 60 m (197 feet) overlooking Lake Toba. For comparison, the famous Christ the Redeemer in Rio de Janeiro is only 30 m in height.

spots.name: Florawisata Santerra de Laponte
spots.desc: Hundreds of types of flowers, replicas of foreign buildings, many contemporary photo spots, and various kinds of rides.

spots.name: Yang Highland Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.desc: Yang Highland Wildlife Sanctuary (or Hyang Mountains Wildlife Sanctuary) a wildlife sanctuary in Java Island.

spots.name: Bukit Merese
spots.desc: One of Lombok's finest viewpoints, Bukit Merese is a grassy headland overlooking Tanjung Aan Beach, the Indian Ocean and the rugged southern coastline. A short but moderately steep walk leads to panoramic views in every direction. Sunrise and sunset are the most popular times to visit, when the hills glow golden and the beaches below are particularly photogenic. There is a small entrance fee and…

spots.name: Kedung Kayang Waterfall
spots.desc: A 30m tall waterfall, about 3 km east of Ketep.

spots.name: Sopo Guru Tatea Bulan
spots.desc: an open-air museum presenting the creation myth of Batak.

spots.name: Mega Mall - Batam
spots.desc: This mall is quite a good mall like in Jakarta.

spots.name: Gua Kreo
spots.desc: A modest cave formation surrounded by a man-made lake with a resident band of long-tailed macaques. Can get crowded on the weekend, but you may have it all to yourself on a weekday. Near the cave, there is Waduk Jatibarang or Jatibarang reservoir with a beautiful sight.
spots.addr: Jl Raya Goa Kreo, Kandri, Gunung Pati

spots.name: Layur Old Mosque
spots.desc: Masjid Layur, or commonly called the Masjid Menara, is an old mosque building in the city of Semarang which was founded around 1802. Precisely located on Jalan Layur, Kampung Melayu area. This mosque was built by Arab traders. There is a minaret that is an icon of the mosque.

spots.name: Rumah Akar
spots.desc: An alley with some buildings with tree roots growing on its walls. Many people make it as a photo background even for pre or post-wedding photos.

spots.name: Gedung MARBA
spots.desc: Marba (Martak Badjened) is a company owned by a Yemen-Indonesia businessman who is engaged in export and import. This building was built in the mid-19th century.

spots.name: Gedung PTPN XV
spots.desc: Built in the early 19th century and used for Cultuur-Maatschappij der Vorstenlanden N.V., a Dutch company engaged in plantations and agriculture. The company opened a branch in Semarang in 1888. Now, the building is owned by state-owned PT Perkebunan Nusantara.

spots.name: Taman Puri Maerokoco
spots.desc: Tawangmas PRPP, a Central Java Miniature like Indonesia Miniature of TMII (East Jakarta). Facilities: cultural and art shows, boat, water bike, small train, fishing pond. It also contains Kampoeng Laut, a famous over-the-water restaurant. On the other hand, you also can walk around the mangrove forest there.

spots.name: Burung Kuntul Banteng Raider
spots.desc: Do birdwatching, white egrets in some tamarind trees beside the road.

spots.name: GOR Jatidiri
spots.desc: There is a sports complex owned by the Central Java government. Main football stadium, swimming pool, indoor stadium, roller skate velodrome, and so on. You may watch the tier-1 Indonesian football league match on the weekend.

spots.name: Lumpia Gang Lombok
spots.desc: The pioneer of Semarang's many lumpia (spring roll) stalls. Started operating before the Second World War. Some of the owners of other lumpia outlets started by working at this place. Uses both dried shrimp and fresh shrimp. Semarang lumpia is known for the use of bamboo shoots, which give them a distinctive taste.

spots.name: Moaci Gemini
spots.desc: Kue moaci is a Semarang mochi stuffed with the peanut paste and sesame seeds outside.

spots.name: Semarang Creative Gallery
spots.desc: Gallery of creative products & unique crafts from Semarang craftsmen.

spots.name: Pasar Bulu
spots.desc: In addition to providing ingredients for cooking, there is also a food court here.

spots.name: Kue Lekker Paimo
spots.desc: A Javanese crispy flat cake. The Indonesian version of Dutch baby pancakes and French crêpe. There are two types of kue lekker, the sweet and the salty one.

spots.name: Toko Oen
spots.desc: A Semarang institution since Dutch colonial days. Famous for its ice cream, steak and fried rice, and bread and cookies. Still with the atmospheric original decor. Serves pork.

spots.name: Dharma Boutique Roastery
spots.desc: A coffee shop that has been established in 1916. There is traditional coffee processing.
spots.addr: Jl. Wotgandul Barat No.14, Kranggan, Central Semarang

spots.name: Malang Night Paradise
spots.desc: Family entertainment place with 2 theme parks. There are some replicas of dinousaurs.
spots.addr: Jl. Graha Kencana Raya No.66, Balearjosari, Blimbing, Kota

spots.name: Tugu Pahlawan & Museum Sepuluh November
spots.desc: A monument dedicated to the fallen heroes of Surabaya during the Independence war of 1945-49. Adjacent to the monument area is Museum Sepuluh Nopember, named after the declaration of war against the Dutch colony on November 10, 1945. There are uniforms, pictures, dioramas and a large collection of World Was II era weapons (pistols, rifles, machine guns and a mortar). Most of the information is…
spots.addr: Jalan Pahlawan, Kel. Alun-Alun Contong, Kec. Bubutan

spots.name: House of Sampoerna
spots.desc: Situated in "old Surabaya"‚ this stately Dutch colonial-style compound was built in 1862 and is now a preserved historical site. Once a top tourist destination in Surabaya, the building has been closed since the pandemic.

spots.name: Kenjeran Beach
spots.desc: A beach with black sand. There is also a bridge and water fountain show in the evening.

spots.name: Kahayan Bridge
spots.desc: One of the icon of Palangka Raya. The bridge connects to Palangka Raya and the other regencies in Central Kalimantan.

spots.name: Masjid Jami' Pontianak
spots.desc: The oldest mosque in Pontianak. This mosque is one of two buildings that marked the founding of Pontianak City in 1771 AD, besides the Kadriyah Palace.

spots.name: Kadriyah Palace
spots.desc: The palace of the Pontianak Sultanate which was built from 1771 to 1778 AD.
spots.addr: Jl. Tj. Raya 1, Dalam Bugis, Pontianak Timur

spots.name: Radakng House
spots.desc: Radakng is a long house derived from Dayak Kanayatn original house located in the province of Kalimantan Barat

spots.name: Ambon War Cemetery
spots.desc: The cemetery contains Australian soldiers who died during the Japanese invasion of Ambon and Timor in World War II

spots.name: Christina Martha Tiahahu Monument
spots.desc: Located in a hilly area. The best visiting time is in the afternoon because the statue or monument faces sunset and ambon bay. That is an amazing view to take some pictures of.

spots.name: Liang Beach
spots.desc: A white sand beach with trees. Very suitable for family picnics by laying out mats because of the shady atmosphere. There are food stalls sell fresh coconut drink and local instant noodles dish called Sarmento.

spots.name: Wisata Kolam Morea Larike
spots.desc: Watching giant freshwater eels named Morea in a clear and clean river. You can feed them with small fish which can be bought from local people for Rp20,000.
spots.addr: Larike, West Leihitu, Central Maluku Regency

spots.name: Lubang Buaya Morela Beach
spots.desc: A diving and snorkeling spot with many fish dan enormous coral reefs. Sometimes you can see the wild dolphins from the beach.

spots.name: Hatuasa Hot Spring
spots.desc: A natural hot spring in the middle sago forest. There are various pools based on the level of heat of the water.

spots.name: Taeno Waterfall
spots.desc: Located in a district with a forestry area in Ambon City. There is a natural pool below the waterfall. The water is really refreshing.
spots.addr: Rumah Tiga, Ambon Bay district, Ambon City

spots.name: Natsepa Beach
spots.desc: Try Rujak Natsepa, slices of fruits in sticky sweet spicy peanut sauce.

spots.name: General MacArthur Memorial
spots.desc: A monument honoring the American general Douglas MacArthur that defended the Philippines, New Guinea, and Australia from Japan on World War II; Then-Hollandia was where the military airplanes and operations took off. Whilst the memorial is basic, the steepness of the terrain makes the site a spectacular vantage point. A number of old Dutch colonial houses can also be seen on the road up to the…

spots.name: Base G Beach
spots.desc: A white sandy beach with pristine light blue waters overlooking the Pacific Ocean. Quiet and undisturbed, yet not so far from the city center. The gazebos there are for rent though and preferable for a long rest in groups. Though entrance to the beach is free, beware of rip-offs from locals.

spots.name: Hamadi Beach
spots.desc: A local harbor beach near the city. On the beach are four large artillery emplacements from the World War II. Further down the beach are the local fish markets. The beach is not very well-kept and covered in rubbish. However, at night a number of food stalls are set up and provides plenty of atmosphere. Also the new Holtekamp Bridge nearby is quite an eye-catching phenomenon.

spots.name: Harlem Beach
spots.desc: Watching sunset in the dusk. There is a natural freshwater pond on this beach.

spots.name: Lake Sentani
spots.desc: A large freshwater lake surrounded by steep mountains. A small number of restaurants and guesthouses are located on the edge of the lake.

spots.name: Teletubbies Hill
spots.desc: A scenic grassy hill that was named for its resemblance to the hill from the Teletubbies television show.

spots.name: Border Post Skouw
spots.desc: The border post between Indonesia and Papua New Guinea. There is a lighthouse so you may watch Solomon beach, Wutung in Papua New Guinea from above.

spots.name: Lukas Enemble Stadium Complex
spots.desc: There is an aquatic center, shooting range, indoor stadium, and football main stadium. You may see a football match on the weekend.

spots.name: Pantai Gunung Kunyit
spots.desc: This beach has small sand hills and is located near Mount Kunyit.
spots.addr: Jl. Ikan Terbang, Bumi Waras, Kec. Telukbetung Selatan

spots.name: North Sumatra Museum
spots.desc: It is the largest museum in North Sumatra which displays various historical and cultural relics of the nation, arts and crafts from various ethnic groups in North Sumatra.

spots.name: Tip Top Restaurant
spots.desc: Used to be the restaurant in Medan, this unique restaurant can trace its history back to the Dutch colonisation. The food has a nostalgic taste clinging on every bite, such as the ox-tongue sandwich and the bitter-ballen, but the best experience you could have here is watching the buzz of Kesawan Square from your rattan chair on the verandah. Also famous for its cake.
spots.addr: Jalan Jenderal Ahmad Yani no 92 A-B

spots.name: Besakih Temple
spots.desc: This temple complex is the holiest in Bali. It consists of 23 temples. The biggest, not surprisingly, has the word "agung" ("greatest") in its name and is called “Pura Penataran Agung”. The temple has six tiers, built as terraces.

spots.name: Alun-Alun Puputan
spots.desc: The huge four-faced, eight-armed Catur Mukha statue is situated here at the centre point of the city (Jl Gajah Mada/Jl Suprati). Representing the Lord Brahma and it serves as a guardian of each cardinal point. The square is a key point of orientation for the whole city. If you get lost, find your way back here and all will be clear. Often, locals play kite in the day and evening.

spots.name: Lapangan Puputan Margarana
spots.desc: This rather grandiose park is home to the huge Bajra Sandhi monument (literally Balinese People's Struggle). The design of the grey stone monument symbolises the date of Indonesian independence, August 17th 1945. There are eight entrances, 17 corners and the height is 45 m. The monument is most significant though for its commemoration of the various puputans (suicidal fight to the death) of the…
spots.addr: Renon, Denpasar Selatan, Panjer, Denpasar Selatan

spots.name: Palace of Satria and the Royal Temples
spots.desc: The palace and temple of the royal family of Denpasar which is beautifully kept. It is open to all residents of Denpasar for worship. Some wonderfully ornate carvings, even by Balinese standards.

spots.name: Pura Agung Jagatnata
spots.desc: A state temple which was built in 1953. Dedicated to the supreme being Sanghyang Widi Wasa, this temple is open to all worshipers without any restriction as it is a government building and not a village temple. 15-30 min visit. There are large ceremonies here twice a month at full moon and dark moon. Ask at the tourist office for a detailed schedule.
spots.price: Register and donation, usually Rp 20,000-100,000 with sarong. Guide Rp 10,000-50,000 (be clear to refuse if you don't…

spots.name: Taman Wedhi Budaya Cultural Centre
spots.desc: A museum that covers the history and essence of Balinese art. The classical schools are well represented by both paintings and sculpture and there is a large section featuring contemporary Balinese art. Gamelan orchestra performances are also held.

spots.name: Kereneng Night Market
spots.desc: This market starts up at sunset every day and is open until dawn. All manner of Indonesian food served from dozens of stalls. It is rough and ready, but the food is excellent and 100% authentic.

spots.name: Atoom Bara
spots.desc: Chinese restaurant specialising in seafood. It appears unimpressive but the food is fantastic.

spots.name: Warung Ayam Betutu Bu Ferdi
spots.desc: A halal Balinese cuisine such as Ayam Betutu, Nasi campur and Tum ayam.
spots.addr: Jl. Gn. Cemara Raya No.16, Tegal Harum, West Denpasar

spots.name: Kak Man
spots.desc: This place is an absolute institution. Truly excellent Balinese food including bebek betutu (smoked duck).

spots.name: Ayam Goreng Nyonya Suharti
spots.desc: Famous fried chicken cooked with an old family recipe from Java. A bit out of the way but definitely worth the effort in getting there.

spots.name: Ayam Taliwang
spots.desc: A restaurant noted for the Lombok speciality of Ayam Taliwang (grilled or fried young chicken). Spicy and delicious.

spots.name: Bali Bakery
spots.desc: Long established bakery and bistro/cafe. Very good quality bread, pastries and cakes produced fresh every day. Large lunch and dinner menu which includes local favourites and some well chosen international dishes.

spots.name: Cianjur
spots.desc: Named after a town in West Java, its dishes are influenced by Sundanese cuisine. A little out of the city centre in the suburb of Renon. The grilled and sour-sweet Ikan Gurame is especially recommended.

spots.name: Warung Wardani
spots.desc: Excellent Indonesian cuisine. Look no further than the Nasi Campur (rice with various spicy side dishes) which is what everyone comes here to eat.

spots.name: Hanamasa
spots.desc: Serves Japanese food like yakiniku, shabu-shabu, and robatayaki.

spots.name: Kereneng Night Market (Pasar Malam Kereneng)
spots.desc: This market starts up at sunset every day and is open until dawn. All manner of Indonesian food is served from dozens of stalls. It is rough and ready, but the food is excellent and authentic.

spots.name: Kopi Bali
spots.desc: An absolute must for coffee lovers. Indonesia produces some of the best coffee in the world and here you can order your favourite brew as well as buy the beans. Products include coffee from Central Java, Toraja from Sulawesi, Mandailing from Sumatra, and of course the very best of Bali coffee. The outlet of the famous Butterfly Globe brand.

spots.name: Lurik Yojo
spots.desc: Traditional back-loomed lurik cloth and hand-drawn batik in natural colours.

spots.name: Kopi Petruk
spots.desc: From the Lintas Merapi community group. Arabica beans and ready-ground, identified by the preparation process, roasting date, depth of roast, altitude of the plantation, and the farmers' group who grew it. Available in the delicatessen attached to the Mediterranean restaurant in Jogja.
spots.addr: Deles Indah RT27/009, Sidorejo, Kemalang, Klaten

spots.name: Museum Gunungapi Merapi
spots.desc: A volcano museum. There is a jeep or motorbike trail (Kinahrejo) from where tourists can see the destructive forces that shaped the landscape from the last major eruption.

spots.name: Girpasang Bridge
spots.desc: A suspension bridge for pedestrians. There is also a gondola that stretches over the river.

spots.name: Merapi Golf Yogyakarta
spots.desc: 8 holes designed by Thomson, Wolveridge & Perrett. On the slopes of Mount Merapi, where you can enjoy the scenic view of the mountains while playing. The course was partially damaged during the 2010 eruptions but has been restored.

spots.name: Kampung Pelangi Kalisari
spots.desc: A multi-colored rainbow village focused on sustainable initiatives. Near the village, there is a Kalisari floral market and a promising outlook in the wood construction library that won Architizer A+ Awards 2020 and became the winner of ArchDaily building of the year 2021, named .

spots.name: Semarang Contemporary Art Gallery
spots.desc: Modern gallery offering a selection of contemporary art in revolving exhibitions. Strong focus on Asian artists in general and Indonesian artists in particular.

spots.name: Taman Srigunting
spots.desc: A small, shady square nestled by the Gereja Blenduk. Good for a quick sit-down after the exertions of walking around the Old Town, and great for indulging in a bit of the Indonesian national pastime of taking selfies. Expect to be invited to join in photos with other visitors.

spots.name: Gedung Djakarta Lloyd
spots.desc: Gedung Djakarta Lloyd was once the office of the largest shipping company in the Netherlands named Stoomvaart Maatschappij Nederland (SMN). This building was designed by Ir. Thomas Karsten in 1930. SMN was later nationalized to become Djakarta Lloyd. Until now this building is still used as the office of state-owned, Djakarta Lloyd.

spots.name: Gedung Monod Diephuis & Co
spots.desc: Located in the middle of Hoogendoorpstraat, now Jalan Kepodang. Monod & Co company was founded in 1882 by CLF Monod de Froideville and is one of the oldest companies in Semarang. This company is engaged in brokerage, especially sugar, coffee, copra, and other agricultural products for export to Europe. The building is used for art galleries, public libraries, and wedding halls also social…

spots.name: Gedung Oudetrap
spots.desc: The building has a spiral staircase in front of the building, which was built in 1834. It was used as a spice warehouse in the Dutch colonial era.

spots.name: Gedung PELNI
spots.desc: This building was used by Koninklijke Paketvaart Maatschappij (KPM) in the early 20th century. The building is an Art Deco Indies style building that was first built in Semarang. Designed by F.J.L Ghijsels of the AIA bureau in 1917. Construction took a year and was only completed in 1918. Now, It is owned by the national marine passenger transport company, PT PELNI.

spots.name: Museum Kota Lama
spots.desc: The history of Semarang City since 1547. It is free but you have to make a reservation on Lunpia App, the application can be downloaded on Apple Store or Google Play.

spots.name: Hutan Wisata Tinjomoyo
spots.desc: A city forest with a lush atmosphere and an iconic suspension bridge. It is good for picnics and camping. Some music events had been held there.
spots.addr: Jl. Tinjomoyo Barat, Sukorejo, Gunung Pati

spots.name: Ngrembel Asri
spots.desc: Do paintball and fishing. There is also a kid's playground & pool also a restaurant serves ikan bakar (grilled fish).

spots.name: GOR Tri Lomba Juang
spots.desc: Running track, badminton, and tennis venue. Every afternoon, many Semarang people run and jog in this place.
spots.addr: Jl Kapten Piere Tendean No. 5, Sekayu

spots.name: Dug Der Festival
spots.desc: Annual festival, one week before fasting month, or puasa. The name is derived from the sound of bedug ("Dug" - the sound of a gigantic drum often associated with Islam), and meriam bambu ("Der" - the sound of the traditional bamboo cannon). At the end of the festival, there's "Ngarak Warak", meaning a procession to bring Warak across the city's main street (normally from the Mayor's office to the…

spots.name: Jaran Sampo
spots.desc: Attend the biggest ceremony of the Chinese community in Java, featuring a colourful procession and dances of decorated horses and 'liong' (dragon).
spots.addr: Tay Kak Sie and Sam Poo Kong Temples

spots.name: Jateng Fair
spots.desc: Annual showcase of the Central Java Promotions and Development. It's held between June and July.

spots.name: Loenpia Jazz
spots.desc: Etesian jazz music festival. Presenting local and national musicians. The event is hosted by the Semarang jazz community, Jazz Ngisoringin.

spots.name: Semarang Great Sale
spots.desc: Annual shopping promotions and discounts with lucky draws are held by the city council.

spots.name: Semarang Night Carnival
spots.desc: Yearly fashion carnival around Semarang city main road. It usually starts at the city hall.

spots.name: Wayang Wong Ngesti Pandowo
spots.desc: A weekly show of Javanese drama in the form of the human puppet (wayang orang in Indonesian or wayang wong in Javanese), with stories from folklore, Mahabarata, and Ramayana. There is a show every Saturday night. An excellent chance to get a glimpse of Javanese culture in Semarang

spots.name: Bandeng Juwana Elrina
spots.desc: Bandeng presto, lumpia Semarang, wingko babat, ganjel rel cake and more. Free tasting.

spots.name: Wingko Babat Cap Kereta Api
spots.desc: This outlet is just on the edge of Semarang's Old Town. In addition to wingko they have a wide range of other sweet and savoury snack stuffs, and a small selection of souvenirs like fridge magnets. The shop is a much calmer experience than the toko oleh-oleh of Jl Pandanaran which can be crowded and hot, especially if a coachload of tourists arrives.

spots.name: Tahu Baxo Ibu Pudji
spots.desc: Tahu bakso is tofu stuffed with beef or fish dough. It is a delicacy of Ungaran, Semarang (Regency).

spots.name: DP Mall
spots.desc: The mall has three floors. Fashion tenants include H&M, Uniqlo, and Giordano. It is a comfortable place to hang out with culinary tenants including Sushi Tei, Yoshinoya and Istana Mie & Es. There are the Cinema XXI cinema and Masterpiece karaoke on the second floor.

spots.name: Mall Ciputra
spots.desc: The ground floor has many fashion options, including The Bra House, Andre Valentino, Batik Keris, Hammer, Giordano, Nike, dan Rotelli Shoes. The first floor has more with Planet Surf, Wacoal, Warna Fashion dan Fada Boutique. The second floor has XXI and Citra 21 cinemas.

spots.name: Pasar Karangayu
spots.desc: One of the biggest traditional markets in Semarang. Just 5 km away from the airport.

spots.name: Pasar Peterongan
spots.desc: Known for its old tamarind tree. It is older than the market which was built in 1916.

spots.name: Ayam Goreng Mbok Berek
spots.desc: Ayam penyet (traditional Javanese fried chicken that is smashed in a mortar and pestle so you can enjoy the sumsum - marrow), served with sambal and lalapan (raw vegetables).

spots.name: Nasi Goreng Babat Hengky
spots.desc: Nasi goreng babat is a typical Semarang's nasi goreng with tripe. It is a sweet, spicy, and savoury dish. Also, try babat gongso (tripe in sweet, spicy, and garlicky sauce).
spots.addr: Jl. Puri Anjasmoro Blok K, Tawangsari

spots.name: Tahu Petis Prasojo
spots.desc: Tahu petis is a typical Semarang fried tofu with black coloured shrimp paste sauce called petis inside, eat them while they're hot with a green chilli named cabe rawit if you love spicy hot snack.

spots.name: Gule Kambing Bustaman Pak Sabar
spots.desc: Gule is a type of Javanese food containing rich, spicy, and succulent curry-like soup. The main ingredient of this dish is goat meat.
spots.addr: Kota Lama (Old City), Tanjung Mas, North Semarang

spots.name: Kampung Serabi Kalicari
spots.desc: Try the local dessert of Semarang, bubur serabi, pudding with some small pancakes in a sweet coconut milk soup. It is served in a bowl made from banana leaves.

spots.name: Kedai Beringin Indonesia
spots.desc: frequently visited by office workers at lunchtime for its cheap and good Javanese-style dishes - rice with various soupy dishes (rawon, asem-asem daun kedondong, etc), nasi campur, gado-gado and so on. Various ice-based desserts are also available. Halal. Opens for two sessions a day. The first, at lunchtime, offers the Javanese menu. Opening again in the late afternoon and evening, it offers a…

spots.name: Mie Kopyok Pak Dhuwur
spots.desc: Mie kopyok is boiled noodles served in garlic soup with slices of fried tofu, rice cake, bean sprouts, and crushed crackers, sprinkled with sliced fresh celery, and fried shallot.

spots.name: Penyet Kuah Timoho
spots.desc: Spicy Indonesian soups, including tempeh, tofu, chicken & seafood, are on offer in this snug neighborhood eatery. Usually, ayam penyet is an Indonesian fried chicken with sambal and raw veggies. Unlike the case here, ayam penyet kuah is a chicken served in thick and spicy coconut milk gravy. The pioneer of penyet in gravy in Semarang.
spots.addr: Jl. Timoho Raya No.32, Bulusan, Tembalang

spots.name: Semawis Night Market
spots.desc: Night market, Friday, Saturday and Sunday nights. Hawker-style local food. There's also an annual, larger Semawis Market before Chinese New Year.

spots.name: Simpang Lima
spots.desc: This square in the heart of Semarang has plenty of stalls offering a variety of local food. Prices are low: a piece of fried chicken, a thigh or a leg, plus a plate of steamed rice for as little as Rp15,000. Some stalls offer lesehan (sitting on a mat), with or without a low table. Active from early morning until late at night. The best stalls are busy and sell out quickly. You will also find…

spots.name: Soto Bangkong
spots.desc: Clear chicken soup, a local variation of the soto ayam found across Indonesia. A Semarang institution.
spots.addr: Ruko Bangkong Plaza, Jl. Brigjen Katamso No. 1, Peterongan

spots.name: Warung Bubur Berkah
spots.desc: Serves porridge bubur terik and bubur ketan kinco for breakfast.

spots.name: Ikan Bakar Cianjur
spots.desc: Highly dependable Sundanese food with quick service in lovely old Dutch bank building. The name refers to the grilled fish for which it is famous.

spots.name: Dyriana Bakery & Cafe
spots.desc: Freshly baked bread — try "roti pisang" (bread with a small banana inside) —– cakes, and a nice cafe serving local hot food and cold drinks. Air-conditioned. Often has demonstrations of traditional products being made (call first, often around 15:00-17:00).

spots.name: Elrina Restaurant
spots.desc: Serving different dishes of milkfish with local taste, Chinese and seafood. Air-conditioned.

spots.name: Gelato Matteo
spots.desc: Real Italian gelato made by a real Italian man. All the favourite flavours plus some specials. Cups, cones and in brioche. Small range of other snacks, and proper Italian coffee.

spots.name: Karuna
spots.desc: One of Semarang's only vegetarian restaurants. In the Chinese style, this replicates meat-dishes but with mushrooms, beancurd and tempe. Canteen-style, where you look in the case and point to what you want. On Saturdays it has a fixed-price all you can eat offer, but you have to clear your plate. If not, you will be fined. Has a small selection of wholefoods for sale as well - pulses, dried…

spots.name: Mbah Jingkrak
spots.desc: One of the chain of Javanese restaurants. Choose from a large number of dishes laid out - white or red rice, beancurd and tempe dishes, devil's hair chicken (pitik rambut setan), hot and sour steamed chicken (garang asem). Staff will spoon portions of those you point to, then the total is added up when you get to the end. Bentuman Steak shares the same building.

spots.name: Nglaras Rasa
spots.desc: Regular food and buffet. Specialising in catering for large groups, including coach parties. Air-conditioned.

spots.name: Sate & Gule Kambing 29
spots.desc: Anything you like, as long as it is goat. Famous for its goat sate and soup. This is the original restaurant, with original interiors and no air-conditioning. There are two more branches in Semarang - less inspiring interiors, but they do have AC, and a branch in each of Yogyakarta and Jakarta.

spots.name: Talisman Rotisserie
spots.desc: It's all about chicken - mostly cooked on a rotisserie, but also soups. Salads and sides, including mashed potatoes. Part of the same group as the Basilia and Massimo restaurants.
spots.addr: Jl Teuku Umar No. 18, Gajah Mungkur

spots.name: Warung Kepala Manyung Bu Fat
spots.desc: Offering mangut ikan manyung (ariid catfish in yellow coconut milk-curry soup).

spots.name: The Blue Lotus Coffeehouse
spots.desc: Famous for the freshly home-roasted Indonesian coffee and eight different ways of brewing, but has a great selection of Western food and Japanese cheesecake. Comfy sofas and strong Wi-Fi.

spots.name: Bowery
spots.desc: Steaks, wine, cocktails, mocktails, generally fine dining. Western and Asian. Black and chrome, atmospheric lighting, Gotham-city vibe. Paired with the more casual dining Eastman.

spots.name: Holliday
spots.desc: Chinese food, including dim sum, is often considered the best Chinese restaurant.

spots.name: Pesta Keboen
spots.desc: Indonesian and Dutch cuisine served in a restored Dutch colonial house furnished with antiques and Dutch East Indies memorabilia. Go there for the ambiance.

spots.name: Pringgading Restaurant
spots.desc: Chinese food with an Indonesian flair. Yum cha on Sunday mornings. Always full, very lively, and chaotic. Service is not outstanding.

spots.name: Rinjani View
spots.desc: One-stop entertainment, food, and beverage centre in the upper town. Rinjani View consists of six outlets: Resto, Lounge, Teraz, Karaoke, The Cafe, and Apartment's View. There's a fabulous view of Semarang City and Java Sea from all six. Serves Western, Chinese, and Indonesian food. WiFi is available.
spots.addr: Jl Rinjani No.12 (across the street from Hotel Candi Baru)

spots.name: Seoul Palace
spots.desc: Korean-style restaurant, with delicious barbecue, flavourful soups, and noodle dishes. Does not serve pork.

spots.name: Sisingamangaraja Site
spots.desc: A modern and hip mixed-use complex where people can hang out, drink, eat Japanese, Peranakan, or Western cuisine, or have coffee and desserts.

spots.name: Spiegel Bar and Bistro
spots.desc: Thoughtful and atmospheric reworking of an almost derelict heritage building, which was a general store during colonial times. Pizza, burgers, pasta, steak, fish and chips, Caesar salad - the menu is similar to all other Indonesian venues of this kind. A few surprises here and there. It's a bar too, so there is alcohol, but also means smoking is allowed. The building also hosts two related…

spots.name: The Tavern
spots.desc: Steaks, burgers, grills, pasta, pizzas. A selection of Indonesian dishes. Beer, wine. Fills up quickly so book or go early.

spots.name: Trattoria
spots.desc: One of the chain of Italian restaurants found across southeast Asia. Dependable and good - pizzas, kinds of pasta, steak. Also serves Japanese sushi and sashimi. Serves wine by the glass.
spots.addr: The Vee Building, Jl Gajah Mada, Brumbungan

spots.name: Xiang Yuen
spots.desc: Jl Sisingamangaraja No. 16. M-F 06:00-15:00 & 18:30-22:30, Sa-Su p7:00-15:00 & 18:30-22:30. Authentic Cantonese & Szechuanese. Rp100,000-1,000,000.

spots.name: Marabunta Resto and Bar
spots.desc: Using one of the old historic buildings in the old town. During the Dutch colonial period in Indonesia, this building was used as a city theater building. During its active period, the Marabunta Building was used as a special recreational building for the Dutch. The building was only used for comedy, orchestra, and ballet performances. The bar serves cocktails and Western & Indonesian foods.

spots.name: Es Cao Gang Lombok
spots.desc: Es cao is a traditional Semarang iced drink with black grass jelly, coconut, and red colour coconut pandan syrup.

spots.name: Es Kelapa Muda Kartika
spots.desc: One of the most delicious young coconut drinks. Daytime only, just get there early because in late afternoon they're most likely sold out already.

spots.name: Es Puter Cong Lik
spots.desc: A traditional ice cream based on coconut milk, with fruits, coconut and jelly.

spots.name: Jamu Jun Mbak Lina
spots.desc: Jamu jun is a typical Semarang's jamu (Indonesian herbal medicinal drink). It is made from rice flour and some spices.

spots.name: Wedang Kacang Kapuran
spots.desc: Offering one of the traditional drink of Semarang, wedang kacang tanah (hot drink made from peanut).

spots.name: Northern alun-alun
spots.desc: Large open field associated with the royal palace. A favourite place for walking, jogging, hanging out during free time. Usually has food stalls. Best times of the day are early morning, late afternoon or in the evening.

spots.name: South Alun-alun
spots.desc: the King's ground. Closed for renovation until further notice at May 2024.

spots.name: Puro Mangkunegaran
spots.desc: Palace of the Mangkunegara Princes. A beautiful palace built in 1757 with an awe-inspiring main audience hall. Facility: museum, art and cultural centre.
spots.price: Entry fee: Rp 20,000 for domestic tourist, Rp 50,000 for international tourist, photo fee Rp 3,500. Guide included, tip…

spots.name: Taman Monumen 45 Banjarsari
spots.desc: This park was a horse racing ground. The area surrounding the park was turned into villas for Dutch plantation workers. Monumen 45 was built on November 10, 1976 on the park grounds to commemorate the Four-Day General Assault which happened on the park from August 7 to August 10, 1949.

spots.name: Tien Kok Sie Temple
spots.local: Wihara Sudiroprajan, Klenteng Sudiroprajan, Vihara Avalokiteśvara
spots.desc: Temple combining elements of Buddhism, Confucianism and Taoism (sometimes known as tridharma), built in 1745.

spots.name: Sahasra Adhi Pura
spots.desc: A new Javanese Hindu temple and Kundalini yoga centre with 50 miniatures of sacred sites from around the world. Offers Ganesha fire meditation M and Th at 17:00.

spots.name: Kampung Batik Kauman
spots.desc: The batik products of Kauman village are made from natural silk and weaving silk materials, and premmisima cotton.

spots.name: Windujenar
spots.desc: A popular antique market in Solo. Beware of counterfeits but, if you look carefully, you might find an item from the palace.

spots.name: Galabo Night Food Court
spots.desc: Street of food vendors. Hundreds of tables under umbrellas. Closed if raining. Orders are placed with the food vendor and they bring it to your table.

spots.name: Bakmi Jawa Padmasari
spots.desc: Bakmi Jawa are fried or soupy noodles found across Java. Traditionally cooked on a charcoal stove (anglo) to give it the distinctive taste.

spots.name: Sate Kambing-Buntel Pak H. Kasdi
spots.desc: Try Sate buntel, a type of satay made from minced mutton wrapped in goat fat and then grilled. Originating from Solo.

spots.name: Timlo Solo
spots.desc: Timlo is made from seasoned chicken liver, eggs and fried pastry with meat filling (sosis Jawa).

spots.name: Gudeg Margoyudan
spots.desc: Gudeg is worth a try in Solo, even though the gudeg of Jogja is acclaimed as being the original and best. Gudeg from Jogja is considered drier and sweet, while that from Solo is saltier with more sauce. This one is very popular and often crowded.

spots.name: Serabi Notosuman Nyonya Lidia
spots.desc: Serabi are pancakes made from rice flour and coconut milk. Extremely popular as oleh-oleh carry-home gifts, but are much better eaten warm from the shop. There are many versions including with chocolate sprinkles. This is the original shop for this brand, but there are branches across Central Java and beyond.
spots.addr: Jl Mr. Moh. Yamin No.28, Jayengan

spots.name: Selat Solo Tenda Biru
spots.desc: A specialty dish of Solo, selat Solo, veggies, meat, and egg in gravy.
spots.addr: Jl. Dr. Wahidin No.26, Purwosari, Laweyan

spots.name: Pasar Gede
spots.desc: Eat some traditional Solo food such as cabuk rambak, rice cake with special sauce and crackers, also brambang asem kangkung, water spinach dish with gembus (Javanese tofu dregs).
spots.addr: Jl. Jend. Urip Sumoharjo, Sudiroprajan, Jebres

spots.name: Soga Restaurant & Lounge
spots.desc: In the House of Danar Hadi complex. This is a proper casual dining restaurant, the cuisine offered is a blend of traditional Javanese as well as some western/Dutch colonial cuisine. Dishes are presented elegantly and the atmosphere is grand and cosy, with colonial antiques and batik decorating the interior as well as TVs. Live piano and music every night. An alternative to the street food culture…

spots.name: Northern alun-alun
spots.desc: Built for training the Sultan's army, it was opened to the public during the reign of Sultan Hamengkubuwono IX. Now used for the quarterly Garebeg parade held in the months of Maulud, Besar and Sawal, according to the Javanese calendar. In the parade, the Sultan's servants carry huge cone-shaped offerings to the alun-alun. After the parade, attendees scramble to get a scrap of the offering as it…

spots.name: Carriage Museum
spots.desc: Houses the Sultan's horse-drawn carriages, including two beautiful carriages imported from the Netherlands and known as Golden Carriages (kereta kencana).
spots.price: Foreigners: adult Rp30,000, child Rp25,000; domestic: adult Rp20,000, children Rp15,000

spots.name: Bentara Budaya
spots.desc: A cultural institute set up by the Kompas Gramedia publishing and media group. Branches in Jogja, Jakarta, Solo and Bali. Art exhibitions, movies, book discussions.

spots.name: Cemeti Art House
spots.desc: Fine art and modern art exhibitions, book discussions and performances.

spots.name: French/Indonesian Cultural Center (LIP)
spots.desc: Art exhibitions, movies, book discussions, performances, library.

spots.name: Kedai Kebun
spots.desc: Art space managed by artists including gallery, performance space, bookstore and restaurant. Art exhibitions, performances, book discussions. Has accommodation for rent.

spots.name: Tjokrosuharto
spots.desc: This handicraft shop opens its door for business in 1954 and still operating today. It offers a large selection of Javanese handicrafts such as wayang kulit (leather puppet), wayang golek (wooden puppet), batik, keris, silverware, sculptures, and traditional outfits.

spots.name: Dagadu
spots.desc: Offers funny contemporary t-shirts and souvenirs that revolves around Yogyakarta people's culture.

spots.name: Ciamis Art Shop
spots.desc: Shadow puppets, masks, carvings, and more at fixed prices that are lower than in the market.

spots.name: Nadzar
spots.desc: Huge souvenir shop specializing in batik, art, jewellery, and more. Has every souvenir you could imagine at fixed prices.

spots.name: Hamzah Batik
spots.desc: The large family-owned store offers plenty of handicrafts, not only from Yogyakarta but also from all parts of Indonesia.

spots.name: Ori Art Gallery
spots.desc: A reputable batik painting shop with a large selection and fair prices, and you can usually watch an artist there demonstrating the fascinating and meticulous technique.

spots.name: Galleria Mall
spots.desc: A compact mall anchored by Matahari department store. The food court at the basement is popular among the youths. Features many interesting restaurant including KFC, McDonald's Express, Thai Express, Bakso Gress (Chinese meatballs served with noodles), Mie Nusantara, Bee's (Japanese Bento), Es Teler 77, and Cheers Cup (assortments of fresh drinks).

spots.name: Ramai Mall and Ramai Supermarket
spots.desc: Big department store. The least expensive A/C supermarket in Jogja.

spots.name: Angkringan Tugu
spots.desc: Famous for its small rice packets (sego kucing). Drink kopi joss, strong Javanese coffee heated by dropping a piece of glowing charcoal into it.

spots.name: Bakmi Jawa Harjo Geno
spots.desc: Be prepared to wait up to two hours! Tip: if you think that fried noodles go well with beer, you can grab a Bintang at the nearby Tante Lies restaurant.

spots.name: Gudeg Tugu
spots.desc: Popular Gudeg stall. A complete dish consists of: warm rice, shredded chicken, brown hard-boiled egg, gudeg, areh sauce, and the hot & spicy sambal goreng krecek.

spots.name: Kamikoti Cafe
spots.desc: Serving good quality milk, coffee & tea at affordable prices, near Masangin and the Taman Sari complex.

spots.name: Rame Rame Vegetarian
spots.desc: A very small restaurant with meat and vegetarian options and owned by a very friendly woman. Has a delicious soup, noodles, mushrooms, vegetables, meatballs and cilantro for Rp9,000.

spots.name: Rumah Makan Es Ceria
spots.desc: Great, cheap food including a smorgasbord where you choose what you like and then the cashier estimates a price. Tasty and cheap. Also ice desserts and fruit shakes.

spots.name: Sagan Super Sambal
spots.desc: Specialising in sambal, the Indonesian delicacy of spicy, hot chilli infused sauce. Also, Indonesian-style beef ribs.
spots.addr: Jl Sagan I no. 5 and Jl Timoho no. 111

spots.name: Soto Pak Soleh
spots.desc: This well-known restaurant is Pak Soleh's family business and is now operated by his son. They only serve Yogyakarta-style beef soup as their main menu, which has a spicy taste from ginger.

spots.name: Waroeng Jepara
spots.desc: Famous for their traditional Jepara flavours (only warung in Jogjakarta that serves Jepara food), this modern-furnished warung is run by friendly locals. Speciality includes "pecil pari" (spicy stingray), "bothok tahu" (tofu in papaya leaf) and "sayur lodeh" (jackfruit soup).

spots.name: Xtra Hot
spots.desc: A local tent (tenda) restaurant specialising in grilled food, with a good variety of sambals (chili) to choose from, yet with good prices.

spots.name: The House of Raminten
spots.desc: Javanese restaurant with traditional food like jamu godhog (Indonesia's herbal recipe).

spots.name: Dapur Solo
spots.desc: Special Yogyakarta and Jawa Tengah delicacies. Famous here are nasi timlo and nasi liwet.

spots.name: Empek-Empek Kamto
spots.desc: Originating from Palembang, deep-fried fish cake and served with sour soy sauce. There are many varieties of empek-empek: kapal selam (means submarine) comes with boiled eggs inside, adaaan/bulat has a garlic taste, while lenggang is an empek-empek omelette.

spots.name: Bakmi Kadin
spots.desc: Javanese style soft-fried noodles. Don't miss the popular wedang bajigur, a local beverages made from warm coconut milk with subtle ginger flavour and garnished with diced coconut and kolang-kaling. Local kroncong street quartet often performs in the area.

spots.name: Sate Karang
spots.desc: Grilled beef satay served with lontongs (rice cake), peanut sauce and thin curry soup.

spots.name: Easy Groovy
spots.desc: A beautiful restaurant & bar on a lively spot with a nice terrace. serving tasty Mexican, Indonesian and Western dishes in a comfortable and warm atmosphere. Also a great place to sit on the terrace to enjoy a drink. Happy Hour until 19:00 discount on beers, wine and cocktails. Wifi is free of charge. Live Music on the weekends from 8:30pm.

spots.name: FoodFezt
spots.desc: Many kinds of local Indonesian foods: Nasi kebuli, nasi merah, soto betawi, sate buntel, mushroom satay and also dessert-like pancakes, and ice creams. It has a garden with lots of bamboo trees and other plants. The waiters use wireless gadgets to serve their customers in order to maintain a 'paperless' order system.

spots.name: Gudeg Sagan
spots.desc: An eating place in Jalan Sagan (in front of Toko Sagan Baru) offering rice, seasoned porridge, gudeg, areh sauce, sambal goreng krecek, complete with chicken and brown hard-boiled egg.

spots.name: Kedai Rakjat Djelata
spots.desc: Javanese cuisine with a modern twist. Tasty food in a nice setting, yet not expensive.

spots.name: Kedai Tiga Nyonya
spots.desc: Peranakan food restaurant, a fusion of Indonesian, Chinese and Dutch cuisine. Their speciality is grilled fish, sour ribs soup and candlenut chicken.

spots.name: Kesuma Restaurant
spots.desc: Local home cooking in the familiarity of a typical Kampung house.

spots.name: Mie Bandung
spots.desc: Despite the name, this is not a noodle restaurant, but rather a Chinese restaurant. Don't expect authentic Chinese food, but rather Indonesian-Chinese. The wonton is really good though, and they also serve beer! If you find yourself craving Chinese food in Jogja, this is one of the few places you can go to.

spots.name: Pesona Rasa
spots.desc: A nice Chinese food family restaurant. Serves delicious and fresh Chinese dishes such as: fried rice, fried noodle, tofu, fresh capjay and vegetables. In Pathuk area, 5 minutes from Malioboro. With friendly service and wallet-friendly prices.
spots.addr: Jalan Aip. II K. S. Tubun no. 15

spots.name: Sendang K Pitoe
spots.desc: A famous shrimp and sea food restaurant located on the outskirts of the city, specifically Jamur, Minggir, Sleman. Very delicious fried shrimp served fresh from the ponds in the still relatively untouched village. Should not be confused with the nearby Mang Engking, also a shrimp restaurant with an ill-earned reputation for dirty food.

spots.name: Takigawa
spots.desc: Japanese restaurant that also serves shabu-shabu (Japanese hot pot).

spots.name: Mediterranea
spots.desc: Serves French and Mediterranean dishes. Open all day, serving breakfast before midday. Sells espresso and has a wide range of fresh juices available. Also includes a small specialty shop with imported goods and fresh baked bread and pastries. Best croissants in Jogja.
spots.price: main course Rp100,000-300,000, breakfast Rp37,000-70,0000, pizza Rp53,000-81,000, dessert Rp35,000-45,000

spots.name: Embassy
spots.desc: In Sheraton Hotel complex area (there's a tunnel connecting the club). Entrance fee around Rp35,000-100,000, depends on the event. Full set DJs. Music ranges from trance, house, to dubstep. The drinks are genuine, but are pretty pricey. Have a weekly discount night called Monday Madness 50% off. Usually they have free drinks from 22:00-02:00 on the last Thursday of every month with a fee of…

spots.name: Easy Garden
spots.desc: Cosy beanbags in a lush garden or sitting under grape pergola. Offers shisha as well for Rp75,000. Live music Th-Sa nights from 21:00. Free plunge pool, billiard table & wifi.

spots.name: Perpustakaan Pusat Studi Pedesaaan dan Kawasan UGM
spots.desc: Unlike most of the other university libraries in the city, this one is open to the general public. The collection is mostly about the social sciences.
spots.addr: Bulaksumur G/7 PO. Box. 2 UGM, Sayap Selatan

spots.name: Ijen Boulevard
spots.desc: This is a quite beautiful street. It is lined with well-tended bougainvillea against a backdrop of old colonial structures. The street houses a number of interesting buildings including the Brawijaya Army Museum, the Catholic Church and the city library. Usually every Sunday, there is an event called "Car Free Day" when almost all of Ijen Boulevard is free of motorised vehicles. There is also a…

spots.name: Soekarno Hatta Boulevard
spots.desc: Hub for shopping, dining, and entertainment, offering a diverse array of modern amenities and attractions. It’s home to numerous cafes, restaurants, and retail stores, making it a popular destination for both locals and tourists. Whether you’re looking to explore trendy boutiques or enjoy a delicious meal, Soekarno Hatta Boulevard provides a dynamic and lively atmosphere that captures the essence…
spots.addr: Jl. Soekarno Hatta, Jatimulyo, Kec. Lowokwaru

spots.name: Fabulous Spa & Salon
spots.desc: Offers professional massage and spa treatments in clean and relaxing ambience including body spa, body scrub, Balinese touch massage, manicure and pedicure spa. There is also a hair salon which offers haircuts and styling. Supplies are ordered in small and selected batches to ensure freshness when they are used. Fresh new towels are provided for each guest.

spots.name: Mall Olympic Garden (MOG)
spots.desc: Numerous well-known retail stores, trendy fashion outlets, and a variety of dining establishments, from local favorites to international cuisine.

spots.name: Malang Town Square
spots.desc: Premier shopping and entertainment destination in Malang. Matos offers a diverse range of shops, from trendy fashion boutiques to electronics stores, in addition to shopping, visitors can enjoy a variety of dining options, from casual eateries to popular fast-food chains. The mall also features a cinema and entertainment zones, providing a complete leisure experience for families and friends.…
spots.addr: Jl. Veteran No.2, Penanggungan, Kec. Klojen

spots.name: Warung Pojok
spots.desc: Very well known for rujak (salad with spicy sweet peanut sauce).

spots.name: Martabak Cairo
spots.desc: The kopi jahe is infused with cloves for a powerful and simply decadent taste. Serving martabak, sate kambing and nasi goreng cairo.

spots.name: Warung Subuh
spots.desc: Dizzying array of foods, incredibly cheap, fresh and delicious. This place is booming with locals, so you know it's good. A great place to try some new and interesting food and drink.

spots.name: Kongkow cafe
spots.desc: Friendly owner who speaks good English and has good knowledge of area. Good and free wifi. Reasonable prices with western movie themed menu. Is about 500 metres northwest of railway station. Corner of Jl. Patimura and Jl. Trunojoyo

spots.name: Museum Rudi Isbandi
spots.desc: Holdings collected from 1952 to 2009. Opened in 2009, and named after collector Rudi Isbandi. Address: Karangwismo I/10, Surabaya.

spots.name: Museum H.O.S. Tjokroaminoto
spots.desc: A national hero museum, H.O.S. Tjokroaminoto was an Indonesian nationalist. He became one of the leaders of the Sarekat Dagang Islam (Islamic Trade Union).
spots.addr: Jl. Peneleh Gg. VII No.29-31, Peneleh, Genteng

spots.name: Museum Dr. Soetomo
spots.desc: A national hero museum, Soetomo was a doctor, politician, and National Hero of Indonesia.

spots.name: Museum De Javasche Bank
spots.desc: A Bank museum. Bank of Java (Dutch: De Javasche Bank, DJB), which had been created in 1828 to serve the financial needs of the Dutch East Indies.
spots.addr: Jl. Garuda No.1, Krembangan Sel., Krembangan

spots.name: Gereja Kelahiran Santa Perawan Maria
spots.desc: The oldest Catholic church in Surabaya. Beautiful glass panels and serene surroundings.

spots.name: Hok An Kiong Chinese Temple (Klenteng Jalan Coklat)
spots.desc: Excellent example of an older Chinese Southeast Asian temple, built in the early 19th century. Numerous old wooden carvings and statues from around the region. Just ask a bicycle to bring you to "Jalan Coklat" (Chocolate street) and you'll see a bright red temple building. Afterwards, walk westward then north through some of the city's numerous examples of old colonial commercial architecture.

spots.name: Masjid Ampel
spots.desc: Built in 1421 by Sunan Ampel, this is the oldest mosque in East Java. In the left side of the mosque there is a well that is believed to be the auspicious well, typically used by believers to strengthen a pledge or oath. Sunan Ampel's tomb complex is located in the area.

spots.name: G-Walk
spots.desc: In west Surabaya (CitraLand). There are many food stalls and bazaars at night where you can find a lot of good food. It gets very crowded at night and it's a place for a lot of young people to hang out. There is a food market, and close to G-Walk you'll also find some bars. G-Walk is located between Pakuwon Super Mall and Ciputra Golf.

spots.name: Ekowisata mangrove wonorejo Rungkut - Surabaya
spots.desc: About 30 min boat to seaside with bamboo bridges and shelters. good for picnic and chill. Expect wait for boat depending on conditions.
spots.addr: Jl. Wonorejo Timur No.1, Wonorejo, Kec. Rungkut

spots.name: Bukit Darmo Golf
spots.desc: This golf course is located in the elite housing area in West Surabaya. This course has 18 holes, designed by Jack Nicklaus II.
spots.addr: Jl. Bukit Darmo Golf Blok G-2

spots.name: Ahmad Yani Golf Club
spots.desc: This course is built in hilly terrain and is the oldest course in town, built in 1898, with the crypt of the last Dutch Governor on it.

spots.name: Golf Graha Famili
