spots.desc: 18 holes, inside Graha Famili real estate site, near the Bukit Darmo Golf.

spots.name: Pakuwon Golf
spots.desc: For beginners, try this golf course instead within Pakuwon Estate - an 18-hole par 3 course; the 'back nine' are quite challenging.

spots.name: Golf Petrokimia Gresik
spots.desc: This 9-hole Par 3 course can be found on the estate of Petrokimia Gresik in Gresik.

spots.name: Grand City Mall
spots.desc: Next to Grand City Convention and Exhibition Hall. The luxurious mall in Surabaya.

spots.name: Pasar Atom & Pasar Atom Mall
spots.desc: Anchored by Hartani. A large, indoor Chinese and local market, selling food, clothes, jewellery, catering to Chinese locals. You can bargain here. Loads of DVDs, excellent food court (from 12:00), featuring excellent vegetarian cuisine among at least 40 other choices.

spots.name: Plaza Surabaya (Delta Plaza)
spots.desc: Anchored by Matahari and Superindo. One of the oldest shopping malls in town. Beside Delta Plaza is the Monkasel (Monumen Kapal Selam) or the Submarine Monument.

spots.name: Maspion Square
spots.desc: Anchored by Giant. A shopping mall situated in Southern Surabaya.

spots.name: World Trade Center (WTC)
spots.desc: Despite its name, the building is actually more famous as the place to shop for mobile phones. Beware of pickpockets. Locals often refer to it as 'World Telephone Center'.

spots.name: HI-TECH Mall (THR Mall)
spots.desc: Dismall place to shop for computers, software and computer peripherals.

spots.name: Roode Brug Soerabaia
spots.desc: Heritage souvenirs specialist. Reference books about old Surabaya, miniatures of Suramadu Bridge and KRI Pasopati Submarine which is done with a high level of detail. Heritage buildings on T-shirts such as the lindeteves-stokvis & Haven Kantoor building. You can enquire about a special heritage tour to Surabaya old kampong and heritage building.

spots.name: Cak Cuk Surabaya
spots.desc: Eclectic souvenir shop with the theme of Surabaya on many of its products.
spots.addr: Jl Mayjen Sungkono 35, Putat Gede, Sukomanunggal

spots.name: Pasar Genteng
spots.desc: Around this market you'll find shops selling bandeng asap (smoked milk fish) and kerupuk (local chips). Also known as the largest electronic spare part market in Indonesia (level 2 and above).

spots.name: Pasar Ampel
spots.desc: A large colourful Arab market, and a definite highlight of the city. You are able to find unique food here. An excellent place to shop for hats, imported dates, perfumes, water pipes and tobacco, a Quran for that special someone, etc. Dress reasonably conservatively and be friendly. Most people are very warm and it is perfectly safe in the day time, but you can meet the odd person who is less…

spots.name: Pecel Bu Kus
spots.desc: Serves Pecel (traditional Javanese salad with peanut sauce).

spots.name: Lontong Balap Pak Gendut
spots.desc: Lontong balap is made of lontong (compressed rice cake wrapped in a banana leaf), tauge (bean sprouts), fried tofu, lentho (fried mashed beans), fried shallots, petis (black coloured shrimp paste sauce), and sweet soy sauce. It served with sate kerang (clam satay).

spots.name: Sate Klopo Ondomohen Bu Asih
spots.desc: Serves Sate Klopo (beef satay with grated coconut). Small dining area, filled with smoke from the satay grill.

spots.name: Rawon Setan Embong Malang
spots.desc: Serves rawon (dark beef soup). You may try the local Surabaya iced drink es sinom.

spots.name: Tahu Telor Pak Jayen
spots.desc: Serves tahu tek or tahu telor (tofu dish with peanut and shrimp paste sauce).
spots.addr: Jl. Dharmahusada Indah I Blok C No.2, Mulyorejo

spots.name: Kafe Bromo
spots.desc: Offers delicious all day dining in a relaxed setting with a view that gives to pool.
spots.addr: Sheraton Surabaya Hotel & Towers, Jl. Embong Malang 25-31

spots.name: Domicile Kitchen and Lounge
spots.desc: A modern and chic kitchen, serving "new-age" cuisine and pastries. Open for brunch until late night for supper and cocktails.

spots.name: Ahimsa Restaurant
spots.desc: Best known vegetarian restaurant in stylish decor. Pan Asian, Chinese and Indonesian cuisine.

spots.name: Trattoria Valentino
spots.desc: Italian-owned restaurant, wood-fired pizza, hand-made pastas. Family-style, good prices. Italian, English and Indonesian speakers.

spots.name: Lung Yuan Chinese Restaurant
spots.desc: The menu features fresh seafood, premium fish and various Cantonese dishes. Has a private room suitable for a business meeting or family gathering.
spots.addr: Sheraton Surabaya Hotel & Towers, Jl. Embong Malang 25-31

spots.name: Citilites Skyclub & Bistro
spots.desc: On the 21st floor with a good view of the city lights. Regional and international beverages, snacks, and pastries. Cozy and stylish.

spots.name: The D Club
spots.desc: Comfortable place to enjoy wine, and premium cigars from Indonesia, Cuba, Honduras and Nicaragua.

spots.name: Lava Lounge
spots.desc: Cheap beer, great outdoor setting. Nice regulars that are ex-pats and Indonesian. Arak Bali (an Indonesian vodka-like spirit), cocktails, coffee, tenderloin steak, and nachos.

spots.name: Rumah Hutan
spots.desc: Forest area with tree houses. It is located on private property, but the owner allows people to come for picnicking or camping during weekends and holidays.

spots.name: Site Banten Girang Serang
spots.desc: Site of tombs/caves of Kiagusju, early Banten people who were first converts to Islam.
spots.addr: Jalan Raya Pandeglang Blok Sempu Banten Girang No.2, Cipare

spots.name: Masjid Agung Serang
spots.desc: A congregational mosque was founded in 1870. It is one of the oldest mosques in the Banten province.
spots.addr: Jalan Ahmad Yani No.11, RT.5/RW.3, Cimuncang, Serang

spots.name: Mall of Serang
spots.desc: Shopping mall with a variety of shops, cafés, restaurants, and XXI cinema.

spots.name: Rumah Makan Bu Entin
spots.desc: Seafood and barbecue restaurant, also known for 'otak-otak' (grilled fish cake).

spots.name: Orchid House at Bogor Botanical Gardens
spots.desc: Located in the northeast corner of the Botanical Gardens. Large greenhouse housing orchids of all shapes and sizes, with two separate halls so there's always something blooming. Entry is included in the Botanical Garden entry fee.

spots.name: Kujang
spots.desc: This statue commemorates the struggle for Indonesian Independence by people in West Java. Kujang is a traditional weapon from West Java.

spots.name: The Jungle Water Adventure
spots.desc: An amusement park featuring water slides and other recreational attractions. Unfortunately, this place has been closed since COVID-19 rise up.
spots.addr: Jalan Bogor Nirwana Boulevard, Perumahan Bogor Nirwana Residence, Mulyaharja, Bogor Selatan, 16132

spots.name: JungleLand Adventure Theme Park
spots.desc: Other amusement park with jungle in the name, this one more centered around thrill rides and theatrical shows.

spots.name: Devoyage Bogor
spots.desc: Boat rides in a European-themed setting. Or you could just get your selfie in front of the Eiffel Tower replica.

spots.name: One Earth Retreat Center
spots.desc: Meditation, yoga, self development programs, stress management. Sessions are about 90 min long.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Bukit Pelangi Km 2, Ciawi

spots.name: Fishing Valley Bogor
spots.desc: The biggest fishing venue in Bogor. Freshwater fishing in a valley with Mount Salak view. Carp, catfish (lele, patin), Nila, etc).

spots.name: Klub Golf Bogor Raya
spots.desc: Bogor, adjacent to Perumahan Danau Bogor Raya. 18-hole golf course designed by Graham Marsh Golf Design. It is at an altitude of 500 metres above sea level and the setting is natural, with mature trees, natural rivers and lakes. The golf course measures 6195 metres, par 71 with four sets of tee boxes (black, blue, white and red).

spots.name: Rainbow Hills Golf Club
spots.desc: 10 km from Bogor city. J. Michael Poellot Golf Design Group designed the course.

spots.name: Jagorawi Golf & Country Club
spots.desc: The only golf club in the country that offers 45 holes of championship golf.

spots.name: Harly's Cafe and Resto
spots.desc: Serves good food including pizzas but only a few brands of beers other than the locals, Bintang and Anker. The spirits are expensive and most likely watered down and the atmosphere reminds one of something Charles Bukowski may have enjoyed. Dark and smoky and typically filled with older expats and women looking to take their money.

spots.name: Salak Sunset Cafe
spots.desc: Quaint cafe owned by an expat who has been in the city a long time. This is a popular place to have a beer with some freshly cooked peanuts. Wonderful view of the sunset over Salak Mountain.

spots.name: Chiers Sportscafe
spots.desc: Excellent ambiance with the feel of a Dutch pub. Excellent food and standard bar fare including popcorn, peanuts and Dutch bitterballen. Try the Schoarma Schotel with a cold Heineken.

spots.name: Bali Blitz
spots.desc: Asian, fried rice and other Indonesian foods, served with spicy characteristics. 1st floor has a cafe and an internet cafe, 2nd floor has Bali blitz providing 2 music studio rooms and 4 cozy karaoke rooms, 3rd floor has a full bar, with selection of beers and cocktails, a wide dance floor, private section and DJ booth.

spots.name: X-One Club Lounge & Music Center
spots.desc: X-One sits across from Circle K on Jln. Siliwangi. It's open almost every night, and Wednesday, Friday and Saturday are your best bets if you want to dance with a couple hundred other people. It's smoky, it's loud, and there are air conditioners every 2 metres doing their best to keep it cool. Billiard downstairs.

spots.name: Lipss Karaoke Bar and Club
spots.desc: Dancing, drinking, karaoke and billiards. The billiard and karaoke are separate. Can be a little difficult to negotiate entry. There are extremely pricey "table and drink" packages on offer, but, if you ask, you can usually get in for the price of an over priced beer.

spots.name: Mahoni Bar
spots.desc: Happy hour 18:00-20:00, buy 1 get 1. Live music every weekend 21:00-23:99. This is a cute little pagoda bar in the middle of the Novotel resort. It's quiet and friendly, and often quite empty. There's a free billiard table.

spots.name: Katulampa Lounge Bar
spots.desc: The Katulampa is located in the Aston Hotel and Resort. This is a premier hotel and offers a number of attractions next door as well as scenic, modern seating. You can also count on prices that will be higher, and some difficulty in reaching this location because no public transport routes go through the Bogor Nirwana Residence where the Aston Resort is located.

spots.name: Makam Pamijahan
spots.desc: Religious tourism object. This is the place where the tomb of Syeikh Abdul Muhyi, a well-known Islamic missionary, is located.

spots.name: Nasi Tutug Oncom (TO) Benhil 96
spots.desc: A simple establishment selling 'nasi tutug oncom', but one of the most popular of the city.

spots.name: Situ Rawa Gede
spots.desc: A small lake that was used as a place to dump waste. The area is now cleaned, and there are water rides such as boats, water bicycles (sepeda air), and bale kambang, a bamboo boat with four plastic drums that keeps the boat a float. Taking a boat around the lake might take around 25 to 60 minutes. You can also relax at gazebos beside the lake, and there is a restaurant.
spots.addr: Jalan Kampung Bojong Menteng, Kecamatan Rawalumbu, Kelurahan Bojong Menteng, Bekasi City

spots.name: Pasar Proyek
spots.desc: Traditional shopping area with many shops and stalls, not far from the railway station.
spots.addr: Jalan Mayor Oking / Jalan Ir. H. Juanda, Bekasi

spots.name: Mega Bekasi Hypermall
spots.desc: Shopping mall with XXI cinema, NAV family karaoke, and many shops, restaurants, and cafés.
spots.addr: Jl. Jend. Ahmad Yani No.1, Bekasi

spots.name: Ruko Kemang Pratama
spots.desc: Ruko (3-story building normally used to do business on the first floor and use the second and third as house) Kemang Pratama is located along the main road of Kemang Pratama. It's across 2 major school in Bekasi, Marsudirini and Al-Azhar. There are many choices of food from HEMA (Dutch food), Pawon Bulis (Javanese food), NORIKO (International food) to Klenger Burger. Also there are Chinese food…

spots.name: Ruko Galaxi
spots.desc: Try the menus from the street-sellers and stalls, they could provide many Indonesian traditional dishes such as Nasi Kucing (rice with smaller size combined with fried dishes and sambal), Es Doger (shredded ice with syrups and coconut milk, mixed with fermented rice and tapioka), Es Campur (shredded ice with syrups and sliced tropical fruits), Mi Ayam (chicken noodles), Nasi Uduk Pecel Lele…

spots.name: GPIB Immanuel
spots.desc: This is an old church which dates back to the year Cornelis died; its church bell was built in 1675.

spots.name: Sawangan Golf Hotel & Resort
spots.desc: The golf course opened in 1973 and is an 18 holes course par 72 course. It is part of a large resort and has good views of a lake.

spots.name: Cengkareng Golf Club
spots.desc: The airport has its own 18-hole golf course. You can play all day Mondays to Thursdays, and before 11:00 on Fridays for US$60; Sundays after 11:00 for US$100.
spots.addr: Soewarna Business Park Block G Lot 1-2, Soekarno-Hatta International Airport

spots.name: Food Terminal
spots.desc: Has various cuisines from local to international franchises.

spots.name: Geprek Wareg
spots.desc: Indonesian food, ayam geprek (spicy smashed fried chicken). The drinks are mineral water, coffee, tea, and fruit juices.

spots.name: WH Smith
spots.desc: books, stationery, magazines, newspapers, entertainment products, and confectionery.

spots.name: Cengkareng Golf Club
spots.desc: 18-hole course next to the airport, famed for the miniskirted Tangerang girls who go around offering refreshments, and with more of a focus on business schmoozing than playing. The green and caddy fee package will set you back Rp688,000 on weekdays, more during weekends and public holidays. There are discounted rates for members and guests of members.

spots.name: Tang City
spots.desc: Shopping mall in Tangerang's city centre with a wide range of shops, cafés, and restaurants, as well as a Carrefour supermarket and XXI cinema.

spots.name: Restoran Istana Nelayan
spots.desc: Seafood, steak, and Sundanese specialties. Chic garden, pony ride, mini zoo. The main building took the form of a yacht.
spots.addr: Komplek Serpong Town Square, Jalan MH. Thamrin KM 7, Serpong

spots.name: Pondok Kemangi
spots.desc: Various Indonesian food (mainly fusion between Sundanese and Javanese food) can be found here with vast choice of sambal.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Serpong km.4 Ruko Pondok Kemangi No. 2E-2F

spots.name: Salsa Food City
spots.desc: A lot of restaurants here, ranging from Sundanese, Chinese, Makassar, and Western. Entertainment: Live music almost everyday, full bands perform on weekends.

spots.name: Keraton Kanoman
spots.desc: The second sultan's palace, established when there was a division in the Cirebon sultanate in the 17th century. This palace is not as well-maintained as the Kasepuhan palace.

spots.name: Keraton Kaprabonan
spots.desc: The third sultan's palace, established when there was a division in the Kanoman sultanate in the 17th century. This palace is not as well-maintained and well known as the Kasepuhan palace and Kanoman palace.

spots.name: Cirebon Kejaksan railway station building
spots.desc: The station building of Cirebon's main railway station was built during the colonial time, based on a design by Dutch architect Pieter Adriaan Jacobus Moojen. The building is a good example of New Indies Style, combining modern European architecture with local elements.
spots.addr: Jl. Tanda Barat I / Jl. Stasiun

spots.name: Grave of Sunan Gunungjati
spots.desc: Sunan Gunungjati was one of the wali sanga, revered saints of Islam in Indonesia in the 15th century. He was the founder of both the Sultanate of Banten and the Sultanate of Cirebon. Just as the graves of the other wali sanga, his grave is a local pilgrimage site.

spots.name: Taman Wisata Gua Sunyaragi Cirebon
spots.desc: A former rest house for the sultanate family that was built out of coral and takes on the appearance of a cave.

spots.name: Alun Alun Kejaksan Cirebon
spots.desc: City mosque and grassy parkway in front if you're into that sort of thing.

spots.name: Cirebon Waterland Ade Irma Suryani
spots.desc: Marine-type theme park: sea-cottages, flagship, pools with slides, food stalls, etc.

spots.name: Yogya Grand Toserba
spots.desc: Located at the heart of the city, this Toserba (toko serba ada meaning "shop that sells everything") has4 floors: 1st floor - shoes & bags department, 2nd floor - ladies wear & mens wear, 3rd floor - supermarket, 4th floor - Marina Restaurant.

spots.name: CSB Mall Cirebon
spots.desc: Shopping centre with a wide range of shops and cafés, as well as a large supermarket and XXI cinema.

spots.name: Nasi Jamblang Mang Dul
spots.desc: Local 'nasi jamblang' cuisine: a buffet with dishes such as tofu vegetables, liver or meat stews, potatoes, fried eggs, cooked chili, and stewed fish. Key characteristic is the use of teak tree leaves to pack the rice.

spots.name: Nasi Lengko H. Barno
spots.desc: Nasi lengko consists of steamed rice, tempeh and tofu, and bean sprouts, covered with peanuts sauce, garlic chives, and sweet soysauce on top. It is usually served with mutton satay and tapioca starch crackers.

spots.name: Sate Kalong Jalan Kesambi Dalam
spots.desc: Sate kalong is Cirebon-style buffalo satay. The word 'kalong' means 'bat', which refers to that the buffalo satay is usually only sold after dark.

spots.name: Tahu Gejrot Wardi
spots.desc: Tahu Gejrot is a spicy tofu dish. It is sold throughout the city at street food stalls, often for only about Rp5,000 per portion. A well-known seller is Tahu Gejrot Wardi at the corner of the Kanoman market, near the Kanoman palace.

spots.name: Empal Gentong H. Apud
spots.desc: Local spicy curry-like beef soup. H. Apud is a famous restaurant selling this dish.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Ir. H. Djuanda No. 24

spots.name: Empal Gentong & Empal Asam Amarta
spots.desc: Empal asam is the same as empal gentong, but a small star fruit is added, and no coconut is used, making the taste more sour.
spots.addr: Jl. Ir H Juanda No. 37, Plered

spots.name: Es Cuing Ciremai Mang Goyat/Yayat
spots.desc: Es cuing or cuwing is a kind of refreshing drink made from a gel that resembles jelly, the ingredients are made from cuwing leaves (Tiliacora triandra).
spots.addr: Jl. Pangeran Drajat No.19, Drajat, Kesambi

spots.name: Ram Fighting
spots.desc: Villages around Bandung host ram fights on alternate Sundays. It's a big event for locals who turn out in their hundreds to watch 5-minute bouts between prize fighter male sheep. Tournaments are held in purpose-built rings in outlying villages. Best to hire a motorbike/guide in Bandung who knows when and where the next tournament is on. Ram fighting is not a blood sport but animal lovers may be…

spots.name: Puncrut-Lembang walking trail
spots.desc: Begins at Puncrut, Jl. Kiputih, North Bandung. For beginners or who save the stamina, it is better to go to Ledeng first and continue to Lembang by angkot and ask people to go down to Puncrut.

spots.name: Batu Banama
spots.desc: Boulders and rock domes offering incredible views of surrounding area. Site of legend where a person named Kiling was cursed and turned to stone for marrying his mom (Bawi Kuwu). There are also Pura or Hindu shrines Pasah Patahu (areas where donations to gods can be left) and yellow flags left by Dayaknese to symbolize the spiritual nature of the place.

spots.name: Sei Gohong
spots.desc: Basically a swimming hole with black-tea colored tannic water and lots of local people splashing around.

spots.name: Tahai Lake
spots.desc: Boardwalk over an oxbox-type lake and mangrove area (wear long clothes if you don't want to become a mosquito feast).

spots.name: Kum-Kum
spots.desc: Tourist village along the Kahayan River with restaurants and rather sad caged animals like monkeys and crocodiles along a boardwalk. Can try some grilled fish here.

spots.name: Balanga Museum
spots.desc: The place where we can look around the ancient goods from Central Kalimantan, such as traditional weapons, traditional musical instruments, urns in which enemy heads were placed, and so forth.

spots.name: Tangkiling Hill
spots.desc: A 30 minute hiking trail providing a scenic overlook of the Kahayan River and Palangka Raya City from the summit, which is also a sacred place for the Dayaknese. Unfortunately besides seeing deer, you're almost guaranteed to encounter mosquitoes and rubbish.

spots.name: Sandung Ngabe Sukah
spots.desc: Memorial where the tomb of the Ngabe Soekah, the first tribal chief in the village, is located.

spots.name: Pasuk Kameluh Park
spots.desc: Riverside park along the Kahayan River and bridge with food vendors and masjid and monument to Soekarno on southern edge.

spots.name: Bundaran Besar Palangkaraya
spots.desc: Iconic roundabout of Palangka Raya with lots of ornamentation and statuary and state government offices in background. Photo-op.

spots.name: Taman Pemuda
spots.desc: Independence monument depicting a valiant youth with Bundaran Kecil Palangka Raya roundabout leading up to the site and government buildings in the background. Lots of monuments.

spots.name: Dermaga Kereng Bangkirai
spots.desc: Place to walk around over black water, take boat (kelotok) rides to Sebangau National Park, where peat swamps and rassau trees are found, or just explore the docks and eat and buy things.

spots.name: Jalan Batam
spots.desc: At Batam Street there are souvenir shops selling products such as lawung, a headband used as the Dayak people's traditional clothing.

spots.name: Kampung Lauk Restaurant
spots.desc: Riverside seafood restaurant along the Kahayan river and minutes from the Kahayan Bridge, an icon of the city of Palangka Raya.
spots.addr: Jl. Bukit Rawi Km No.2, Pahandut Seberang, Kec. Pahandut, Palangka Raya

spots.name: Tjilik Riwut Gallery and Resto
spots.desc: The place where we can see the belongings of Tjilik Riwut, a hero from Central Kalimantan. We also can eat traditional food from Central Kalimantan there.
spots.addr: Jl. Jend. Sudirman No.1, Palangka, Kec. Jekan Raya, Palangka Raya

spots.name: Rumah Makan Borobudur
spots.desc: Customers can enjoy "ayam kremes (fried chicken)" with "sambal tomat (chili sauce)" and "lalapan (fresh vegetables)".
spots.addr: Jl. Rajawali, Palangka, Kec. Jekan Raya, Palangka Raya

spots.name: Melawai Beach
spots.desc: This may be a beach where you're bobbing around in the water and a plastic bag floats by. But anyway, it's a good one from which to watch sunsets and harbor traffic.

spots.name: Sepinggan Beach
spots.desc: Near airport north-east side, brownish water and very littered.

spots.name: Balikpapan Botanical Garden
spots.desc: Grab-gokek bike Rp 65-70k, car Rp 110-220k. ~45-min drive depending on your exact source location in city. No public transport or angkot.
spots.price: Price foreigner Rp 30k, domestic Rp 15k, children Rp 12k. Cash only
spots.addr: Jalan Soekarno Hatta Km. 15, Karang Joang

spots.name: Hutan Lindung Sungai Wain
spots.desc: Grab-gojek bike Rp 60-80k, car Rp 100-250k. ~45-min drive depending on your exact source location in city. No public transport or angkot.

spots.name: (BOS) Orangutan Sanctuary and Eco Samboja Lodge
spots.desc: See rescued orangutans and sun bear in their natural habitat. Just roaming around for the day or staying at the eco-lodge for a few nights and experiencing the wildlife in the jungle. You can also do a 2-week or 4-week volunteering course, where you can help out with the animals. It is about a 1-hour journey by car from the city centre and if you stay the night or volunteer you will need outdoor…
spots.price: Day visit 4h Indonesian Rp 500,000, foreigner Rp 600,000, Afternoon visit + Sungai hitam 6h Rp 970,000

spots.name: KWPLH Balikpapan
spots.desc: Watching conservation the icon of Balikpapan, sun bear or locals called beruang madu.
spots.addr: Jl. Soekarno-Hatta Km. 23, No. 185 RT. 42, Karang Joang, North Balikpapan

spots.name: Kawasan Kampung Atas Air
spots.desc: One of those floating villages along with a bunch of interconnected docks from which you can watch the refinery belch a fireball into the sky. Also here is a fish market.

spots.name: Jembatan Ulin Panjang
spots.desc: Boardwalk through a mangrove habitat and out into the bay. Watch out for slippery surfaces on rainy days.

spots.name: Mangrove Margo Mulyo
spots.desc: An urban mangrove reserve where you can soak in the sultry habitat with some boardwalk excursions and nature study.

spots.name: Kebun Sayur Traditional Market Center
spots.desc: Stones, gems, jewellery and diamonds of various types and price. Borneo is acknowledged as a rich island, not just with oil and coal, but with beautiful gems.

spots.name: Plaza Balikpapan
spots.desc: This is the first and one of the most popular shopping malls in town, and it is at the centre of the city. A good western supermarket can be found on the ground floor.

spots.name: E-Walk
spots.desc: E-Walk is the busiest mall in the city and is connected to Pentacity via a skybridge.

spots.name: Pentacity
spots.desc: This mall is in Balikpapan Superblock, which is connected to E-Walk via skybridge. It has retail stores, casual eateries, a cinema, and so on.
spots.addr: Balikpapan Superblock, Gunung Bahagia, Balikpapan Selatan

spots.name: Living plaza
spots.desc: A decent modern mall, which has a food court, cinema, kid zone, arcade, furniture store, hardware store, etc.
spots.addr: Jl. MT Haryono, Gn. Bahagia, Kecamatan Balikpapan Selatan

spots.name: Bondy Restaurant
spots.desc: A big restaurant on the main drag with a very nice selection of seafood.

spots.name: Dandito
spots.desc: Crab specialist restaurant. It also serves kepiting soka (soft-shell crab dish).
spots.addr: Jl. Marsma R. Iswahyudi No.70, Gn. Bahagia, South Balikpapan

spots.name: Kepiting Kenari
spots.desc: A very giant fresh crab cooked with some options of sauce (black pepper, sweet and sour, oyster sauce, boiled, etc.).

spots.name: Pondok Nelayan Seafood Restaurant
spots.desc: Originates from Pontianak's (West Kalimantan) well-known seafood restaurant.

spots.name: Kusuma Bangsa Park
spots.desc: Viewpoint offering views of the Central Government Core Area (KIPP).

spots.name: Plaza Seremoni
spots.desc: Mini amphitheater, forest trail, retail gallery, and visitor center

spots.name: Baqa village
spots.desc: Centre of traditional weaving sarong called Sarung Samarinda.
spots.addr: Gg. Pertenunan Jl. Hos Cokro Aminoto, Rapak Dalam, Samarinda Seberang

spots.name: Islamic Center Mosque
spots.desc: Inspired by the Hagia Sophia in Turkey and opened in 2008. A major attraction in the city.
spots.addr: Jl. Slamet Riyadi No.1, Teluk Lerong Ulu

spots.name: Mahakam River boat trips
spots.desc: Only available on weekends (Saturday/Sunday) in one schedule. Trip time is about 3 hours, from 17:00 to 20:00 WITA.

spots.name: Amplang Indah Sari
spots.desc: Local food with delicious taste. Made from special ingredients and local fish.

spots.name: RM Amado
spots.desc: provide Soto Banjar, the most famous Soto Banjar in Samarinda.
spots.addr: Jl. Pangeran Diponegoro No.43, Pelabuhan, Kec. Samarinda Kota, Kota Samarinda, Kalimantan Timur 75112

spots.name: Museum Waja Sampai Ka Puting
spots.desc: this was an old and genuine Banjarese traditional house in "Bubungan Tinggi" style (one of the 12 styles and the most bona fide one) before it was transformed into a museum.

spots.name: Masjid Sultan Suriansyah
spots.desc: The oldest mosque in South Kalimantan, more than 300 years old.

spots.name: Menara Pandang Banjarmasin
spots.desc: A four story observation tower of peculiar architecture from which you can view the Martapura River and expanse of Banjarmasin. It has a lot of resident cats as well and food vendors nearby. Comes alive with lights at night.

spots.name: Siring Martapura River Park/Bekantan Statue
spots.desc: This is the promenade along the Martapura River where floating markets are found as well as captivating monkey statue (Bekantan Statue). The main component extends from the statue northward past the Menara Pandang.

spots.name: Waterboom Alfin
spots.desc: Large outdoor swimming pool with some slides and other attractions.
spots.addr: Jalan Tembus Mantui, Kelayan Selatan, Banjarmasin Selatan

spots.name: Duta Mall Banjarmasin
spots.desc: Modern shopping mall with theater, hotel (Hotel Mercure), and restaurants.

spots.name: Tugu Khatulistiwa
spots.desc: It is built directly under the 0 degrees equator line. It is 11 km from the city centre and is comparably easily and quickly reachable by public buses (Rp2,000). There you can learn lots of interesting facts about the equator and to see how unique is Pontianak, one of the few cities in the world situated exactly on the equator line. There are friendly English-speaking staff and a souvenir shop…
spots.price: Local tourist Rp10,000, international tourist Rp20,000

spots.name: Kalimantan Barat Museum
spots.desc: This museum is made of concrete, with concrete reliefs depicting the lifestyle of the two well-known West Kalimantan ethnicities Malay and Dayak.

spots.name: Papyrus Restaurant at Gardenia Resort and Spa
spots.desc: offers all-day dining with a selection of Asian, Western, and authentic Indonesian favourites. At open deck area, you can enjoy the views of the landscaped gardens while enjoying the chef's specialities.

spots.name: Satria Wangi Dining
spots.desc: They have great local menu at very affordable price and average-English-speaking staff. The restaurant is centrally located. Its signature dishes such Ikan Gurame Terbang, Gulai Kepala Ikan, Ikan Jelawat Kukus, and have been featured and reviewed by many national TVs cooking show.

spots.name: Sotong Pangling Pangkong & Digiling
spots.desc: Serves sotong pangkong, one of Pontianak's specialty dishes, grilled dried cuttlefish with special sambal.

spots.name: Hilyah Bakery
spots.desc: Buy bread ampas terigu that has been packaged so that it can be taken as food souvenirs.

spots.name: Kios Nelly
spots.desc: An antique souvenir shop. Mr. Marwizar speaks fluent English, and will help you in anyway he can.

spots.name: Petak 10
spots.desc: Sell various Ambonese snack like Bagea and Halua Kenari also merchandise including Ambon T-shirt and Ikat woven fabric.

spots.name: Toko Oleh-Oleh Hidayah
spots.desc: Buy Minyak Kayu Putih (Cajeput oil) and Minyak Cengkeh (Clove oil) to warm your body in a winter.

spots.name: Pasar Mardika
spots.desc: Pasar Mardika is the biggest traditional market in Ambon. You may buy fruits, vegetables, meats, and fish also kitchen utensils. In the middle of the year, the specialty fruit of Ambon durian become an attraction because many are sold there with prices starting from Rp10,000 per item. The durian is known for its sweet taste and soft texture, taken from local gardens on the island of Ambon such as…

spots.name: Rumah Makan Akbar/Timbah
spots.desc: Try tumis bia. The restaurant is prasmanan (Indonesian buffet) so you can take your own rice and side dishes by yourself.

spots.name: Rumah Makan Arika
spots.desc: Offering some traditional Ambonese food like grilled fish, sauteed papaya leaf, boiled sweet potato, sambal colo-colo, etc.

spots.name: Sibu-Sibu Cafe
spots.desc: Serves traditional Ambonese food and drink, and is a great spot to chill with a big open front and a wall decoration with pictures of Ambonese singers who perform on the national and international scene. Very popular with locals. Cafe has WiFi, albeit slow. The owner, June, speaks English. Cafe also provides beer, coffee, cakes, and light meals. It is double the size of what it used to be. Try…

spots.name: Swalayan Citra
spots.desc: Affordable and delicious Indonesian and Chinese food. Also serves non-halal food.

spots.name: Imperial Resto
spots.desc: Clean and comfortable environment to have lunch or dinner, offering the best fresh seafood in town, with some specialty menu: Ambon traditional food (papeda, fish yellow soup with walnut), Hong Kong-style steamed fish, sweet and sour fish, black pepper beef, fresh crab in Sze Chuan style. All food is halal.

spots.name: Red Brick Cafe & Resto
spots.desc: In a hilly area, so you can enjoy the view of Ambon City. It serves Indonesian cuisine and Western food like steak and burger.

spots.name: Rumah Makan Ratu Gurih
spots.desc: Serves seafood dishes. Try ikan bakar kenari (Grilled fish in walnut sauce) and jus gandaria drink.

spots.name: Wailela Cafe & Resto
spots.desc: Serves many Indonesian dishes. The outdoor faces the view of Ambon City.
spots.addr: Jl. Ir. M. Putuhena, Rumah Tiga

spots.name: Air Babunyi Beach
spots.desc: A white sand beach with a small waterfall whose water leads to the beach.

spots.name: Jikumerasa Beach
spots.desc: A white sand beach. There is also a lake which is connected with the sea.

spots.name: Tugu Desa Savana Jaya
spots.desc: The village monument of Savana Jaya village was established in 1972. Savana Jaya had become one of the transmigration areas in Maluku Province and also used to be a dumping ground for political prisoners who were considered to be involved in the Communist Party of Indonesia movement.

spots.name: Mie Ikan BTN Dermaga
spots.desc: One of the specialty noodle dish of Buru Island, Mie ikan Namlea

spots.name: Komodo Liveaboards
spots.desc: Komodo Dive Liveaboards cruise gives divers the ability to explore some of the most pristine and diverse marine habitats on the planet, while living right on the Komodo Liveaboard diving boat.

spots.name: Sea Kayaking and SUP'ing Komodo Islands
spots.desc: There are dozens of uninhabited islands within and just outside the Komodo National Park. Many of these are only accessible by unmotorised vessels such as sea kayaks and stand-up paddleboards (SUP). These trips are the only full supported expeditions in the park using proper expedition style sea kayaks, not sit on tops. This agency uses these sit in kayaks as the seas can get turn from tranquil…

spots.name: Wicked Diving, Komodo
spots.desc: Small dive centre in Labuan Bajo operating their own Komodo liveaboard for 3- and 6-day tours. Offering daytrips, training and snorkelling tours.

spots.name: Uber Scuba Komodo
spots.desc: A professionally run scuba diving center with extremely experienced staff, Uber Scuba is also the only Freediving/Apnea operator in Labuan Bajo. They offer daily diving and Komodo liveaboards too. Centrally located and very welcoming.
spots.addr: Jl. Soekarno Hatta, Komodo National Park

spots.name: The Seven Seas Liveaboard
spots.desc: 40-meter (LOA), traditionally built Indonesian sailing schooner built from the finest ironwood. It accommodates 16 guests in 8 state rooms with en suite bathrooms.

spots.name: Masjid Raya Hubbul Wathan
spots.desc: The city's most prominent mosque and one of Mataram's most recognisable landmarks. The complex was completed and inaugurated in 2013 and combines modern Islamic architecture with Sasak and other local design influences. The main dome uses colours associated with Sasambo, referring to the Sasak, Samawa and Mbojo peoples of West Nusa Tenggara. The mosque is particularly impressive from outside and…

spots.name: Lingsar Temple
spots.desc: One of the most unusual religious sites on Lombok, Lingsar is a Hindu temple complex built beside Kemaliq, a sacred site associated with the Sasak Wetu Telu tradition. The two traditions share the same wider sacred complex, making Lingsar an important symbol of the island's Hindu and Muslim cultural coexistence. The complex includes the Hindu Pura Gaduh, the Kemaliq sanctuary and sacred springs.…

spots.name: Meru Temple
spots.desc: \The largest Hindu temple on Lombok and one of the most important reminders of the island's Balinese heritage. Built in 1720, the temple is dedicated to the Hindu trinity of Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. Its most striking feature is the three large thatched meru towers, with 11, 9 and 9 tiers respectively. The towers are associated with the three principal deities and with sacred mountains, including…

spots.name: Jalan Udayana
spots.desc: There is a long strip of warungs and small food stalls lining both sides of the road near the airport between Jalan Gilli Gede and Jalan Adi Sucipto. The area is very popular at night especially on the weekends and is a very popular destination for couples who appreciate both lack of bright lighting and the opportunity to stroll or sit in the lineal parks that line the road on both sides. Parking…

spots.name: Jalan Pejanggik
spots.desc: This very informal night time strip has many street food vendors and 'tenda' roadside eating venues that set up at dusk and trade until later in the night. This area can get quite busy some evenings and there is even a half decent cake shop in this strip at

spots.name: Cycling
spots.desc: Bicycle riding events are common on the weekends, especially Sundays, normally a participation ticket is required and some events attract several thousand participants, there are often prizes given after lucky draws from the ticket numbers. They are large scale community events and normally some roads and streets are closed during the event.

spots.name: Cakranegara
spots.desc: Has the greatest concentration of retail outlets and a produce market. There are a few interesting small shops above the markets and a large area to the rear of the fresh produce area containing a considerable number of clothing and homeware vendors. It is an often dark and confusing maze of little corridors and goods so travellers who are not used to tightly packed and slightly chaotic Asian…

spots.name: Mataram Mall
spots.desc: Lombok's premier shopping mall (don't get too excited), a destination for many residents of the city and from distant kampungs. It has been upgraded and expanded and has parking for cars and motor bikes, an outdoor swimming pool off to the side of the main mall and an amusement arcade on the upper levels. There is a wide range of shops including a smallish Hero supermarket, a Tiara department…

spots.name: Melissa Bakery
spots.desc: Nice cakes and quite edible bread. Redwood Cafe and Lounge is on the 2nd floor and the ground floor also has a small supermarket or minimart with some speciality and general items.

spots.name: MGM Supermarket
spots.desc: It sells a wide range of items on two levels and has some interesting shops surrounding the car park at the rear.

spots.name: Epicentrum Mall
spots.desc: Newest (as of June 2016) and biggest mall in Mataram. Also a good place to find an open restaurant during Ramadan.

spots.name: Blusky Pizza
spots.desc: Popular with the locals. Real pizza oven in the street corner.

spots.name: Goa Kristal Bolok
spots.desc: A beautiful lagoon inside a dark cave in which you can swim. Guides wait outside the entrance to take you in. Be sure to take a powerful torch or else you will be forced to rent one for an exorbitant Rp100,000.

spots.name: Golden Garuda
spots.desc: A giant golden bird head mounted atop an abandoned building, because why not? It's worth a quick photo.

spots.name: Lasiana Beach
spots.desc: A beach and restaurant area to the east of the city. The beach itself is not particularly attractive.
spots.price: Rp3000 children, Rp6000 adults, plus a parking fee (Rp3000 for two wheels, Rp5000 for four wheels)

spots.name: Roslin Orphanage
spots.desc: Google and YouTube "Roslin Orphanage" for more information. Peggy and Budi Soehardi are CNN heroes and once you read about their story, you will understand why.

spots.name: Oeba Market
spots.desc: A large outdoor market. Close to the water is the fish market. Further inland you will find produce. And closer to the main road you find clothing, luggage, etc.

spots.name: Flobamora Mall
spots.desc: The largest mall in area is the Ramayana Department Store which includes shops, food courts, games and other facilities. Flobamora Mall is a family mall concept to provide all the needs of the family in one place.

spots.name: Lippo Plaza Kupang
spots.desc: A two-floor shopping center with Matahari Department Store and Hypermarket.

spots.name: Night Market
spots.desc: Every night there is a street food market not far from the shore. The stalls fry up lots of fresh seafood - fish, lobsters, crabs, etc., while the tahu tempe penyet is a great vegetarian option. Next to the food stalls are drinks stations where the best options are the fresh juice. Juice avokap (avocado juice) and jus naga (dragonfruit juice) are especially common and are blended with ice, sugar…

spots.name: Restoran Nelayan
spots.desc: Beachside restaurant with lots of choices including seafood. You can enjoy this dish in huts on the seafront

spots.name: La Cove Beach Resto & Bar
spots.desc: Here you can eat grilled banana with a variety of flavors while enjoying the sea breeze.

spots.name: Muca Cafe
spots.desc: Popular with the hip younger crowd. The food on the menu usually isn't available.

spots.name: 999 Resto Kupang
spots.desc: Live music and pool tables. A good place to grab a beer and watch the ocean.

spots.name: Jayapura City Hill
spots.desc: An equivalent to Seattle's Kerry Park or Los Angeles' Griffith Park, the park on the mountain has a wide and perfect view of the Jayapura city and the bay it nestles in.

spots.name: Lake Sentani Festival
spots.desc: Every June, a portion of the lake (both the shore and the water) is used for a 4-day festivity that celebrates the diverse indigenous culture of Papua. The stage is lit with dances and traditional ceremonies, as crafts and local food & beverage favorites are on sale.

spots.name: Rumah Laut
spots.desc: An upmarket place, built on stilts above the waters of Jayapura Bay. Literally meaning "The Sea House", the menu includes seafood in addition to the usual Indonesian classics.

spots.name: Ungkea Jungle Resto
spots.desc: Traditional Papuan restaurant in the middle of sago plantation. They serve authentic Papuan dishes, papeda (the jelly carb from sago), ouw (grilled sago wrapped in banana leaf), kha ebehele (snakehead fish in black gravy), etc.

spots.name: Trek Papua
spots.desc: Organiser of Carstensz Peak Expeditions and other adventures in Papua. Contactable on WhatsApp.

spots.name: Pujasera Dermaga Biryosi
spots.desc: A food court is close to the sea. It serves seafood and Indonesian food.

spots.name: Sou Raja
spots.desc: Oldest traditional house and former royal residence in Palu.

spots.name: Datokarama Park
spots.desc: A grand vantage point of Palu Bay and also some of the rather depressing memories of the 2018 tsunami with the Masjid Argam Bab Al Rahman sticking out of the water, ruins of the Mercure Hotel, and the mouth of the Palu River where the iconic Palu Bridge IV once stood.

spots.name: Nosarara Nosabatutu Monument
spots.desc: Observation platform/monument overlooking Palu City and Palu Bay. Good photo opportunities.

spots.name: City Forest Park
spots.desc: A small urban forest reserve with some banana trees and other specimens interspersed with trails. Probably not too exciting but may be good for a walk.

spots.name: Citimall Gorontalo
spots.desc: The only "upscale" mall in Gorantalo, it has a movie theatre, a department store, a couple of places to eat and a Hypermart (no beer).
spots.addr: Jl. Sultan Botutihe No.68, Heledulaa Sel

spots.name: Night market
spots.desc: A number of food stalls sell the usual suspects. Fried rice, Fried noodles, Soto Ayam and Gado Gado. The food is good, and the seating area near the stalls makes it a great place to mingle with the locals who seem ridiculously happy to say hello to you.

spots.name: Ohara Restaurant
spots.desc: Here you can enjoy ikan bakar (grilled fish) from a seat overlooking the Sungai Bone (river).

spots.name: Red Black
spots.desc: Your typical fast-food joint. Try the tiny burger. It's small but it's tasty. As always with western food in Indonesia, you pay more than you would for rice and noodles (ca. 10,000 for a burger), but after the Togean diet, you can treat yourself.

spots.name: Rumah Makan Intan
spots.desc: Serves Gorontalo satay called sate tuna. It is tuna skewers served with separated peanut sauce and sambal.

spots.name: Rumah Makan Sabar Menanti
spots.desc: Nasi kuning kaldu Gorontalo, a plate of yellow rice with tuna floss, served with separated vermicelli soup and boiled egg.

spots.name: Rumah Makan Tondano
spots.desc: Serves Milu siram, a corn soup dish with lemon basil. A delicacy from Gorontalo.

spots.name: Manado Boulevard
spots.desc: Jalan Pierre Tendean, usually known as Manado Boulevard, is the city's principal waterfront road and a popular place for an evening stroll. The road runs along the bay past restaurants, cafés and shopping areas, with views towards Manado Tua. At sunset and after dark it becomes one of the liveliest parts of the city.

spots.name: Zero Point
spots.desc: Zero Point is a small waterfront public space near the centre of Manado, marked by a monument and surrounded by streets, shops and restaurants. It is a popular meeting place and a convenient starting point for exploring the older central part of the city. The waterfront provides views across Manado Bay and towards the surrounding mountains.

spots.name: North Sulawesi Provincial Museum
spots.desc: The North Sulawesi Provincial Museum contains collections relating to the history, archaeology and traditional cultures of North Sulawesi. Exhibits include archaeological objects, traditional weapons, textiles, household objects and material associated with the region's diverse ethnic groups. It is a useful introduction to the Minahasa and other cultures encountered elsewhere in the province.

spots.name: Soekarno Bridge
spots.desc: The Soekarno Bridge (Jembatan Soekarno) crosses the mouth of Manado Bay and is one of the city's most prominent modern landmarks. The long cable-stayed bridge provides elevated views over the waterfront, harbour and surrounding mountains. It is particularly photogenic around sunset and when illuminated after dark.

spots.name: Pasar Bersehati
spots.desc: Manado's traditional markets provide a lively glimpse of everyday life and the region's distinctive food culture. Pasar Bersehati, near the waterfront, is one of the city's principal traditional markets and is particularly active in the morning. Other markets around the city sell vegetables, fruit, spices, household goods and prepared food. Visitors interested in local culture should go early…

spots.name: Mega Trade Centre Manado
spots.desc: The shopping place for electronics and bulk purchase. Similar to Mangga Dua ITC in Jakarta or Makassar Trade Centre.
spots.addr: Kawasan Megamas, Jl. Piere Tendean Boulevard

spots.name: Rahang Tuna Om Iker
spots.desc: Offering Rahang tuna (grilled Tuna jaw). It is served with Sambal dabu-dabu (spicy condiment commonly found in Manado cuisine).
spots.addr: Marina Plaza, Depan Hash Inn, North Wenang

spots.name: Nasi Kuning Selamat Pagi Kampung Kodo
spots.desc: Nasi kuning manado (Manado yellow rice dish) is yellow rice with cakalang pampis (skipjack tuna-like floss) wrapped in woka palm leaf.

spots.name: Jalan Flamboyant
spots.desc: Multiples cafés and restaurants (bar n bar ramen, the flamb...) and many street food stalls in the evenings.

spots.name: Bambuden Seafood Restaurant @Sario
spots.desc: Well-known locally for grilled and fried fish, and also offers a variety of seafood dishes.

spots.name: Raja Sate BBQ & Asian Resto
spots.desc: Asian cuisine, with an emphasis on satays and barbequed seafood.

spots.name: Warong Rica Rica
spots.desc: A seafood restaurant at Bahu Mall Bay street cafe. Local seafood with panoramic sea views.

spots.name: Rm. Rasa Laut
spots.desc: Very good place for seafood like wild lobster, crabs, shellfish, and barbecued fishes, with a lower price than some other places. Beach front and with a wonderful view of the sunset, Bunaken and Manado Tua islands.

spots.name: 99 Domes Mosque Makassar
spots.desc: This mosque with a very beautiful and interesting architecture is included in the list of 30 most unique mosques in the world.

spots.name: Paotere port
spots.desc: Makassar's main port and home to many of its ships, including traditional "Phinisi" boats. Locals are friendly and you might even get invited to have a look inside the ship. You need to pay 10000 rupiah to get inside and then you're free to explore. Be aware that it's not a tourist destination but actual port. Expect to have lots of attention, locals taking photos with you, becak drivers and…

spots.name: Trans Studio
spots.desc: The largest indoor theme park in the world. Having more than 20 games and equipped with facilities such as shopping malls, restaurants, hotels, and marina.

spots.name: Restoran Nelayan
spots.desc: Famous seafood restaurant. They serve various fish, shrimp, squid, lobster (sometimes), chicken, traditional vegetables, etc. There are other similar restaurants around the city, you might want to try Dinar or Ratu Gurih, both on Jl. Lamadukelleng.

spots.name: Sop Konro Karebosi
spots.desc: One of the most famous Sop Konro restaurants. They serve Sop Konro (beef ribs in traditional dark soup) and Konro Bakar (grilled beef ribs, served with tasty peanut sauce). There are some other Sop Konro restaurants.

spots.name: Cafe Mama
spots.desc: A cozy cafe. They serve traditional cakes, cookies, sweets, and drinks. They also serve home made ice cream.

spots.name: Pallubasa Serigala
spots.desc: The most famous Pallubasa. Note: Avoid lunchtime as it is very difficult to get seats on lunchtime.

spots.name: Surya Restaurant
spots.desc: One of the biggest Chinese food restaurant in Makassar. They are famous for their crab dishes. Ask for the female crab (it might cost more than the male crabs), female crabs have the delicious crabs egg inside them.

spots.name: Nasi Kuning Emon
spots.desc: If you have a midnight hunger, you might take a walk to this place.

spots.name: Ikan Bakar Paotere
spots.desc: Famous seafood restaurant, they are famous for their grilled milkfish served with peanut sauce and coconut milk soup. Other seafood restaurant also sell grilled milkfish, but this one is remarkable.

spots.name: R.M. Ramayana
spots.desc: Traditional restaurant offering mixed Indo-Chinese food in Makassar. They are famous for variety of food such as Mie Hokkian, Mie Kuah, Makassar Fried Rice, Bakpao (Makassar signature Pork Meat Bun), Healthy Soy Drink. They have many local and tourist customers especially during peak seasons.

spots.name: Krispi Kriuk - Donald Bakmi
spots.desc: Krispi Kriuk - Donald Bakmi serves Ayam Goreng 'Kampung' and Bebek Goreng with local spices and serve on banana leaves, kakap fillet, lele goreng, and crispy fried shrimp, which all are served on banana leaves. They also serve Makassar favorite noodle 'Mie Pangsit' and many more noodle dishes and desserts like Es Sarang Burung, which is a mix fresh fruits served in a coconut. And fresh local…
spots.addr: Jl. Boulevard, depan BCA, Panakukkang Mas

spots.name: Rumah Makan Makassar Kuliner
spots.desc: Famous for its local traditional food and various of seafood. Located near Sahid Hotel and MARI mall.

spots.name: Mie Titi Panakkukang
spots.desc: Offering Chinese-Makassarese noodle dish, Mie kering Makassar. The dish is dry noodles with seafood and thick savory sauce.
spots.addr: Jl. Boulevard Ruko Ruby No.25, Masale, Panakkukang

spots.name: Kafebuku
spots.desc: A small cafe-library near the harbor and is a good place for coffee and some Indonesian literature. There are also some books in English.

spots.name: Kopi Api
spots.desc: Nice café with excellent local coffee (in particular Arabica from Tana Toraja). Many other nice cafés in the same area.

spots.name: Kopi Ujung
spots.desc: Excellent locally blended coffee made by award-winning barista.
spots.addr: Jl. Somba OPU No.36, Bulo Gading

spots.name: Cut Nya Dien House
spots.desc: Cut Nya Dien was an Indonesian woman revolutionist from Aceh. The house is a replica of the heroine Cut Nyak Dhien House, from the Aceh War. The colonial forces burned down the house but a replica was built later. This house in Lam Pisang, about 6 km from Banda Aceh and is now a museum. The house is in Lampisang Village, Lhok Nga subdistrict, Greater Aceh district. Although Lhok Nga was the area…

spots.name: Graveyard in Bitay Village
spots.desc: In Bitay the grave of a saint, Teungku di Bitay, may still be seen. The tomb of Tuan di Bitay, who taught the Achehnese among other things the art of casting cannon, and the mosque which stands beside the grave are revered as sacred up to the present day. Aceh and Turkey had a close relationship in times past. Many technicians and weapons from the Turkish fleet came and settled in Aceh.…

spots.name: Indonesian Airline Monument
spots.desc: The monument was erected to commemorate the heroic contribution of the Acehnese to the emergence of the Republic of Indonesia. When Indonesia became independent in 1945 the Dutch intended to reoccupy the country. In the ensuing struggle in 1949 much area had fallen to the Dutch, the Republic of Indonesia was badly in need of an airplane to avoid the blockade of the enemy. Soekarno, Indonesian…

spots.name: Kerkhof
spots.desc: Kerkhoff or War Memorial Cemetery or known by local peoples as Peucut Kerkhoff, 2,000 Dutch soldiers who died in an Aceh War were buried in this graveyards. On the walls of the Kerkhoff entrance gate you may see the names list of the persons buried including details of where and when they died.

spots.name: Ulee Lheue-Banda Aceh
spots.desc: Ulee Lheue is a shore line facing the Malacca straits; when the tsunami hit Banda Aceh on 26 December 2004, the beach line and the village nearby were severely damaged and submerged by a 10 m high wave. Now the local government has built a new seaport at Ulee Lheue, and if you have plans to visit Sabang and Weh island, you can take a Ro-Ro ferry or speed boat from Ulee Lheue. Ulee Lheue beach has…

spots.name: Aceh Culture & Tourism Agency
spots.desc: Very friendly and helpful staff. They provide (free): a map of Banda Aceh and the region around Banda Aceh, a map of the Aceh-province, a very nice Aceh Guide Book (colorprint). These items are put in a small, really beautiful, shopping bag with pictures of Aceh on it.
spots.addr: Jl. Tgk. Chik Kuta Karang No. 3

spots.name: Fisherman boat on an inhabitant house
spots.desc: 59 people were reportedly saved by boarding this small boat and riding it to safety. Very dramatic image indeed.

spots.name: Floating Electric Generator Ship
spots.desc: A ship was carried 5 km inland during the tsunami. You can get a nice overview of the city from the top of the ship.

spots.name: Mountain Biking Cycling Hiking
spots.desc: Cycle around the mountains, rice fields and beaches near Banda Aceh. Hike and bike tours and mountain bikes available
spots.addr: Jl Al Huda Blok B, No 2

spots.name: Banda Aceh city highlights tour on a Bicycle.
spots.desc: A bike is a great way to explore both the long history of Banda Aceh as well as the impact of the 2004 Tsunami. Bicycles, maps and route descriptions are available at Aceh Adventure.
spots.addr: Jln Al Huda Blok B, No 2

spots.name: Tour around on a Motorbike
spots.desc: After the tsunami international donors and the Indonesian Government build plenty of excellent roads. The road along the west coast is of great beauty. Expect green hills and mountains and behind every corner an even more beautiful beach.
spots.addr: Jl Mesjid Al Huda Blok B No 2

spots.name: Island dropping
spots.desc: The uninhabited island of Pulau Kreusik has a splendid, mosquito free white beach and is about 1 hour from Banda Aceh. The island has safe swimming. You can either make a day trip to the island or stay overnight.
spots.addr: Jl Mesjid Al Huda Blok B no 2

spots.name: Sulthanah Safiatuddin Park
spots.desc: located in the northeast of the city center of Banda Aceh. You can reach the park by private vehicle or public transportation.
spots.addr: Jl Teungku H. M. Daud Beureueh

spots.name: Aceh Culture Week
spots.desc: the 5 year annual festival held in Banda Aceh with typical culinary delights and souvenirs from all districts in Aceh

spots.name: PaceBene
spots.desc: A great restaurant for its fresh seafood, pasta and pizza, and also its beautiful roof top garden. Dishes work from an Italian template, but with the best ingredients Banda Aceh has to offer. And watch out for when the salsa comes on, for the wait staff burst into spontaneous song. Also open weekdays for lunch.

spots.name: Istana
spots.desc: Two locations. Offers your typical Aceh fare in an A/C dining area. Careful ordering - they may serve and charge you two dishes.

spots.name: Hermes Palace
spots.desc: The restaurant here presumably offers the best hotel food in town and has nice dinner buffets as well as à la carte.

spots.name: My Juice
spots.desc: On what you might call "Auto Blvd", this clean, friendly restaurant features some of the best juice combos around. Try the terung belanda fruit juice, which is only indigenous to Sumatra.
spots.addr: Jl. Twk M. Daud Syan, No. 9-11

spots.name: Black and White rumoh kuphi
spots.desc: A cozy place to hang out with friends. You can find friendly faces although if you come solo. Coffee, local food including mie Aceh and various fresh juices. Free wifi is available.

spots.name: British Cemetery
spots.desc: A compound of 18th-century British cemetery. Only 50 European style headstones remained as of 2016. Bring umbrella or visit the place in the morning/late afternoon since there is no shaded area around.
spots.price: Free. You may give tips to the cemetery guard

spots.name: Jakat Beach
spots.desc: Beach featured on this page's banner. Nestled in Segara Bay, the water here is deemed calmer and safer. You can swim as well as rent jet-ski or banana boat. Near the road, you can find many stalls selling fish and deep fried seafood for a cheap price.

spots.name: Teluk Sepang Beach
spots.desc: You may encounter seashore wildlife such as small fish and invertebrate on the beach's tide pools. Its proximity to the city's seaport thankfully does not affect its condition. Locals usually flock nearby the lighthouse

spots.name: Bakso Arema Rizki
spots.desc: Serves meatballs soup with noodle and shaved ice desserts. You'll eat on long bench-table, so avoid late afternoon as it gets very crowded.
spots.price: Rp15,000 per bowl plus iced tea

spots.name: Warkop Palembang
spots.desc: Popular place for breakfast. They serve various Chinese-influenced foods such as stir-fried noodle, noodle soup, chicken porridge, and vegetable stew; as well as pempek dishes

spots.name: Sembam Ikan Marola
spots.desc: Serves seafood dishes, both traditional and modern. They count the dish per portion instead of grams, unlike usual seafood place

spots.name: Taman Tanggo Rajo
spots.desc: Taman Tanggo Rajo is a kind of park alongside Sungai Batanghari river bank. If you go there in the afternoon, you can find a lot of snacks like grilled corn, bakso, chicken noodle, and sugar cane juice.

spots.name: Jamtos
spots.desc: One of the largest malls in Jambi city. Jamtos stands for Jambi Town Square.
spots.addr: Jl. Kapten A. Bakaruddin No 88, Sipin

spots.name: Mall WTC Batanghari
spots.desc: One of the oldest malls in Jambi city, WTC stands for Wiltop Trade Center. There are a lot of shops inside, for example: A&W, KFC, J&CO donuts, Bread Talk, Hypermart, and Ramayana.

spots.name: Matahari
spots.desc: Matahari is one of the city's department stores. There are a lot of shops in front of Matahari. It is next to Novita Hotel.

spots.name: Pempek Asiong
spots.desc: Pempek Asiong, in business since the late 1960s, is a very authentic and traditional restaurant in Jambi. This restaurant sells an Indonesian traditional food called pempek. Pempek is a kind of fish cake, made from a mixture of fish, flour, and water. It may take various shapes: some are cylindrical, some are curly, and some are round. They also serve a large variety of other fish dishes, such as…

spots.name: Mie Pangsit Jambi
spots.desc: Mie Pangsit Jambi is one of the most famous noodles in Indonesia. It could only be found in Jambi, thus, it is one of the must-eat dish in Jambi. There are two kinds of Mie Pangsit; first is the normal size and shape noodle and the second one is called Mee Pokk, which means that the noodles are thinner and bigger compared to the normal noodle. Some stores in Jambi sell this noodle with pork soup…
spots.addr: Easy to find around Jambi City

spots.name: Durian
spots.desc: Durian is a kind of fruit found in Indonesia. It has a very strong smell but is considered by many in the region to be the "King of Fruits," due to its unique, rich taste. In Jambi, durian is cheap because it grows here.

spots.name: Sate Padang
spots.desc: Sate Padang is a kind of roasted beef on a skewer, marinated in a traditional rempah (spice mixture). It is a little hot.

spots.name: H.Hussin Restaurant
spots.desc: This is a traditional Indian restaurant. It has been in business for many years and is said to be the most popular Indian restaurant in Jambi. They serve roti canai, Indian martabak and nasi briyani.

spots.name: Saimen bakery and restaurant
spots.desc: Saimen bakery and restaurant is in the heart of Jambi city. They serve many kinds of cakes and other baked goods, in both traditional and modern styles. Attached to the bakery is a restaurant that serves fried chicken, french fries, noodles, fried rice, and traditional foods and beverages.

spots.name: Holala Restaurant
spots.desc: Holala restaurant serves many kinds of Western and Eastern foods.

spots.name: Puncak Mas
spots.desc: Something like a hill station or viewpoint overlooking the city where you can get all your Instagram photos. Some also come to admire the sunsets.

spots.name: Teropong Kota Bukit Sindy
spots.desc: Overlook and coffee drinking respite. The view is a bit underwhelming, perhaps if the city were a little more attractive...

spots.name: Wira Garden
spots.desc: Botanical garden with waterway and some sandstone formations.

spots.name: Taman Wisata Hutan Kera
spots.desc: Monkeys everywhere. Free opportunity to hang out with them and let them raid your belongings if you don't bring food (preferably healthy fruits and such).
spots.addr: Jalan Dr Cipto Mangunkusumo, Sumur Batu, Teluk Betung Utara, Sumur Batu, Kec. Tlk. Betung Utara

spots.name: Taman Wisata Dan Taman Satwa Lembah Hijau
spots.desc: Kind of second-rate amusement/water/zoological park in that animal and amusement upkeep isn't exactly optimal and the water is sometimes dirty. And you have to pay additional fees for certain attractions such as the water park and elephant rides after paying the general admission fee. Has ropes course, bumper cars, sun bears and deer on display, etc.
spots.addr: Jl. Raden Imba Kusuma Ratu Jl. Sukajadi No.21

spots.name: Slanik Waterpark
spots.desc: Another water park with more dirty water issues at times, dirty toilets, crowded and a malfunctioning wave pool. But it does have pretty cool features like an artificial mountain with water pouring out of it and Indonesian huts.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Karang Anyar Jl. Karang Turi

spots.name: Pasir Putih Beach
spots.desc: a busy tourist area with beautiful reefs and very calm waves.

spots.name: Pantai Sari Ringgung
spots.desc: Another beach, but entry fee is a bit steep. The highlight here is taking a boat ride or rental to a 'floating' mosque on Tegal Pulau island or a sandbar.
spots.price: ~Rp20,000 plus extra for boat ride to Tegal Pulau

spots.name: Pantai Pasir Putih Lampung
spots.desc: Yet another beach, but sometimes with lots of plastic debris and foul smell. It's located in a somewhat industrial area. Boat rides to nearby islands are an additional Rp100000. Has pretty offshore haystack rocks and islets though.

spots.name: Lampung Walk
spots.desc: Water park and recreation center with futsal court. Food court.

spots.name: Graha Maria Annai Velangkanni
spots.desc: Catholic shrine with Tamil Hindu-style architecture, devoted to Our Lady of Good Health.
spots.addr: Taman Sakura Indah, Jalan Sakura III No. 10 Tanjung Selamat

spots.name: Sikh Temple
spots.desc: Located in the old Chinese school 50 m to the right of the Shri Mariamman Tamil Hindu Temple, opposite the maternity hospital. After you walk in to the impressive grounds, turn to the left and walk behind the stairway. The humble temple hall is located to your left. Note: Do not enter without both permission and proper attire! There is supposed to be a larger one elsewhere in the city.

spots.name: Medan Zoo
spots.desc: See critically endangered local fauna, Sumatran tiger. It is the only surviving tiger population in the Sunda Islands.

spots.name: Pantai Cermin Theme Park & Resort
spots.desc: The water theme park is located in Cermin Beach, Serdang Bedagai. The theme park is organized by a Malaysian investor and the local government. Swimming, sun bathing and kayaking. To go there, take a rental car, private car or mini bus (sudako) at Jalan. MT. Haryono (in front of Medan Mall) and stop at Perbaungan city. Then take a machine trishaw to the beach. The whole journey may take about 1-2…
spots.price: weekdays: Rp40,000 (adult), Rp20,000 (children); weekends and public holidays: Rp60,000 (adult), Rp40,000 (children)
spots.addr: Sales office : Jalan D.I. Panjaltan No. 153, Theme Park : Dusun 1 Desa Pantai Cermin Kanam, Kec. Pantai Cermin, Kabupaten Serdang Bedagai

spots.name: Quan Spa
spots.desc: Located on the 17th floor of the JW Marriott has full 5-star hotel spa facilities, with a one hour massage from Rp250,000 for 1-hour massage, more for more elaborate rituals. This is of course a very expensive fee in Indonesia.

spots.name: Zengarden
spots.desc: Located in the heart of Medan. Skillful, clean and very affordable by local standards. Reservations are recommended.

spots.name: Eucalyptus Spa
spots.desc: There are two branches of Eucalyptus Spa in the city, one at the Travellers Suite hotel. Prices there are lower, from Rp120,000 for 1 hour.

spots.name: Cambridge City Square
spots.desc: Cambridge City Square consists of office spaces, a mall, condominium and the Grand Swiss-Belhotel International linked together. The mall is less than a quarter of the size of Sun Plaza, but houses many restaurants and cafes like Nelayan Jala-jala (dim sum restaurant), Starbucks Coffee, Es Teler 77 (Indonesian street food), Pepper Lunch (teppanyaki restaurant), Haagen-Dazs, Magal and many more.…
spots.addr: Jl. S. Parman No 217 (intersection of Jl. S. Parman, Jl. Gajah Mada & Jl. Zainul Arifin

spots.name: Centre Point
spots.desc: An upscale-mall, Centre Point aims to combine mall, apartments, hotel and office into one big integrated complex. Has Mr. DIY, Lotte Mart (Korean hypermarket), Cinema XXI (movie theater) & food court in top floor, Metro (department store), a modern gym, and many more international retailers of brand-name items. If you take a train from airport, after exiting train station, you can cross the…

spots.name: Plaza Medan Fair
spots.desc: One of the major malls in Medan, renowned for selling electronics and gadgets. Has Transmart Carrefour (hypermarket), Matahari (local department store), Ayam Kalasan (Indonesian restaurant famous for its roast chicken), and many other chain restaurants. Slightly cheaper than Sun Plaza. On the top floor, you will find many small outlets selling gadgets or PCs and accessories and a Mr DIY. Cell…

spots.name: Thamrin Plaza
spots.desc: One of the oldest malls with large Matahari (department store), Timezone arcade, top-floor food court and limited international brand stores. Located near Chinatown. There's a wholesale market beside Thamrin Plaza called Pasar Rame that opens from 09:00-17:00 daily. Look around for dried fruit with sugar.

spots.name: Yuki Simpang Raya Shopping Mall
spots.desc: A long-running little shopping center across the street from the big mosque, very convenient to the hotel district, but not yet recovered from the Corona period. It may look abandoned, but it's open. Unlike the giant chain malls, this one sells mostly locally made clothing and home furnishings. Lots of rattan furniture, interesting plastic table and chair creations, toys, tents... There is also a…

spots.name: Pasar Petisah
spots.desc: A central market, sells vast array of meat, fish, fruit and vegetables. Plaza Medan Fair is very nearby.

spots.name: Gelora Supermarket
spots.desc: A supermarket and small department store for children's school uniforms and other items. Their old building next to the railway tracks is now closed and they have moved into the Madani Hotel Building.

spots.name: Mr Ben
spots.desc: Not a mall, just a good sized shop that has been a long running source for all those hard to find food items that foreigners crave. They have a lot of competition since the giant supermarket chains have arrived, but you will still find items here that you won't get anywhere else in Medan. Personal service and very reasonable prices. Cheeses, interesting local coffees, and health food items. Well…

spots.name: Kedai Kopi Apek
spots.desc: Historic coffee house with excellent Lintong Coffee served up by Apek. This place was set up by Apek's father in 1922. Serves kopi susu and roti bakar srikaya (kaya toast). Contains stalls with Indian roti cane bread with goat curry, martabak and soto soup. Outside are nasi gurih, bakmi and kwetiau noodles. Piece of Medan history.

spots.name: Cahaya Baru Indian Restaurant
spots.desc: The North and south Indian restaurant is one of Medan's best kept secrets, which has been featured in Kompas newspaper as the only restaurant in Medan which serves a wide range of authentic North-Indian cuisine. It offers delicious vegetarian and curry dishes.
spots.price: Main dish Rp 20-70k, drink 10-50, lassi 30-35, beers 40-50, nasi kandar 15-35, martabak 25-50, add 10% service tax

spots.name: Restoran Garuda
spots.desc: Well known for its rendang (Padang-style beef dish cooked slowly in coconut gravy and chili) and ayam pop (Padang-style chicken dish cooked in coconut gravy), it has many branches including RM Berjaya.

spots.name: Lontong Kak Lin
spots.desc: Serving tasty and cheap lontong sayur (rice cakes in hot vegetables curry), this humble eatery is not much to look at for the uninitiated. There are queues to buy breakfast and lunch here.

spots.name: Mie Aceh Titi Bobrok
spots.desc: Has been dubbed by an Indonesian lifestyle magazine as the most popular local dish in Medan. A simple dish of noodle served with chili sauce and crab, rumour has it that the secret ingredient which make the Aceh-style noodle irresistible is a dash of Acehnese marijuana, which is the commonest drug that could be imported illegally from the region. But that, of course, only heightened the mystery…

spots.name: Pagaruyung Alley
spots.desc: Located in Medan's "Little India" or Kampung Keling as it's called by locals. They offer, of course, Indian and Indonesian cuisine. Business begins when the sun sets and goes until 02:00 Well known for satay (chicken, lamb, mutton, liver, intestine, etc.), fried rice and martabak telur (egg pancake topped with diced potatoes, and onions, often served with curry). Also excellent Minang style "pick…

spots.name: Mie Ayam Jamur Juara
spots.desc: Small street food stall. Likely one of the cheapest places but still good.
spots.price: Main dish Rp 10-13k, drink 6-10k. Example: nasi ayam penyet 10k

spots.name: Koki Sunda
spots.desc: As the name implies, serves tasty Sundanese food and beverages such as Nasi Liwet and Es Delima. It's at the heart of the city at the corner of S.Parman and Hasanuddin so it's hard to miss if you travel around the city. Its reasonably priced and wide array selection of delicious food is well known to the locals and visitors. Koki Sunda now opens in Tanjung Morawa and Pekan Baru.

spots.name: Jalan Selat Panjang/ Sumatra/ Semarang
spots.desc: This is where some of the oldest Chinese eateries in Medan serve their renowned cuisines, such as mie pangsit tiong-sim (noodle served with stuffed dumplings), kwetiau goreng (wok-fried Chinese rice-fettuccine), popia (Chinese-style vegetable-stuffed spring roll) and many more. If you want to eat halal, of course you should beware of the pork content in the dishes, but you could always ask for a…

spots.name: OnDo Grill Batak
spots.desc: A unique Batak restaurant where you can find the gems of Batak dishes, without all the germs. Cafe-like ambience with non-stop jazz music. Serves a reasonably-tasting saksang (a pork dish cooked in pork blood), babi panggang karo (Batak/Karo-style chopped roast-pork) and arsik (Batak-style fish dish). Don't forget to taste the hot pora-pora (a dish of sauteed papaya and cassava leaves cooked in…

spots.name: Rumah Makan Islam Marikena
spots.desc: Serves traditional Halal Batak-Karo dishes, like arsik, a traditional goldfish/carp dish, and ayam cipera, a type of Karo soup made with corn, chicken, and other spices and left to stew in water.

spots.name: Taipan Restaurant
spots.desc: Serves mainly Chinese style menu. Dim sum is served usually for breakfast and lunch only. Try their coconut Thai dessert or specialty tofu dish.

spots.name: Bolu Meranti
spots.desc: The home-made roll cakes with variety of tastes, such as cheese, blueberry, mocha. The most famous roll cakes in town.

spots.name: Medan Home Dairy
spots.desc: They have European-style "best natural yogurt in Indonesia". Located at TASBI Complex. They are producing many kinds of goat and cow milk cheeses, as well. For the goat milk products they are using fresh, pasteurized (twice) organic goat milk.

spots.name: Zuki Bakery
spots.desc: Bika Ambon, spekoek, prunes, roll cake (Bolu Gulung), breads. They bake items fresh every day and also make their on syrups, including marquisa syrup, terong belanda syrup and kietnah syrup.

spots.name: Harbour 9
spots.desc: Offer outdoor seating just beside Deli river, but many mosquitoes at night.

spots.name: Healy Mac's
spots.desc: The only branch of Healy Mac's in Indonesia. Nice food. Priced reasonably.

spots.name: Holywings
spots.desc: Good food and reasonable priced drinks. Live music usually starts at 21:00. Occasionally may hires famous singers.

spots.name: Shoot Resto Bar Club
spots.desc: A pool bar with big screen playing sports channel (football games on the weekends) accompanied by regular live bands and DJ performance. It also has a large collection of wine from all over the world.

spots.name: The Tavern Pub
spots.desc: Was once one of the most popular going out pubs for expats in the city, but now is a little run down and attracts a sleazier crowd. It features live music from local bands. It's fairly small, fairly popular and is crowded on the weekends with groups of friends, couples, and some rather friendly girls hanging out. A bit expensive for the standard.

spots.name: Bawomataluo
spots.desc: Bawomataluo is a traditional hilltop village renowned for its preserved architecture and megalithic culture. The village is laid out around a large stone-paved central plaza, lined with imposing wooden houses (omo hada) raised on massive pillars. It is best known for the stone-jumping ritual, once a test of warrior strength, in which young men leap over a two-metre-high stone wall.Dating back…

spots.name: Kampung Tionghoa Melayu (Chinatown)
spots.desc: The city's little Chinatown. Chinese New Year festival held here

spots.name: Labersa Water Park
spots.desc: Water park, golf course, 5-star hotel and convention centre.

spots.name: Limbungan Reservoir Park
spots.desc: Popular just to people from other regencies and towns in Riau province.

spots.name: Alam Mayang Park
spots.desc: Popular just to people from other regencies and towns in Riau province.

spots.name: Pasar Bawah
spots.desc: You can find souvenirs, traditional foods and snacks, traditional products, and import products.

spots.name: Mall Ciputra Seraya
spots.desc: You can find Matahari Dept. Store, Food Mart, KFC, Texas Chicken, A&W, Pizza Hut, Solaria, Rice Bowl, J.CO Donuts and Coffee, New Zealand Natural Ice Cream, Bakso Lapangan Tembak, Disc Tarra, Time Zone. Riau21 (a branch of 21 bioskop) is located here.

spots.name: Metropolitan City (MTC)
spots.desc: You can find Giants Hypermarket.Kentucky fried chicken and solaria restaurant.

spots.name: Pondok Gurih
spots.desc: When you enter this restaurant, the staff will hit the gong at the entrance.

spots.name: Restoran Taman Anggrek
spots.desc: If your taxi driver can find it, good Chinese and Indonesian food. The chili garlic crab is excellent and if the matriarch is there the service is excellent. There's also Anom Restaurant at Anom Hotel on Jl. Gatot Subroto, they have the same owner. Whatever food you find on Restoran Anom Taman Anggrek, you also can find at Anom Restaurant.

spots.name: Minang Soto
spots.desc: Famous for the Soto Padang. There are two restaurants with a same name in the street. Recommended is the one in a shophouse.

spots.name: Pondok Samba Lado Hijau
spots.desc: The speciality here is fish, infused with Minangkabau/Malay style.

spots.name: RM Kota Buana
spots.desc: Minangkabau restaurant. Famous for their Rendang and Cincang Kambing.

spots.name: Apollo Seafood Restaurant
spots.desc: One of a number of Chinese restaurants in Pekanbaru, and also has branch on Jl. Jend. Gatot Subroto no. 30-32 Phone +62 761-35234.

spots.name: Ayam Goreng Suharti
spots.desc: Famous for its Javanese fried chicken and Yogyakarta food such as gudeg and sambal krecek.

spots.name: Bakmi Gila
spots.desc: A new place in town for people who like noodles & spicy food, bakmi gila means crazy noodle.

spots.name: Kedai Kopi Seleraku
spots.desc: Famous for Nyonya food, lots of choices. One of the oldest Kedai Kopi in PekanBaru.

spots.name: Kedai Kopi Gundaling
spots.desc: You can taste the most authentic localized Chinese food in this Chinese kopitiam, especially an original menu from Bagan Siapi-api that cannot be found anywhere else. A specialty named Karipeng contains pork and is non-halal.

spots.name: Batam Golf
spots.desc: Batam is a golfers paradise. Batam Island is blessed with 7 great golf courses providing top class championship golf and great hospitality.

spots.name: Sebauk
spots.desc: There is a restaurant just by the city head office in Senggarang. It is often visited during lunch. It has views of the open sea. Sometimes the waves and the wind are breezy and put you to sleep. Few tourists know of this place.

spots.name: Bukit Seguntang
spots.desc: Bukit Siguntang is a low hill in Palembang, widely regarded as one of the most important sacred sites associated with the ancient Srivijaya Empire. Archaeological finds and local tradition suggest the area was a spiritual centre, and it is believed to have been occupied as early as the 7th century. Today, the hill is a landscaped park containing a number of revered tombs linked to legendary Malay…

spots.name: Ong Boen Tjiet's House
spots.desc: Former residence of Ong Boen Tjiet, a famous 20th-century Palembang merchant of Chinese-Indonesian background. Facing Musi on its southern bank, it features a mix between Palembang Malay and Chinese architectural elements, and hosts collections owned and maintaned privately by Ong Boen Tjiet's family. Can be also be reached through land route, though the alleyways to the house fit motorcycle only.
spots.addr: Lorong Saudagar Yucing no. 55, 3-4 Ulu, Seberang Ulu I 30124

spots.name: Kambang Iwak Besak
