spots.desc: A major urban park consisting of a large pond surrounded by vegetations and a nearby smaller pond. Every Sunday morning the streets around the park are closed to traffic, giving space for pedestrians to stroll around and street vendors to sell local specialties and delicacies.
spots.addr: Jl. Tasik, Talang Semut, Bukit Kecil 30121

spots.name: Palembang Square
spots.desc: A quaint yet crowded mall at the heart of the city, attached to the Aryaduta Hotel and Siloam Hospital. While the original mall looks old, its new underground extension is more spiffy and has better restaurants.

spots.name: Pasar 16 Ilir
spots.desc: To the right of the Ampera bridge is one of the most crowded places in Palembang. Some people refer to this bazaar as the Tanah Abang of Palembang. Women's clothing is widely sold. A lot of clothing sold here are in beautiful colours and embroidery with Indian/Pakistani styles. Bargaining here is a must. Pasar 16 is also good to buy traditional palembang textile called Songket. A must-buy in…

spots.name: Palembang Indah Mall
spots.desc: The classiest mall in Palembang. The most quantity of branded fashion, anchor stores, and food tenants in one building. It also hosts a lavish cinema.

spots.name: Mie Celor 26 Ilir H. M. Syafei Z.
spots.desc: The most famous mie celor restaurant in Palembang, situated at a market. The Mie Celor is similar to laksa, but less spicy and more condensed broth, with scents of prawn and coconut milk.
spots.addr: Jl. Merdeka No.54, Talang Semut, Kec. Ilir Bar. I

spots.name: Pempek & Es Kacang Vico
spots.desc: A constant flow of customers are craving for pempek at this tenant across the Palembang Indah Mall. Its Es Kacang Merah (red bean ice) can neutralise the spiciness of the broth or to be enjoyed on its own on a hot day. A popular gift idea from Palembang, they do delivery across the country even by air cargo!

spots.name: Pempek Saga Sudi Mampir
spots.desc: While most of the pempek you see are typically either fried or steamed, this establishment has it baked or grilled, making the texture crispy outside and soft inside, without the guilt of too much oil. Recommended for its pempek lenggang (pempek filled with duck egg, grilled while wrapped in banana leaves).

spots.name: Martabak HAR
spots.desc: The HAR stands for its founder, an Indian immigrant named Haji Abdul Razak who opened the murtabak restaurant which still stands 70 years later in the same spot! One of the most famous restaurants in town, their specialty is the Murtabak filled with minced meat and duck egg, eaten with curry. You can also order a plain murtabak or prata, or other Indonesian delights.

spots.name: Pagi Sore
spots.desc: Most major cities in Indonesia have at least one prominent Padang restaurant, and this is the one that Palembang has. Famous for all-rounders of the spicy Padang food.

spots.name: Sri Melayu
spots.desc: The restaurant, which is next to the governor's office, offers pindang - a smoked or steamed fish in a sweet, sour, and spicy soup - as its specialty. While Palembang primarily uses Pangasius (ikan patin) fish as its ingredient, the restaurant has other varieties such as fish head, shrimp, or other fishes, such as the second most favourite, ikan baung. Top it off with the sweet srikaya pudding or…

spots.name: La Vita Bella Casual Dining
spots.desc: A Western restaurant with an open kitchen concept. Chic and quaint British style exterior and so is the food, from steaks to pizzas, for a generally lower price than hotels.
spots.addr: Jl. AKBP Cek Agus 284 Kenten Golf

spots.name: River Side Restaurant
spots.desc: A dining experience by the bank of the Musi River with a fantastic view of the iconic Ampera bridge. Primary offerings include the Palembang's local delicacy, especially its pindang, seafood, and a few Chinese dishes.

spots.name: Masjid Al-hakim
spots.desc: Nice all white mosque on the seaside, especially at dusk. Side entrance on north to see sunset which seems enjoyed a lot by locals.
spots.addr: Jl. Samudera, Berok Nipah, Kec. Padang Bar., Kota Padang, Sumatera Barat

spots.name: Hike Bukit gado gado
spots.desc: Recommended: good shoes, long pants, trekking poles, water, snack, mosquitos repellent. Avoid if rainy. Start early to avoid heat. Route mixed: concrete, dirt, asphalt. Many parts are steep and can be very slippy if after rain. Start from Siti Nurbaya Bridge, take one of the two paths (stairs) uphill and turn left on the road (not in the many houses around). You will see multiple Chinese tombs…

spots.name: Pulau Asli Tour
spots.desc: Community-based operator run by a family native to Siberut Island, arranging both a Mentawai surf camp and multi-day cultural tours to Sikerei host families on Siberut. Handles Mentawai Fast ferry tickets and all logistics from Padang as part of every package.
spots.price: Surf camp packages from around US$950 per person; multi-day Mentawai tribal tours from around US$200 per person

spots.name: Ramayana
spots.desc: Shopping district, locally famous. Great bargains can be picked up here.

spots.name: Lamun Ombak
spots.desc: Busiest Minangnese restaurant due to its location in the heart of the city.

spots.name: Safari Garden Cafe & Restaurant
spots.desc: One of the restaurants that serves Angus beef steak. Popular amongst the tourists for the extensive menu of western foods.
spots.addr: Jalan Nipah No.21, Berok Nipah, West Padang

spots.name: Waroenk Kito
spots.desc: Asian foods. The menu is extensive. Has indoor and outdoor seatings.

spots.name: Rohana Kudus
spots.desc: One of the favorite places to buy snacks to bring home as gifts, including the snack the area is famed for, Kripik Balado or Kripik Sanjay.

spots.name: Dr. Yap Prawirohusodo Museum
spots.desc: A medical museum was built in 1922.
spots.addr: Jl. Cik Di Tiro No.5, Terban, Gondokusuman

spots.name: Surabaya expats football team
spots.desc: Plays every Saturday at 3pm. Feel free to join!

spots.name: Siwalima Museum
spots.desc: Maritime and traditional object of Ambonese and Moluccas.
spots.addr: Jl. Dr. Malaiholo, Taman Makmur, Nusaniwe

spots.name: Pintu Kota Beach
spots.desc: Beach with rocky cave. One of the Icon of Ambon City.

spots.name: Lake Imfote
spots.desc: A love-shaped lake.

spots.name: Youtefa Bridge
spots.desc: A new landmark of Jayapura.

spots.name: Warung De Rujak
spots.desc: Serves Balinese dish, Rujak kuah pindang and Tipat cantok.
spots.addr: Jl. Pulau Misol No.4, Dauh Puri Kauh, West Denpasar

spots.name: Kopi Petruk
spots.desc: A cafe on the slopes of Mount Merapi.
spots.addr: Jl. Deles Indah, Dusun 1, Sidorejo, Kemalang

spots.name: Gondoriyo Waterfall
spots.desc: A waterfall with lights at night.

spots.name: Taman Garuda
spots.desc: A small park with Garuda monument.

spots.name: Kampung Anggrek Sodong
spots.desc: Orchid cultivation village.

spots.name: Cozy Feet
spots.desc: Reflexology and massage.
spots.addr: Jl Kapten Piere Tendean No. 5, Sekayu

spots.name: Yu Zu Tang
spots.desc: Reflexology and massage.
spots.addr: Jl Anggrek Raya Blok C No. 20-22, Pekunden

spots.name: La Vogue
spots.desc: The city's oldest antique shop.

spots.name: Lia's Gallery
spots.desc: Fine art calligraphy painting.

spots.name: Pasar Antik Semarang
spots.desc: Semarang antique market.

spots.name: Batik Temawon
spots.addr: Jl. Batik No.746, Kampung Batik, Rejomulyo

spots.name: Golden Valasindo
spots.addr: Jl Jend Sudirman 322, Ruko Siliwangi Square Kav 10

spots.name: Rudo Indovalas Dunia
spots.addr: Jl Simpang Lima, Gajah Mada Plaza Bl A/9-10

spots.name: Supit (branch office)
spots.addr: Mal Ciputra Shop Office Bl B/4, Jl Simpang Lima 1 1

spots.name: Ayam Goreng Kalasan
spots.desc: Traditional boiled and fried chicken.

spots.name: Ayam Goreng Salim
spots.desc: Tasty fried chicken.

spots.name: Nasi Ayam Bu Wido
spots.desc: Nasi Ayam Semarang (Semarang-Javanese Chicken Curry Rice).

spots.name: Nasi Kucing Pak Gik Gajahmada
spots.desc: Cat portion rice with various side dishes.

spots.name: Bakso Kakap Pak Wahid
spots.desc: A snapper fishball soup. One of delicacy from Semarang.

spots.name: Gudeg Koyor Mbak Tum
spots.desc: A typical Semarang's gudeg with koyor (knee-tendon beef).

spots.name: Warung Makan Asem-Asem Koh Liem
spots.desc: Offering Asem-asem daging (beef in a sour clear soup).

spots.name: Gama Ikan Bakar & Seafood
spots.desc: Indonesian seafood, with indoor and outdoor eating areas.

spots.name: Han's Kopi

spots.name: Yeh Pulu
spots.desc: This complex of rock carvings is close to Goa Gajah but far less well known. The carvings date from the fourteenth or fifteenth century, and are set in a very attractive rice field. You can reach Yeh Pulu on foot through the rice fields from Goa Gajah, but you will definitely need a guide for the 45-minute walk as there is no path to speak of. In addition to the carvings, there is a holy well…

spots.name: Monkey Forest
spots.desc: A sacred forest full of monkeys, which are not at all afraid of people and will happily climb all over you if you're not careful! They love to look in backpacks and often take people's sunglasses or wallets. Don't bring any food or you will risk getting bitten. If you are bitten, visit the first aid clinic near the entrance at the bottom of Jalan Monkey Forest. You will need rabies shots. Stroll…

spots.name: Selogriyo Temple
spots.desc: This Hindu temple is estimated to have been built in the 9th century AD, during the Mataram Kingdom, and is at an altitude of 740 meters above sea level.

spots.name: Mount Andong
spots.desc: Has an altitude of 1726 masl. It is good for beginner mountaineers.

spots.name: Umbul Temple
spots.desc: Bathing in an ancient hot spring pool. It was built in Syailendra/Shailendra dynasty which reigned from 600-900 AD.

spots.name: Situ Gunung Suspension Bridge
spots.desc: Situ Gunung Resort. About 240 m long, this suspension bridge is claimed to be the longest in Asia.

spots.name: Chapel of Mother Goddess, Rajarajeshwari Tripurasundari
spots.desc: A modern chapel dedicated to the feminine aspect of the divine, such as Kuan Shih Yin, Mary Magdalene, Mother Mary, Lakshmi, Durga, Kali, Saraswati, Gayatri and others.

spots.name: Pura Gunung Lebah
spots.desc: Pura Gunung Lebah sits at the confluence of the Campuhan and Wos rivers beside Campuhan Bridge. Dating from the 8th century, it is one of Ubud's oldest and most sacred temples. Dedicated to the spirit of the surrounding valleys, the temple is known for its peaceful atmosphere, traditional stone carvings and lush jungle setting. It also marks the southern entrance to the popular Campuhan Ridge…

spots.name: Setia Darma House of Masks and Puppets
spots.desc: This fascinating museum displays more than a thousand masks and puppets from across Indonesia and around the world. Traditional Balinese, Javanese and international theatrical traditions are represented within a peaceful complex of traditional wooden houses surrounded by gardens.

spots.name: Tegallalang
spots.desc: Northeast of Ubud, the land starts to become more undulating, and this is a good place to view Bali's classic rice terraces. This village is somewhat a tourist trap, but it is worth braving the hordes of trinket peddlers to view the stunning terraces. From the town center, take Jl Raya as far east as you can go, and then turn north and continue about nine km until you reach Tegallalang. Look for…

spots.name: Bali Bird Park
spots.desc: A splendid 2-hectare aviary park with more than 250 species of birds in well thought out, attractive enclosures. The park has an enlightened, modern attitude to exhibiting animals, and this is obvious from the very open, walk-in aviaries, and the number of free range birds throughout the park. Also has a notably good cafe. One of Bali's best formal attractions.
spots.addr: Jl Serma Cok Ngurah Gambir, Singapadu

spots.name: Botanic Garden
spots.desc: The Botanic Garden is a wonderful way to spend a few hours walking around and exploring the valley that it fills. It is best to go in the morning and avoid the afternoon heat.

spots.name: The White Herons of Petulu
spots.desc: Every evening between 15,000 and 20,000 cattle egrets, known colloquially as white herons and in Balinese, kokokan, roost in the village of Petulu just ten minutes north of Ubud. It is quite a spectacle as these large, elegant white and rusty orange birds arrive in countless groups and tussle for the prime roosting spots. Each morning at dawn they leave en-masse to find feeding spots around the…

spots.name: Pyramids of Chi
spots.desc: Pyramids of Chi is a wellness centre offering sound healing, meditation and relaxation sessions inside pyramid-shaped buildings designed to enhance acoustics. Sessions combine music, vibration and guided meditation.

spots.name: Blanco Gardens
spots.desc: The gardens surrounding the Blanco Renaissance Museum feature tropical landscaping, sculptures and free-roaming exotic birds. They provide a peaceful setting overlooking the Campuhan valley.

spots.name: Bali Swing
spots.desc: Bali Swing offers giant swings suspended high above jungle valleys and rice terraces, along with a variety of photo platforms. While primarily designed for photography, it has become one of Bali's best-known attractions.

spots.name: Nyuh Kuning Village
spots.desc: Just south of the Monkey Forest, Nyuh Kuning is a quiet village of cafés, gardens and traditional homes. Wide tree-lined streets make it a pleasant place for a leisurely walk away from central Ubud.

spots.name: Campuhan Ridge Walk
spots.desc: Campuhan Ridge Walk begins beside the Pura Gunung Lebah and follows a gently undulating 2 km paved ridge trail. This walk was recommended in the early 21st century but as of 2026 the views have sadly been ruined by development. Still, it is a nice enough walk. The best way to do it is to take a Grab to Bankiang Sidem, the village on the northern end of the walk. This way, you'll be walking…

spots.name: Sari Organik Walk
spots.desc: The Sari Organik Walk is an easy stroll through rice fields immediately north of central Ubud. Passing small cafés, traditional farms and coconut palms, it offers a peaceful escape from the busy streets and is especially pleasant early in the morning or around sunset.

spots.name: Kajeng Rice Field Walk
spots.desc: This pleasant walk begins near Jalan Kajeng and quickly leaves central Ubud behind, passing rice fields, small cafés and traditional homes. It is quieter than the Campuhan Ridge Walk and offers a glimpse of everyday village life.

spots.name: Sweet Orange Walk
spots.desc: The Sweet Orange Walk is even better than the Campuhan Ridge Walk was before it was ruined by development. It follows narrow paths through rice fields just north of central Ubud, passing cafés, rice fields, homestays and art studios. It is a relaxing walk suitable for most visitors. Loop back into central Ubud by turning onto Jalan Kajeng and browse its art and trinket stalls.

spots.name: Bali Center for Artistic Creativity (BCAC)
spots.desc: Art studio nestled in beautiful grounds and galleries offering art classes from beginners to teachers, and internationally accredited courses run by Bruce Sherratt.

spots.name: Payuk Bali Home Cooking Class
spots.desc: Traditional Balinese cooking such as sate lilit, Balinese salad, and nasi kuning.

spots.name: Paon Bali Cooking Class
spots.desc: Traditional Balinese cooking class in the home of a very hospitable family. They offer a pick-up in Ubud.

spots.name: Pemulan Bali - Balinese Farm Cooking School
spots.desc: A new community project to save the organic farmer in the village. They have the cooking classes every day for vegetarians and meat lovers. The program consists of a visit to a local market, an organic farm tour, picking some ingredients for cooking and hands-on cooking experience (you will cook your food).

spots.name: Ubad Ubud Bali Cooking Class
spots.desc: Introduction to the exotic ingredients and unique culinary heritage of Bali, set in Balinese compound.
spots.addr: Jln. Ki Pasung Grigis, Banjar Tengkulak Kaja, Desa Kemenuh

spots.name: Ubud Cooking Class with Putu
spots.desc: Private Balinese cooking class at Putu's family compound in Pejeng, near Ubud. Guests prepare five dishes and eat the meal they make. A morning market visit is available with a separate package. Pickup and return from accommodation in Ubud are included.
spots.price: Cooking class and meal: US$60 for one adult; US$45 per person for 2–4 adults; US$40 per person for 5 or more adults.…
spots.addr: Banjar Pesalakan, Pejeng Kangin, Gianyar, Bali

spots.name: Barong Dance
spots.desc: Kecak and fire dance at 6:30 and Barong dance at 09:30, every day. Each lasts about an hour and the ticket is sold separately. Barong dance is very much a performance for tourists, and the story is of the never-ending battle between good and evil. There is actually not much dancing and a lot of talking in this performance. While buying a ticket, you will get an outdated description of the…

spots.name: Pura Dalem
spots.desc: One of the best kecak performances in Ubud, every Friday and Monday evening. Staged in beautiful surroundings outside under the banyan trees, and followed by a fire dance. Excellent ambiance and the fire dance at the end is impressive. A leaflet in several languages is at disposal to understand the illustrated Ramayana story. However, parts of the performance can get repetitive.

spots.name: Puri Saren & Puri Saraswati
spots.desc: Smack dab in the centre of town, dance performances are staged here almost nightly.

spots.name: Bali Healing
spots.desc: Even for the experienced massage consumer, this six-bed massage centre is an experience. A 1-hr massage is about Rp80,000. Magic warm stone massage for Rp120,000. Several other deep tissue and reflexology treatments are available

spots.name: Bamboo Bali Spa
spots.desc: Friendly and attentive service in a comfortable setting, with interiors featuring soft cream colours and tasteful ornaments. The therapists deliver top-notch therapeutic massages. You can enjoy cups of comforting rosella or ginger tea at the cosy seating area after treatment.

spots.name: Sang Spa
spots.desc: Small full-service day spa, owned and run by a young couple named Ngurah and Asti. Simple, secluded, clean and nicely decorated. Very professional staff.

spots.name: SenS Spa
spots.desc: SenS Spa, inside the SenS Hotel & Spa, features 1 couples treatment suite, 2 single suites and 3 foot reflexology stations.
spots.addr: 1 Jalan Sukma, junction of Jalan Raya Ubud and Jalan Sukma

spots.name: Ubud Sari Health Resort
spots.desc: Emphasis on Balinese-style healing therapy. Offers alternative health care, a day spa, beauty salon, health massage, vegetarian restaurant and yoga.

spots.name: Verona Spa
spots.desc: Private individual or coupled rooms that open onto a rice terrace. 4-hour package called the Verona Spa Experience has a massage, body scrub, flower bath, facial, manicure, pedicure, and hair creme bath (not to be missed if you like having your head massaged).

spots.name: Tamarind Spa
spots.desc: Excellent spa with professional and well qualified therapists. which attracts rave reviews. Full spa menu and spa packages menu. They are also able to give massage training lessons. www.murnis.com.

spots.name: Pertenin Body Care
spots.desc: Facial treatments and massage in a relaxing, modern environment. Customer may select the oils and herbs for any treatment.

spots.name: Adventure & Spirit
spots.desc: Canyoning is an outdoor adventure and sport using a variety of techniques that may include walking, abseiling, jumping, sliding down natural slopes and swimming in white water for aquatic canyons. And of course discover beautiful and hidden places at the heart of Balinese nature.

spots.name: Bali Countryside Cycling
spots.desc: A/C hotel return, 3½ hours downhill biking, Light Breakfast, Bike and Safety equipment, Guide, Mineral water en route, Lunch and Insurance covered.

spots.name: Bali Bintang Tour
spots.desc: Hotel transfer, light breakfast overlooking Mt. Batur, well maintained bikes, water en route, lunch, insurance covered.

spots.name: Bali Budaya Eco Tours
spots.desc: Free pickup from hotel, breakfast with a view of Mount Batur, visit to coffee plantation, downhill cycling through rice paddies and villages, visit to a Balinese family compound, optional flat/uphill cycling and a generous buffet lunch. Two guides per group, bikes in good condition, helmets, water also included. Also do volcano climbs, jungle treks, etc.

spots.name: Bali Bike Adventures
spots.desc: Includes return hotel transfer, mountain bike with safety helmet, breakfast, towel and mineral water, all entrance fees, professional guide, buffet lunch, insurance covered for each participant.

spots.name: Bali Hai Adventures Specialist
spots.desc: See the Bali countryside at a leisurely pace on a bicycle. Includes private A/C van (min 2 pax booking), mountain bike and safety helmet, breakfast and lunch, fruit and mineral water on tour, entrance fees and personal insurance coverage.

spots.name: Bali Adventure Tours
spots.desc: Established in 1989, one of the first whitewater rafting adventures in Bali. They offer packages that include their elephant safari park & lodge, cycling, rafting and an elephant safari. Free pickup from hotel. US$100,000 insurance is provided.

spots.name: Sobek Bali Utama
spots.desc: Specialise in white-water rafting and cycling tours. Established in 1989, this was the first company of its type in Bali, and they are distinctly less package-oriented than their main competitor.

spots.name: Ubud Yoga Centre
spots.desc: Expat-run centre offers everything from single attendance classes up to residential yoga instructor training courses.
spots.price: From Rp160,000 per session. Ten class pass for Rp1,200,000, monthly unlimited for Rp2,250,000
spots.addr: Singakerta Raya No. 108 (Jembatan Nyuh Kuning), Nyuh Kuning, Ubud, Gianyar, Bali 80571

spots.name: The Yoga Barn
spots.desc: The most well known and the biggest studio in Ubud. Offers a huge of classes (can get up to 30+ different classes every day) and an excellent set of teachers mostly in the Ashtanga/Vinnyasa school. At the same time - can be quite crowded without much of the individual approach because of the scale. Upper studio has great views of the surrounding rice terraces. Residential packages, multiple day…

spots.name: Alchemy Yoga and Meditation Center
spots.desc: One of the several major yoga centers in Ubud, offering quite a unique classes which are usually called like "Fire / Ether / Earth Class" with different goals and practices in a beautiful setting. Has a restaurant with the same name nearby.

spots.name: Radiantly Alive Yoga
spots.desc: Pleasant and well-known studio in the center of Ubud offering a variety of classes
spots.price: Starting from a 165'000 for a single drop-in class

spots.name: Intuitive Flow
spots.desc: One of the most well known yoga studios with good reviews to the west from the center
spots.addr: Banjar Penestanan Kaja, Jl. Raya Campuan Jalan, Sayan, Kecamatan Ubud

spots.name: Anand Ashram@Ubud
spots.desc: Non-profit institution offering yoga, meditation, satsang, kirtan, bed and breakfast. Visiting teachers and students are welcome to use the space for their programs and stay on donation basis.

spots.name: Bali Yoga School
spots.desc: Offers yoga classes with a creative blend of the classical and modern yoga philosophies. Their courses in Bikram, Iyengar, Ashtanga, Dharma, and Forest Yoga are challenging but can heal physical and mental problems with fun.

spots.name: Taman Hati Yoga and Meditation Center
spots.desc: This centre was founded in 2000 by two local men, both from families containing many generations of Hindu priests. Set up for both complete beginners, and those already experienced but wishing to broaden their horizons. Every Wednesday at 19:30, there is a free class entitled "World Peace Meditation".

spots.name: Bali Yoga Teacher Training Center
spots.desc: Yoga school with instructors from diverse regions, bringing a variety of yoga styles.

spots.name: Bali Yoga Teacher Training Center (Bali YTTC)
spots.desc: Yoga Alliance certified RYS 200/300 yoga school located in a peaceful jungle river valley in Bitera, 10-15 minutes outside central Ubud. Offers 21-day residential Hatha, Ashtanga & Vinyasa teacher training courses with organic plant-based meals and villa accommodations.
spots.addr: Villas Dur Pekerisan, Bitera, Gianyar Regency, Ubud

spots.name: Ganesha Bookstore
spots.desc: Second hand bookstore. Also has great range of new books about Bali and Indonesia. Been around since 1986 and now has a second branch in Seminyak.

spots.name: Pondok Pekak Library & Learning Centre
spots.desc: This privately run community library often has decent fiction and other books for sale. By buying here you are supporting their mission to make free books available to Balinese schoolkids. When you visit, check to see if they have any cultural performances coming up. Also has a small cafe serving home-made snacks.

spots.name: Threads of Life
spots.desc: A fair trade store that stocks commercially made, traditional hand-woven textiles from Bali and all points east in Indonesia. Or better yet, go to the shops that are actually from the villages and outer islands like Timor and Flores, and specialize in traditional weavings.

spots.name: Bubu Warung
spots.desc: Healthy and delicious Balinese cuisine with plenty of choices on the menu. If you have any special requests, Ibu Made will be happy to cater for you.

spots.name: Dewa Warung
spots.desc: Dewa's is one of the better cheap places to eat in town. Serves all the usual Balinese and Indonesian dishes. Most mains Rp24,000 - 36,000.

spots.name: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka 1
spots.desc: A Bali culinary experience. The babi guling (spit-roasted pig) here is world-famous, and this humble eating place is virtually a place of pilgrimage. The roast pork is served with rice and spiced veggies, order the special (Rp55,000) to get a bit of everything — including offal and blood sausage. There are normal tables and chairs but you can also sit on the floor at low tables inside the…

spots.name: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka 2
spots.desc: Unlike the original, where comfort and appearance are not strong points, this outlet is a two-storey restaurant which is spotless, airy and comfortable.

spots.name: Pizza Bagus
spots.desc: Provides fresh made to order pizzas, pasta and other Italian style meals. Italian gelato and a full deli are also available. Eat-in, take-out or delivery. Organic market held every Saturday morning. Games and TV are provided to entertain children. Free wifi.

spots.name: Sawah Indah Resto Ubud
spots.desc: Lunch or dinner with a rice field view. Fish pond. Relaxing and good for a family or group.

spots.name: Sari Bamboo
spots.desc: A tourist class warung, with food freshly cooked to order, set amid tropical gardens on the main road to Penestanan village. Mainly Indonesian food flavoured to suit the taste of western visitors. The warung and bungalows are easily distinguishable by the display of modern art works by the resident artist. No hard sell though, just good food in beautiful surroundings at good prices. Serves…

spots.name: Sun Sun Warung
spots.desc: One of Ubud's best-loved local warungs, Sun Sun Warung serves authentic Balinese cooking in a relaxed atmosphere. Housed in a rustic double-storey building with gardens and pavillions to sit in as well. Excellent food and service.

spots.name: Warung Siam
spots.desc: Warung Siam brings authentic Thai flavours to central Ubud with fragrant curries, spicy salads, noodle dishes and traditional stir-fries. Fresh ingredients, generous portions and reasonable prices make it one of the town's most reliable choices for Thai food.

spots.name: Warung Mangga Madu
spots.desc: Popular with locals and travellers looking for authentic flavours, Warung Mangga Madu specialises in freshly prepared Balinese and Indonesian favourites. Its relaxed atmosphere and consistently good food make it one of Ubud's hidden culinary gems.

spots.name: Warung Lokal
spots.desc: Warung Lokal offers excellent Indonesian comfort food in a clean, modern setting. The varied menu includes everything from nasi goreng and satay to regional specialties, making it a reliable choice for an inexpensive meal.

spots.name: Sayuri Healing Food
spots.desc: Sayuri Healing Food has become one of Ubud's best-known vegan restaurants. The menu features colourful organic dishes, raw food creations, smoothies and fresh juices, with an emphasis on healthy, nutrient-rich ingredients and sustainable eating.

spots.name: Fu Shou Noodle Club
spots.desc: Fu Shou Noodle Club focuses on freshly made noodles inspired by regional Chinese cuisine. Handmade dumplings, rich broths and bold flavours have quickly earned it a reputation as one of Ubud's best noodle restaurants.

spots.name: Alchemy
spots.desc: A 100% raw vegan organic cafe & juice bar, organic health food store, and holistic clinic. Yummy breakfast bar with fruits, nuts, seeds, and raw vegan organic nutmilks and yoghurts from 07:00-11:00, delicious salad bar with amazing superfoods and toppings from 11:00-21:00. Alchemy has an Instagram account at @alchemybali.

spots.name: Kafe Batan Waru
spots.desc: Long established Ubud institution. Excellent Balinese and other Indonesian food as well as western options, in a well designed space. Also serves top quality coffee, and has a dessert menu which includes an especially notable version of Balinese black rice pudding (bubur injin). Indoor and outdoor seating.

spots.name: Clear Cafe
spots.desc: An organic cafe with a variety of vegetarian, vegan, and raw food-friendly selections. Free Wi-Fi. Try free samples from their bakery at the front of the restaurant!

spots.name: Cafe des Artistes
spots.desc: This Belgian-owned eatery serves Indonesian dishes as well as a vast array of international classics. Famous for their grilled tenderloin steaks. Extensive winelist, cocktails, Belgian beers and homemade desserts. Free wifi from 11:00-18:00. To make sure you get a table for dinner, call ahead.

spots.name: Casa Luna
spots.desc: Large, long-established restaurant serving western and local dishes, and plenty that fall somewhere in between.

spots.name: Murni's Warung
spots.desc: Excellent western and Balinese food in a stunning, gorge setting. Elegant lounge bar. Historic, being the 1st real restaurant in Ubud founded by Murni herself in 1974. Also a shop with interesting collectibles and the odd real antique.

spots.name: Naughty Nuri's Warung and Grill
spots.desc: Crowded roadside watering hole. Microbrews, great martinis and slabs of BBQ ribs. This is very much a standard stop for Korean or Japanese tour buses. Once a week they do amazing grilled tuna. Careful that the waitresses do not stick other peoples drinks on your bill. A few times a year they have parties where drinks are US$10 for as much beer as you can handle, for example during USA elections…

spots.name: Nomad
spots.desc: A long-standing institution that serves up a good selection of Balinese, Indonesian, and western dishes, but deservedly popular is their version of a tapas selection, consisting of bite-sized portions of local flavors. 12 pieces of tapas served with rice costs Rp90,000 and feeds two. Also serves a wide range of cocktails and spirits.

spots.name: Taco Casa
spots.desc: Mexican Restaurant. Open kitchen, simple and fresh tacos (soft and crispy), nachos, 8-layer burrito, fajitas, cheesy enchiladas, quesadillas and taco salad bowl. Fresh blended tropical fruit juices or lassies, milkshakes, freshly prepared lemonade, pure juices, mineral water, hot drink, margarita, mojito, sangria and soft drinks.

spots.name: Uma Resto
spots.desc: Provides an Asian (Balinese, Indonesian, Thai) and Western cuisine, and various of beverages; cocktail, mocktail, coffee or tea. Free wifi

spots.name: Milk & Madu Ubud
spots.desc: Outstanding breakfasts and artisan coffee, wood-fired pizzas and hearty lunches. The beautiful high-ceilinged light-filled room gets quite warm on hot days.

spots.name: Hujan Locale
spots.desc: Created by renowned chef Will Meyrick, Hujan Locale celebrates Indonesia's extraordinary regional cuisine through beautifully presented modern dishes. Combining traditional recipes with contemporary techniques, it has become one of Ubud's leading destinations for Indonesian fine casual dining.

spots.name: Nusantara by Locavore
spots.desc: Nusantara by Locavore showcases the incredible diversity of Indonesian cuisine, with recipes collected from islands across the archipelago. Beautifully prepared and presented, it offers one of the best opportunities in Bali to explore authentic regional cooking beyond the familiar Balinese classics.

spots.name: Donna
spots.desc: Donna combines Mediterranean flavours with a lively rooftop atmosphere, offering tapas, grilled meats, seafood, handcrafted cocktails and live music. Its stylish setting makes it one of Ubud's most popular evening dining destinations.

spots.name: Zest
spots.desc: Set beside the Campuhan valley, Zest has earned a reputation as one of Bali's finest vegan restaurants. The creative menu features beautifully presented plant-based dishes inspired by Indonesian and international flavours, complemented by excellent coffee, juices and desserts.

spots.name: The Elephant
spots.desc: The Elephant combines fresh vegetarian cuisine with one of Ubud's most peaceful dining locations overlooking the Campuhan valley. Seasonal ingredients, excellent coffee and panoramic views make it a favourite for breakfast, brunch or a relaxed lunch.

spots.name: Seed Eatery
spots.desc: Seed Eatery offers quality coffee, fresh breakfasts and creative brunch dishes prepared with seasonal ingredients. Bright interiors, friendly service and consistently excellent food have quickly made it one of Ubud's favourite cafés.

spots.name: Umah Pizza
spots.desc: Uma Pizza specialises in authentic wood-fired pizzas made with quality ingredients and traditional techniques. Fresh pasta, salads and Italian desserts complete a menu that has made it one of Ubud's favourite casual Italian restaurants.

spots.name: Honey & Smoke
spots.desc: Honey & Smoke celebrates cooking over fire with expertly grilled meats, seafood and seasonal vegetables. Mediterranean influences, creative cocktails and stylish surroundings make it an excellent choice for an evening meal.

spots.name: Mazzoni Pizza
spots.desc: Mazzoni Pizza brings traditional Italian flavours to Ubud with slow-fermented dough, wood-fired pizzas and homemade pasta. Friendly service and consistently high-quality ingredients have made it a favourite among both visitors and local residents.

spots.name: Pukako
spots.desc: Nestled in the rice fields of North Ubud, this cafe-restaurant has beautiful views from its lovely outdoor eating area. Fantastic paninis, smoothie bowls, and western delights

spots.name: Bebek Bengil
spots.desc: An interesting restaurant with paddy field views and nice gardens. Famous for their crispy fried duck and some European-based menu items. They have a good selection of cakes as well. Free wifi in the area closest to the street.

spots.name: Cascades Restaurant
spots.desc: A fine dining restaurant with French inspired menus mixed with Asian influences. Good views and hushed atmosphere. Has a large wine list.

spots.name: Mozaic
spots.desc: The brainchild of chef Chris Salans, this is one of the leading restaurants in the whole of Bali, and one which will please even the most jaded of foodies. Multi-award winning, including the coveted Les Grandes Tables du Monde award (the only restaurant in Bali ever to achieve that). Western prices, but worth it as a special treat. Try the degustation menu.

spots.name: Apéritif Restaurant
spots.desc: Views of a jungle valley and colonial-era decor, under the guidance of chef Nic Vanderbeeken.

spots.name: Locavore NXT
spots.desc: Locavore NXT continues the legacy of one of Asia's most celebrated restaurants. Combining cutting-edge culinary techniques with locally sourced ingredients and a strong focus on sustainability, it offers an unforgettable tasting-menu experience that ranks among Indonesia's finest dining destinations.

spots.name: Room4Dessert
spots.desc: Created by award-winning chef Will Goldfarb, Room4Dessert is unlike any other restaurant in Bali. Multi-course dessert tasting menus are paired with creative savoury bites and cocktails, making it one of Ubud's most original and internationally recognised dining experiences.

spots.name: Sayan House
spots.desc: Perched above the Ayung River gorge, Sayan House combines Japanese precision with bold Latin American flavours. Creative cocktails, beautifully presented dishes and breathtaking sunset views have made it one of Ubud's premier dinner venues.

spots.name: The Melting Pot Game Room and Pub
spots.desc: Pool hall and games room with full bar. Every nation is represented with a flag and customers are encouraged to sign their country’s flag. Food, music, table tennis, darts, foosball, video games, pool tables, and a general atmosphere make it a place where locals, ex-pats, and tourists often congregate. 8 Ball tournaments every Tuesday night and 10 ball tournaments on Fridays are open to all.

spots.name: Bali Pulina
spots.desc: Sprawling venue with lush, tropical vegetation, coffee and tea tastings, also a zipline through the foliage. Try Kopi Luwak.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Pujung Kaja, Sebatu, Tegallalang

spots.name: Seniman Coffee Studio
spots.desc: A popular retro cafe that serves a variety of selected coffees & food from several local regions.
spots.addr: Jl. Sri Wedari No.5, Banjar Taman Kelod

spots.name: Fold
spots.desc: This cafe-bakery-pizza place-restaurant has the best barista coffee in Ubud. They also have the excellent, local Kura Kura beer on tap.

spots.name: Last Wave
spots.desc: A very large selection of menus, like burgers & salads, premium sandwiches, pastas & pizzas, desserts, to classic finger food. Also including a huge assortment of alcohols & cocktails.

spots.name: Made's Warung
spots.desc: Traditional Balinese restaurant, sometimes also featuring other Indonesian dishes.

spots.name: Tembeling Rainforest & Spring
spots.desc: The whole southern coast of Nusa Penida has spectacular, high white limestone cliffs. Tembeling rainforest is the last remnant of rainforest that covered the island many years ago. Green, leafy and cool there are also two natural springs that you can bathe in. Continue your walk down to the beach for spectacular views.

spots.name: Peguyangan Spring
spots.desc: Set on the south side of the island the spring is at the bottom of 700 blue stairs. The spring at the bottom is small but the scenery on the way down and at the bottom is magnificent. Wear proper shoes as footings can be a little precarious. This climb down and up is not for everyone especially those that do not like heights as the steps are set at the side of the cliff.

spots.name: Atuh Beach
spots.desc: At the east side of the island Atuh beach welcomes the sun first every morning. Walk along magnificent limestone cliff tops and if you are up for a bit of exercise climb down the steps to the beautiful white sand beach. A photographer's delight. Food and refreshments are available, and there is good snorkelling for small fishes.

spots.name: Suwehan Beach
spots.desc: Set in the south east corner of the island, Suwehan is one of the most remote beaches. The steps down (and up!) are a little strenuous but worth it for the beautiful, secluded white sand beach and magnificent scenery. The beach is not necessarily swimmable, depending on tides. The scenic drive to Suwehan takes one through farming communities, although the road is poor and quite steep in parts.

spots.name: Kelingking Beach
spots.desc: A hidden beach in the village of Bunga Mekar, with iconic views over the hills. The sight features a limestone headland covered in green, against the deep blue waters of the ocean. This unique formation is reminiscent of a Tyrannosaurus Rex head, hence its nickname ‘T-Rex Bay’. The secluded beach itself is down a rugged 400-m cliffside hike, recommended only for the fit and adventurous.

spots.name: Pura Goa Giri Putri / Goa Karang Sari
spots.desc: Large limestone caves on the east coast about 4 km north of Suana village, near the village of Karangsari. The entrance is a short, vertical climb from the road level, and leads to the temple; you will need to be suitably clad in a sarong (can be rented for Rp 5,000 from the shop at the roadside), sign the visitor book, and make a donation. Of great religious and cultural significance, there are…
spots.price: Rp 5,000 to hire a sarong, and a temple donation of Rp 20,000 or so

spots.name: Pura Ped
spots.desc: An extremely important temple to the Balinese Hindus many of whom make an annual pilgrimage to Nusa Penida specifically to pray here. Worth a visit especially at full moon for the ceremony which goes on into the night. Entry in full ceremonial dress (sarong and sash) for both men and women is required.

spots.name: Pura Batu Medahu and Pura Batu Kuning
spots.desc: Two interesting and stunningly located temples on the east coast road south of Suana. Instead of taking the main road from Suana heading south west, continue on the coast road towards the tiny village of Semaya. You will come to the two temples (Pura Batu Madan first) after about 1.5 km and before you reach Semaya.

spots.name: Crystal Bay
spots.desc: A stunning white sand beach at Banjar Penida west of Sakti village on the north western coast facing Nusa Ceningan. Perfect clear waters and excellent snorkelling. Lovely white sand beach and a great place for a picnic. A truly idyllic spot and you are likely to have it to yourself apart for the odd local villager and maybe a diveboat offshore.

spots.name: Puncak Mundi
spots.desc: The highest point of Nusa Penida at some 521 metres above sea level. Great views from here. This area is also home to now defunct alternative energy facility with wind turbines and a solar panel farm. Puncak Mundi temple perches high on the hill.

spots.name: Broken Beach & Angel Billabong
spots.desc: Stunning views from cliff tops show off the natural hole that encompasses Broken Beach. You can enter the infinity pool at low tide, but for safety reasons please do not enter at high tide when waves are crashing over the edge.

spots.name: M Bistro
spots.desc: Mediterranean and international cuisine. Popular for sunset dining and cocktails.

spots.name: Taman Kyai Langgeng
spots.desc: An educational-cum-recreational park which features rare plants, dinosaur statues, and airplane prototypes. It provides a playground with some facilities. Rafting can be organised (when the nearby Progo River is in full flow).

spots.name: Volcanic stone carvings
spots.desc: Many stalls selling carved stone items, including statues, garden lamps, mortar and pestles.

spots.name: Armada Town Square
spots.desc: Fashion, department store, supermarket, food court, and cinema.
spots.addr: Jl. Mayjen Bambang Soegeng No.1, Kedungdowo, Mertoyudan

spots.name: Bakso Krikil Pak Bendot
spots.desc: Local Magelang cuisine, bakso krikil (small gravel-shaped beef ball).
spots.addr: Jl. Ade Irma Suryani, Potrobangsan, North Magelang

spots.name: Blendrang Ayam Munthilan
spots.desc: Local Magelang cuisine, bubur blendrang (local chicken porridge)
spots.addr: Karaharjan, Wonosari, Gunungpring, Muntilan, Magelang Regency

spots.name: Kupat Tahu Pak Pangat
spots.desc: Local Magelang cuisine, kupat tahu Magelang (tofu with rice cake in peanut sauce)
spots.addr: Jl. Panembahan Senopati No.41, Jurangombo Utara, South Magelang

spots.name: Banaran 9 Coffee
spots.desc: A roadhouse run by the state-owned plantation company whose coffee plantations flank the road at this point. An acceptable place to pull in for a quick break if on a long road trip or if the road is jammed. Bathrooms are kept clean, food is standard plates of rice and chicken etc served quickly and hot. And the coffee isn't bad either.

spots.name: Es Semanggi
spots.desc: A well-known beverage from Magelang, with a recipe handed down since the 1960s.
spots.addr: Jl. Semarang - Yogyakarta No. 367, Keramat Selatan, Magelang Utara

spots.name: Pekalongan Batik Museum
spots.desc: Pekalongan is very well-known among collectors and experts for its traditional cloth, so it makes sense to visit this museum while you're there. The museum covers batik motifs from throughout Indonesia.
spots.price: Adults Rp 7,000, children Rp 3,000, international tourist Rp 20.000

spots.name: Pasar Grosir Setono
spots.desc: Covered bazaar is known for its vendors of traditional batik apparel for men, women & children.
spots.addr: Jl. Dr. Sutomo No.1 - 2, Karangmalang, East Pekalongan

spots.name: Nasi Megono RM Tjukup
spots.desc: Nasi megono is a typical rice dish of Pekalongan Regency made from pieces of young jackfruit with a blend of grated coconut. It is usually served with mendoan, black cooked squid, balado egg, tempeh orek, cucumber, and chili sauce.
spots.addr: Jl. Manggis sebelah PLN Pekalongan No.10, Sampangan, East Pekalongan

spots.name: Sate Batibul Bang Awi
spots.desc: This is goat satay made from kids under three months old (the name batibul is from di bawah tiga bulan = below three months), a specialty of Tegal.

spots.name: Kupat Glabed Randugunting
spots.desc: Serves kupat glabed, rice cake with tempeh in gravy. It is served with satay.
spots.addr: Jl. Ayam No.26, Randugunting, Tegal Selatan

spots.name: Agrowisata Salib Putih
spots.desc: You can camp, swim at the swimming pool with the beautiful view of the town and Lake Rawa Pening, and take a field trip of the coffee, tea and clove plantations, as well as a dairy farm. You can learn how to plant crops, make organic fertilizers, and get milk from cows.

spots.name: Atlantic Dreamland
spots.desc: Atlantic Dreamland is an amusement park that offers attractions like water boom, water toys, bom-bom car, softplay, flying fox, circular track, mini coaster, carousel, water roller, 4D theater, and ATV.

spots.name: Havana Horses
spots.desc: Horse riding school, where the horses live outside all year round in herds, eat locally-available grasses and hay, go barefoot, and are ridden without bit, spurs or other means of force.

spots.name: Saloka Theme Park
spots.desc: A theme park located just 8 km from Salatiga on the road to Semarang. It has 25 rides with the theme of the legend of the people of Central Java, including a Ferris wheel. It also has a science center.
spots.price: M-Fr Rp120,000; Sa-Su and public holidays Rp150,000
spots.addr: Jl. Fatmawati No.154, Tuntang, Semarang, Jawa Tengah 50773

spots.name: Cenik Jegeg
spots.desc: Artisan textiles created with natural dyes. Leaves are pinned onto the cloth, and then simmered to leave an imprint of the leaf on the cloth, in shades of strong purple, and soft greens, yellows, browns and pinks. Call first, this is a home-based industry.
spots.addr: Jl Kota Baru II No. 150, Blotongan

spots.name: SAPU
spots.desc: Sapu Upcycle is part of a community of artists and activists that upcycles waste materials into valuable products. They work with bus and truck inner tubes, canvas from former army tents, shipping container webbing straps and circuit boards from mobile phones to make bags, wallets, pouches and jewellery.

spots.name: Toko Sederhana
spots.desc: Buy food souvenirs from Salatiga including the famous enting-enting gepuk, a peanut snack.

spots.name: TigaDara Cake & Cookies
spots.desc: Traditional Indonesian cookies kue kering like nastar and kastengel.

spots.name: Wisata Belanja Kue Kering UMKM “Saga”
spots.desc: Saga is short for “Snack Salatiga” which was inaugurated by the Mayor of Salatiga. Favorite foods are available such as enting-enting gepuk, kripik paru (lung chips), abon (meat floss), kecap (sweet soy sauce), dendeng (beef jerky), and others.

spots.name: Biztro
spots.desc: A long menu of pizza, pasta, Mexican, steak, chicken, Chinese and Indonesian dishes, but the kitchen seems to cope. Friendly service, and a choice of 'spaces' to sit in, including the garden.

spots.name: Waroeng Joglo Bu Rini
spots.desc: A restaurant with a view of rice fields and Mount Merbabu, offering traditional dishes, especially ribs.

spots.name: Sitinggil Muncul - Javanese Restaurant
spots.desc: Traditional Javanese farm to table cuisine in our traditional Javanese restaurant suitable for in-house and external guests. Event space available with a rice field and mountain view (Telomoyo, Merbabu and everything in between), for a minimum of 15 guests. Choice of venues to sit including 150-year-old traditional Javanese house, garden and 6-person lesehan-style (low table) Joglo. Fresh…

spots.name: Ronde Sekoteng Jago
spots.desc: This dessert is one of the most popular dishes in Salatiga. Ronde sekoteng jago is made of 9 different ingredients which consist of ginger, sugar, ronde (sticky rice ball filled with crushed peanut), dried fruits, sagu delima (tapioca pearl), kolang-kaling (sugar palm fruit), and seaweed. That variety of ingredients makes ronde sekoteng jago a unique, delicious and popular choice.

spots.name: Warung Sate Sapi Suruh
spots.desc: Sate Sapi Suruh is a popular street food vendor in Salatiga. Sate Sapi Suruh serves skewered beef grilled over a charcoal fire until tender. These satay are served with their specialty peanut sauce and lontong/ketupat (Rice wrapped banana leaf and steamed).
spots.addr: Komplek Ruko 16 no. F1 Pasaraya 2, Jl. Jend. Sudirman, Kutowinangun Kidul, Kec. Tingkir, Kota Salatiga

spots.name: Bakso Sari Roso ABC
spots.desc: Its location is very strategic that even people from outside Salatiga can quite easily locate this place. A portion of Bakso Sari Roso ABC contains just several beef bakso but, despite its simplicity, the flavor it presents is loved by locals and visitors alike.

spots.name: Bakpao Luber
spots.desc: Bakpao Luber is a Chinese steamed bun filled with various fillings. Bakpao luber offers lots of bakpao fillings, but most people choose chocolate and cheese as their favorite.

spots.name: Soto Esto
spots.desc: The difference between soto esto and other soto is that other soto places have clear soup, but soto esto uses coconut milk that makes it distinctly yellowish in color. A portion of soto esto contains rice, with Soto Esto’s signature soup, in combination with shredded chicken and bean sprouts, then sprinkled with chopped celery leaves.

spots.name: Singkong Keju D-9
spots.desc: Singkong Keju D-9 is cassava that is seasoned using spices and mixed with cheese with various flavour varieties, making it a great quality and delicious product that many people outside Salatiga come to buy Singkong Keju D-9.

spots.name: Bentar Beach
spots.desc: Popular beach backed by mangrove forest known for its long wooden pier & migrating whale sharks.
spots.addr: Jalur Pantura Mayangan, Karang Anyar, Curahsawo, Gending

spots.name: Beejay Bakau Resort
spots.desc: is an eco-tourism spot in the city of Probolinggo, reside at bay and in a mangrove forest.

spots.name: Ketan Kratok Ex. Bioskop Garuda
spots.desc: Serves a local breakfast snack of Probolinggo called ketan kratok.

spots.name: Soto Pak Koya
spots.desc: A typical Probolinggo soto ayam kampung (free-ranged chicken soto) called soto Kraksaan.

spots.name: Warpang Bu Khasanah
spots.desc: East Javanese specialities, kupang (small clams) and lontong balap.

spots.name: Rawon Pecel Jumaro
spots.desc: Near Probolinggo station, only serves in the morning. East Javanese specialities: rawon (black beef soup) and pecel (peanut sauce salad).

spots.name: Gado-Gado Merpati
spots.desc: Gado-gado (salad with peanut sauce). Small place, may consider take away.

spots.name: Sumber Hidup
spots.desc: One of the oldest still-running restaurant in town, well known for its Chinese food.

spots.name: Pesenkopi Plus
spots.desc: Wide and modern coffee shop. Packed at certain times. Might not suitable for working from cafe, but perfect for hang out.

spots.name: Pondok Halimun
spots.desc: At the mountainside of Mount Pangrango, you can find panoramic views of tea farms, with Sukabumi city as the background. You may stop at a local traditional coffee or tea cafe to enjoy the fresh and natural mountain breeze, or do jogging around the tea plantations. There are also several other plantations in the area, such as for tomatoes and chilli peppers.

spots.name: Merdeka Square
spots.desc: The main square of Sukabumi where people all around Sukabumi gather to conduct sport and fun activities. It is the best place to blend with and get informations from locals. Usually crowded during Saturday and Sunday morning.

spots.name: Citimall Sukabumi
spots.desc: Basically the only mall in Sukabumi. Hence it's always crowded.

spots.name: Mochi Lampion
spots.desc: Sukabumi-style 'mochi', Japanese rice cake. There are several variants including Kitkat Greentea, Nutella, and Ovaltine.

spots.name: Taman Kota 1
spots.desc: Nice public park with a fair jogging track, well lit and safe.

spots.name: Gading Raya Padang Golf & Club
spots.desc: 75 hectares private 18-hole golf course, tennis, and a swimming pool.
spots.addr: Jl. Bulevar Gading Golf, Gading Serpong

spots.name: AEON Mall BSD City
spots.desc: A chic mall with a heavy presence of Japanese tenants including the namesake department store. There are three food courts in which two of them are specifically cater to Japanese cuisine. Look out for assorted sushi that is sold by the piece in the department store. Parking is very user-friendly for Indonesian standards, especially for the disabled.

spots.name: Bintaro Jaya Xchange Mall
spots.desc: One of the best malls the region can offer. Has a spacious green area, jogging track, ice ring and fish pond.
spots.addr: Boulevard Bintaro Jaya Blok. O-2, Bintaro Jaya Sektor VII, Pondok Jaya, Pondok Aren, Tangerang, 15227

spots.name: ITC BSD
spots.desc: Shopping mall with among others a Carrefour supermarket, boutique shops, and a food court.

spots.name: Pasar Modern BSD City
spots.desc: A modernized traditional market. There are many stalls selling fresh vegetables, fruits, meat, and other raw foods. There is also a food court which opens after 18:00 and contains many culinary options.
spots.addr: Jl. Letnan Sutopo, Rw. Mekar Jaya, Kec. Serpong, Kota Tangerang Selatan

spots.name: Bakmi Bebe
spots.desc: Chinese Noodle Restaurant. Menu: BBQ Pork Ribs Noodle, Various Pork Noodle, Chicken Noodle.
spots.addr: Pasar Modern BSD City, Ruko R73

spots.name: Bakso Trisno
spots.desc: Bakso restaurant that exists since 1985. Several types of bakso (Indonesian meatball) dishes, including mie bakso kuah (noodle soup with meatballs).

spots.name: Snorkeling
spots.desc: Day-trips can be arranged through guest houses in Banda Neira or locals owning boats. Great drop-offs include Pulau Hatta, Pulau Pisang, Batu Kapal, Pulau Ai and the northern shore of Pulau Gunung Api just off the cold lava stream. Make sure that your boat captain knows the sites and make arrangements for lunch as there are no warungs on most islands! If you're staying in Pulau Ai or Hatta, you…

spots.name: Diving
spots.desc: There are two dive operators: Naira Dive Resort is on Hatta Island, and Dive Bluemotion is on Banda Neira.

spots.name: Climb Gunung Api
spots.desc: Climbing the highest peak of the Bandas (667 m above sea level) offers great views. The trail starts at the few houses on the eastern shore and although it is unmarked almost impossible to miss. Bring plenty of water as the trail is steep, taking about 2 hours. Hiking boots are advisable as the path is stony and slippery. Guide recommended if going alone. The fare for boat transport from…

spots.name: Island Walk
spots.desc: Stroll around the island to explore smaller villages in the north and the runway of the airport.

spots.name: Harbor market
spots.desc: Upon the arrival of the PELNI ships, the harbor area comes to life with dozens of street stalls selling fresh grilled fish and vegetable dishes. Try spicy tuna on a stick with sambal.

spots.name: Rumah Makan Nusantara
spots.desc: A well-established restaurant to get decent local dishes. Wi-Fi available.

spots.name: Museum Kedaton Kesultanan Ternate
spots.desc: This museum highlights the past rule of the Sultanate of Ternate and is housed in the actual palace built for the sultan in 1813. No shorts allowed; must remove shoes at entrance.

spots.name: Benteng Oranje
spots.desc: The largest fort in Ternate island. It has thick walls that are, despite frequent earthquakes, still in good conditions. It represented the heart of Dutch operations in the Spice Islands until that era ended and Dutch interests moved on to Batavia. One of the buildings houses a small branch of the National Indonesian archive (Arsip) that can be visited free of charge.

spots.name: Benteng Tolukko
spots.desc: Portuguese fort constructed in 1512 that has, over the years, also seen occupation by the Dutch, British, and a Sultanate. Abandoned in 1864 and then the focus of renovation efforts in 1996, it has a nice phallic shape.

spots.name: Benteng Kalamata
spots.desc: Fort Kalamata is a Portuguese star fort that was built in 1540 and also later saw occupation by Dutch and British forces and then subsequent restoration by Indonesia in 1994. It was originally called Santa Lucia and offers a good view of Tidore from its ramparts.

spots.name: Masjid Raya Al Munawwar Ternate
spots.desc: One of those grandiose mosques dominates the skyline, but it particularly stands out with the way it kind of hangs precariously to the shoreline. In fact, apparently, some minarets were previously jutting out of the sea until the sea decided to claim them. No entry for non-Muslims.

spots.name: Lake Tolire
spots.desc: Crater lake with green water that supposedly hosts a small crocodile population with Mount Gamalama in the background. Trails to rim of lake. There is a wild legend associated with the lake which is explained in the Wikipedia article.

spots.name: Batu Angus
spots.desc: Observation area of old lahar from Mount Gamalama, picnic area, the viewpoint of other islands of Maluku. Small admission fee.

spots.name: Lake Ngade
spots.desc: Another lake with majestic views of Tidore Island and Mount Kiematabu.

spots.name: Falajawa Beach
spots.desc: Dive to see endemic species of walking shark (Hemiscyllum halmahera) or hiu berjalan (in Indonesian).
spots.addr: Jl. Falajawa No.1, Muhajirin, Ternate Tengah

spots.name: Taman Moya Mabuku
spots.desc: A park in a hilly area to see the view of the downtown of Ternate. It is good to go there in the afternoon or evening.

spots.name: Taman Nukila
spots.desc: Seaside park with promenade and benches for viewing the great expanse of land and sea. Also, don't miss the Ternate Landmark — there's a monument to either Vasco da Gama or Magellan— immediately to the south for great selfie and sunrise viewing opportunities.

spots.name: Sulamadaha Beach
spots.desc: Pretty black sand beach surrounded by trees with clear calm waters good for snorkeling.

spots.name: Mount Gamalama
spots.desc: Exercise caution in climbing in consideration of its volcanic volatility and its past eruption in 2011.

spots.name: Salero Yellow Rice
spots.desc: Nasi kuning is a cheap food for breakfast. It is a plate of yellow rice with some side dishes like fish and egg.

spots.name: Pondok Katu Ternate
spots.desc: Try ketam kenari (coconut crab) cooked in padang sauce or oyster sauce.

spots.name: Kawasan Tapak
spots.desc: There are many food stalls or hawkers beside the coastline which sell traditional Ternate ginger drinks called air guraka. It is served with some snacks including fried anchovy, fried peanuts, banana chips called pisang mulu bebe, and sambal roa.

spots.name: New Palace
spots.desc: A recreation of the original sultan's palace, at the same place.

spots.name: Sultan's Memorial Museum
spots.desc: On the premises of the sultan's palace. May not be open for visits.

spots.name: Royal Port
spots.desc: The sultan's jetty and unlike in the heyday of the sultanate, it's nowadays used by local fishermen at most.

spots.name: Royal tombs
spots.desc: The tombs of the Tidorese royal family are just north of the palace.

spots.name: Magellan monument
spots.desc: At the southern edge of Rum, there's a monument to Magellan's round the world expedition who reached the island in 1521.

spots.name: Clove harvesting
spots.desc: The clove harvest season corresponds to the Northern Hemisphere summer. During that time, locals climb up trees to pick the buds of the clove trees, which are then laid out along roads to dry, giving off a pleasant smell.

spots.name: Hot Springs beach
spots.desc: The island's most popular beach, busy at the weekends. Next to it, there's a hot spring you can bathe in.

spots.name: Kiematabu
spots.desc: Like many Indonesian islands, Tidore is a volcano. There is a path up to the caldera summit, Gunung Kiematabu, 1730 m above sea level. The path starts from the village of Gura-bunga, on the way between Rum and Soadara and the path isn't well marked so you probably want to have a guide. You'll walk up through forest for about two hours with great views over the island along the route before…

spots.name: Segara Anak
spots.desc: The crater lake of Mount Rinjani. Segara Anak translates to "Child of the Sea", as the lake water has the same colour as the sea. The water is heated by the volcano keeping the temperature just above +22°C and releasing gas bubbles into the water. The lake used to be depicted on the 10,000 rupiah banknote.

spots.name: Aik Kalak hot springs
spots.desc: Three hot springs, that are of spiritual significance. According to local belief, bathing in one of them will slow ageing and rejuvenate you — give it a try! Also, a mixture of their water and coconut oil is used as a traditional medicine against many diseases.

spots.name: The Mulang Pakelem
spots.desc: An annual Hindu event, held before the rainy season at the crater lake featuring hundreds of Hindu pilgrims in white clothing. The event is to celebrate the Balinese invasion of the island in the 18th century.

spots.name: Gua Susu
spots.desc: One of the mountain's famous caves (the others are Gua Payung and Gua Manik), this one is filled with hot steam and a popular place for meditation.

spots.name: Sendanggile Waterfall
spots.desc: Located at the foot of Mount Rinjani, featuring great views.

spots.name: Ahmed Expeditions
spots.desc: Main office is located on Senaru village at Segara Anak Cottage & Restaurant. Provides trekking packages to Mount Rinjani from budget to luxury.

spots.name: Full Rinjani
spots.desc: Offers a Rinjani trekking package. They tout their team as experienced, professional, friendly and caring about the environment and provide high-quality camping equipment (tents, sleeping bags, mattresses, pillows, camping chairs and a toilet tent) and tasty food.
spots.price: 2 days 1 night US$230, 3 days 2 nights US$250

spots.name: Lenk Rinjani
spots.desc: Provides trekking packages to Mount Rinjani can be sharing package (join group) and private trek tour by sembalun gate or senaru gate trekking start

spots.name: Rinjani Fun Trekking
spots.desc: Reliable Mount Rinjani trekking organizer established by experienced local guides.
spots.price: 2 days 1 night US$200, 3 days 2 nights US$245

spots.name: Herman Trekker Rinjani
spots.desc: Headed by Herman, who used to work as a barman and is familiar with western culture and accommodation. Team of experienced guides for Mt. Rinjani. The team speaks good English and is polite and accommodating. Herman has a high respect for the environment and practices sustainable trekking activities.

spots.name: John’s Adventures
spots.desc: Established agency with full range of trekking packages. John has been guiding climbers and arranging treks up Rinjani for over 20 years. Comfortable base at Senaru with a cafe, pickups are available from hotels and the airport.

spots.name: Lombok Rinjani Trek Organisation
spots.desc: Official partnership between the national park authority and local communities with support from NZ AID. Full range of trekking packages. City office in Mataram and one at each of the two trek departure points.

spots.name: Rinjani Footprint
spots.desc: Professionally run expeditions under the management of an experienced operator. All trek teams work to prescribed standards including; direct first hand experience at the destination, respect for the environment, social and cultural sensitivities & strict labour policies. Search & rescue training is provided for the trek teams, licensed travel agent, subscribed to the Travel Compensation Fund…

spots.name: Rinjani Trekking
spots.desc: Provides Rinjani Mountain information and trekking packages.

spots.name: Rinjani Trekking Club
spots.desc: Team of young biologists and naturalists providing expert trekking guides experienced on Mount Rinjani Lombok. Teams are trained and licensed in search and rescue technique (SAR-Lombok). Local porters are used and they work to a code of environmental respect and sustainable use of the trekking routes. The manager is Imron Rosadi (Ronie), who is well respected in the field of Rinjani trekking…

spots.name: Trekking Rinjani Organizer
spots.desc: Tour packages offering the ascent of Mount Rinjani, 2 days 1 night, 3 days 2 nights, 4 days 3 nights, 5 days 4 nights and 6 days 5 nights.
spots.addr: Jalan cendrawasih No 8 Cakranegara, Nusa Tenggara Barat

spots.name: Rinjani Golden, Rinjani Trekking Organizer
spots.desc: Cheaper offering with all the base equipment even if missing toilet tent. Good team usman in Senaru, guide uwan, porters sian and udin. Guide taking care of slower members. Can rent some equipment like trekking poles, headlamp, or gloves. Equipment: LWY Compass 2-person tents (not ok if >1.8m else good), restli mattress (yoga mat like, a bit light but fine for 1-2 nights), lafuma sleeping bag…
spots.price: 3 days 2 nights Rp 1,800,000 (via Gili Air Fantastic BnB)

spots.name: Taman Burung Aimas
spots.desc: A bird park. You may see Australasian birds like the cassowary, crowned pigeon, and the cockatoo.

spots.name: Tanjung Tinggi Beach
spots.desc: The most famous beach in Belitung. White sand & granite rocks of all sizes alternating, left you wonder where all these lumps of boulders came from. You can even climb on them or enter the gaps of the giant rocks.

spots.name: Tanjung Kelayang Beach
spots.desc: There are 2 sides on the beach: the mainly sandy east, or the more rocky west. The rock formations are not as big, but some of them are in the middle of the sea and qualifies as islands. Fisherman boats are waiting on the east side if you wish for an island-hopping tour (no rocks on the vegetated islands).

spots.name: Tanjung Binga Beach
spots.desc: Not a very scenic beach, no white powdery sand or rocks, but there's a marina full of fishing boats. This is the primary departure point for island hopping tours to the northwest islands, especially Lengkuas Island.

spots.name: Penyabong Beach
spots.desc: An enchanting beauty at the island's southern coast if you are bored with rigid rocks. There is a giant organized flat row of stones that everyone can step in.

spots.name: Burung Mandi Beach
spots.desc: If you are bored with rocks, any rocks, this is the place. More quiet, more laid back. Literally means "bathing bird", it faces a mountain for its namesake. There is a Buddhist temple as a landmark, the largest in the island.

spots.name: Lengkuas Island
spots.desc: An outlying island famous for its century-old lighthouse that is still active to this day, get up its 18 flights of stairs to capture the image of the whole outlying island(s). You can also walk on the rock formations on the shallow water, swim or snorkel to see the reefs and fishes. At the sandy beach, you are facing Aji Island, reachable by swimming or by boat.

spots.name: Kepayang Island
spots.desc: A great place to dive, a resort open for a visit, and a marine conservation where baby turtles are bred until old enough to plunge into the open seas and coral gardens are restored.

spots.name: Burung Island
spots.desc: Known for its rock formations that shapes like a bird. Nothing else very scenic but the water is calm enough for a swim.

spots.name: Pulau Lutung
spots.desc: Actually they are two islands, but at low tide you can walk between the two. The south side of the bigger island has a cape of sand half the size of a football pitch and no rocks.

spots.name: Batu Baginde
spots.desc: A unique bulging formation of two granite rocks, as if they were husband and wife.

spots.name: Museum Kata Andrea Hirata
spots.desc: The author of Laskar Pelangi sequel, Andrea Hirata, erected Indonesia's literature museum here. Behind the scenes of Belitung in year 1978 with his memorabilia, and a corner of tin mining equipments. Periodically, Andrea himself comes to his hometown giving art and band lessons to local community.

spots.name: Replica of Muhammadiyah Primary School
spots.desc: If you did watch Laskar Pelangi, you will find this place memorable. Remember the struggle and fun of the author (Ikal) and 9 other children taught by one single teacher (Ms. Muslimah). The real school was destroyed by wear and tear to its roots so a replica was built and used for the movie.

spots.name: Gurok Beraye
spots.desc: The waterfall was sourced from Belitung's highest point, Mount Tajam (510 above sea level). Be careful along the way for deep gorges but the journey is worth the beauty. The water falls to a wide lake perfect for a swim.
spots.addr: Dusun Air Pegantungan, Kacang Botor village, Badau

spots.name: Lake Mempayak
spots.desc: Used to be called "open pit" by mining company BHP Billiton, the mine is now abandoned. What still lefts is a beautiful brown ground, green lake and trees, and locals mining by traditional equipment. The road that leads here is not very good.

spots.name: Batu Malang Penyu
spots.desc: At the waters between Lengkuas and Kepayang Island, it is a prime spot for both snorkeling and diving in Belitung, with colorful corals in between schools of fish. A nearby shipwreck is also worth visiting. It is one of the two places in the world where you can dive between granite rocks, the other is at Seychelles on the other side of the Indian Ocean.

spots.name: Batu Mentas Conservation Center
spots.desc: A conservation center at the foot of Mount Tajam. A few last meters to the entrance is still of soil but what awaits at its end will awe you. Go tubing along the river (like rafting but with individual buoys), see the endangered tarsius, stroll around the green forest or do the outbound activities. You can also swim at the shallow river with small fishes. It also houses a restaurant and a resort.

spots.name: Avalokitesvara Temple
spots.desc: a Buddhist Temple, which houses the Statue of Kwan Im (Goddess of Mercy). At 22.8 m high, is the tallest statue of its kind in Indonesia. The temple complex is accessible from Jl. Pane. Connected by a bridge, adjacent to the new complex across the river of Bah Bolon, the old building of the temple was burned completely in an inferno in May 2008.

spots.name: Pematangsiantar Zoo
spots.desc: The only zoo worth visiting in North Sumatra, it has a good collection of Indonesian native animals, most notably birds, tigers and apes. The zoo itself boasts abundant tropical trees and plants, some of which are quite old. The location is surprisingly close to the main roads of the city (within walking distance).
spots.price: Rp25,000 per person - children under 3 years old free

spots.name: B and J's (formerly Apache Cafe)
spots.desc: Great, reasonably priced food and friendly staff that speak very good English. They can also arrange tours and give information on transport.

spots.name: Coffee House / tree table cafe
spots.desc: Fruit juices, beer, soft drinks, Indonesian + European dishes - reasonably priced and excellent quality. English spoken.

spots.name: TARUKO caferesto
spots.desc: A unique riverside restaurant at the bottom of the green Sianok Canyon with beautiful scenery and delicious Indonesian, Thai, Chinese, Indian and Western food and drinks. The traditional architecture of the restaurant, surrounded by terraced rice fields and the crystal-clear river crossing beside a beautiful garden.
spots.addr: Jalan Taruko, Jorong Lambah, Nagari Sianok Anam Suku, Kecamatan Ampek Koto

spots.name: Pulau Asli Tour
spots.desc: Community-based operator run by a family native to Siberut Island, offering multi-day cultural visits to Sikerei host families and traditional uma longhouses, plus a surf camp on the same coast. Both government and tribal-chief permits are arranged as part of the trip.
spots.price: Tribal tours from around US$200 per person for multi-day group trips; surf camp packages from around US$950 per person
spots.addr: Padang, West Sumatra (departure point; tribal visits take place on Siberut Island)
