spots.addr: JL. Jend. Sudirman, Sokanegara, East Purwokerto 53115

spots.name: Lake Kastoba
spots.desc: Located in the middle of the island with a height of 400 m above sea level.

spots.name: Misool
spots.desc: One of the best diving spots in the south of Raja Ampat. You may also see a pre-historic karst cave there.

spots.name: Arborek's village
spots.desc: One of the most prominent dive sites. Manta Rays are available in abundance. Visitors can dive and watch groups of mantas & stingrays.

spots.name: Gunarsa Museum of Classical & Modern Art
spots.desc: Owned by Nyoman Gunarsa, one of Bali's most famous modern artists, and exhibits his work. Also of great interest is a huge collection of traditional Balinese art and other objects. Really worth a visit and gets far fewer visitors than it deserves.

spots.name: Kamasan village
spots.desc: This ancient village is the centre of the classical wayang style of painting. Many studios to visit and a large amount of art to appreciate.

spots.name: Puputan Monument
spots.desc: This monument commemorates the 200 Balinese from the Klungkung royal family and court who died in the sacrificial puputan when fighting the Dutch in 1908. The large four sided statue in the centre of the same crossroads is the Kandi Pat Sare which symbolically guards the four cardinal points of the earth.

spots.name: Pura Masceti
spots.desc: This is the least well known and the least visited of Bali's nine directional temples. It serves as a guardian to the island from evil sea spirits. It is an elabaorately decorated temple and is often the start point for large purification ceremonies on the nearby beaches.
spots.addr: Jl Prof Dr Ida Bagus Mantra, Pantai Masceti, Gianyar

spots.name: River Unda
spots.desc: This is one of Bali's major rivers and you travel over it via a large bridge when leaving the town heading towards Padang Bai.

spots.name: Taman Gili
spots.desc: The remains of the original palace of the Klungkung royal family. Especially notable is the painted ceiling of the Kerta Gosa pavilion as this is the only surviving example of classical wayang art in the whole of Bali. Much of the rest of the palace was destroyed when fighting the Dutch in the early 20th century but there are some other interesting remnants. The local government tourist office is…

spots.name: Pura Goa Lawah
spots.desc: This is one of the 9 directional temples in Bali and important to all Balinese Hindus. This temple is built in front of a cave where thousands of bats sleep during the day. If you come shortly after sunset you will get to see the bats flying out of the temple in massive clouds. There is an entrance fee to be paid and you need to wear a sash and sarong (can be rented at the entrance)

spots.name: Gedong Kirtya
spots.desc: A library and museum dedicated to the cataloging and preservation of old lontar (paper made from the rontal palm) scripts. Also houses some bronze inscription plates dating from the 10th century. Very much worth a visit.

spots.name: Pura Jagatnatha
spots.desc: This is the most important temple in the city and the largest in the whole of North Bali. Non-Hindu visitors will not normally be allowed to enter. It is though still worth a visit to admire its magnificence from outside.

spots.name: Yudha Mandalatama Independence Monument
spots.desc: This rather splendid monument commemorates a local freedom fighter killed in the war against the Dutch. It is the dominant feature of the ramshackle but charming seafront of the city. Explore the surrounding area for a feeling of what Singaraja might have been like in its days as an important colonial port.

spots.name: Air Sanih
spots.desc: A quaint, tiny coastal village with a notable cold spring bathing area set in nice gardens. The spring water here is said to originate from holy Lake Batur. A warning that the springs are very popular with local children, and can get noisy. Don't let that put you off though, this is a very charming spot.

spots.name: Gitgit Waterfalls
spots.desc: You are on the northern slopes of the central mountain range here, and there are three spread out waterfalls around the village of Gitgit. When driving south from Singaraja to Bedugul you cannot miss the signs and car parks. The best of the falls is the southernmost which drops about 50 metres. Some opportunities for bathing in the cool and fresh mountain waters.

spots.name: Pura Meduwe Karang
spots.desc: A lovely looking temple, perhaps one of the most impressive in North Bali, and the location of the famous original carving of the Dutch cyclist which you see copied all over Bali. The temple is devoted to deities of agricultural matters.

spots.name: Pura Beji
spots.desc: A splendid pink sandstone temple with especially dramatic stone carvings. The temple is dedicated to the goddess of rice, Dewi Sri.

spots.name: Pondok Cabe
spots.desc: A restaurant in the form of a pondok or village house where locals and tourists enjoy Indonesian and Western cuisine. Good place to eat if you can't find any Indonesian food which suits your taste. Meals served by experienced chef with work experience overseas. The atmosphere is very quiet and relaxing. A very cheap, sanitary and quiet place to eat. Prices range from Rp 6,000 to 25,000.

spots.name: Warung Kota
spots.desc: A favoured hangout of local students, especially in the evenings. Good place to make friends and chat. You will find the locals very friendly indeed. Decent, standard Indonesian food at budget prices.

spots.name: Bali learn to surf
spots.desc: Has an office at the Hard Rock Hotel, as well as a beach presence. Offers equipment in good condition and premises for a surfing introduction in calm water at the swimming-pool of the Hard Rock Hotel. An introductory lesson costs US$45, lasts 2.5 hours and students are offered hotel transfers and fresh water. A 3-day course costs US$120, and 5-day courses include a "surfari" to other surfing…

spots.name: Bali Wave Hunter
spots.desc: Surfing charters and tours from Bali to Nusa Lembongan, Lombok & Sumbawa. Uses an 80-ft Indonesian jukung outrigger with full size beds, shower and toilet, TV, DVD player and stereo and wake boarding facilities. 240 v power with, kitchen with fridge and freezer. Smaller boat also available.

spots.name: Carla Spa
spots.desc: Very good full body oil massage for not too much money, ask for Alfa. Opposite side of Artawan, same side as "The Steps", a bit further towards JL Legian.

spots.name: Kimberly Spa
spots.desc: This massage and day spa is of good quality unlike some of the ones found in Kuta along the small side alleys. There is a cluster of such good places near here on the edge of the main club and bar scene on Jalan Legian.

spots.name: Paradiso Bowling Centre
spots.desc: An 18-lane bowling centre. Large number of pool and snooker tables as well.

spots.name: Manta Manta Diving
spots.desc: Daily snorkelling & diving trips to Nusa Penida, Tulamben, Padang Bai and Amed. PADI courses offered.

spots.name: Release a baby turtle
spots.desc: Volunteers protect turtle eggs and release newly born turtles back to the sea during nesting season on Kuta Beach, from March to September. They have release days when have enough hatchlings 16:00.

spots.name: Ticket to the Moon
spots.desc: Just in case you left yours at home, the flagship showroom of this famous Bali brand is here in Legian. Hammocks made from parachute fabric that fold up into the smallest, lightest package imaginable.

spots.name: Balinesia Tattoo
spots.desc: You’ll find plenty of local free parking. The studio has a relaxed atmosphere with staff both friendly and helpful. Experienced artists.

spots.name: Laundry
spots.desc: There are plenty of places that do laundry for about Rp7,000/kg, but their scales are often rigged. A 1.5-kg bag could be charged as being 2.5 kg. Take your own scales and receive some unfriendly response.

spots.name: Wina Optic
spots.desc: If you need a new pair of glasses or new lenses, this is a great value optician. Ask to see Hendrie. Transition lenses cost Rp400,000 for a pair and can be fitted in 4 days. Frames from about Rp200,000. Varifocal lenses cost Rp700,000.

spots.name: Money Changer (Bemo Corner)
spots.desc: A money changer offering good rates with no nonsense in an air-conditioned office. See map link for location at end of Jalan Legian.

spots.name: Indo Ink Bali Tattoo
spots.desc: Great tattoo studio with very knowledgeable artists. Very understanding and good service.

spots.name: Lippo Mall
spots.desc: Two-story shopping centre with hypermart and Cinemaxx Theatre on basement level.

spots.name: Hamburger Lady
spots.desc: As food can no longer be made at the beach, this hamburger stall owner walks around the beach with a menu and takes orders. She makes the burgers on the side of the tourist police station next to the shopping mall on the beach.

spots.name: Kedai Nasi Uduk
spots.desc: Small warung serving the Jakarta speciality Nasi Uduk (rice cooked in coconut water and various aromatic spices, served with chicken or beef and vegetables). Well prepared, authentic food.

spots.name: Kedin's Cafe
spots.desc: Good, typical local Indonesian food. They show sport or occasional Hollywood movies.

spots.name: Mie88
spots.desc: Indonesian noodles in large portions at very good prices. Excellent budget option - spend Rp15,000 for a delicious meal.

spots.name: Nusa Indah
spots.desc: Good, very cheap Indonesian food and cold beer. Great staff and always fun. An old school backpacker type hangout, the like of which has rapidly disappeared from Bali.

spots.name: Tree House Cafe
spots.desc: A busy and crowded budget restaurant. Their specialties are Dutch snacks, such as kroket and frikandel.

spots.name: Warung Indonesia
spots.desc: Popular with locals and long-stayers and is packed most nights. Some of the best food is not on the menu but laid out behind a glass display from where you can pick the food you want. Fresh fruit juices are all good and cheap, from Rp9,000. There are several other good cheap eating places along this narrow lane between Poppies I and II such as Fajar Resto next door that does a great Nasi Campur…
spots.price: Rp1,000-5,000 per choice, eat very well for Rp10,000-25,000

spots.name: Warung 96
spots.desc: This popular restaurant that serves Western food at reasonably low prices but not as cheap as some of the places found between Poppies 1 and 2, has been open since 1996, hence its name. The manager and staff are very friendly.

spots.name: Bamboo Corner
spots.desc: Popular with backpackers, very cheap Indonesian food from Rp15,000. Fresh fruit juices are good and cheap, from Rp8,000

spots.name: Blue Fin
spots.desc: Good quality Japanese fusion food at reasonable prices. Tempura is especially good as is the salmon salad.

spots.name: Havana Club Bali
spots.desc: Restaurant on two floors and the upper level can be reserved for private parties. Tasty food.

spots.name: Made's Warung
spots.desc: This is the original Made's, the forerunner of the now very successful Seminyak restaurant. One of the very first restaurants in Kuta, now on two floors and still doing a roaring trade. The menu includes Indonesian, Balinese and Western food. Try the pork ribs with green papaya.

spots.name: Mojo's Flying Burritos
spots.desc: Mexican restaurant serving California-style Mexican food and juices. Open kitchen where you can watch the cooks making tortillas and salsas. Margaritas by the pitcher. Rp35,000-70,000.

spots.name: Kafe Batan Waru
spots.desc: An institution in Ubud for many years. Great regional Indonesian cuisine, cocktails and coffee.

spots.name: Kuta Plaza Restaurant
spots.desc: Very popular restaurant serving Chinese Indonesian food. It is a typical Chinese restaurant - loud, bright and brash - but the food is excellent. Seafood is chosen live from tanks in the window. If that is not your thing, there are many other options including excellent pork ribs.

spots.name: Macaroni Chill Out Bar
spots.desc: Restaurant & lounge with good Italian food and some Asian fusion. Excellent service and desserts.

spots.name: The Bounty
spots.desc: Looks from the inside like a torn ship with several different areas including pool tables. The party starts every day from 22:00 but really gets going at midnight. Go here to get 'Blasters'. Rough and ready and it gets very messy.

spots.name: Eikon
spots.desc: Lounge bar which frequently has a decent cover band playing R&B.

spots.name: The Engine Room
spots.desc: Small lounge bar and dance club. A little more sophisticated than some of the options on this street.

spots.name: Mbargo
spots.desc: Large air-conditioned bar on two floors. Models are on tap to serve you drinks. Hosts regular fashion shows. A favourite with Australian teenagers. Security is especially tight.

spots.name: Vi Ai Pi
spots.desc: Lounge style bar and restaurant with nice breezy open upper level.

spots.name: Sky Garden
spots.desc: Big modern building in a metallic half open air architecture, with several atmospheres, each club has its own DJ. Sexy dancers on bar tops, sometimes fire shows in Dome. They have a lot of security, probably due to the 2002 bombing nearby. They sometimes require ID to prove age. Live band starting 22:30 but not on Mondays. The large open air rooftop terrace is awesome. Rp50,000 for small Bintang.…

spots.name: Apache Reggae Bar
spots.desc: Live music every night, great reggae and rock cover bands in the bar right on the street, then DJs. In the back there is another big reggae venue with another good cover band that plays Bob Marley covers non-stop from midnight.

spots.name: Alleycats
spots.desc: The busiest pre-club bar. Go here for their "Double Doubles".

spots.name: Bagus Pub
spots.desc: Favourite drinking den of Aussie all-day drinkers. Great place to watch the world go by.

spots.name: The Steps
spots.desc: Not a bar as such, it's some steps in front of a mini market with a boom box for entertainment. A Kuta institution favoured by the surf crowd that's often busier than a lot of the real bars.

spots.name: Twice Bar
spots.desc: A dark setting perfectly suited to the heavy metal bands that play here several times a week, popular with many of the local Kuta scene.

spots.name: Piggys Bar
spots.desc: A smaller version of Bagus Pub but with live bands and open 24 hours a day.

spots.name: Kama Sutra
spots.desc: Cavernous bar and club on the beachfront which is very popular with young Indonesians.

spots.name: All Stars Surf Cafe
spots.desc: Non-stop surf videos, huge jugs of icy beer, sumo wrestling and limbo dancing.

spots.name: Stadium Sports Cafe
spots.desc: Long established sports bar with two huge projection screens. Shows lots of the Premier League, plus Australian and American sports.
spots.addr: Complex Kuta Side Walk, Jl Kartika Plaza

spots.name: Gloria Jean's coffees
spots.desc: Nice coffee shop with lots of comfy seating upstairs overlooking a scenic temple.

spots.name: BRI Museum
spots.desc: A museum dedicated to R.A. Wiriatmaja, who pioneered the Indonesian banking system and was the founder of BRI (Bank Rakyat Indonesia).

spots.name: General Soedirman Underpass
spots.desc: Finished in 2019, it is a beautifully-decorated underpass to separate the traffic from the rail tracks. Dedicated to General Soedirman.

spots.name: Gada Rujak Polo Monument
spots.desc: Finished in 2020, it is a monument on a roundabout just before the underpass. It has a dancing fountain.

spots.name: General Gatot Subroto Monument
spots.desc: A monument that is dedicated to Indonesian National Hero Jenderal Gatot Subroto.

spots.name: Andhang Pangrenan Park
spots.desc: This park has playground for kids and also a stage for events.
spots.addr: Jalan Gerilya Purwokerto Selatan, Karangklesem, South Purwokerto 53142

spots.name: Balai Kemambang Park
spots.desc: This well-decorated park is mostly visited by families with kids since it has a playground inside and also a small dancing fountain.
spots.addr: Jl. Karang Kobar No.9, Bancarkembar, North Purwokerto 53115

spots.name: Pangripta Brubahan Park
spots.desc: A local community park completed with a walkway that is suitable as a jogging track.

spots.name: Satria Park
spots.desc: A local community park completed with a walkway that is suitable as a jogging track.
spots.addr: JL. Jend. Sudirman, Berkoh, South Purwokerto 53146

spots.name: Satria Sport Complex
spots.desc: This is the largest sport complex in town. Contains a football stadium, tennis courts, reflection park, and a few other venues. Usually locals visit in the morning, especially on Sunday when there is an event called sunday morning (sunmor)
spots.addr: Jl. Prof. Dr. Suharso, Purwokerto Lor, East Purwokerto 53121

spots.name: Soesilo Soedarman Sport Complex
spots.desc: which has better jogging track and a daily football match played by local football teams.
spots.addr: Jl. DR. Soeparno, Grendeng, North Purwokerto 53122

spots.name: Wijayakusuma Golf Course
spots.desc: The only golf course in Purwokerto. It's relatively small but very affordable.
spots.addr: Jalan Profesor Doktor Bunyamin No.10, Bancarkembar, North Purwokerto 53121

spots.name: Rita Supermall Purwokerto
spots.desc: The only modern shopping mall in Barlingmascakeb agglomeration region. It attracts many local visitors from neighboring regencies and always packed every end of the months and holidays. You may find everything in here.
spots.addr: Jl. Jend. Soedirman No.296, Sokanegara, East. Purwokerto 53116

spots.name: Moro Mall Purwokerto
spots.desc: another so-called "shopping mall" that has a large supermarket with cheaper prices.
spots.addr: Jl. Perintis Kemerdekaan No. 7, Purwokerto Kulon, South Purwokerto 53141

spots.name: Living Plaza Purwokerto
spots.desc: Contains ACE Hardwares and Informa Furnitures stores. There is also Chatime and KFC inside.
spots.addr: Jl. Jend. Soedirman No.447, Sokanegara, East Purwokerto 53116

spots.name: Empal Kupat Bu Karsih
spots.desc: A traditional and legendary Purwokerto breakfast food, Empal kupat

spots.name: Serabi Jalan Bank "Mbok Sur"
spots.desc: available early in the morning is a local favourite. The queue is sometimes very long, especially during holiday season.
spots.addr: Jl. RA Wiryaatmaja No.2 RT 1/4, Kedungwuluh, West Purwokerto 53131

spots.name: Richeese Factory
spots.desc: Serve fried chicken with cheese and spicy sauce. It has drive-thru service.
spots.addr: Jl. Jend. Soedirman No.530, Sokanegara, East Purwokerto 53116

spots.name: Meteeor Cafe
spots.desc: One of the best places in town for hangout, offers Italian, Chinese, and Japanese cuisines and snacks.
spots.addr: Jalan Jend. Sudirman, Satria Plaza no. 1-2

spots.name: Pringgading
spots.desc: a garden-restaurant in DI Panjaitan street, offers Indonesian and Chinese cuisine.
spots.addr: Jl. DI Panjaitan No.217, Purwokerto Kidul, South Purwokerto 53141

spots.name: Oemah Daoen
spots.desc: a garden-restaurant in Karangklesem, a few meters south of Andhang Pangrenan Park.
spots.addr: Jl. KH. Wahid Hasyim No.101 - 103, South Purwokerto 53144

spots.name: D' Java Steak
spots.desc: Low-key steakhouse serving classic cuts & sides in airy quarters with traditional Javanese decor.
spots.addr: Jl. Kranji No. 28, Purwanegara, East Purwokerto 53116

spots.name: Table Nine Resto
spots.desc: Roomy restaurant with outdoor seating furnishing traditional favorites, set meals & hot pots.
spots.addr: Jl. Profesor DR. HR Bunyamin, Pabuaran, North Purwokerto 53124

spots.name: Ketan Pencok Majapahit
spots.desc: A special snack from Bumiayu District in Southern Brebes, ketan pencok, a sticky rice cake with pencok on top. Pencok is stir-fried grated coconut mixed with brown sugar.
spots.addr: Jl. Majapahit No.16, Pesantren, Kalierang, Bumiayu

spots.name: SARITEM
spots.desc: Brebes drink called sari beras hitam, a drink made from the extract of black rice.
spots.addr: Jl. Bulakwungu, RT.01/RW.06, Bulakwungu, Benda, Sirampog

spots.name: Deer Reserve
spots.desc: Bawean deer (Axis kuhlii), also known as Kuhl's hog deer or Bawean hog deer, is a highly threatened species of deer found only on the island.

spots.name: Warung Nasi Bu Nor'a
spots.desc: Serves nasi campur (rice with veggies and protein side dishes) also fish crackers including posot-posot.

spots.name: PPI Bawean
spots.desc: Traditional market with various local dishes such as nasek ghulung and koncok-koncok.

spots.name: Cafe Lestari
spots.desc: Serves grilled fish, lobster, koncok-koncok, and bakso ikan (fishball soup).

spots.name: Museum Arum Dalu PT. INKA
spots.desc: A railway museum of state-owned PT. INKA, there is also a cafe.

spots.name: Taman Trembesi Kota Madiun
spots.desc: A rain-tree park. Tree-shaded, relaxed city park with paths, a children's play area & plenty of seating.

spots.name: Bluder Cokro
spots.desc: Sells bluder, a kind of bread which is known for its soft texture and taste. It is offered in 14 variants, from raisins to cheese.

spots.name: Warung Nasi Pecel Yu Gembrot
spots.desc: Serves pecel (Javanese salad) also peyek cracker. It serves on folded banana leaves called pincuk.
spots.addr: Jl. Imam Bonjol No.33, Klegen, Kartoharjo

spots.name: Pentol Corah Bu Suti
spots.desc: Serves Madiun snack, pentol corah, made from tapioca and wheat flour stuffed in tofu skin and served with special spicy sambal.

spots.name: Dawet Suronatan
spots.desc: A Madiun iced dawet/cendol consists of pink dawet (rice flour jelly), ketan hitam (black glutinuous rice), tape singkong (fermented cassava), and bubur sum-sum (Indonesian rice pudding).

spots.name: Alun Alun
spots.desc: A small park in the middle of Batu town, where locals regularly take walks and idle about. The newly re-worked Alun Alun is adorned with representations of pretty much all of Batu's specialities: apples, strawberries, milk-producing cows, rabbits, etc. as booths, lanterns and statues. There is also a decent-sized Ferris wheel with Rp5,000 entrance fee.

spots.name: Taman Rekreasi Selecta
spots.desc: This landscaped park was established by the Dutch in 1930 and although very changed, it remains a charming place to visit outside of the school holiday seasons when it is overrun with children. Nice swimming pool. There are hot showers for Rp5,000, but no hot springs or hot pools. Opportunities for some guided walks and horse riding. There is a hotel and restaurant attached to the park.

spots.name: Punten
spots.desc: Hectare after hectare of apple orchards and orchid nurseries. Pay a nominal rupiah sum and pick and eat as many apples as you can manage. Other villages nearby have similar setups and include Sidomulyo and Pandanrejo.

spots.name: Songgoriti
spots.desc: This is probably the single most attractive village in the area and a day or half day spent just wandering here will be time well spent. Don't get cheated, they sell some hot showers as "hot springs". There's also a notable Hindu temple dating from the Majapahit period in the 15th century.

spots.name: Toko Linda
spots.desc: A one-stop-shop on the way towards Selecta, where you can get various Batu snacks specialties. The shop also sells everything from daily needs to clothes.

spots.name: Pasar Senggol
spots.desc: A large array of local food and snacks, served in permanent makeshift tents that gives you truly local tastes and lifestyle. Most famous street food includes tahu brontak (deep fried stuffed tofu), pisang molen (banana wrapped in flour-based batter), pisang goreng (fried banana), ketan (sticky rice, served with ground soy bean and coconut), bakso (meatballs in soup), and tahu lontong (tofu and…

spots.name: Sate Hot Plate
spots.desc: Sate kambing (goat satay), and other sate, including beef and chicken. Steaks and many vegetable, noodle, tofu and tempe dishes are also on the menu.

spots.name: Depot Santai
spots.desc: Delicious local interpretations of Chinese cuisine. Generous portion with local price range. Lesehan (sitting on the floor) dining is available. Specialities include Fu Yung Hai, Koloke and fried rice.

spots.name: Cart Food
spots.desc: Cart food are commonly sold in batu. The single-manned hand-pushed carts commonly sell food such as bakso (meatballs in soup), Mie tek tek (fried noodles), Tahu Lontong (tofu and rice cake in peanut sauce), Roti Goreng (Sweet fried bread), Putu (steamed pandanus cake served with coconut and red sugar), etc. They come with eating utensils handy, and will wait for you to finish eating before moving…

spots.name: Jagung Bakar
spots.desc: A lot of the tents on the roadside on the mountains of Pujon sells Jagung Bakar (barbecue corn), where you can pick your own corn from the stack and season the corns yourself if you prefer. The sites juts precariously out the ledge of the roads, propped with bamboo. Beautifully casual, one can see the city of Batu with the lights at night. It gets chilly, so be prepared.

spots.name: Mayofield Mall Cilegon
spots.desc: The largest shopping mall in Cilegon, with a range of shops, cafés, and restaurants.

spots.name: Warung Gonjleng Hj. Wiwi
spots.desc: Small restaurant selling 'nasi gonjleng', a typical fried rice dish from Cilegon. Also satay, soups, and roasted chicken and fish.

spots.name: Situ Mustika
spots.desc: A small lake surrounded by forests. It has an orchid park (Taman Anggrek). You can relax at gazebos on an island in the middle of the lake, and there are several selfie spots.
spots.price: Entry Rp5,000 weekdays, Rp7,500 weekends and public holidays, Taman Anggrek Rp15,000 weekdays, Rp20,000 weekends and…

spots.name: Situ Leutik
spots.desc: Another small lake. There is a jogging track and gazebos, and as of September 2019, tourism facilities are being built.

spots.name: Situ Bentang
spots.desc: A fishing spot, but there is no tourism facility at this lake.

spots.name: British Council Indonesia Foundation
spots.desc: Centre of cultural exchange between the United Kingdom and Indonesia. Serves as the IELTS test centre in Indonesia.

spots.name: Gudang Sarinah Ekosistem
spots.desc: Art and creative space founded in 2015. Usually used for various events such as music festival, concert, and education. It was once a warehouse (gudang) owned by the Sarinah mall in Central Jakarta.
spots.addr: Jl. Pancoran Timur II No.4, RT.9/RW.4, Cikoko, Pancoran

spots.name: Dia.lo.gue Artspace
spots.desc: Contemporary art centre and exhibition with coffee shop inside. The name can be interpreted as "she/him, you, and me", or conversation in Bahasa Indonesia.
spots.addr: Jl. Kemang Selatan No.99A, RT.1/RW.2, Bangka

spots.name: A3000 Cultural Collaboratory
spots.desc: Formerly known as Aksara Bookstore back in their days. Nowadays serves as an art space and has an oyster bar.

spots.name: Djoko Sutono
spots.desc: This statue commemorated Professor DR. Djoko Sutono, SH, the founder of Indonesian Police Academy.
spots.addr: Police Academy (PTIK) Jalan Tirtayasa 6, Kebayoran Baru

spots.name: Gajah Mada
spots.desc: This statue commemorated the establishment of Bhayangkara/Police corps led by Patih Gajah Mada from Majapahit Kingdom (14th century).
spots.addr: Indonesian Police HQ, Jalan Trunojoyo 3, Kebayoran Baru, South Jakarta

spots.name: Pondok Indah Water Park
spots.desc: A water park, perfect if what you want is leisure rather than adrenaline. Not many slides but very kid-friendly.

spots.name: Puri Santi Spa
spots.desc: Single treatment rooms with ensuite shower / bathtub, VIP couple suite with garden view with private jacuzzi & hot steam shower. A luxurious place and all products are made from pure plant based ingredients. Opening hours: daily 09:00 - 20:00.

spots.name: Pondok Indah Golf and Country Club
spots.desc: A huge sign "Pondok Indah Golf and Country Club - 1983 World Cup Venue" marks the entrance. Has a driving range. 2 levels of driving range bays, with a beautiful view. The range area is water, with several islands for you to aim at.
spots.price: Rp40,000 for 100 balls. + Rp20,000 is the (caddy fee)

spots.name: ITC Kuningan
spots.desc: A lower class mall, with small shacks of micro businesses. Get cheap fashion or moreover, fix your electronic devices here. In contrast, the upper floor has premium dining options, while lower floor has Carrefour.

spots.name: Epiwalk
spots.desc: Much smaller mall because there are just a few options for dining and shopping. Home of the two biggest screening theatres in Jakarta (from 21Cineplex chain).
spots.addr: Jl. H. R. Rasuna Said, RT.2/RW.5, Karet Kuningan, Setiabudi

spots.name: Setiabudi One
spots.desc: A lot of mid to upscale dining options are available here. On the 2nd floor, you can find XXI Theatre (from 21 Cineplex) as well.
spots.addr: Jl. H. R. Rasuna Said Kav. 62, RT.18/RW.02, Karet Kuningan, Setiabudi

spots.name: Plataran Dharmawangsa
spots.desc: A mall to go to if you don't like the crowded hype. Close to the premium hotel of the same name is a mall with premium tenants (well, most are not chain brands) and dining options.

spots.name: Pasaraya Grande
spots.desc: Great hangout place in South Jakarta with its many cafes and restaurants. It has a big food court in the basement with an extensive selection of local and international cuisine. The mall itself sprawls a wide array of clothing items from local and international designers. It has a floor dedicated entirely to Indonesian traditional clothing and handicrafts, although the items are a bit pricey.

spots.name: Agneya Restaurant
spots.desc: Serving mostly Indonesian cuisines but with a different twist on the cooking process.
spots.price: Typically Rp200,000 per person (incl. food and drink)
spots.addr: Jalan Wijaya IX No.23, RT.2/RW.5, Melawai

spots.name: Koi Kemang
spots.desc: Serves Western and Asian cuisine with a wide variety selection of wines and beers and also live music
spots.addr: Jalan Kemang Raya No.72b, RT.7/RW.2, Mampang Prapatan

spots.name: Pondok Nasi Kebuli Ibu Hanna
spots.desc: Nasi kebuli is an Arab-Betawi dish of rice with spices and meat like lamb.
spots.addr: Jl. KH Abdullah Syafei No.4, Bukit Duri, Tebet

spots.name: Rumah Makan Betawi Haji Nasun
spots.desc: Serves some Betawi cuisine such as Pecak gurame (Gourami fish in spicy Betawi sauce) and Gabus pucung (Snakehead fish in black soup).
spots.addr: Jl. Moch. Kahfi II No.21 A, Srengseng Sawah, Jagakarsa

spots.name: Ayam Bakar Wong Solo
spots.desc: Traditional grilled chicken chain. Menu: grilled chicken, fried fish, prawn, tom yam, salad. Many women's rights activists boycott this place because the restaurant owner aggressively promotes polygamy.

spots.name: Ayam Goreng Mbok Berek
spots.desc: Traditional fried chicken restaurant. Menu: fried chicken, gudeg, gado-gado (salad with peanut sauce), salad.

spots.name: Warung MJS
spots.desc: A semi-outdoor restaurant serving Javanese cuisine with live Javanese music.
spots.addr: Jl. Setia Budi Tengah No.11, RT.1/RW.1, Setiabudi

spots.name: Warkop Pasundan
spots.desc: A warung (or mini restaurant) selling various types of comfort food such as instant noodles, fried noodles, Magelangan (a mix of fried rice and fried noodles), etc.
spots.addr: Jalan Setiabudi Tengah No.14, RT.1/RW.1, Setiabudi

spots.name: Mie Aceh Bang Iwan
spots.desc: An Acehnese restaurant specialising in Mie Aceh in the Setiabudi vicinity.
spots.addr: Jalan Setiabudi Barat No. 25, RT.2/RW.2, Setiabudi

spots.name: Kinara
spots.desc: Indian restaurant. Menu: lamb, chicken, salad, tandoori, soup, seafood, breads. One of the best Indian restaurants in Jakarta.
spots.price: approx. US$16/person, except Lobster Mughlai, US$45

spots.name: Pizza Place
spots.desc: A New York-style pizza food stall. One of few pizza places that also serve by the slices as well either for take away or dine in.
spots.addr: Como Park, Jl. Kemang Timur Raya No. 998, Kemang

spots.name: Shabu Ghin
spots.desc: All you can eat shabu-shabu restaurant with different choices of beef.
spots.addr: Jalan Wolter Monginsidi No. 53, Kebayoran Baru, RT.1/RW.1

spots.name: Sushi Hiro
spots.desc: Popular for an extraordinary display of sushi and has many branches throughout the city.
spots.addr: Jalan Suryo No.24, RT.10/RW.3, Rw., Kebayoran Baru

spots.name: Tanpopo Jakarta
spots.desc: Outdoor Japanese street food such as Kushiyaki, Yakiniku, Teppanyaki, and Shabu-Shabu.
spots.addr: Jalan Sultan Iskandar Muda No. 99E, Arteri Pondok Indah

spots.name: Amigos Bar & Cantina
spots.desc: One of a few Mexican restaurants in Jakarta. Serves mostly American Traditional and Tex-Mex food.
spots.addr: Kemang Club Villas, Jalan Kemang Selatan I, RT.8/RW.3, Mampang Prapatan

spots.name: Shisha Cafe
spots.desc: Modern but pleasant Middle Eastern food, with the full range of mezze (Rp10,000-20,000) and kebabs (Rp30,000 up) and no less than 15 varieties of flavored water pipe tobacco, from cappuccino to coconut. Indoor (aircon) and outdoor seating, belly dancing on Fridays and Saturdays.

spots.name: Tamnak Thai
spots.desc: Thai restaurant. Menu: salad, soup, prawn, lobster, squid, crab, asparagus, fish, sapo soya bean curd, fried chicken, duck, grilled beef.
spots.addr: Jalan Kemang Raya No. 17, RT.6/RW.1, Kemang

spots.name: Pho 24
spots.desc: Vietnamese restaurant. Menu: spring rolls, salad, noodle soup, grilled beef, fried chicken, rice vermicelli noodle.

spots.name: Fish Streat
spots.desc: Seafood restaurant, specialising in fish and chips. Popular amongst locals for its cheap price and delicious tasting fish and chips.
spots.addr: Jalan Tebet Timur Dalam No.44B, RT.4/RW.5, Tebet

spots.name: Burgreens Darmawangsa
spots.desc: One of the pioneers of organic restaurant in Jakarta, serving burgers as the main course.

spots.name: Die Stube Germany Resto & Bar
spots.desc: A popular German restaurant in Jakarta due to their regular happy hour promos. Filled mostly with expats and also locals.
spots.price: About Rp420,000 for two people (incl. food and drinks)
spots.addr: Plaza Bisnis Kemang I, Jl. Kemang Raya 2, Kemang

spots.name: Lawless Burger Bar
spots.desc: A burger joint in the heart of Kemang vicinity owned by a clothing store and a tattoo parlour, Lawless. Popular amongst the locals due to its affordable price for an enormous burger and also sells alcoholic drinks and liquors.
spots.price: from Rp45,000 to Rp200,000 for the meals. Drinks can cost up to Rp3,000,000 for a bottle of single-malt whisky
spots.addr: Jalan Kemang Selatan VIII No.67G, Bangka, Mampang Prapatan

spots.name: Le Burger
spots.desc: A gourmet burger curated by father and son duo of Michelin-starred chef Jean-Claude and Cédric Vongerichten.
spots.price: Burgers from Rp110,000 and beverages from Rp45,000

spots.name: Tokyo Skipjack
spots.desc: Steakhouse restaurant in the heart of South Jakarta, Blok M district. A different approach to their sauces, where you can choose from 6 variants to accompany your dish.
spots.addr: Jalan Bulungan No.20, RT.11/RW.7, Kramat Pela, Kebayoran Baru

spots.name: D's Place
spots.desc: Facility: nice bar downstairs, a small pool annex, dance floor upstairs, nightly dance competition.
spots.addr: Jl. Falatehan I No. 1 C., Blok M

spots.name: Debasic
spots.desc: Facility: bar, live music (hip hop, retro and jazz), restaurant, discotheque. Drinks: fine wine, cocktail, liquer based coffee, Debasic Sensation, Strawberry Basic Margarita, Long Basic Island. Specialty: Caesar Salad, Goulash Soup, Calamari Calypso, Entrecote Conosierre, Veal Escallop St. debasic, Deep Fried Oxtail.

spots.name: Eastern Promise
spots.desc: Favorite expat hangout, nice bar with Indian/English restaurant, pool table,darts, big screen, big outdoor garden with live music: every Wednesday live jazz, weekends rock/pop/blues or latin, price: moderate

spots.name: Plaza Senayan Arcadia
spots.desc: Mall with two barsː Molly Malone's Irish Pub and Prohibition.

spots.name: Filosofi Kopi
spots.desc: Probably famous due to the name, which is directly derived from the book and its film adaptation, "Filosofi Kopi" by Dewi Lestari. Located in the famous Blok M district.
spots.addr: Jalan Melawai 6 Blok M No 8, RT.3/RW.1, Melawai

spots.name: One Fifteenth Coffee
spots.desc: The name is derived from a well-known coffee-to-water ratio, 1:15. Famous for the unique name and also its head barista, Doddy Samsura, received first place in World Barista Championships.
spots.addr: Jalan Gandaria 1 No.63, RT.2/RW.3, Kebayoran Baru

spots.name: Toko Kopi TUKU
spots.desc: First location in the city and becomes one of the established coffee chains in Jakarta. The name is also used for a MRT Jakarta Station in Cipete.
spots.addr: Jalan Cipete Raya Blok B No.7, Cipete Selatan, Cilandak, RT.6/RW.3

spots.name: Smoking Barrels Atelier (Cipete Branch)
spots.desc: One of many coffee shops in Jakarta that provides padel courts.

spots.name: Toraja Coffee House
spots.desc: A coffee house in Jakarta, where only Toraja coffee beans - a region in the south of Sulawesi - are used.

spots.name: Kem Chicks
spots.desc: A supermarket chain inside Pacific Place mall, sells mostly beers and wines with limited selection.
spots.addr: Pacific Place, LG Floor Unit 99, Jalan Jenderal Sudirman Kav. 52 – 53, South Jakarta 12190

spots.name: The Pot Hole Wines
spots.desc: A wine bar with a hole in the wall concept, similar to the one in Florence, Italy.
spots.addr: Jl. Bulungan No.9 LT 2, RT.4/RW.6, Kramat Pela

spots.name: Apollo Bar & Lounge
spots.desc: A place for you if you into cabaret lipsync show of transgender divas or muscled gogo dancers. It is the hippest gay club in Jakarta.
spots.addr: Bellagio Boutique Mall UG Level, Jl. Mega Kuningan Barat VII

spots.name: Dragonfly
spots.desc: Expensive restaurant and stylish nightclub in shades of black and red, with a two-story wine rack. A place for the idle rich to see and be seen, so expect long queues on weekends unless you show up before midnight or know the right people. Free entry, but steeply priced drinks at Rp 70,000 and up.
spots.addr: Jl Jend Gatot Subroto Kav 23 Graha BIP Lt 1

spots.name: Monaco Club
spots.desc: Discotheque, dance,Karaoke rooms, Bar. Japanese and French cuisine: escargot, sushi, sashimi. Drinks: Mojito, Cinzano Piccolo, Vino de Monaco, Vodca Martini. Opening hours: Tu-Th 18:00-02:00, F Sa 18:00-03:30, Su 19:00-01:00. Price: splurge.
spots.addr: Hotel Gran Mahakam, Jl Mahakam I no 6

spots.name: Nirvana
spots.desc: Facility: disco, karaoke, home band, dance floor. Music style: tribal, garage, oldies, underground. Opening hours: 23:00 to 04:00. Karaoke facility on 2nd floor: 10 rooms from US$10/hour.

spots.name: X-Lounge/Vertigo
spots.desc: Two interconnected clubs, the more nightclubby Vertigo upstairs playing harder dance music and the more bar-like X-Lounge downstairs spinning R&B and pop. Entrance Rp 80,000 on weekends, which gets you a drink and access to both.
spots.addr: Gedung Veteran RI 16-17F (in Plaza Semanggi), Jl. Gatot Subroto

spots.name: Tendean Residence
spots.desc: Studio-style rooms with balcony. Pantry at every floor and outdoor terrace at selected floors. Having that said, no breakfast provided apart from cup noodles.

spots.name: Snorkeling
spots.desc: Two of the most popular start points are Pramuka Island and Tidung Island. From there, you can rent snorkeling gears for as low as Rp 30,000, and hire a boat (can be filled up to 15-20 people).

spots.name: Birdwatching
spots.desc: Rambut Island is the sanctuary for 20,000 birds and 30,000 migratory birds because of its width and its mangrove forests.

spots.name: Nature conservation
spots.desc: A lot of nature conservation is going on here. There is a sea turtle sanctuary at Pramuka Island. One of the best things to do is releasing the hatchlings. The still-small sea turtles will come back to the water find their mother when they are able to swim, so it has a ceremonial feeling to the scene. You can also do mangrove planting on the same island.

spots.name: Cidayu Monument
spots.desc: Cidayu stands for Chinese, Dayak and Malay. The monument depicts the life of the surrounding community, harmony of different ethnic groups.

spots.name: Lotus Lake
spots.desc: An artificial lake. Aside from viewing the lake, you can ride water bike, swimming in the pool, or eat at the restaurants available in there.

spots.name: Bougenville Hill Recreation Park
spots.desc: As the name suggests, the park is dominated by colorful bougenvilles. You can find 46 different species of bougenville! Some of them were imported from other countries, as well. There is also another types of flowers like orchid, antorium, and aglonema. Not to mention several fruit plants grow there including avocado, durian, rambutan, and star fruit. That means visitors can either buy or eat…

spots.name: Toko Tanjaya
spots.desc: Buy joss sticks, candles, and Buddhist accessories. This shop is one of the biggest of its kind in Borneo Island in terms of trading volume. Expect crowd of buyers, especially during Capgomeh festival (15 days after Chinese New Year).

spots.name: Ngurbloat Beach
spots.desc: The Lonely Planet states that Ngurbloat Beach has the smoothest sand on earth. The sand is so powder-fine here that National Geographic had to dub Ngurbloat Beach as the softest beach sands in Asia.

spots.name: Ngurtavur Beach
spots.desc: A white sand beach on a remote island. Also, become the habitat of the Australian pelican.

spots.name: Desa Wisata Letman
spots.desc: Do a traditional flying fox. Also, boating around the Letman coral island group.

spots.name: Amphibious Tank Sites
spots.desc: A site of Landing Vehicle Tracked Mark 2 was used by US Navy in World War II.

spots.name: Dodola Island
spots.desc: A white sand island that is separated into two islands in the afternoon because of the tide.

spots.name: Mount Kelimutu
spots.desc: The main attraction, Kelimutu is Keli=Mount and Mutu=Boiling means mount is always active. Beautiful at sunrise, the 3 mineral lakes at the top (in the craters) change colour with the changing of the volcanoes activities. The lakes change color completely from time to time. In the national park you can see a table of what color the lakes were for each year going back 20 years. It is impossible to…

spots.name: Monkeys
spots.desc: On your way down the volcano you will find the monkeys have awoken. There is an official feeding ground where you can go and feed the monkeys. Be careful, they are sneaky buggers, and there's always a risk of being bitten or scratched when interacting with wild animals.

spots.name: Nearby villages
spots.desc: Moni is surrounded by spectacular scenery, landscapes dotted with palms and banana trees. There are also a number of visible burial sites in front gardens, a local cultural tradition.

spots.name: Hot springs
spots.desc: Near the entrance to the Kelimutu National Park you find the hot springs. A perfect end to an early morning.

spots.name: Waterfalls
spots.desc: Opposite Rainbow Cafe, a small path leads down to a roaring waterfall. Popular with the young locals, this is considered the perfect site for a picnic.

spots.name: Chenty Restaurant
spots.desc: Beside Bintang Restaurant. Their specialty is delicious Moni cakes - mashed potatoe with herbs deep fried til crispy and well worth the wait.

spots.name: Lake Nirvana
spots.desc: A stunning turquoise lagoon connected to the ocean by a 300-metre-long channel. It is filled with starfish and lovely to swim in. You can rent a kayak to get there, or you charter a small boat.
spots.price: Kayak rental about costs Rp50,000 per person for 1/2 a day. Boat charters are Rp100,000-300,000 depending on your…

spots.name: Thousand Mouths
spots.desc: Take a boat tour through the forested islets and rock formations of the Thousand Mouths area, drifting over clear turquoise and emerald-green waters.
spots.price: Tours range anywhere from Rp100,000 for a simple charter to Rp750,000

spots.name: Termanu Rock
spots.desc: A beautiful rock formation and a great place to watch the sunset. There are two approaches, the beach route and the hill route. The beach route is only accessible at low tide.

spots.name: Mangrove Beach
spots.desc: A unique and gorgeous mangrove where lush green trees grow out of brilliant turquoise water.

spots.name: Mando'o Hill
spots.desc: Nearly 500 stairs up to the top of a hill with fantastic views over the island. (It used to have only 300 stairs and was called Bukit Tangga 300 meaning "300-stair hill"; the name has stuck.) It is difficult to get to by road and the stairs are in poor condition... be careful!
spots.price: Rp3000 per person entrance fee, Rp1000 parking fee

spots.name: Rumah Adat Keluarga Manggi
spots.desc: A traditional Rote house and household. The Manggi Family still lives here; be respectful.

spots.name: Widow's Field
spots.desc: A splendid field of purple globe amaranth flowers (Gomphrena globosa) on Nuse Island. Peak flower season is March through June.

spots.name: Papela Harbour
spots.desc: Filled with colourful fishing boats that make for a picturesque scene. Many are still built without motors because the 1974 MOU Box agreement with Australia preserves fishing rights for Indonesian fishers using traditional methods within Australia's Exclusive Economic Zone.

spots.name: The southernmost point of Asia
spots.desc: There's little to see here, other than a ruined lighthouse and a concrete marker. But, hey, you'll have been to the southernmost point of Asia! To visit Ndana Island, you must first obtain a permit at Kampung Merah Putih Desa Oeseli in Oeseli. Ask around about chartering a boat. Once you arrive on the island, you must register with the island authorities.

spots.name: Nembrala Beach
spots.desc: The famous surf beach, although not the best for swimming, as it is only possible at high tide and tends to have a lot of seaweed.

spots.name: Bo'a Beach
spots.desc: A beautiful white sand beach and a great surf spot. Swimming possible, even at low tide.

spots.name: Loedi Beach
spots.desc: A good beach for swimming and snorkelling, although it can have a bit of a rubbish problem on the shore if the adjoining resorts haven't got around to cleaning it up.

spots.name: Pantai Batu Pintu
spots.desc: A visually stunning beach and rock arch formation. It'll likely be just you and the horses set against the crystal clear water. You can climb up around the arch to the west and view Ndana Island and the southernmost point of Asia. Unfortunately quite a bit of plastic rubbish has washed up on shore, particularly on its western end.

spots.name: Oeseli Beach
spots.desc: Not much of a sandy beach but a good place to rent kayaks to paddle around the serene turquoise waters or charter a boat to Lake Nirvana.

spots.name: Pantai Tongga
spots.desc: A white sand beach on the northwest corner of Rote, most notable as the launching point for boats to Nuse Island.

spots.name: Pantai Sai Oebole
spots.desc: A tranquil beach with soft white sand on the north coast of the island.

spots.name: Inaoe Beach
spots.desc: A rocky coastal area with secluded beaches squeezed in between the cliffs.

spots.name: Pantai Oesosole
spots.desc: A pristine beach with mushroom-like rock formations sticking out of the turquoise waters. Absolutely no food or services.

spots.name: Danau Laut Mati
spots.desc: A brackish water lake where you can snorkel with stingless jellyfish. No services, bring your own gear.

spots.name: Pulau Helehanak
spots.desc: A tiny island off of Rote's south coast with some excellent snorkelling and diving.

spots.name: Smart Minimarket
spots.desc: The largest store on the island with most daily necessities.

spots.name: Pasar Delha
spots.desc: The market closest to Nembrala. Produce, 2nd-hand clothing, etc.

spots.name: Pasar Ba'a
spots.desc: The largest market on the island. Not tourist-oriented at all. Excellent prices compared to Nembrala.

spots.name: Kampung Tenun Ikat Rote Ndao
spots.desc: A collection of traditional fabric weavers. Bargaining is encouraged, but know that high quality pieces are pricey.

spots.name: Warung Mbak Jawa
spots.desc: A nice warung that feels somewhat upmarket with its pleasant seating area, though it retains warung prices.
spots.price: Meals from Rp25,000, drinks from Rp10,000

spots.name: Warung Makan Om Nus
spots.desc: Seafood restaurant. Choose your fish and they grill it for you.

spots.name: Becky Boo's Restaurant
spots.desc: Large menu, mostly western/international food, but famous for its pizza.

spots.name: 81 Palms Restaurant
spots.desc: Restaurant at the 81Palms resort with a Spanish-inspired menu and run by a Michelin-rated chef.

spots.name: Masjid Sultan Muhammad Salahuddin
spots.desc: Historical mosque built in 1770 by Sultan Abdul Kadim Zillulah Fil Alam.

spots.name: Masjid Hidayatullah Saonek
spots.desc: The oldest mosque in Southwest Papua that was founded in 1505.

spots.name: Scuba Republic Indonesia
spots.desc: Based in Raja Ampat, Komodo and South Sulawesi, Scuba Republic is in the prime spots for adventure. The main product is a liveaboard diving trip all around Raja Ampat or Komodo on a Phinisi Boat.

spots.name: Batuangus Beach
spots.desc: This beach has clear water and allows for snorkelling. Also a popular place for camping or having a picnic.

spots.name: Aertembaga Market
spots.desc: A lively, local market in Bitung where a variety of produce and items are sold, including fresh and smoked fish, spices, vegetables, rice and clothes.

spots.name: Triple Sari Resto & Cafe
spots.desc: Minahasan (Manado) cuisine with an abundance of seafood options.

spots.name: Tammasapi Waterfall
spots.desc: Tammasapi Waterfall features a series of gentle cascades flowing into natural pools suitable for swimming in suitable conditions.

spots.name: Kilometer Nol
spots.desc: The westernmost point in Indonesia is on Pulau Weh. You can rent a motorbike from Iboih for around Rp 100,000/day and head out on your own, or rent a minivan and guide to take your group.

spots.name: Rubiah Tirta Divers
spots.desc: Dive school based in Iboih, with a lot of restaurants and accommodations nearby. Has a big boat (under repair in early 2013) and two smaller boats, nice staff and many knowledgeable instructors and leaders. The place has a very collegiate atmosphere with lots of divers hanging out after their excursions. Local coconut artist Andy Coco works here as an instructor.

spots.name: Lumba Lumba Diving Centre
spots.desc: Popular western-owned dive operator in Gapang beach. Provides premium accommodations (for divers only). If you want something else than diving and hanging around with them 24/7, or tend to be more price-conscious, consider the other options.

spots.name: SCUBA Weh
spots.desc: A new shop, just opened by a local diver (Salim) with fifteen years experience, offering courses and more personalized dives at about the same price as the other shops. He usually does two dives in the morning and one in the afternoon, depending on weather conditions. Because Salim keeps the number of divers limited to four, it's a good choice if you're diving with one or two friends as you can…

spots.name: The Padé Dive Resort
spots.desc: The Pade Dive Resort is on Lhong Angen Beach on the very quiet westcoast of Pulau Weh. Here some of the islands' best divesites such as Batee Meuduro, Pantee Peunateung and The Canyon can be found. Well maintained rental equipment and NITROX is available for divetrips to all of Pulau Weh's divesites on the four boats. The housereef, which is also ideal for snorkeling, is easily accessible from…

spots.name: We Care Program
spots.desc: This school provides free English lessons, lessons on the environment and key skills to disadvantaged children in Bukit Lawang. They appreciate any time you can give: You can join them for one lesson or volunteer long-term. They provide free accommodation for long-term volunteers. Visitors to the school are also welcome. You can also pay to trek with the teachers; proceeds will go to the school.

spots.name: Green Hill
spots.desc: Has great views of the jungle and their food is great. The restaurant is a lovely open plan space and a good menu and is brilliant for vegetarians, e.g. banana and chocolate pancakes, tempe rendang, veggie curry.

spots.name: Indra Valley Inn and Resto
spots.desc: Have a wonderful riverside location with jungle views. The restaurant & bar offer offer a variety of delicious fresh meals and snacks with a good variety of vegetarian options. Ask the staff about their river surfing- for those wanting to work up an appetite before they dine.

spots.name: Jungle Tribe
spots.desc: A cocktail bar and restaurant owned by Erika-Canadian woman and her husband Agun. Situated next door to Sam's restaurant across the road from Sam's Bungalows- 3 very pleasant rooms with great views of the river.

spots.name: Sam's Bungalows
spots.desc: Right next door to Jungle Tribe cocktail bar, this restaurant has the best in panoramic views of the river. Sam's cook uses an array of herbs and spices that give her cooking an extra dimension. Try the Gado Gado special. All the curries are rich in flavor, filled with nutritious and natural food.

spots.name: Tony's Restaurant
spots.desc: Serves excellent home made pizza for those craving a touch of the west. The best spaghetti this side of Roma and a great tasting Gado Gado for those seeking some of the local fare.

spots.name: Yusri Cafe
spots.desc: Situated across from the National Park Ticket Office. A very homely feeling cafe with Yusuf and Rita (with Rita & her mum doing all the cooking) taking care of you. Serving tasty local food at local prices with decent portion sizes. Good western selection of food for breakfast. Nasi Goreng Rp 8,000, Nasi Ayam Rp 10,000, Black Tea/Coffee Rp 2,000 with milk Rp 5,000, Banana toast Rp 7,000, Banana…

spots.name: Taman Metro Indonesia Indah
spots.desc: A recreational place with waterboom, outbond, swimming pool, futsal court, and park.

spots.name: Tomb of King Sidabutar
spots.desc: The Batak king who adopted Christianity is buried in Tomok, a village 5 km southeast of Tuktuk.

spots.name: Speed boat rides
spots.desc: Private boat to Tomok or Tuktuk costs Rp 700,000 and takes 10 minutes.

spots.name: Cotney Restaurant
spots.desc: Rendangs, curries. Internet is available at a reasonable local price.

spots.name: Jenny's Restaurant
spots.desc: Restaurant with view of Lake Toba. Curries, fresh lake-fish, steamed or grilled, western food such as schnitzel (breaded pork or chicken chop pan fried). Desserts include fresh papaya that grows in the back-yard or a golden-brown banana pancake with chocolate sauce and a sprinkle of coconut. Once all the guests in the small place with only about 5 tables are fed and happy, Rinto will take the…

spots.name: Joe's Restaurant
spots.desc: A family restaurant with a kind, friendly owner. Chicken à la batak Rp 25,000, banana chocolate cake Rp 80,000 (for a whole cake). Also has fresh vanilla for sale (Rp 70,000 for 100 grams) and motorbike rental.

spots.name: Leo's Restaurant
spots.desc: Batak food, including pork and lake fish with local spices. Large Bintang Rp 35,000, 100 g fish Rp 8,000, served with fried potatoes (one portion of fish is 500 g normally, but they might have bigger ones, too). Family run, used to be one of the first restaurants in Tuktuk, then closed for some time and reopened in 2010 by the son of the previous owner.

spots.name: Marco Polo
spots.desc: Views and reasonably priced food. Make sure to try the avocado sandwich for Rp 10,000, the avocado tree can be seen from the balcony. The owners are extremely nice and helpful but don't seem to get many customers as they are past the main tourist area.
spots.addr: Close to the northern tip of Tuk Tuk

spots.name: Maruba Restaurant
spots.desc: Traditional Batak and Indonesian food and a variety of Western meals such as schnitzels, real homemade burgers, pasta and roast chicken with fresh herb stuffing. Brown bread, burger buns and baguettes baked most days. English breakfast with smoked bacon is delicious. You can order a Batak feast one day (or less) in advance. Some choices are boneless fish curry, ikan na neura (very fresh raw fish…

spots.name: Orari Restaurant
spots.desc: Restaurant with traditional Batak, Indonesian and European cuisine. Spaghetti bolognese, nasi goreng 'special', beef rendang, BBQ fish. Restaurant has a view of the lake. Motorbike rentals also available for Rp 60,000.

spots.name: Tabo Cottages
spots.desc: Free wifi, western-styled food served, the extensive menu is possibly pricier than other options. They have baked goods and European quality natural yoghurt. Fish is caught directly from the lake.

spots.name: Today's cafe
spots.desc: The owner of this small cafe, Juliet, is very friendly. Main meals from Rp 20,000-35,000. Wifi for Rp 100,000 an hour.

spots.name: Samosir Cottages
spots.desc: you will provide a wonderful local Batak performance that is a mixture of traditional dances and fantastic drinking songs.

spots.name: Hibiscus Bar
spots.desc: It is on the main street is hosted by two wonderful local girls and plays cool tunes.

spots.name: RM Gule Masam Gaok
spots.desc: A variety of fresh seafood, cooked by request. Try their famous gule masam (sour curry).

spots.name: Pondok Naga Pantai Galau
spots.desc: Lots of choices of foods: fish, shrimp, shellfish, pempek, chicken. The juices is also great.

spots.name: HL Vegetarian
spots.desc: Lacto-ovo vegetarian Asian food, coffee, salads. Free Wi-Fi.

spots.name: Mie Sagu Marineford
spots.desc: Serves mie sagu, Riau specialty noodles made from sago starch.
spots.addr: Jl. Nelayan Laut Gg. Family No.16, Pangkalan Sesai, Dumai Barat

spots.name: Mifan Water Park
spots.desc: Big palm-tree-filled water park with serpentine slides, pools & bumper boats, plus accommodations.

spots.name: Pak Datuk
spots.desc: Padang-style food served in a Minangkabau style building. Excellent roti cane.

spots.name: Minang Asli
spots.desc: Serving typical Indonesian food and is not too seasoned, so it's perfect for those who don't like spicy food.

spots.name: Agro Tourism Kaligua

spots.name: Pantai Geger
spots.desc: This is the public beach in Nusa Dua. This splendid white sand beach at the western edge of the enclave retains lots of the character that is missing in the sanitised Nusa Dua resort zone. Generally safe for swimming and some beach side warungs. The restaurant, beachbeds and massage ladys all work for the local cooperative. By supporting them you support the locals. Geger has a cooling breeze as…

spots.name: Panama Tea Plantation
spots.desc: A scenic tea plantation with a restaurant nearby. Rolling hills, lush greenery, and parallel lines make for an ideal landscape for photographers. Flying Fox attraction (starting at Rp20,000 per person) and ATV tours (Rp120,000/hour) are also available.
spots.addr: Jl. Rakai Garung No.KM. 5, Tlogo, Garung, Wonosobo

spots.name: Menjer Lake
spots.desc: A lake on the foothills of Dieng. You can feel the tranquil and calm nature of this lake from viewpoints on hills. Boat tours cost Rp20,000/person, while camping fees are Rp30,000–35,000.

spots.name: Dusun Butuh
spots.desc: The highest hamlet in Magelang with an altitude of 1600 masl and is on the slopes of Mount Sumbing.

spots.name: Jatibarang Sugar Mill
spots.desc: Walking around in an inactive old sugar mill. You may see historical buildings and heritage sugar cane trains.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Tim. No.1, Penumbukan, Jatibarang Kidul

spots.name: Candilawang Temple
spots.desc: A Hindu temple of the Ancient Mataram Kingdom was built in the 9th century.

spots.name: Candisari Temple
spots.desc: A Hindu temple is on a small hill with an altitude of 991 meters above sea level.

spots.name: Tumpak Sewu Waterfall
spots.desc: Tumpak Sewu Waterfall or also called Coban Sewu is a waterfall with a height of about 120 meters. This waterfall is bordered by Lumajang Regency and Malang Regency.

spots.name: Kangean Islands
spots.desc: The Kangeans are an archipelago of about 30 islands 120 km to east-north-east of Madura. These are relatively little known but with far better boat transport options than used to be the case, the islands are accessible for the adventurous traveller. The largest island is Kangean itself at about 490 sqkm. Others are as small as 1,800 sqm. The key attraction here is marine life and there is good…

spots.name: Bandealit Beach
spots.desc: Do birdwatching by camping on the beach. Forest trekking to Gua Jepang (Japanese soldier bunker). Canoeing in telaga (lake) near the beach.

spots.name: Tabuhan Cave
spots.desc: A cave with stalactites and stalagmites that produce musical tones if struck.

spots.name: Watu Karung Beach
spots.desc: Two world-class waves. There once held the World Surf League competition.

spots.name: Jamus Tea Plantation
spots.desc: Tours of a plantation with terraced fields of tea trees in mountain foothills, with gorgeous views.

spots.name: Presidential Palace
spots.desc: Along with the Negara Palace and others minor buildings, it forms the Presidential Palace complex. Built in 1796 as a mansion for a Dutch businessman, it became the centre of the Dutch administration during the 19th century, and the official residence of every single president. As of 2014, the Palace doesn’t seem to be open for public.

spots.name: Sangeh Monkey Forest
spots.desc: The macaques here act as guardians of Puri Buki Sari (Bukit Sari Temple). Legend has it that these monkeys are descendents of the army assembled by the monkey king Hanuman and that the forest here is a fragment of Mount Meru that fell to earth. The temple was built in the 17th century. The monkeys here are as bold as elsewhere in Bali so hang on to your belongings. Sangeh combines well with a…

spots.name: Subak Museum
spots.desc: This museum is dedicated to the famed subak system of unmechanised irrigation which has been in use in Bali since 600 CE. It has collections of Balinese traditional agriculture tools and old documents. Domestic and international tourists may be charged different rates.

spots.name: Batur Geopark Museum
spots.desc: Well presented exhibits here include explanations of the pacific ring of fire and Indonesia's position within that, local vulcanology and the history of eruptions of Mount Batur, volcanic rocks collected locally, films and computer animations explaining why volcanoes erupt and a telescope to view the mountain. Definitely worth a visit.

spots.name: Toyo Devasya
spots.desc: Soak in these hot springs right by the lake side in the village of Toya Bungkah. Very relaxing, and a great way to warm up on the frequent chilly days up here.

spots.name: Brahma Vihara Arama
spots.desc: Bali's largest Buddhist monastery is near the village of Dencarik. The monastery is absolutely charming and commands lovely views. Whilst obviously Buddhist with its orange roof, numerous gold Buddhas and stupas recalling those at Borobudur, the carvings and ornamentation are very Balinese. The combination works well and if it were in a location easier to reach, it would receive far more visitors…

spots.name: Coba Baca Public Library
spots.desc: A collection of Indonesian, English and Dutch books. Courses in Indonesian language are offered for tourists and expats. The main activity of the organization is to increase the knowledge level of the local inhabitants. This is done with help of English courses, books and other activities. The NGO was founded in 2009 and the number of members is growing. A visit to the library combines well with…

spots.name: Banjar Hot Springs
spots.desc: This is an enchanting hot springs with stone carved mouths gushing water in a lush garden setting. The waters are naturally a very pleasing temperature and have a high sulphur content. The whole experience here is extremely therapeutic and cleansing. Changing rooms and lockers are provided on site. This is not a straightforward place to get to, and for that reason it is often way less crowded…

spots.name: Morning Dolphin Watching
spots.desc: Enjoy the morning dancing dolphins in their natural habitat accompanied by beautiful sunrise, it's really unforgettable experience lifetimes.

spots.name: Bali Spice Dive
spots.desc: Offers day trips to all of the dive spots on the northern coast of Bali. Guides are available in a variety of languages and multi-day discounts are available. Long-established and the largest dive operator in the area. Has a handy booking office in Jl Bina Ria, Kalibukuk, and the main centre is on the beach at Kaliasem close to the Aditya Beach Resort.

spots.name: Lovina Dive
spots.desc: PADI dive centre with a full range of courses and fun dives to the major dive sites in north Bali.

spots.name: Agung's Spa
spots.desc: Offers body scrubs, facials, and massages. The nicest spa facility in Lovina, though it is much smaller and basic than what you would find elsewhere on the island.

spots.name: Adjani
spots.desc: Small family-run cooking school near the post office on the main road at Kaliasem. Classes include a trip to see the growing of medicinal herbs and a spice garden. In 2-3 hours, students learn five Balinese recipes.
spots.hours: Daily 10:00-13:00, book a day in advance
spots.price: Vegetarian class US$30; non-vegetarian $35; mixed program $40; Balinese cooking $45

spots.name: Barakuda
spots.desc: Popular restaurant specializing in Indonesian seafood. A good value for the set menu.

spots.name: Kakatua
spots.desc: Popular with tourists and not without reason. The menu is varied, the staff friendly and you can see the food being prepared and cooked from fresh ingredients.

spots.name: Kopi Bali
spots.desc: Cheap and cheerful Indonesian food. Extremely popular with budget travelers and a good place to hang out to talk travel.

spots.name: Sea Breeze
spots.desc: Very well known eatery on the beach in Kalibukuk. Been around for many years serving good value meals. Fish is especially recommended.

spots.name: Warung Bambu Pemaron
spots.desc: Balinese and other Indonesian food at excellent value prices. Often has live dance performances and also offer cookery courses.
spots.addr: on the entrance road to the Puri Bagus resort

spots.name: Warung Jegeg
spots.desc: The really nice lady Wayan offers authentic and delicious Balinese/Indonesian cuisine as well as cooking classes. Great value for money!

spots.name: Volcano Club
spots.desc: The only disco in town. A rather bizarre rustic building which resembles a concrete cave.

spots.name: Waru Bali
spots.desc: Cool place to get a beer and watch the sun go down. One of the oldest warungs in Kalibukbuk and still very popular. Stay late and you might enjoy a singalong with some of the locals.

spots.name: ZiGiZ Bar
spots.desc: Acoustic music with 2 guitar players and DJ every night, starts around 20:00. Large cocktail selection. Satellite TV sports broadcasts on 4 screens.

spots.name: The beach
spots.desc: Jimbaran Bay is fringed by one of the best beaches in Bali. The sand is fine and white, and the calm waters make it very suitable for swimming, children and adults alike. The southern end of the beach close to the Four Seasons Resort is the quietest but the whole stretch is very pleasant indeed.

spots.name: Alam Jimbaran Spa
spots.desc: Day spa, traditional Balinese massage, Indian ayurvedic spa, hot stone therapy and hammam herbal therapy.

spots.name: Bamboo Spa, By L'Occitane
spots.desc: 5 single treatment rooms, 9 double treatment suites for couples, a private steam room, a relaxation lounge, reflexology area and the L’Occitane retail boutique. All therapists in Bamboo Spa have received French style training from L'Occitane en Provence.

spots.name: Bliss Massage
spots.desc: Not a spa as such, but a traditional massage parlour. Excellent, traditional Balinese-style therapeutic treatments.
spots.price: Balinese massage is Rp 77,000 at their place or Rp 120,000 if they come to your hotel

spots.name: Henna Spa
spots.desc: 5-star standard spa providing Javanese and Balinese style treatments.

spots.name: Jimbaran Market
spots.desc: Slightly further north of the boutique and antique area is Jimbaran Market. This is a hive of activity every morning as the local community goes about its business and is a notably good place to purchase fresh produce.

spots.name: Jenggala Gallery
spots.desc: Large gallery and retail showroom for Balinese ceramics. Regular exhibitions of paintings and other art by up and coming local artists. Worth a visit, and it's hard to miss the enormous pink limestone clad building. Has an excellent cafe.

spots.name: Jimbaran fish market
spots.desc: A traditional fish market is located at the northern end of the bay right by the beach at the junction with Jalan Tukad Ayung. The catch comes in every morning here and customers include most of Bali's fine dining restaurants. All manner of fish and shellfish are on available. You can get your purchases grilled elsewhere in the market for a fee.

spots.name: Depot Joko
spots.desc: A very popular, a no-frills local restaurant serving all manner of Indonesian food. Recommended if you want a real taste of Indonesia.

spots.name: Jimbaran Beach Club - JBC
spots.desc: Fresh seafood, prepared with a Mediterranean influence and served on the sandy beach. Well stocked bar, good wine list, tropical cocktails, and seasonal fruit juices.

spots.name: The Open House Restaurant
spots.desc: A mix of modern Asian cuisine and Mediterranean dishes (pizzas and pastas) in an agreeable ambience. Bamboo structure and alang-alang roof overlooking a swimming pool. Excellent background music selected by David Mordoh

spots.name: Pepe Nero
spots.desc: An Italian restaurant in an unlikely location with nice views of Jimbaran Bay. Pastas and pizzas.

spots.name: Sate Lilit Pak Lengar
spots.desc: Serves Balinese satay, Sate lilit made from seawater fish which is then mixed with grated coconut, thick coconut milk, lemon juice, shallots, and pepper.

spots.name: Bawang Merah Beachfront Restaurant
spots.desc: Located in the northern section of Jimbaran Bay, this place is set away from the crowded main strip of seafood cafes. It has a natural, secluded appeal and a vast beach.
spots.addr: Jl. Pantai Kelan, Tuban, Kec. Kuta Sel., Kabupaten Badung, Bali 80361

spots.name: Jaansan Beach House
spots.desc: Elegant yet relaxed Beach Restaurant, Bar & Lounge, with a shady terrace, clean sands, pool, scenic views and a vast range of food: Indonesian - Asian - International. Specialised in Peking Duck and Steaks.
spots.addr: Jl. Pantai Kelan, Tuban, Kec. Kuta, Kabupaten Badung, Bali 80361

spots.name: Pizzeria Romana Bali
spots.desc: Owned and Run but an actual Italian it has good, authentic Italian pizza and pasta dished.

spots.name: Sandpiper Bali
spots.desc: Stylish all-day café and restaurant serving breakfast, brunch and international dishes, with excellent coffee, fresh salads, burgers and Indonesian favourites in a relaxed contemporary setting.

spots.name: Mahadeva Art Gallery
spots.desc: Has a collection of interesting paintings. You can also get custom-made paintings here.

spots.name: Quiksilver surf school
spots.desc: Offers lessons lasting 2½ hours for Rp 390,000. They also rent boards for Rp 50,000 per hour, but if you have taken lessons with them, you can get a reduced rate of Rp 20,000 per hour. If renting from locals on the beach, be sure to use this fact to get a good price.

spots.name: Glow Spa At Mandira
spots.desc: A spa treatment based upon the principles of restoring balance, beauty and harmony to mind and body.

spots.name: Calming Spa
spots.desc: A full range of treatments on offer including from basic therapeutic massage, to Javanese 'Lulur' body scrub and "Rempah and Honey" treatment, a traditional massage followed by a body mask of honey, clay, flowers and roots.
spots.price: Massage from Rp 200,000, waxing from Rp 80,000

spots.name: Warung Pan Dira
spots.desc: Local joint, run and owned by a Balinese family. Try their nasi kuning (yellow rice with sides), or soto ayam (chicken soup). They also pay a lot of attention to their cleanliness and health standards.

spots.name: Bali Beach Shack Bar & Restaurant
spots.desc: Live music daily, Indonesian drag cabaret every Th F Sa at 22:15 and 23:15. Good service, Australian and Indonesian food. Despite the name, it is not by the beach.

spots.name: Fresh Warung
spots.desc: Fresh Warung specialises in local & international dishes. It is small but cheerful, clean & serves up well-priced quality food. Emi, the owner, is cheeky and provides great service.

spots.name: Gosha Bar and Restaurant
spots.desc: A huge, cavernous restaurant. The ambience and set up is not great, but the food is very reliable and this is a popular restaurant with Australian visitors especially. Been around since 1985. Broad menu offering seafood, western and Indonesian dishes.

spots.name: Island Cafe
spots.desc: Italian coffee (Segafredo), healthy food choices, Free WiFi and a relaxed environment. Wood fire pizza oven.

spots.name: Lanai
spots.desc: On the site that used to be Benny's Cafe, Lanai serves up big portions and has great views of the beach from the upstairs balcony.

spots.name: Lemongrass Thai Restaurant
spots.desc: Dine-in or takeaway Thai food. Lots of seafood and vegetarian options.

spots.name: Seaside
spots.desc: Open from mid-afternoon. Food is decent, beachside setting very good indeed, and they have great bar. Closest restaurant to Hotel Jayakarta.

spots.name: Tekor Bali
spots.desc: Broad Indonesian menu and all food is beautifully presented. Great for Balinese and Indonesian specialties: try the Bebek Betutu, slow-roasted duck with Balinese spices. Perhaps the best breakfast on the beach in Bali. Midrange prices (entree Rp 50,000-100,000) for upscale food, this is one of Bali's best bargains.

spots.name: Waroeng Asia
spots.desc: Popular Thai restaurant with very affordable prices. Large range of mid-priced meals.

spots.name: Zanzibar
spots.desc: A well-established restaurant with excellent Italian cuisine and especially good pasta dishes. On the Blue Ocean beach, and so a good spot to watch all the action whilst enjoying an excellent meal.

spots.name: 66 Corner Restaurant & Cafe
spots.desc: 66 Corner offers cuisine from all over the globe. Happy hours from 16:00-18:00 with 30% off all beverages and free wifi is available. Covers also all sports games live on big screen TV, such as rugby, football, F1 and many more. Film nights every Tuesday and Thursday.

spots.name: de ja vu
spots.desc: A happening beach-side dance bar. Popular with the pre Double Six crowd from about midnight-03:00. Lightweight clubwear is appropriate and they can get sniffy about singlets and sandals. Check local listings for special events and name DJs.

spots.name: Jaya Pub
spots.desc: This live music bar has been around forever and gives a distinct impression of being stuck in a timewarp. Still, the bands are fun and beer is cheap.

spots.name: Monsoon
spots.desc: Opening in the afternoon and closing at 01:00. Offers entertainment with a large collection of retro music videos from 1964-2000. A good variety of Tapas and drinks at reasonable prices. Selected smoking areas.

spots.name: Pura Geger Temple
spots.desc: Classic Balinese temple surrounded by twisty, gnarled tree trunks.

spots.name: Bali Beach Country Golf Club
spots.desc: One of three top notch golf courses in Bali, and perhaps the most popular of them all due to its convenient location. Any hotel will be able to arrange a round for you - ask about packages on offer as these can save you a lot of money. Booking a tee time is very important on this very busy course.

spots.name: Thalasso Bali Spa
spots.desc: In front of the beach, it offers wide range of Thalasso and spa treatments.

spots.name: Bali Water Sport
spots.desc: Water sport beach activities such as parasailing, jet skiing, banana boat, snorkeling, intro diving, wake boarding, glass bottom boats to Turtle Island, donut rides, fly fishing, trolling fishing, fly boarding and sea walker.
spots.addr: Jalan SMKI, Gang Ulunsuwi No 8 Batubulan, Sukawati

spots.name: Bali Collection
spots.desc: An open air shopping area with many clothes and swimwear shops, souvenirs shops. At the center is COCO Supermarket, with a wide range of local and foreign food and drinks, including fruits and alcohol.

spots.name: Bumbu Bali
spots.desc: Bali’s first authentic Balinese five star restaurant, with food prepared and served it in a traditional manner. There are now two Bumbu Bali restaurants, named Bumbu Bali One and Bumbu Bali Two respectively, about 500 metres from each other. The menu of Two is similar to One with the addition of meat and prawn skewers.

spots.name: Nusa Dua Beach Grill
spots.desc: A great long-established dining option on a dreamy white sand beach. One of the few quality options to dine outside of hotels in the Nusa Dua area.

spots.name: Jaansan Bali Restaurant
spots.desc: Balinese owner-managed restaurant offering a vast range of meals: local food such as Ayam Betutu, Bebek Goreng, first-grade seafood, vegetarian dishes, Bali duck, chicken and beef. All pork-free. Daily open for lunch and dinner in a relaxed yet elegant ambience.
spots.addr: Jl By Pass Ngurah Rai Mumbul, No. 96-B, Nusa Dua

spots.name: Mangrove Information Centre
spots.desc: Visit the well-appointed Mangrove Information Centre set in the huge 600-hectare mangrove forest which fringes the east coast south of Sanur. There are two different boardwalks through the mangrove forest. This centre is doing great work in educating local schoolchildren as well as visitors, about the importance of mangrove forests. A good place to spend half a day for adults and children.
spots.price: Rp 200,000 for foreigners, Rp 50,000 for locals
spots.addr: Jalan By Pass Ngurah Rai Km. 21, Suwung Kauh

spots.name: Serangan Island Turtle Conservation Centre
spots.desc: Visit the Turtle Conservation and Education Centre and learn about current conservation initiatives. This island used to be the centre of the Balinese trade in turtle meat until the practice was banned.

spots.name: Blue Oasis Beach Club
spots.desc: A specialist water sports centre which offers sea-kayaking, kitesurfing, parasailing, wakeboarding, waterskiing and windsurfing, as well as being a dive school.

spots.name: Bali Kite Surfing School
spots.desc: IKO certified kite surfing school. The lessons are conducted in a safe, user-friendly environment and lessons can be structured to suit individual needs. The school uses three specially designed rescue boats to keep a close eye on you.

spots.name: International Kite Festival
spots.desc: The annual international kite festival takes place here every July. Traditional Balinese giant kites up to 10 m in length are made and flown competitively by teams from different villages around Bali. The origins of this event are as a festival intended to send a message to the Hindu Gods to create abundant crops and harvests. Aside from the organised festival, from June to August each year…

spots.name: Artasedana
spots.desc: Formerly Hardy’s. This was Sanur's main supermarket before Grand Lucky and a good centrally located place for stocking up on regular items.

spots.name: Gudang Keramik
spots.desc: This is the outlet for seconds of the famed Jengala Ceramics company (main showroom in Jimbaran). Their standards are very high and you may not notice why some of these items are classed as seconds. Some superb bargains to be had in everything from decorative vases to flatware.

spots.name: Nogo Bali Ikat Centre
spots.desc: Specialises in the quality woven ikat fabrics from Bali and elsewhere in Indonesia. If you are looking for cheapies, don't go here. You can purchase fabric by the piece, made up as clothing or homewares, and examine their impressive genuine antique collection.

spots.name: Abian Boga Restaurant
