spots.desc: Grilled seafood accompanied by a Balinese dance performance. Great service too with a local hotel pick up and drop off.

spots.name: Cafe Batu Jimbar
spots.desc: Every Sanur expat's favourite cafe hang out. Good deli food and passable coffee.

spots.name: Kayu Manis
spots.desc: Western and Asian fusion cuisine at great value prices. A favourite with both travellers for the price and foodies for the quality of the meals.

spots.name: Massimo
spots.desc: The superb home made gelato here is the ideal treat after a hot day wandering in Sanur. Also excellent pizzas and pastas at this authentic south Italian-owned and -run restaurant.

spots.name: Smorgås Café
spots.desc: Perhaps the best coffee shop in Sanur. Homemade sandwiches, pastry and quiche. Owned by Swedes and they make their own gravlax.

spots.name: Stiff Chilli
spots.desc: Beach-front restaurant from the Stiff Chilli chain. Mid-priced, mainly Italian food in a great location.

spots.name: The Village
spots.desc: Attached to the Griya Santrian Hotel, this is perhaps the best known upmarket eatery in Sanur. The food is slick Italian style and they do a reasonable job of creating a suitable atmosphere. Not a good as it was and certainly not cheap, but a decent option in a part of Bali not known for it high quality restaurants. Has an independent street front entrance, and you would not know it is attached…

spots.name: Warung Blanjong
spots.desc: One of the best places to eat Balinese in Sanur. They are especially well known for their pepes be pashi (steamed fish wrapped in banana leaves), and the be siap betutu (chicken prepared similarly) is also good. Very much worth a visit.

spots.name: Fortune Cookie
spots.desc: Healthy western-style Chinese Restaurant, no MSG, organic ingredients, they also have free delivery in Sanur. Popular with expats.

spots.name: Salt and Malt
spots.desc: British-style fish and chips made by the wife of a Londoner. Optional mushy peas.

spots.name: McDonald's
spots.desc: Sanur has a long running McD's that can be a useful landmark due to its main road junction location.

spots.name: Selada Bali Restaurant
spots.desc: Serving modern Asian cuisine with distinct European influences.

spots.name: Arena Pub & Restaurant
spots.desc: Austrian owned and run sports bar and cafe. The beer is very cold, reasonably priced and this place is always busy.

spots.name: Sanur Internet Service
spots.desc: A comfortable and speedy internet cafe. Air-con, 2 seater sofa and equipped with 17-inch LCD monitors, head sets, scanner & printer. Free mineral water and helpful staff.

spots.name: Pura Petitenget
spots.desc: This is a compact, pretty Balinese temple, which is known for particularly spectacular beach-side ceremonies. There has been a temple here since at least the 16th century, and although this is not one of the key nine directional temples of Bali, it is an important link in the series of west coast temples between Pura Uluwatu and Pura Tanah Lot.

spots.name: Nautilus Diving Bali
spots.desc: PADI dive center. Courses, trips and safaris around the island. Languages: English, German, Spanish, French and Bahasa.

spots.name: Amo Beauty & Spa
spots.desc: A spa run by former model Navia Nguyen that offers massages and various spa treatments.

spots.name: Amoaras Spa
spots.desc: Traditional Balinese massage and treatments in a well established spa.

spots.name: Coco Grande - male spa
spots.desc: Male spa offering wide range of treatments and quality services. Staff is male only. Also outcall service.

spots.name: Glo
spots.desc: A self-styled hip spa offering many different treatments. Positions itself to appeal to younger clientele than many of Bali's spa establishments.

spots.name: Jari Menari
spots.desc: Superb massage centre in Seminyak. The team who set up Jari Menari consult worldwide for other spas and massage houses. Also offer massage training classes.

spots.name: Spa Venus Bali
spots.desc: Simple Balinese traditional massage to a complete detox programme including colonic cleansing and fasting, infra red sauna, deep healing treatments, allergy elimination, herbal medicine.
spots.addr: Jl Raya Seminyak, Gg Plawa No33F

spots.name: Lagoon Spa
spots.desc: Lagoon Spa offers a wide arrange of indulging body and beauty treatments. With relaxing environment, a Romanesque jacuzzi, sauna, rain shower and public pool. The treatments are drawn on the ancient health and beauty traditions of Asia.

spots.name: Bamboo Blonde
spots.desc: Innovative women's wear and notably helpful and friendly staff.

spots.name: Biasa
spots.desc: This is the flagsghip store of the Bali fashion brand. Lightweight womenswear using natural fabrics.

spots.name: Bong's
spots.desc: This second line store owned by an Indonesian haute couture designer. High end fashion clothing made out of silk, linen and cotton.

spots.name: Body and Soul
spots.desc: Women's sportswear, beachwear and swimwear. Flagship store is on Jl Raya Seminyak and they also have an outlet in Seminyak Square.

spots.name: Indigo & Rose
spots.desc: Sister label of Indigo Kids. Stylish women's clothes, accessories, sandals, jewellery and children's wear. The flagship store is on Jl Oberoi next to Seminyak Square and there is a second store on Jl Seminyak.
spots.addr: Jl Seminyak (50 m from Bintang Supermarket) and Jl Oberoi, opposite Seminyak Square

spots.name: Mario Silver
spots.desc: The retail outlet of one of Bali's leading silver jewellery designers and manufacturers. Wide range of high quality items.

spots.name: Religion
spots.desc: A well established fashion boutique. Funky, eclectic and popular with a young clientele.

spots.name: Sabbatha
spots.desc: If bling is your thing, you will like it here. Those of a more tasteful disposition might not. Glitzy, kitschy bags and other accessories.

spots.name: Shaman
spots.desc: A funky store which is an outlet for the Shaman Electro brand. Young streetwear.

spots.name: we'ar concept store
spots.desc: A very nice and colourful store which is the concept store for the we'ar brand. Great yoga wear and street wear.

spots.name: Folk Art Gallery
spots.desc: A great collection of art from all over South East Asia with an emphasis on Burma. fabulous collection of Burmese Buddhas but also beads, textiles, jewellery. Prices are from a few dollars up to US$10,000 (for an almost life-sized Marble Buddha). Caters to collectors or for gifts to take home.
spots.addr: Jl Laksmana 17, Also known as Jl Oberio

spots.name: Lukisan traditional & modern paintings
spots.desc: Stocks traditional Balinese, Buddhist, abstract, modern and pop art paintings. It is all a bit production line, but this is a gallery with very reasonable prices.

spots.name: Richard Meyer Culture
spots.desc: An elegant gallery showcasing art, photography and sculpture from contemporary Balinese artists.

spots.name: Bintang Supermarket
spots.desc: This is the grand old aunt of supermarkets in Bali. It is a bit faded and old-fashioned looking these days but remains popular, and is a very convenient one stop for those visitors looking for the supermarket-type items that they would find at home. Also has a hardware section upstairs.

spots.name: Seminyak Square
spots.desc: Chic and modern shopping complex housing designer stores, restaurants and an excellent Periplus bookshop. Most unusually for Seminyak, there is a lot of public parking available here.

spots.name: Baku Dapa
spots.desc: This great value warung is something of a legend in Seminyak. Stays open very late and is popular with the partying crowd. Serves Manado style Indonesian food at very keen prices. Highly recommended as a real taste of Indonesia.

spots.name: Café Tahu
spots.desc: Popular with locals, this restaurant has raised seating around a central courtyard and offers up a menu of tofu, tofu and more tofu, cooked Indonesian style for about Rp 10,000 per dish. The tofu is all made on premises and you can even buy a pack to take home. Concessions to meat-eaters include satay and grilled chicken.

spots.name: Kolega
spots.desc: This simple, unassuming Javanese warung is an absolute institution amongst locals and expats alike. When it first gained the attention of travel guides there was a collective groan, but it has remained remarkably free from attention of the tourist hoardes. Choose your rice (options of plain, yellow and sometimes red) and the dishes to go with it. The various beef, chicken and fish dishes are…
spots.hours: About 11:00-15:00, sometimes open in the early evening also

spots.name: Little Green Cafe
spots.desc: 100% vegetarian and uses almost exclusively organic ingredients, most of them locally sourced. Excellent homemade cakes, cookies, fruit bars and fresh juices, as well as salads, soups, veggie burgers and daily specials. A little off the beaten path, but well worth the effort to get there.

spots.name: Mano Beach Side Café
spots.desc: True to the name, this is a simple but stylish blue building by the beach, offering all sorts of drinks for around Rp 10,000 as well as sandwiches and pasta for around Rp 30,000 — not to mention cool breezes and great sunsets.

spots.name: Warung Batavia
spots.desc: After years on Jl Kerobokan this long-established warung which serves excellent Javanese food has opened at a location with better parking. Always busy, but lunchtimes especially. Choose your food at the counter and sit at the sociable, shared tables. Spend Rp 25,000 for a fantastic quality meal.

spots.name: Warung Sobat
spots.desc: Good value and popular Indonesian restaurant. Main dishes about Rp 20,000 to 30,000.

spots.name: Biku
spots.desc: Exactly what it says on the label, "a tea lounge, restaurant, antiques and bookstore". Quirky place with a lovely atmosphere. Great range of homemade desserts, salads and sandwiches, amongst more formal fare. The traditional English tea, complete with scones and cream, is a real hit. When you have finished eating have a browse through the antique gallery and the branch of Ubud's famous Ganesha…

spots.name: Cafe Jemme
spots.desc: Discrete, charming little restaurant set away from the road behind the Jemme jewellery shop. Serves creative food with Asian accents at very reasonable prices for the area. The crispy duck is especially recommended, and leave space for a superb line in desserts.

spots.name: Cafe Seminyak
spots.desc: Established in 2000, this is where the local community meets. All day long, this very busy cafe serves breakfasts with French croissants, baguettes and a big English breakfast with beans and sausage. The only downside here is that it is an outdoor cafe right beside a very busy and noisy road.

spots.name: Gourmet Cafe
spots.desc: This is the cafe outlet of Bali's most gourmet catering company. Superb salads, pastries, home baked breads, all day breakfasts, Italian coffee, and a quite remarkable range of teas. Also have great line in high quality frozen and fresh ready meals, both here and in their nearby shop. This is very handy if you are staying in one of Seminyak's private villas. Indoor seating area which is…

spots.name: Junction Cafe
spots.desc: Excellent cafe serving the best baguettes imaginable and salads at lunchtime, and specialising in pasta in the evening. Free WiFi. Belgian owned and operates.

spots.name: Le Tebu
spots.desc: The French-owned Le Tebu offers diners salads, sandwiches and a few token Indonesian items. Dishes start from Rp 30,000.

spots.name: Made's Warung
spots.desc: A Seminyak institution that was established (in a different location) in 1969. Wonderful Indonesian food in a great location in a courtyard off of the main road in Seminyak. The western food is OK but nothing special; stay with the Indonesian dishes. Certainly not over-priced by Seminyak standards.

spots.name: Queen's Tandoor
spots.desc: The best Indian restaurant in Bali by a country mile. Consistently wins awards and it is easy to understand why. Superb tandoori chicken and fish, and huge, authentic biryanis. Vegan options available. Also has a delivery service.

spots.name: Rumours
spots.desc: Incredibly popular restaurant serving great value western food. You cannot book here and there is often a long queue for tables.

spots.name: Sate Bali
spots.desc: Low-key but tastefully done open-air restaurant with well presented Balinese favorites like sate lilit (spiced meat on lemon grass sticks), plenty of pork dishes and fresh fish.

spots.name: Ultimo
spots.desc: Italian food is the go at this popular Laksmana restaurant. Good pastas and steak and carpaccio are the highlights. Same ownership as Rumours, just a few doors up the street.

spots.name: Waroeng Bonita
spots.desc: A vast selection of western and Indonesian dishes, served in a garden courtyard. Prices start from Rp 50,000.

spots.name: La Lucciola
spots.desc: Right on Petitenget beach, serves breakfast, brunch, lunch and dinner. Home of the Frangipani Bar, a popular choice for watching the sunset.

spots.name: Metis
spots.desc: After 10 years as Bali's top French restaurant the former Warisan closed and the management team from there have opened Metis, has ample parking.

spots.name: Sardine
spots.desc: Specialises in fish and other seafood prepared with a Mediterranean ethic. Intimate restaurant with an all bamboo design and clear views over the rice paddies.

spots.name: Sarong Restaurant
spots.desc: Original takes on Asian street and country food in a chic 5 star setting.

spots.name: Hu'u
spots.desc: Part of the Singaporean nightspot chain. The star attraction is the lit central swimming pool, where the bold and the beautiful can jump in. The rest of the complex is chilled-out drinking and dining in the garden and pavilion. Draught beer at Rp 20,000 a glass, with cocktails around Rp 115,000.

spots.name: Ku De Ta
spots.desc: Stylish bar-restaurant complex with 2 bars, restaurant seating indoors and beachside divans to laze on while the DJ spins an eclectic mix of music, new and old. Soft drinks from Rp 20,000, cocktails from Rp 70,000, including bizarre selections such as black pepper and grilled pineapple Martini. Gets packed at weekends.

spots.name: Lita Gunardi & The Backyard Lounge
spots.desc: A lounge bar and restaurant attached to the Lita Gunardi boutique. The bar serves good cocktails and the restaurant specialises in Italian food.

spots.name: Red Carpet Champagne Bar
spots.desc: A fairly ritzy bar, unsurprisingly, specialising in Champagne. Not as expensive as you might imagine, but by no means a place for a cheap drink.

spots.name: Potato Head
spots.desc: Great beach club to mingle through the day and do people watching. Day beds are to be seen and require reservation. Food and drinks are nice. Especially popular for sunset

spots.name: Motel Mexicola
spots.desc: Mexican bar and restaurant that is popular for the Mexican dishes and the colourful design. Popular for drinks in the evening and the small dishes.
spots.addr: Jl Kayu Jati No 9, Petingenget Beach

spots.name: Izzi Rooftop
spots.desc: Fifth-floor rooftop lounge and restaurant with west-facing ocean and sunset views. Shisha, cocktails and a kitchen serving international, Asian and Eastern European dishes (borscht, dumplings, stroganoff) until late.
spots.addr: Jl. Batu Belig No.38, Floor 5, Kerobokan Kelod

spots.name: Dream Beach
spots.desc: A small, white sand beach, located on the south coast. The roads from Lembongan village to the beach are signposted. There are a few resorts bordering the beach, the rest of the beach is surrounded by cliffs so walking through the resorts is the only way to get to the beach. Be very careful though about entering the water here as the rips can be fierce. Only the strongest swimmers should consider…

spots.name: Sandy Bay
spots.desc: A small but spectacular beach with white sand and crashing waves, located just to the north of Dream Beach, and easiest reached via the same route. The excellent Beach Club at Sandy Bay is located here and this should encourage visitors to spend the day. At low tide a dramatic cave is exposed in the low limestone cliff at the eastern side of the bay. You can explore it but make sure you are not…

spots.name: Marine Megafauna Foundation
spots.desc: A marine research centre set up to monitor the manta ray and mola mola populations around Nusa Penida. MMF works with the Lembongan dive shops to gather information about these magnificent creatures and their critical habitats that will eventually be used to help protect them. MMF lectures are given on Tu and Th at 18:30 the Yoga Shack. You will get an in depth look at the exciting marine life…

spots.name: Devil's Tear
spots.desc: A rocky outcrop on the south western coast. Spectacular crashing waves and water plumes at times. Ticket booth is not in use as of mid-2026. There are barrier ropes but do not venture past them: many tourists have fallen to their deaths here.

spots.name: Mangrove Forest
spots.desc: Northern Nusa Lembongan has an extensive forest of mature mangroves which can be explored in a jukung outrigger boat. Also great for families at high tide as perfect lagoon for kids swimming.

spots.name: Puncak Sari Temple
spots.desc: The largest and grandest Hindu temple on the island. Good views over the straits back to Bali from this area.

spots.name: Seaweed Farms
spots.desc: Seaweed farming takes place in many parts of the island, but the most accessible farms are on the southern side of Lembongan Village. Most of the seaweed grown here is destined for the Asian cosmetics industry.

spots.name: Panorama Point
spots.desc: This is a small clearing on Bukit Jungut Batu with nice views over Jungut Batu. It is on the main road headed south out of Jungut Batu so you won't even need to seek it out. You will find yourself here while exploring the island.

spots.name: Yellow Bridge
spots.desc: This quirky yellow suspension bridge was built in 2017 after the previous bridge, made of wood, collapsed during a religious procession in 2016, killing at least eight people. You can walk or bike across the bridge to neighbouring Nusa Ceningan. The noise it makes can be quite scary, and contributes to what is an all-round Indiana Jones-type experience, but the bridge is safe. There are very rare…

spots.name: Blue Lagoon Nusa Ceningan
spots.desc: Front entrance through Klyf club/hotel, open to public, no entrance fee, drones forbidden. Right side entrance via small dirt path after the club and secret point huts, but before their parking. Small sign "Blue Lagoon Ceningan". Left side with hotel in construction. Similar to Devil's Tear but less tourists and free. Be careful on rocky path and stay away from the edge - there are no barriers!

spots.name: Yoga Shack Lembongan
spots.desc: Hatha, Vinyasa and Yin drop in classes. No booking required. All levels of experience. Multi-class discount cards available.

spots.name: Yoga Dunia Lembongan
spots.desc: have juice shop too. no booking needed for daily one-hour practices at 8:30 or 17:00. various yoga types per schedule. see website or shop.
spots.price: one session Rp 120,000, pack3 Rp 320,000, pack5 Rp 540,000, monthly pack up to 30 classes 2,160,000, juices Rp 30,000…
spots.addr: Tamarind Road, Jungutbatu, Kec. Nusa Penida, Nusa Lembongan, Bali 80771

spots.name: Monkey Surfing
spots.desc: The first surf school to open on Nusa Lembongan. Certified instructors and lifeguards. They teach in small group for beginners as well as intermediate guiding and also private lessons. Lessons include all the gears and boat to the surf spot. Surf boards and SUP for hire. Surf lessons are available in English and French

spots.name: Newbro Surfing School
spots.desc: Friendly surf school that provides the whole package: surfboards, boat, photography and instructors that have been surfing for over 20 years. Professional staff speak English and provide great lessons ranging from beginner level to advanced. Lessons to small groups or one on one.

spots.name: Bali Diving Academy
spots.desc: A PADI 5* resort established in 1991, offering a full range of PADI courses in multiple languages, including English, French, German, Italian and Indonesian. Up to 4 departures per day to the region's best dive sites, keeps the group sizes small and all dives are guided by experienced PADI professionals. Night dives are also available. Divemaster/diver ratio 1:4.

spots.name: Big Fish Diving
spots.desc: A PADI 5* dive resort based at the Secret Garden Bungalows offering daily diving, scuba diving courses in multiple languages and manta/mola specials. Also, daily yoga classes (Vinyasa Flow, Hatha Flow and Yin Yang classes to suit all levels of experience, 08:00 and 16:00, drop-in classes) at the Yoga Shack and home to MMF, Lembongan's dedicated marine research center.

spots.name: Blue Corner Dive
spots.desc: Beach-front PADI eco-resort (PADI 5-Star IDC Resort #22557), owned by a marine biologist. Specialises in guiding small dive groups around the Nusa Penida Marine Protected Area. Naturalist and scientific diving courses. They also conduct ongoing coral reef monitoring at several sites around Nusa Penida and Lembongan. Beginner to professional dive training.

spots.name: Indo Divers Lembongan
spots.desc: Small PADI dive school in Mushroom Bay offering a range of courses in English, German, Dutch and French. All dives guided by experienced PADI dive professionals. Small groups.

spots.name: French Kiss Divers
spots.desc: SSI Dive Center, and only SSI Instructor Training Center of Nusa Lembongan. French Kiss Divers opened in September 2017, on jungut batu with Puri Nusa resort, and has also a booking office on the main road. The team is international and teach mainly in English, French, German and Spanish. They have their own swimming pool and boat.

spots.name: Legend Diving Lembongan
spots.desc: PADI Dive Center S-25289 offering daily diving trips to Nusa Lembongan and Nusa Penida marine protected area. Personalized service with small diving groups adapted for Manta rays and Mola Mola dives. Full range of PADI courses in various languages from beginner to professional divemaster internships. Snorkeling and private tours available. Transportation to/from Bali mainland or Gili Islands can…

spots.name: Lembongan Dive Adventures
spots.desc: A locally-owned dive resort catering to small groups, PADI courses from open water through to divemaster in several languages, taught by international instructors, using the resort training pool.

spots.name: Lembongan Dive Center
spots.desc: Locally-owned PADI dive resort #S-22362 with local guides experienced in diving the waters around Nusa Penida and Nusa Lembongan. Small groups preferred. Individual service with a range of PADI courses from Discover Scuba Diving to Divemaster. Snorkelling trips and transport can also be arranged to and from Bali and the Gili Islands.

spots.name: Planet Nomadas
spots.desc: Besides diving, this company also has a surfing school, yoga classes, snorkeling and land tours. The resort has all in one facilities such as restaurant, pool and bungalows. Courses and guiding given in several languages.

spots.name: World Diving
spots.desc: The island's first full PADI 5 Star dive centre. All courses are offered from Discover Scuba through to Assistant Instructor.

spots.name: Lembongan watersport
spots.desc: Located end of the Mangrove beach, this place offers snorkelling day trips, scuba diving, stand-up paddling and kayak trips.

spots.name: Ocean Dreams
spots.desc: Boat Captain Diasa is locally famous for his snorkelling trips. PADI dive master, he is very good guide and takes pride in his safety and environmental awareness. He swims with his clients, especially beneficial when trying to spot manta rays. Based in Jungutbatu at D&B Warung and Bungalows.

spots.name: Aquaman Snorkeling Trip
spots.desc: Friendly crew, good boat, earlier departure than most it seems around 8:15 (pickup before), back around 12:00.
spots.price: Half-day snorkeling Rp 300,000 (3 spots, including mask, fins, water, snack, towel, underwater photos, up to 20p and…

spots.name: One Breath
spots.desc: AIDA freediving courses for beginners and advanced. Surfers will grow in confidence and handle wipeouts in big waves while divers will be pleased to reduce their air consumption and try a different approach.

spots.name: Lembongan Fun Activities
spots.desc: Activities in lembongan fun Activities, tour and snorkeling.
spots.addr: Jl. Mangrove, Jungutbatu, Kec. Nusa Penida, Kabupaten Klungkung, Bali 80771

spots.name: Lulur Spa
spots.desc: Complete spa with rooms for facials, massages, pedicure, manicure and hair treatments. Local products are used as well as some imported from Australia. Each room is set with ambient music and A/C. Changing rooms with clean treated hot water and a relaxation room are provided.

spots.name: Mushroom Spa
spots.desc: Relaxing massage, body scrub, pedicure or manicure overlooking the clear waters of Sanghyang Bay.

spots.name: Warung 99 Meals House
spots.desc: Tasty local style warung with all the usual Indonesian favourites. Cheap and cheery. The owner might sit and have a chat with you.

spots.name: Green Garden Warung Coffee Juice and Food
spots.desc: Offers cheap and tasty Indonesian and Western food. The owner Dodi is extremely kind and some of the menu items are grown in his garden. The Warung is around 75 m off the main road (about half way down and turn to the right) but there is a large sign and getting there is pretty easy if you pay attention. Nice ambiance. Free wifi.

spots.name: The Beach Club at Sandy Bay
spots.desc: A large open bar and restaurant area with a beach-front pool abutting a white sandy beach. Daily BBQ with seafood and steaks, extensive range of cocktails, the beer is very cold and they have a wine cellar. Breakfast, lunch and dinner. The quality of food here is extremely high for Nusa Lembongan and would not be out of place in top restaurants in mainland Bali. Free WiFi.

spots.name: The Bar at Mushroom beach
spots.desc: Mexican traditional dishes such as quesadillas and nachos to fajitas with a range of lovely fillings. Cocktails such as mojitos and fresh or frozen margaritas.

spots.name: B'Fresh Juicebar & Coffee Corner
spots.desc: Breakfast foods and snacks during the day. All you can eat buffets and enjoy traditional Indonesian foods with some western favorites. Everything is made fresh on site and sourced locally in Indonesia.

spots.name: Ketut Warung
spots.desc: Great atmosphere, huge plates, good Indonesian and Thai food at really cheap prices. The owners, the Ketut Malom family, are friendly hosts.

spots.name: Maria's Boemboe Bali Warung
spots.desc: Fresh, delicious local food, fish and seafood; also has western dishes like pasta, burgers and pizza. Possibly the best value eatery on the island. Best time to go is probably around sunset until closing. Try the rosella tea, calamary fritty, tuna bamboe bali combo Rp40k, small Bintang beer Rp22.
spots.addr: At the north end of the island, on the beach, close to the mainroad

spots.name: Mangrove Restaurant
spots.desc: At the eastern end of the only spit of land that runs through the northern mangrove forest. From Jungut Batu, take the beach road north and turn into the mangroves (possible by motorcycle or of course on foot). Just keep going for about 1½ km and you will find the restaurant. Alternatively, arrive by boat - any boat captain will know the way. Indonesian meals and some European options.

spots.name: Nyoman's Warung
spots.desc: Nyoman's Warung is on the north beach of the island with sweeping views of Mount Agung. The traditional Lembongan menu changes daily to reflect the catch of the day.

spots.name: Pisang-Pisang
spots.desc: A very chill hang out place. Delicious smoothies, fresh juices, and healthy meals all day. Friendly staff, fast service. Free Wi-Fi.

spots.name: Nano Nano restaurant
spots.desc: Nicely located almost at the end of the mangrove road. This place is located directly opposite the best sporkelling spot on the island, which is accessible for only about an hour before and after high tide. Otherwise you will be walking on coral. If you want to snorkel, then it's probably best to book a half day snorkeling trip visiting 3 or 4 of the best snorkelling spots in the area and perhaps…

spots.name: The Deck cafe and bar
spots.desc: Located along the boardwalk waterfront with lovely views. They serve gourmet baguettes, paninis, freshly baked pies, pizzas, home baked cakes, gelato ice cream, fresh juices, smoothies and real coffee.

spots.name: Ohana's beach lounge & boutique resort
spots.desc: Ohana's is on the beach in the front of Shipwrecks surf break in Jungut Batu. It features sun lounges, day-beds, bean bags and offers casual dining. There is a swimming pool for guests. Bookings are strongly recommended for day beds or dining.
spots.addr: On the beachfront in Jungut Batu

spots.name: Warung Sate Madura Lembongan
spots.desc: Nice food stall with probably among the cheapest prices with soto ayam or bakso at Rp 15,000 (without side-rice). Very good satay.
spots.price: Chicken satay Rp 25,000, Goat satay Rp 35,000, other dishes Rp 15,000-35,000, drinks Rp 8,000-20,000, desserts Rp…

spots.name: Bali Eco Deli
spots.desc: A cozy place on the main road, behind the busy Jungut Batu beach. Real espresso coffee, slow juiced fruits and twice daily baked treats such as cookies, muffins, brownies and Belgian waffles. Open from early morning to mid-afternoon. Eat-in & take-away. Everything is home made using ingredients sourced from organic and fair-trade farms across Indonesia. Free water refills & free Wi-Fi. Bring in…

spots.name: Blue Corner Bar
spots.desc: Bar and restaurant located on the beachfront by Blue Corner Dive Resort. Bean-bag chairs with umbrellas on the beach, WiFi, and free use of swimming pool. Sunset beach volleyball every day, Wednesday night pub trivia quiz. On Friday nights expats, the dive community and tourists party here with a beach fire and drinks until very late.
spots.addr: On the beach north of Jungut Batu

spots.name: Scooby Doo Beach Bar
spots.desc: Beachside bar which is especially popular with the Australian surfing crowd. Expect cold beers, lots of chat about waves and sport on the television.

spots.name: WBM Coffee Shop and Grill Ribs
spots.desc: They have all homemade recipes and fresh ingredients. They make great coffee, freshly brewed every day. They have many combinations of espresso served hot or cold. Their specialty food is American style pork ribs.

spots.name: Sirawe Waterfall
spots.desc: Besides the waterfall, there is also a hot pool for bathing.

spots.name: Festival Serayu
spots.desc: A lot of activities including Parak Iwak, the procession of releasing tens of thousands of kilos of fish of several types later become a catch attack by residents who have stayed in the Serayu River. They use various ways to catch these fish, some use nets or nets like fishermen, while others use perfunctory tools such as the shirts they wear (of course for men).

spots.name: Pengilon & Warna Lakes
spots.desc: Twin lakes, one green, and the other emerald, offer great scenery at sunrise. Best seen from the .

spots.name: Bu Djono Losmen & Restaurant
spots.desc: A cheap restaurant with friendly staff. Doubles as a guest house and provides excellent advice about the sightseeing in the area. It’s also possible to book tours and rent vehicles.

spots.name: Temu Jumpa Coffe & Resto
spots.desc: Clean and spacious space with various menu. Some of staff can speak English and will be happy to give you any suggestion on how to enjoy dieng at any season.

spots.name: Sentul Garden
spots.desc: A traffic themed park suitable for kids and family's vacation

spots.name: Goentoer Darjono Sport Complex
spots.desc: This is the largest sport complex in town. Contains a football stadium, courts, park, food stalls, and a few other venues. Usually locals visit in the morning, especially on Sunday for jogging.

spots.name: Snorkelling day tour
spots.desc: Typical tour includes one snorkel (near Pulau Menjangan Kecil, 1 hr), one island stop for lunch and leasure (Pulau Cemara Besar, Rp 5,000), another snorkel (sea but nearest Pulau Cemara Kecil, 1 hr) and another island stop (Pulau Cemara Kecil) from 09:00 to 17:00. Staff usually has a waterproof camera and will share photos after, usually through hotel. Group up to 12 persons. May try to get your…
spots.price: Snorkelling day tour Rp 200,000-250,000 including equipment and lunch but excluding one island entrance Rp 5,000

spots.name: Kemujan Island
spots.desc: Shipwreck diving. The cooperation coal ship between Indonesia and Norway sank in the water of Kemujan in 1960.

spots.name: Alun-alun Karimunjawa
spots.desc: In the alun-alun (town public park), there are a lot of seafood stalls. They serve grilled fish and the local dish tongseng cumi.

spots.name: Posong
spots.desc: This is a viewpoint on the southern slopes of Mount Sumbing, facing south. In clear weather, it should be possible to see across a good swathe of Central Java - Mount Slamet in the west, past Mount Sumbing, the twin peaks of Merapi and Merbabu to the southeast, and Ungaran to the northeast. If lucky, maybe across to Mount Lawu on the border with East Java. Getting up early to be there for the…
spots.addr: Jl Parakan-Wonosobo Km 09, Tlahab village, Kledung district,

spots.name: Pringapus Temple
spots.desc: This temple was built with andesite stone material and is estimated to have been built in 850 AD.

spots.name: Situs Liyangan
spots.desc: A residential area that includes the remains of buildings (temples, houses), roads, rice fields, as well as various artifacts located in Liyangan hamlet.

spots.name: Jumprit Forest Park
spots.desc: Flying fox, archery, and forest trekking. Also you may visit umbul jumprit, a historical natural spring.

spots.name: Umbul Songo Waterfall
spots.desc: A seasonal waterfall which is completely dried up during the dry season! Umbul Songo literally means "nine fountains". There's also a public waterpark.

spots.name: Taman Wisata Kopeng
spots.desc: Swimming (if you can stand the freezing cold pool water). The playground is quite good for children to have fun.
spots.addr: Jl. Magelang - Salatiga No.KM. 15, Dukuh, Kopeng, Getasan

spots.name: Kopeng Treetop Adventure Park
spots.desc: This park is in the middle of 7 hectares of pine forest. It has outbond activities, Zipcoaster (a fusion between flying fox and roller coaster, which passes through an iron track along 500 meters), camping grounds, and Treetop Sky Resto, a tree house restaurant.
spots.price: Admission Rp50,000 (weekday), Rp60,000 (weekend), for attractions see web page

spots.name: Pasar Kopeng
spots.desc: Fresh vegetables, fruits and flowers. Also, you can find some food and drink for hiking to Mount Merbabu peak.
spots.addr: Jl. Magelang - Salatiga, Plalar, Kopeng, Getasan, Semarang Regency

spots.name: Pasar Selo
spots.desc: Fresh vegetables and fruits. Also, you can find some food and drink for hiking to Mount Merbabu peak.
spots.addr: Jl. Ampel Cepogo, Dusun I, Samiran, Selo, Boyolali Regency

spots.name: Cerita Kita Cafe and Eatery
spots.desc: Has views of the surrounding mountains. This cafe is very instagramable with a garden and a pool.

spots.name: Merbabu View & Cafe
spots.desc: Hilltop observation deck with mountain views cafe and sunset photo opportunities. It serves Indonesian food and coffee.

spots.name: Lontong Lemprak Mbak Moer
spots.desc: Lontong lemprak is a Batang dish of lontong (rice cake) with boiled tofu, village chicken, and coconut milk.

spots.name: Rujak & Pecel Yongki
spots.desc: Try local Batang cuisine, pecel mie kenyol, a noodle with veggies in peanut sauce.

spots.name: Rest Area Heritage Km 260B Banjaratma
spots.desc: The souvenir center uses the old sugar factory building, Banjaratma Sugar Mill. There are a lot of food and souvenir stalls including telur asin (salted duck egg) with various variants boiled (original), grilled, roasted, and onion.

spots.name: Kupat Blengong Kasturi Rajak
spots.desc: Serves Brebes specialty dish kupat blengong, a rice cake in coconut milk soup with sate blengong (blengong meat skewers).
spots.addr: Jl. KH. Hasyim Ashari, Pasar Batang

spots.name: Rujak Belut Ibu Ribut
spots.desc: Local Brebes cuisine, rujak belut, fried eels in a peanut sauce with slices of shallot, and fresh tomato.

spots.name: Alun-Alun Pemalang
spots.desc: The city park is popular for strolling & jogging, with food vendors and a shiny pineapple sculpture.

spots.name: Museum R. Hamong Wardoyo
spots.desc: Collection of statues of the Hindu-Buddhist period which are ancient objects found in the Boyolali area.

spots.name: Cipto Mulyo Mosque
spots.desc: The mosque was built by the King of the Surakarta Sunanate, Pakubuwono X in 1905.

spots.name: Bekol Savannah
spots.desc: This is the main viewing point for the herds that gather to drink at the water hole. You really will believe you are in Africa here gazing across dry savannah against the backdrop of Mount Baluran. There is also a tower which allows panoramic views of the whole area.

spots.name: Bama Beach
spots.desc: Nice white sand beach with good live coral close offshore. Decent snorkelling spot. There is some basic accommodation here. There are usually ojek riders waiting at Bekol to ferry visitors across the Bama Beach.

spots.name: Mount Baluran
spots.desc: Climb Mount Baluran. Not a high peak by Javanese standards (1,247 m) but the views from the top are excellent in all directions including across the ocean to Madura. You can see Bali on a clear day.

spots.name: Jazz Gunung
spots.desc: Jazz Gunung (Mountain Jazz) is an annual music event that is held at Java Banana Bromo's open stage every July. It is a unique event that celebrates music, nature and culture since 2009. The stunning scenery in breezy mountainous tropical climate with the temperature around 14–18°C (57–65°F) during daylight and hit as low as 6–10°C (42–50°F) at night distinguish this event from other jazz…

spots.name: Bromo Corner Cafe
spots.desc: Decent cafe serving the usual Indonesian staples and excellent local coffee.

spots.name: Waroeng Basuki
spots.desc: Nice eatery at Cemoro Lawang serving many traditional Indonesian dishes such as tahu tek (tofu/beancurd), rujak cingur (salad with a sweet and spicy sauce and garnished with ox-nose). Also serves Chinese food. Reasonably priced.

spots.name: Bawangan Resto
spots.desc: A restaurant inside Bawangan Bromo Hotel, on the way to Bromo. Serving Indonesian traditional simple cuisine. Has beautiful view.

spots.name: Bukit Arosbaya
spots.desc: the limestone is redder than Bukit Jaddih, due to iron content and it is more secluded with the high cliff.

spots.name: Gili Iyang Island
spots.desc: The island has been noted for its plant diversity and high concentrations of oxygen. It is known as the oxygen island.

spots.name: Kalianget Old Town
spots.desc: Kalianget Old Town is one of the first modern cities on Madura Island. This city was built during the VOC era and continued by the Dutch East Indies government. You may see the remnants of the old city in the PT Garam (a state-owned company) area.

spots.name: Sumenep Palace
spots.desc: This is the modern day office of the Bupati (administrative head of the regency) of Sumenep and also houses the Royal Carriage House Museum. The palace was built in 1762. Very notable are the huge original teak pillars. Lots to see here including palanquins, weapons, Chinese porcelain, wooden handicrafts and beautifully carved furniture. The single best place to get a real handle on Madurese…

spots.name: Kepatihan Ngawi Building
spots.desc: Kepatihan Ngawi is one of the cultural attractions in Ngawi which is located in the ex-Kepatihan on Jalan Patiunus, Ketangi Village, Ngawi District of the city, Ngawi. This building includes the legacy of Patih Pringgokusumo, an important figure in the history of the Duchy of Ngawi. The Joglo house and the 2 hectare land belong to the Ngawi regional government which it is hoped will become one of…

spots.name: Dungus Bridge
spots.desc: A historical bridge decorated with lights and lighter colors. This bridge has a long history of Ngawi because in ancient times this bridge was the only crossing access from the west and east of Ngawi City.

spots.name: Pendopo Wedya Graha
spots.desc: The center of activities is located in a historic building that has high historical value
spots.addr: Jl. Teuku Umar no. 12 Kluncing, Ketanggi

spots.name: Ngawioboro Street
spots.desc: Many local people call it "Ngawioboro Street" or "the Malioboro" of Ngawi city. Facilities such as rows of long chairs and round chairs in the shape of cartoon ladybugs are of concern to tourists, there are several tables and decorative lights in creamy yellow which give the impression of being a classic.

spots.name: Baiturrahman Grand Mosque
spots.desc: Spiritual tourism destinations for Muslims. This mosque is one of the cultural heritages in the Ngawi city.
spots.addr: Jl. Imam Bonjol no. 3 Kerek, Margomulyo

spots.name: St Joseph's Catholic Church
spots.desc: Spiritual tourist spot for Catholics. This church building is one of the cultural heritage buildings in Ngawi city.
spots.addr: Jl. J.A Suprapto no. 6 Kluncing, Ketanggi

spots.name: Sien Hien Kiong Temple
spots.desc: This building is one of the Confucian worship buildings which is also a cultural heritage in Ngawi.
spots.addr: Jl. Sultan Agung no. 76 Sidomakmur, Ketanggi

spots.name: Dungus Park
spots.desc: Dungus Park is a green open park where there is a statue of a farmer with two buffaloes 7 meters high in the middle of the park and surrounded by a fountain.

spots.name: Candi Park Kartoharjo
spots.desc: The Candi park is a tourist and play park located near the dead river or indentation of the Madiun river which is in the form of a small lake. This park is located in Candi Hamlet, Kartoharjo Village, Ngawi District of the city.

spots.name: Central Park Ngawi Regency
spots.desc: Besides having a large area, Ngawi Square also has a number of facilities. Ngawi Square has an area of ​​68,310 square meters. Ngawi Square is an object of tourist attraction (ODTW) for visitors from outside District of the city and even outside Ngawi Regency.

spots.name: Ngudal Park
spots.desc: A park where there is a natural water source which is usually taken by drinking water companies.

spots.name: Soekarno Youth Park
spots.desc: A park and monument to Bung Karno to commemorate his services at that time
spots.addr: Jl. Ir. Soekarno (Ring-road barat) km. 6 Ngronggi, Grudo

spots.name: Kali Tempuk Indah
spots.desc: A tourist destination of choice to enjoy the beauty of the confluence of the two major rivers, namely the Solo rivers and Madiun rivers near the site of the Van den Bosch fort.

spots.name: Supermarket Luwes
spots.desc: Luwes Supermarket is one of the malls in Ngawi City. You can enjoy this shopping tour by walking around from the mall. Apart from retail, there are also clothes, books, daily necessities and entertainment vehicles in this mall.
spots.addr: Jl A Yani no. 58 West Balong, Beran

spots.name: Tiara Supermarket
spots.desc: This supermarket is one of the shopping destinations in Ngawi. This supermarket provides a variety of household items and necessities of life that you buy.
spots.addr: Jl A Yani no.45 (Near the Klitik intersection and southern ring road) Jetak, Klitik

spots.name: Toserba Matahari
spots.desc: This clothing store provides a variety of clothing you need. Starting from clothes, pants, underwear to bags, shoes and other accessories.

spots.name: Lethok Mbah Jan
spots.desc: Serves nasi lethok, rice with veggies and protein side dishes doused with lethok (rotten tempeh sauce).
spots.addr: Jl. Trunojoyo No.6, Tanjungrejo, Central Karang

spots.name: Tahu Tepo Mbah Nem
spots.desc: Serves tahu tepo, slices of tepo (rice cake) with veggies, tofu omelette, peanut sauce, and spiced sweet broth.

spots.name: Bakso dan Mie Ayam Pak Cipto
spots.desc: Provides meatball and chicken noodle dishes that can be enjoyed by visitors.

spots.name: RM Yu Sri Adem Ayem
spots.desc: Adem Ayem restauran, Culinary tourism for tourists and travelers .
spots.addr: Jl. Ir. Soekarno (ring road), Dadapan, Klitik

spots.name: RM Padang Minang Solok
spots.desc: Providing various kinds of Padang specialties consisting of beef rendang, chicken, green chili (sambal ijo) sauce to various processed vegetables with thick coconut milk gravy.
spots.addr: Jl. A Yani no. 117 East Balong, Beran

spots.name: Sambal Bakar Kondang
spots.desc: Sambal Bakar Kondang is a restaurant in Ngawi that provides various kinds of chili sauce and how to serve it baked in a clay pan.
spots.addr: Jl. Patiunus no. 168, Pelem III, Pelem

spots.name: Ayam Goreng Yogya Pak Manto
spots.desc: One of the fried chicken-based restaurants located in Ngawi. This restaurant is always crowded with culinary lovers.
spots.addr: Jl. Teuku Umar no. 102, South Cabean, Ketanggi

spots.name: Panggang Ayam Kampung Mbak Ambar
spots.desc: The only restaurant that provides a variety of culinary delights by ordering per package, not per portion.
spots.addr: Jl. Supriyadi RT 003 RW 005, Pangkur, Kartoharjo

spots.name: Graha Rasa Seafood Resto
spots.desc: This place is a culinary destination for those who like seafood.
spots.addr: Jl. MH Thamrin no. 4 Kerek, Margomulyo

spots.name: RM Bu Djar Karangdowo Sragen Cabang Ngawi
spots.desc: This restaurant provides various types of culinary delights that are liked by tourists visiting Ngawi.
spots.addr: Jl. Trunojoyo RT 003 RW 003, Kerek, Margomulyo

spots.name: RM Accord
spots.desc: Restaurant with full dishes. This restaurant is the umpteenth time reference for tourists or travelers who come to Ngawi.
spots.addr: Jl. Dr Wahidin Sudirohusodo no. 4 Sidomakmur, Ketanggi

spots.name: Dapoer Sangit Ngawi
spots.desc: One of the favorite places to eat with a cultural background. Suitable for tourists and families
spots.addr: Jl. Patiunus no. 17 Cabean Lor, Pelem

spots.name: Gudeg Jogja Dapur Meranti
spots.desc: One of the restaurants that provide typical Jogja gudeg dishes. For tourists, this place is certainly the main destination for culinary tourism.
spots.addr: Jl. Yos Sudarso no. 34 Kerek, Margomulyo

spots.name: La Densa
spots.desc: Cafes that provide various kinds of processed meat including steak.
spots.addr: Jl. Raden Saleh no. 6, South Cabean, Ketanggi

spots.name: Bintang Seafood Ngawi
spots.desc: All kinds of seafood are here. For tourists who love seafood can come here.
spots.addr: Jl. Trunojoyo Gg. Wijaya Kusuma no. 49 Kerek, Margomulyo

spots.name: Kopi Kenangan
spots.desc: This coffee shop provides various types of processed coffee types in Indonesia, especially in the Ngawi region. The taste of coffee in this shop is certainly much different compared to other coffee places.
spots.addr: Jl. Teuku Umar no. 24 Sidorejo, Ketanggi

spots.name: Warung Kopi "Anthurium"
spots.desc: This shop provides a variety of processed coffee, including Arabica and Robusta coffee

spots.name: The Real Coffee and Eatery
spots.desc: A variety of selected coffee drink menus are available here.

spots.name: Selomangleng Cave
spots.desc: located on the slope of Mt Klotok (Gunung Klotok) to the west of Kidiri has two small caves and interesting reliefs. There is also a swimming pool and jaranan's performs every week.

spots.name: Sumber Podang
spots.desc: There is fresh stream with pine forests. There is also a Balinese cafe near the stream.

spots.name: St. Mary Lourdes Cave and Pohsarang Church
spots.desc: Pohsarang Church was built by Romo Wolters, one of the first Roman Catholic missionaries in Java. St. Mary Lourdes Cave is a replica of the St. Maria Lourdes Cave in France. There is a huge monument of St. Mary in front of the cave.

spots.name: Asmaul Husna Tower
spots.desc: Asmaul Husna means the 99 names of Allah and the tower is 99 metres tall.

spots.name: Gong Cave
spots.desc: A cave with unique formations and colorful stalagmites and stalactites.

spots.name: Putri Cave
spots.desc: A cave with unique formations and colorful stalagmites and stalactites.

spots.name: Song Gupuh Cave
spots.desc: A cave with unique formations and colorful stalagmites and stalactites.

spots.name: Song Terus Cave
spots.desc: A cave with unique formations and colorful stalagmites and stalactites.

spots.name: Monument of General Sudirman Pakis Baru
spots.desc: There is a replica of the house when the national hero General Sudirman did a guerrilla war.

spots.name: Klayar Beach
spots.desc: A white sand beach, with raised coral formations, and a blowhole up to 10 meters high.

spots.name: Srau Beach
spots.desc: Offers three spots for intermediate surfers, and a white sand beach.

spots.name: Warung Makan Sego Gobyos
spots.desc: Serves rice with various super spicy side dishes. The special menu is usus kuah santan (chicken intestine cooked in coconut milk soup).

spots.name: Museum Desa Bedingin
spots.desc: Agricultural tools, household tools, ancient books, ancient Qur'an, and heirlooms. Near the museum, you may visit a historic site Sirah Keteng.

spots.name: Stone carving
spots.desc: Walk in from the main road, on the northern side, and you will probably bump into a couple of people in the yard of a house carving away at a huge lump of stone, turning it into a Buddha, or a Ganesha, or some such. Often on commission from a hotel or wealthy individual. Working at too large a scale for there to be chance to buy anything, but interesting to look at.

spots.name: G-Land Bobby's Surf Camp
spots.desc: Run by a Balinese surfer who took over the original surf camp operation from the Boyum brothers.

spots.name: G-Land Jack's Surf Camp
spots.desc: Also have an office at Okie House, Poppies II, in Kuta, Bali.

spots.name: Joyo's G-Land Surf Camp
spots.desc: Also have an office in Bali at Gang Benesari 77, Poppies II, Kuta, Bali.

spots.name: See a magician
spots.desc: From all over the archipelago Indonesians flock to consult Banyuwangi's famous and infamous practitioners of white magic and the darker arts, the dutak.

spots.name: Gallery & Museum Mozes Misdy
spots.desc: Mozes Midzy is a renowned Javanese modern artist and he was born in Banyuwangi in 1941. This gallery showcases his painting work and pieces are available for purchase.

spots.name: Latisana Drink and Eatery
spots.desc: A more modern eatery serving a variety of popular Indonesian dishes. Larger portions and very good quality.

spots.name: Paralayang Kemuning
spots.desc: Doing an extreme sport, paragliding with amazing natural landscapes.

spots.name: Agrowisata Amanah
spots.desc: It is an agriculture-themed attraction on the slopes of Mount Lawu. It has ATV, flying fox, jembatan ogal agil, and wall climbing. You can also see an organic fruit and vegetable farm. You can also interact with farm animals such as goats, horses, cows, rabbits, ducks, and chickens. It also has a swimming pool and a restaurant.

spots.name: Sego Gablok Pasar Tawangmangu
spots.desc: Sego gablok Tawangmangu is a specialty rice dish in Tawangmangu. It is coconut milk spiced rice wrapped in banana leaf. Eaten with another banana leaf-wrapped side dish like Bothok so/mlanding and Gadon ayam.

spots.name: Sakaw Coffee & Bites
spots.desc: The coffee shop with various menus. It also serve traditional Javanese snack, Singkong goreng and Pisang owol. It also sells many variations of freshly roasted coffee beans.

spots.name: Dawet Lawu
spots.desc: A purple dawet drink made from rice flour and purple sweet potato.

spots.name: Bubur Ayam Lestari Cianjur
spots.desc: Simple eatery selling bubur Cianjur as well as several other dishes, including fried chicken, fried rice, noodles, and fresh fruit juices.

spots.name: Taman Sari Royal Heritage Spa
spots.desc: Pamper yourself after a day at the hectic city with Indonesian style massages. For your well-being, the spa also offers swimming pool, sauna, gym, whirlpool, and manicure & pedicure.
spots.price: Massages from Rp150,000; spas/body scrubs from Rp250,000

spots.name: Citywalk Sudirman
spots.desc: Many options of food and drink, decent shopping options such as Daiso Japanese 100-yen shop.

spots.name: Harco Mangga Dua
spots.desc: This is the place for computers and gadgets (but in most cases, not mobile phones). Come here to get a fix.

spots.name: Jakarta Design Centre (JDC)
spots.desc: 7 floors of furniture showrooms, from vintage to modern minimalist.
spots.addr: Jl. Jend. Gatot Subroto Kav. 53, Petamburan, Tanah Abang

spots.name: Mangga Dua Mall
spots.desc: One part of the Mangga Dua strip is where the locals shop for electronics, from game consoles to Hi-Fi speakers. Note that unless you ask not to, most of the software sold here are pirated.

spots.name: Surabaya Street
spots.desc: A famous flea market located in Central Jakarta. Art, antique and souvenir shops. Favourite place for bargain hunters. Beware of pickpockets.

spots.name: Bakmi Gang Kelinci
spots.desc: By default, go with the mie ayam that features yellow noodles with braised chicken and mushrooms. Other dishes include vermicelli, kway teow, and Chinese style snacks and entrees. And they are halal which factors in the frequent crowds.
spots.addr: Jl. Gang Kelinci Raya No. 1-3, Pasar Baru

spots.name: Gado-Gado Bonbin
spots.desc: A very popular place for the Indonesian salad gado-gado and the so-called lontong cap gomeh.

spots.name: Nasi Goreng Kambing Kebon Sirih
spots.desc: A street stall that has been a longtime favourite for Middle Eastern lamb (or mutton) fried rice, in which it has a complex scent made from various spices. Expect to be very packed!
spots.addr: Jl. Kebon Sirih Barat Dalam I

spots.name: Ragusa Es Italia
spots.desc: Established by the Italian Ragusa brothers in 1932, this hole-in-the-wall gelato parlor provides your imaginable ice cream menu, but has an antique charm that entices you to come back for more.

spots.name: Happy Day
spots.desc: This restaurant can satisfy those that are on the budget while missing food especially from European or the US, or if you feel peckish for anything else. And where else can you find pizza for just Rp35,000?
spots.price: Rp25,000 to Rp60,000; steaks from Rp80,000

spots.name: Kedai Nasi Uduk & Ayam Goreng Zainal Fanani
spots.desc: Come in to treat yourself with nasi uduk, Jakarta's style of rice cooked in coconut milk and your choice of chicken or beef anyhow you want to have it on the side.

spots.name: Beirut Lebanon Restaurant
spots.desc: Reasonably authentic and affordably priced Lebanese eats, with bonus points for the bizarre decor of Arabic weaponry and plastic scenes of green rural idyll.

spots.name: Ganesha Ek Sanskriti
spots.desc: While Indian restaurants are few and far between, this establishment nails it by serving both the northern and southern Indian delicacies.

spots.name: Kafe Pisa
spots.desc: A longtime favourite for Italian cuisine and some gelato. Live music every night.
spots.price: Pizzas from Rp120,000; entrees from Rp80,000; Gelato from Rp50,000

spots.name: Lara Djonggrang
spots.desc: Old house named after a legend from Prambanan and retrofitted with the contents (and roof!) of a 300-year-old temple that was in Semarang, serving up pompously self-styled "imperial Indonesian cuisine". The staff will be happy to show you around if it's quiet; be sure to check out the gorgeous Lara Djonggrang room. If you are eating with a big group (more than 20 people), book ahead and you will…
spots.price: Menu packages from Rp200,000; entrees from Rp50,000
spots.addr: Jl. Teuku Cik Di Tiro 4, Menteng

spots.name: Maple & Oak
spots.desc: Bistro featuring all-day brunch with diner style menus and a modest selection of desserts. Or drop by to drink coffee and mocktails (soda cocktails).

spots.name: Martabak Pecenongan 65A
spots.desc: Mouthwatering sweet martabak with a few classic flavours like bananas, cheese and chocolate, in addition to more expensive ingredients like the Ovomaltine, Toblerone and Green Tea Kit Kat. 10 pieces in a medium would already get you through 2 to 3 meals, and even more for the regular 16-piece. The savory egg martabak is also worth trying.

spots.name: Pondok Laguna
spots.desc: Seafood restaurant. Simultaneously big and noisy yet outdoors and peaceful, this popular seafood joint is packed every mealtime with punters queuing up for their famous grilled fish (gurame goreng) and fried tofu with shrimp (tahu kipas). Wash it down with an improbably tasty glass of cucumber juice (es timun).

spots.name: Kikugawa
spots.desc: Established in 1969, Kikugawa is the oldest Japanese restaurant in Jakarta since the Second World War. Serving authentic Japanese cuisine in simple Japanese house atmosphere. The owner is Japanese-Indonesian couple who had also established "Bengawan Solo" Indonesian restaurant in Tokyo.

spots.name: Tamnak Thai
spots.desc: While their seafood and tom yam are expensive, they are worth the price for using fresh catches. Their pineapple fried rice is a hit.

spots.name: Ya-Udah Bistro
spots.desc: A budget to mid-range option for European specialties, with an emphasis on German breads and pork. Don't let the old interior throw you away!
spots.hours: Daily 08:00–22:00 (00:00 during Ramadan on Sat and Sun)

spots.name: Al Jazeerah Signature
spots.desc: A splurge Arabian fix frequented especially at dinnertime. The hummus and pita bread are desirable while the rice has a variety of fragrant you can choose from. Top it with a huff of shisha.
spots.price: Curries from Rp50,000; grills from Rp125,000

spots.name: Bistro Baron
spots.desc: Upscale bistro that serves French haute cuisine with a selection of premium tea and desserts to accompany.

spots.name: Kintan Buffet
spots.desc: All you can eat Japanese BBQ where you can also upsize to savour the top quality wagyu beef.
spots.price: Lunch from Rp150,000; Dinner from Rp200,000
spots.addr: Senayan City, Jl. Asia Afrika No.19

spots.name: Momozen
spots.desc: A fusion of Japanese and French cuisine that is mainly frequented for tapas. Premium meat and seafood entrees. Reservation required.
spots.addr: The Plaza Level 46, Jl. M.H. Thamrin No 1

spots.name: Skye
spots.desc: Take your dining experience up, way up on the rooftop of a 56-floor building overlooking the forest of Jakarta's skyscrapers. European and American cuisine, some with an Asian twist, and an extensive collection of booze.
spots.price: Appetisers from Rp55,000; entrees from Rp80,000

spots.name: Tugu Kunstkring Paleis
spots.desc: A Rijstafel-styled fine-dining restaurant in an old-fashioned Dutch house, serving mostly Betawi and Indonesian cuisine.
spots.addr: Jl. Teuku Umar No.1, RT.1/RW.1, Gondangdia, Menteng,

spots.name: Giyanti Coffee Roastery
spots.desc: Mainly serves coffee and has indoor and outdoor spaces for drinking. No smoking allowed.

spots.name: Tanamera Coffee
spots.desc: A wide selection of many Indonesian coffee beans. Offers training classes as well such as barista class, latte art basic class, roasting class etc.
spots.addr: Jl. Kebon Kacang Raya, Tanah Abang, RT.8/RW.9

spots.name: Watt Coffee
spots.desc: Has an open roasting site and comfortable seats for hanging out or just working.
spots.addr: The Capitol Park, Apartment, Jl. Salemba Raya No.16, RT.3/RW.6, Kenari, Kec. Senen, Kota Jakarta Pusat, Daerah Khusus Ibukota

spots.name: Es Selendang Mayang Nicholas
spots.desc: Es selendang mayang is a Betawi cold drink made from mixed rice and palm flour jelly with sweet coconut milk and ice.
spots.addr: Jl. Jati Baru, Kp. Bali, Tanah Abang

spots.name: Burgundy Bar
spots.desc: Bar with burgundy (dark shade of red) decoration. The special drink from this bar is called "burgundy crush". Facility: live jazz performance, cigar smoking room. Drinks: fine wine, frozen vodkas, spirit, martini, Caipirinha, Caipiroska etc. It also acts as a bistro that serves snacks to full fledged meals.

spots.name: Churchill
spots.desc: An old-school wine bar that also provides an assortment of cigars to puff.
spots.addr: Jl. Lapangan Banteng Selatan 1, Pasar Baru

spots.name: CJs Bar
spots.desc: Attracts a younger crowd or the youth in spirit because of live music. Cover charge for non-hotel guests: Rp250,000.

spots.name: Grand Manhattan
spots.desc: Retro style cafe with some alcoholic beverages, but the live music & DJ is what draws the crowd.
spots.addr: Jl. Lapangan Banteng Selatan 1, Pasar Baru

spots.name: Tiga Puluh
spots.desc: The Jekyll and Hyde of Jakarta's nightclubs: as you step in, you'll find a stylish, quiet, well-lit wine bar, but behind the double doors lies a dimly lit and noisy nightclub packed with girls. The live bands are, however, a notch above the average.

spots.name: Heroes
spots.desc: This statue commemorates the heroic struggle for Indonesian independence by Jatinegara residents in 1945.

spots.name: Jakarta International Velodrome
spots.desc: An indoor cycling track. There is also a park surrounding it.
spots.addr: Jl. Balap Sepeda No.35, RW.6, Jati, Pulo Gadung

spots.name: Jakarta Golf Club
spots.desc: The oldest course in Jakarta (1872). Thoughtful and precise approach to the putt.

spots.name: Padang Golf Halim
spots.desc: Very close to the airport. Started as the Air Force’s first golf course, now known for its low fees, yet challenging course (high trees, tricky greens). 36 holes (divided into 2 parts).

spots.name: Royale Jakarta Golf Club
spots.desc: 27 golf holes (North, West, South have 9 holes each). Most require long shots. The restaurant and bar overlook the court. The most complete facility.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Halim Tiga, Halim Perdanakusuma

spots.name: Pramuka Bird Market
spots.desc: The biggest bird market in Jakarta and probably in South East Asia.
spots.addr: Jl. Kayu Manis Utara No.19, RT.8/RW.1

spots.name: Asinan Betawi H. Mansyur
spots.desc: Betawi specialties, The vegetable asinan of the Betawi people from Jakarta is preserved Chinese cabbage, cabbage, bean sprouts, tofu, and lettuce served in a thin, hot, peanut sauce with vinegar, topped with peanuts and krupuk, especially krupuk mie (noodles crackers).

spots.name: Martabak Favourite
spots.desc: Popular martabak place among locals. They sell only the sweet martabak variant and for the savoury ones.
spots.addr: Jalan Balai Pustaka Timur No. 24, RT.01 / RW.09, Rawamangun

spots.name: Nyonya Soeharti
spots.desc: Traditional fried chicken chain. Menu: fried chicken, gudeg, fried rice.

spots.name: Pagi Sore
spots.desc: Padangnese Food, one of the notable restaurant chain as 'Sederhana'.
spots.price: Rp. 40,000 - Rp 100,000 per person, depending on your preferences
spots.addr: Jl. Rawamangun Muka Timur No.1A, RT.4/RW.12, Rawamangun

spots.name: Restoran Sederhana
spots.desc: Padangnese Food, you can either 'pesan' (take away) or 'hidang' (dine-in).
spots.price: Rp 30,000 - Rp 75,000 depending on your preferences
spots.addr: Jl. Balai Pustaka No.1, RT.7/RW.15, Rawamangun

spots.name: Quiznos Sub
spots.desc: 'Subway' equivalent in Jakarta. Sells dishes from breakfast to dinner. Popular amongst students for its wi-fi connectivity and its spacious and cozy place.
spots.addr: Jl. Pemuda No.30, Rawamangun, Pulogadung, RT.2/RW.7, Rawamangun

spots.name: The Grill Father
spots.desc: A semi-outdoor restaurant with a bunch of various menus as well from ramen to steak.
spots.addr: Jalan Pahlawan Revolusi No.10, RT.4/RW.3, Pondok Bambu

spots.name: Mr. O Coffee
spots.desc: A cozy, small, coffee shop offers range of mostly locally produced coffee beans selections. Plenty of light bites or snacks.
spots.addr: Jalan Rawamangun Muka Timur No. 54, RT.3/RW.14, Rawamangun

spots.name: Hegemony Coffee and Eatery
spots.desc: Industrial-themed decorated coffee shop with a combination of traditional and modern concept. Sells mostly light bites such as churros, sandwiches, and pancakes besides coffee.
spots.addr: Jalan Sunan Sedayu No.7, RT.1/RW.6, Rawamangun

spots.name: Kedai Locale
spots.desc: A local coffee shop that sells mostly Indonesian coffee. Offers meals ranging from light bites to heavy ones such as Nasi Goreng.
spots.addr: Jalan Balai Pustaka No.C-6, RT.5/RW.10, Rawamangun

spots.name: Galangan VOC
spots.desc: Dating back to 1628, this is the former trade office and ship repair of the VOC (East Indies Trade Company) built by the Dutch. It is the center of the trade routes that stretched from Japan to Cape Town, from the Spice Islands to Persia. The place is now a restaurant, also called the VOC (Very Old Café), but maintains what's left of history.

spots.name: Taman Wisata Alam Angke Kapuk
spots.desc: Similar to Muara Angke but does not require a permit. Larger, even has a place to stay and playing boats. No DSLR cameras allowed. It is an artificial park, not a nature preserve, and patrons can plant mangrove trees there, if they obtain a ticket.

spots.name: Emporium Pluit XXI The Premiere
spots.desc: A movie theater experience taken to the next level. Table dining before the movie. Dedicated studio with plush pillows and bedding. There is a game arcade center inside it.
spots.addr: Emporium Pluit Mall Unit 5-10, Jl. Pluit Selatan Raya

spots.name: Baywalk Mall
spots.desc: It offers premium eateries and chain department stores, and has a dedicated seating area with view of Jakarta's seas and a seaside seafood restaurant.
spots.addr: Jl. Pluit Karang Ayu B1 Utara

spots.name: Pluit Junction
spots.desc: A sleepy and lonely mall across the Emporium Pluit with basic shops. Good only for a fitness center, movies (the cheapest in the area) and watching a live football match at its center stage.

spots.name: Ancol Art Market
spots.desc: Wondering where to buy art in Jakarta? This is where the locals go, especially for Indonesian traditional arts. It's a collector's paradise!

spots.name: Kwetiau Akang
spots.desc: Parking may be tough because the restaurant does not provide its own, but it is worth the time! Famous in the area (and all over Jakarta) for its rice vermicelli (kwetiau), a choice of fried (dry) or siram (wet with gravy). Toppings are usually shrimp, beef (or pork), scrambled eggs, and shallots.

spots.name: Le Bridge
spots.desc: In the middle of the water, the establishment is connected by a man-made causeway that entices couples to hang out waiting for the sun to set. Its menu consists of western cuisine as well as finger bites. One of the cheapest non-chain brand options at Ancol. There are no restrooms due to the fact it is in the middle of "nowhere"!
spots.price: Snacks from Rp20,000; Mains from Rp35,000
spots.addr: Taman Impian Jaya Ancol, Jl. Pasir Putih Raya,

spots.name: B'Steak
spots.desc: A western style dining, with pancakes and steaks as its specialities.

spots.name: Zenbu House of Mozaru
spots.desc: This restaurant takes your typical Japanese cuisine to the next level. As its name suggests, its specialty is the mozaru, rice on the bottom layer, followed by meat and sauce, finally topped with mozzarella cheese — you can choose different options for the first three! There are other things too, especially salmon, pasta, and abundant vegetarian options.
spots.addr: Jl. Pluit Karang Barat G6 No. 34

spots.name: Bandar Djakarta
spots.desc: This is the one of the favorite seafood options in Jakarta. It hosts what resembles a seafood market where you can pick your own fish and have them cook it, or you can order just by sitting at your table and let them do all the work, but the seating area is actually what draws everyone: its panorama of the coastline and the sea breeze, notoriously hot by the afternoon, cool at night. Perfect for…
spots.addr: Taman Impian Jaya Ancol, Pintu Timur, Jl. Lodan Timur No. 7

spots.name: Segarra
spots.desc: A perfect place for a couple and a candlelit dinner under the open sky. Luxurious hotel-like dining experience with Indonesian, Japanese, Italian, and Western options. The sofa chairs on the beach facing the sea or near the pool are the best seats in the house, yet very often reserved in advance. A minimum order must be placed if you wish to sit there though.
spots.addr: Pantai Carnaval - Jakarta Bay City, Jl. Lodan Timur No. 7

spots.name: Manon Chocolatier & Patissier
spots.desc: A French pastry and chocolate shop. Known for signature macaroons, delicious cakes, and chocolates.
spots.addr: Jl. Nias Raya GN no.6, Kelapa Gading.

spots.name: Copper Club Specialty Coffee
spots.desc: Specialty coffee place near Kelapa Gading district. Offers various local and international coffee beans for both filtered and espresso.
spots.addr: Jalan Tarian Raya Timur W1 no 23, RT.5/RW.9, Pegangsaan Dua, Kelapa Gading, 14240

spots.name: Sayap Suci Coffee Kelapa Gading
spots.desc: One of the few coffee places in Jakarta that has a sporting facility (jogging track) and live music.

spots.name: Ratio Coffee Brewers
spots.desc: One of many specialty coffee places in Jakarta that serves local and international beans.
spots.price: Coffee and mains start from Rp50,000

spots.name: Diamond City Drawbridge
spots.desc: A Dutch style drawbridge that crosses a canal, situated near what was once the Diamond Fort.
spots.addr: Jl Nelayan Barat / Jl. Kali Besar Barat.

spots.name: Skyrink
spots.desc: The largest skating rink in Southeast Asia, an oasis worth joining for a cool off in the hot Jakarta, or a reminiscence of the cold winter. It is best to get here on a weekday, as it's dramatically less crowded and you are entitled to an all-day play!
spots.price: Weekdays Rp60,000 all day; weekends Rp70,000 for 2 hours, overtime Rp9,000 per hour
spots.addr: Jl. Letjen S. Parman No.Kav 21, RT.12/RW.1, Tanjung Duren Selatan,. Grogol petamburan

spots.name: Suncity Luxury Club
spots.desc: A one-stop place for karaoke, a spa, eating (especially Chinese cuisine), drinking (including wine and other alcoholic beverages), and sleeping (in their hotel). Also has a ballroom for various events.
spots.addr: Jl. Hayam Wuruk No.127, RT.1/RW.6, Mangga Besar, Taman Sari

spots.name: Bakmi Ayam Acang
spots.desc: A type of Jakarta Ayam Kampung-Mie Ayam (chicken noodle that uses village chicken). A halal dish.
spots.addr: Jl. Dr. Susilo III No.14, Grogol

spots.name: Bakmi GM
spots.desc: The flagship store (or the first) of the Bakmi GM chain branch. You pay once you order and your dish comes out darn quick (in less than 10 minutes). Include the Bakmi Special GM and the Pangsit Goreng with the sweet and spicy sauce.

spots.name: Mie Juhi Babeh Ade
spots.desc: Serves Mie juhi, a Betawi cuisine noodle dish. Noodles with dried squid and vegetables in peanut sauce.

spots.name: Mie Kangkung Si Jangkung
spots.desc: Sell Mie kangkung literally means water spinach noodles. A Chinese-Betawi cuisine.
spots.addr: Jl. Pintu Besar Selatan 2 No.6, Glodok

spots.name: Bakso Akiaw 99
spots.desc: The place is steaming (literally, no AC) as you get here, but pays off with the succulent bakso (meatballs), complemented with a choice of noodles or rice noodles (thick or thin).

spots.name: Kamseng Resto
spots.desc: An especially good option for a dine supper through breakfast, famous for its clay pot porridge, with any options you can add on such as fish or pork, egg (try the premium pitan: fermented chicken or duck egg), and the very enticing cahkwe (shrimp breadstick/youtiao).

spots.name: Kwetiau Sapi 78 Mangga Besar
spots.desc: For its namesake, order the Kwetiau Sapi (beef thick rice noodle), preferably with the gravy (Kwetiau Siram Sapi), or if you don't want it messy or wet in your mouth, the fried one (Kwetiau Goreng Sapi) can be a good option.
spots.addr: Jl. Mangga Besar Raya No. 78 D

spots.name: Suisse Bakery
spots.desc: A bakery that opened in the 1960s, serving delicious bread, both topped and filled.
spots.addr: Jl. Hayam Wuruk 114 Blok A No. 5 - 6

spots.name: Gandy Steakhouse
spots.desc: A longtime favorite steakhouse with retro European wallpaper, waiters in bow ties, and complimentary bread from their bakery downstairs. Live music every night playing oldies and perhaps a couple of songs from the current century.
spots.price: Steaks from Rp150,000; other meals from Rp70,000

spots.name: Nanny's Pavilion
spots.desc: A classy style restaurant where the waiters/waitresses dress up like your nanny. Specializes in western food such as steak and pasta. But the recommendations are the waffles or crepes with ice cream.
spots.addr: Central Park, Ground Floor, Sogo Central Park,

spots.name: Sate Domba Afrika Haji Ismail
spots.desc: An African-Indonesian dish. Grilled sheep with onion and eaten with fried banana.
spots.addr: Jl. Aipda. Ks. Tubun No. 6, Kota Bambu Selatan, Palmerah

spots.name: Tamani Kafe
spots.desc: A western style restaurant, specializing in pasta and steaks. For drinks, have a try of the Thai Iced Tea.
spots.addr: Jl. Hayam Wuruk 96A, Jl. Tomang Raya 15

spots.name: Cafe Batavia
spots.desc: The downstairs music box bar is subtly lit with tables around couches. The upstairs Churchill bar next to the restaurant was rated in Newsweek's Best Bars in the World a few years ago. Great cocktails, beautiful building.

spots.name: Club 36 Bar
spots.desc: Las Vegas style bar/girly bar with karaoke, and gogo dancers. Foreign dancers from Thailand, Turkey, eastern Europe. Opening hours: M-Sa 13:00-05:00, Su 18:00-05:00. 36 karaoke rooms.

spots.name: Dancing Fountain Park
spots.desc: An amphitheatre with the lake Situ Buleud as the main stage for the dancing fountain show. Has the capacity of 5,000 seats for the show. Proclaimed to be the biggest fountain show in Southeast Asia.

spots.name: RM Soto Sadang Asli
spots.desc: Well-known restaurant selling a local style of soto (soup). Choices include chicken soup, beef soup, and oxtail soup.

spots.name: Best Borneo Orangutan Tours
spots.desc: Orangutan tours, river tours, dayak village adventure & more.
spots.addr: Jl. Gerilya No. 369, Gg. Ampera - Kumai Hulu

spots.name: Borneo Discovery Tours
spots.desc: Orangutan tours, river tours, tour operator to arrange your ticket from Jakarta or Semarang to Pangkalanbun.

spots.name: Local Guides
spots.desc: Ecotours with experienced local guides. Fair and transparent tariffs.

spots.name: Fort Duurstede
spots.desc: This historic Dutch fort was established by the Dutch East Indies Company in 1691. In 1817 the fort was conquered by local leader Thomas Matulessi, or famously known as Pattimura, who had all the soldiers as well as the official Dutch Resident and his family killed. The fort has been restored and is open to visitors.

spots.name: Ouw
spots.desc: Several of the villages are nice enough to visit, but Ouw is one of the most interesting ones. It's the best place to see pottery makers at work and it has a small, half overgrown fort of its own. Quite unlike Fort Duurstede, the fort here has not been restored at all and some locals live within its walls, but it has a nice forgotten glory vibe over it.

spots.name: Nolloth
spots.desc: This village on the north-eastern corner of the island has a pretty church, dating back to colonial times. The sago-thatch roof has unfortunately been replaced by tin, but it's still a friendly and peaceful place.

spots.name: Baileu Saparua
spots.desc: A traditional house of Saparua.This house is thought to have been built by four original clans who simultaneously migrated to the Saparua area from a place called Souhuku on Seram Island around 1514 as a sign of their attachment consisting of the Titaley, Anakotta, Ririnama, and Simatauw clans.

spots.name: Takpala village
spots.desc: Traditional Asli village, where you can see traditional houses, customs, clothes and dances.

spots.name: Pantai Reklamasi
spots.desc: Reklamasi is a redeveloped foreshore promenade, with 6-7 cafes, restaurants and bars overlooking the sea-shore. The grilled fish (Ikan Bakar), freshly caught is very popular.

spots.name: Masakan Padang Gantian
spots.desc: good selection of Padang food including beef rendang, fish, egg and other West Sumatran delicacies.

spots.name: Komodo Cruises Tour
spots.desc: A variety of package options, with customer service that can help provide the best package options.
spots.price: Prices start at Rp1,300,000 for one day trip per person

spots.name: Flores Diving Centre
spots.desc: Very friendly staff. The equipment is in good condition and they offer a wide range of daily boat trips to the dive sites including food and drinks
spots.price: Prices start at Rp900,000 for a boat trip with 2 dives.

spots.name: Maika Komodo Tour and Diving
spots.desc: Maika Komodo Tour & diving is a full service agency with liveaboards and daily boats.

spots.name: Fish market
spots.desc: Lots of food stalls along the harborfront in the evening. Fresh fish grilled to order.

spots.name: Green Cherry
spots.desc: Great view of the bay, especially from the upstairs area. Extensive menu with many Chinese and Western dishes. Free WiFi. You can play pool downstairs.

spots.name: Happy Banana
spots.desc: Delicious food. Not only sushi. Wifi and AC. Tables with power outlet.
spots.addr: In front of Mandiri Bank, Jalan Soekarno Hatta

spots.name: Artomoro
spots.desc: Local food for Rp35,000-70,000 and more expensive western food for Rp80,000-100,000 (Feb 2017). Very fresh and tasty.

spots.name: Dapur Tara Flores Restaurant
spots.desc: Community-based traditional Flores restaurant, specialising in traditional Flores food with ingredients mainly from their organic gardens or from the surrounding farmers. All food is prepared over an open fire. Their specialities are Jungle Breakfast and Jungle Lunch, smoked chicken and bamboo rice.

spots.name: MadeinItaly
spots.desc: Wide range of Italian dishes including pizza, pasta, risotto, antipasti and tiramisu. Fairly upscale.

spots.name: Paradise Bar
spots.desc: The only bar that is open until late and has a fantastic view of the sunset. Every Saturday (at least) there is live music till late night, though don't get high expectations about their taste in cover songs. Paradise also serves pretty decent food.

spots.name: The Lounge
spots.desc: The default place for a sundowner. Anker beer is the best-seller, (Rp27,000-25,000 + tax). They also serve cocktails and food until 23:00. Shisha is available, try the apple/mint flavor for that freshmaker feeling.

spots.name: Diving
spots.desc: The waters off nearby Pulau Besar has good reefs for snorkeling and diving. Unfortunately, the dive centres don't get many customers and will only leave with 2 or more guests, so single divers will get a tough time buddying up. Prices hover around US$75-80 for a day with 2 dives, full equipment and lunch. Operators are found at Ankermi, "Blue Crystal Dive Trip", Sea World Club or Wailiti Beach…

spots.name: Snorkelling
spots.desc: Most hotels have snorkel gear you can rent (or simply borrow). You will have to go pretty far out from the shore to get to the reefs, but the currents are not too strong in this area so you should be alright if you are a decent swimmer. Check with your hotel for the best spot - or arrange a boat tour with a local fisherman (around Rp 450,000 for the day).

spots.name: Jetski / Banana boat
spots.desc: Wailiti Hotel offers thrillseeking fun on the banana boat, if you really want to get into the holiday spirit.

spots.name: Warung Jakarta
spots.desc: has fresh fish and seafood at reasonable prices in big portions.

spots.name: Warung Dahlia
spots.desc: Cheap and popular with the locals, this place serves all the usual suspects; soto ayam, nasi campur, ikan bakar. If it's Indonesian they have it. Everything is cooked fresh.

spots.name: Golden Fish
spots.desc: Up market, and highly recommended fish restaurant. Choose your live fish, crab or lobster from the tank and wait while they steam, grill or fry it for you.

spots.name: My Bread Bakery
