spots.desc: The proximity to Gardena Hotel and the heavy amounts of chocolate used in the baked goods here make it a bad combination for your diet. However, once in a while you should allow yourself to indulge in the goodies. You can buy bread, cakes, burgers or mini-pizzas for eating in or take-away.

spots.name: Roxy Supermarket
spots.desc: The well-stocked, low-priced Roxy is a good place to stock up on essentials for the 24-hr boat ride to Makassar.

spots.name: Comtel
spots.desc: offers the most expensive internet in town. However, it is signposted everywhere and has WiFi.

spots.name: Warnet
spots.desc: No WiFi, but you can bring your own laptop and use their ADSL connection.

spots.name: ET Shop Cyber Café
spots.desc: Has internet and WiFi. CDs and other computer accessories are sold here, if you want to transfer your photos to a CD. There is a nice café area in the back, which makes this the perfect place to wait for a delayed Pelni ship.

spots.name: Gili Meno Bird Park
spots.desc: A bird sanctuary in the centre of Gili Meno boasting exotic species in a beautifully landscaped environment. Macaws, flamingos, cockatoos, pelicans, eagles, parrots and more. Also home to a crocodile, some deer and a kangaroo.

spots.name: Turtle sanctuary
spots.desc: Green and loggerhead turtles are now common to the waters around the Gilis. To ensure the on-going survival of these creatures, sanctuaries have been set-up on both Gili Trawangan and Gili Meno. You can visit the sanctuaries, see the baby turtles in their pools and learn more about these fascinating creatures.

spots.name: Sunset on the hill
spots.desc: Great sunset spot with panoramic views of the 3 Gilis and of Lombok and Bali beyond. A good place to take photographs.

spots.name: Jembatan Gantung Sinakma
spots.desc: The traditional suspension bridge has stretched over the Uwe river.

spots.name: Kebun Raya Biologi Wamena
spots.desc: A flora conservation area. You may see rumput mei (pink-purple Wamena grass) in May.

spots.name: Pasar Sinakma
spots.desc: Traditional market in Wamena. You may buy fresh vegetables and fruits.

spots.name: Paisu Batango
spots.desc: A cyan lagoon near Paisu Pok where spring water mixes with sea water. Locals like to wash their clothes and themselves there and fetch spring water.

spots.name: Poganda Beach
spots.desc: A white sand beach and snorkelling spot 30 minutes' drive from Paisu Pok.

spots.name: Gua Susundeng
spots.desc: A cave filled with turquoise and dark blue, very transparent water. Closed when rainy due to slippery paths.

spots.name: Gua Bab'Banang
spots.desc: Another cave, a little smaller but very similar to Gua Susundeng. A little better developed, with a toilet and changing room and better paths. Therefore also open when rainy.

spots.name: Mandel Beach
spots.desc: A long, well-known but remote white sand beach with turquoise water. No infrastructure, a lot of trash lying around, but can still be cropped out of pictures. Due to overfishing nothing much to see underwater according to locals.

spots.name: Bone Pompon
spots.desc: A clean white sand beach. Decent snorkelling, toilets and gazebos available. Showers present but depending on the season and water availability you may have to use the tubs in the bathrooms instead.

spots.name: Oyama Beach
spots.desc: Another well-known white sand beach with turquoise water. Sand almost as fine as flour. Some trash lying around. Nothing to see under the water, but also no jellyfish, even at times when other locations around the east side of the island have them.

spots.name: Long Beach
spots.desc: White sand beach with nice snorkelling. May have seasonal jellyfish around the end of March.

spots.name: Tanjung Gundul
spots.desc: Picturesque cliff with a hole created by sea waves. The floor is made of sand-colored stones. In the water in front of the place there may be seasonal jellyfish, so consider wearing long-sleeved clothes and swimming shoes to get there.

spots.name: Bukit Doa Mahawu
spots.desc: A quiet area for Christian pilgrimage. It has 'Via Dolorosa' at Mahawu (Jalan Salib Mahawu) to remember the sacrifice of Jesus Christ when he died on the cross. Inside the area is a Chapel of Virgin Mary, amphitheatre Mahawu, and man made grotto. All welcome.

spots.name: Buddhayana Monastery
spots.desc: A Buddhist religious and meditation complex. Chinese culture preserved in architecture of statues, Kwan Im goddess palace and pagoda. Religious service every Sunday 15:30.

spots.name: Tomohon Market
spots.desc: Traditional Market, Fresh Market, and Extreme Market (the latter is where they sell various exotic meat such as dogs, bats, snakes). It is called 'extreme" for a reason. If customer buys an animal alive, it will be slaughtered on the spot. Not for the faint-hearted. Come in the morning before 08:00 if you want to see the Extreme Market, it gets quiet after 10:00.

spots.name: Bird watching
spots.desc: Several incredible birds can be found in Mount Mahawu and Mount Lokon in Tomohon and in the other parts of North Sulawesi, such as Rufus Bellied Eagle; Brown Cuckoo Dove; Mountain White Eye; Dark Fronted White Eye; Scarlet Honey-eater; Crimson Crowned Flowerpecker; Sulawesi Spotted Goshawk; Sulawesi Serpent Eagle; Bay Coucal; Yellow Bellied Malkoha; Superb Fruit Dove; Citrine Flycatcher; Streaky…

spots.name: Grand Central Supermarket
spots.desc: The first supermarket in Tomohon, very close to Bethesda Hospital. Selling many kinds of daily needs as well as fashion, computer, multimedia, and so on.

spots.name: Cool Supermarket
spots.desc: Very nice supermarket in southern Tomohon. Selling many kinds of daily needs such as vegetables, herbs, fruits, and the other stuffs, as well as fashion, books, mechanical tools.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Tomohon, Walian - Tomohon Selatan

spots.name: Multi Mart Tomohon
spots.desc: A popular supermarket chain with restaurants and arcade on the upper floor.

spots.name: Tomohon Market
spots.desc: Sell various kinds of vegetables, meat, spices, herbs, fish, meats, fruits, flowers, clothes. Comprises of the Fresh Market, Traditional Market, and Extreme Market (where they sell various exotic meat such as dogs, bats, snakes).

spots.name: Gecko Art
spots.desc: This is one of the souvenir shops in Tomohon. Various kinds of souvenirs are displayed in this small shops.

spots.name: BLPT Kaaten
spots.desc: Locates in Kaaten, Matani 1 - Central Tomohon, BLPT is a coconut wood and arenga palm production. They make various kinds of furniture such as tables, chairs, desk, cupboards, beds, and small items like toys, and also knockdown houses from coconut wood.

spots.name: Gloria
spots.desc: The best pig ribs in the city. A full meal of white rice, 3 pig ribs (costellata), braunebonen (red beans) soup and vegetable only cost Rp 15,000.

spots.name: Risoma Restaruant
spots.desc: The best Minahasan cuisine. It is located out of Tomohon city, and unfortunately the restaurant is hard to achieve just by microlet service. The menu includes Pangi, Acar, Tinorangsak (pork cooked in bamboo), RW (dogmeat), Paniki (fruit bat meat), Braunebonen (red bean soup), Sayor pait (bitter vegetable), and many more.

spots.name: Heng Mien Restaurant
spots.desc: The famous Minahasan cuisine restaurant in Tomohon. Unfortunaley, this restaurant is also located out of Tomohon city on the road to Manado. The menu are almost all the famous of the Minahasan cuisine such as RW, Paniki, Pangi, Sayor Pait, Acar, and so on. To get here, you can charter a mikrolet, the fare starts from Rp 75,000 per trip, or ask the hotel to arrange the dinner here.

spots.name: RM Mie Pangsit Mas Topan Arema
spots.desc: A famous Javanese restaurant in Tomohon. It served mie ayam, bakso Malang, nasi goreng, tahu telor and so on.

spots.name: Fort Patua
spots.desc: A bigger fort complex on the west of the island. Two abandoned cannonade at the back of the complex, which is also the viewpoint.

spots.name: Fort Nata
spots.desc: A small fort on the east of the island. You could find an old well and a grave.

spots.name: In front of Waha Town
spots.desc: Beware of currents, and rather hire a local boat driver to watch over you.

spots.name: Hoga Island
spots.desc: It can be reached by boat from Ambeua. The boat from Ambeua can only leave at high tide.

spots.name: Coral stretch just east of Pantai Hongaha
spots.desc: There is also a World War II ship wreck in that section. Be aware of strong waves sometimes!

spots.name: Close to the Wakatobi Dive Resort on Pulau Tolandona
spots.desc: Extremely diverse sea life and one of the best snorkel spots on Wakatobi! Be aware that you don't enter the premises of the Wakatobi Dive Resort though. This is a tricky one - you must first take a local ferry from the Waitii Ferry Port and then head to Pulau Tolandona. It is also possible to take your rental scooter on the ferry. After you arrive on the Lamanggau Bajo Village, you then follow…

spots.name: One Melangka Beach
spots.desc: Maybe not top-notch for snorkelling, but a very scenic public beach indeed for swimming.

spots.name: Rafflesia Arnoldii

Try coconut drink in a hard shell mixed with mangrove syrup.Spend the time by walking over the wooden track for at least 900 metres, seeing endangered Natuna Island surili known by local as kekah monkey/kekah, tracking the…

spots.name: Setai Island

spots.name: Old Town of Penagi

Even if you don't bring BPJS card, the hospital will bill the prescription and services in a reasonably price rather than private hospital in most metropolitan areas

spots.name: Bingin
spots.desc: A small, attractive surf beach reached by steep paths and stairs through the cliffside settlement. It is famous for its reef break, sunset views and compact beachfront setting, but access, facilities and nearby businesses have changed rapidly following enforcement action against unlicensed cliffside development in 2025. Check conditions locally, especially if travelling with luggage, children or…

spots.name: Nyang Nyang Beach
spots.desc: One of the Bukit’s most scenic and least developed long beaches, backed by dramatic cliffs and reached by a steep descent. The reward is a wide sweep of pale sand, powerful surf and a more untamed atmosphere than the main resort beaches. Bring water, wear suitable footwear for the stairs and do not swim in rough conditions.

spots.name: Green Bowl Beach
spots.desc: A small, secluded cove below Pura Batu Pageh, reached by a long, steep stairway. It has white sand, limestone caves and clear water, but facilities are limited and the climb back up is demanding. Better for fit visitors seeking a quiet, adventurous stop than for families or a casual all-day beach visit.

spots.name: Warung Bu Tika
spots.desc: Indonesian food, choose buffet-style and pay based on what you took. The staff speak enough English for you to ask what things are. Between the jackfruit, tofu, tempeh, and vegetables, vegetarians should have no trouble, but there's plenty of meat too.

spots.name: Atlas Pearl farm
spots.desc: The main farm of Atlas Pearls is on the coast in Penyabangan, east of Pemuteran. While there is a show room and sales area, one can visit the oyster hatchery and watch an interesting video explaining the pearl farming process. One can also observe the hatching process.

spots.name: Museum RA Kartini
spots.desc: Jepara is the birthplace of national hero Raden Adjeng Kartini, a pioneer in the area of education for girls and women's rights. It tells the story of her life, and displays artefacts.

spots.name: Gerbang Kudus Kota Kretek
spots.desc: Modern gate to the city, built to resemble a tobacco leaf and colorfully illuminated at night. A city landmark.
spots.addr: Jl. AKBP Agil Kusumadya No.160, Jati

spots.name: Van Der Wijck Fort
spots.desc: Built in 1818, it is named after the Dutch soldier Van Der Wijck. It was used by the Dutch during the Java War against Prince Diponegoro. However, it is unclear what the main function of the fort was, because there is some argument that it was used for logistics and military training. Now, there is a park and two swimming pools around the fort.

spots.name: Purworejo Railway Station
spots.desc: The heritage inactive railway station was built by the Dutch East Indies company, Staatsspoorwegen in the end of the 19th century.

spots.name: St. Joseph's Catholic Church
spots.desc: A Dutch church built in the early 1900s, this church was the center of missionary activity in Ambarawa.
spots.addr: Jl. Mgr. Soegijapranata, No. 56, Panjang, Ambarawa, Semarang, Jawa Tengah 50614

spots.name: Banaran 9 Coffee & Tea
spots.desc: Serve hot and iced both coffee and tea. Operated by state-owned, PTPN 9. There is a coffee factory and Museum Kopi Banaran (Banaran coffee museum).

spots.name: Bledug Kuwu
spots.desc: A mud volcano. It continuously eruptions of salty mud at regular intervals, about every 2 or 3 minutes.

spots.name: Sendang Sikucing Beach
spots.desc: Bustling beach featuring swimming, sunbathing, picnicking & fishing, plus a nearby park & mini zoo.

spots.name: Pabrik Gula Cepiring
spots.desc: A sugar factory was inaugurated in 1835. There are also some old locomotives that are no longer in operation.

spots.name: Ngempon Temple
spots.desc: A complex of Hindu temples. Surrounding the temple, there is a waterfall called Curug Grenjeng-Ngempon and also hot spring baths.

spots.name: Willem II Fort
spots.desc: Monumental Dutch colonial-era fortress from the 18th century.
spots.addr: Jl. Gatot Subroto, Dliwang, Bandarjo, West Ungaran

spots.name: Giyanti Treaty Monument
spots.desc: There are large trees and stones as witnesses of the Giyanti agreement in 1755 which divided the Mataram Sultanate into the two kingdoms of Yogyakarta and Surakarta.

spots.name: Sondokoro Agrotourism
spots.desc: A park at Tasikmadu sugar factory with a playground, climbing wall, aquarium, aviaries, and a water park. You may ride old sugarcane steamed train there.
spots.addr: Jl. Mangkunegara Bojonegara, Nglande Wetan, Ngijo, Kec. Tasikmadu

spots.name: Alun-Alun Klaten
spots.desc: Energetic recreational park featuring fountains, sports fields, food vendors & festivities.

spots.name: Prigi Beach
spots.desc: Sandy bay beach with rock formations, a fishing harbour, and views of forested mountains.

spots.name: Patuk Gebang Beach
spots.desc: The high wave hitting the rock is one of the main attractions.

spots.name: Sanggrahan Temple
spots.desc: A Buddhist temple which is a relic of the Majapahit Kingdom, built around 1350 AD.

spots.name: Giri Kedaton
spots.desc: A site in the form of a pesantren (traditional Islamic school) was founded by Sunan Giri. This site is on the hill which was founded in 1487.
spots.addr: Jl. Sunan Giri XIII, Pedukuhan, Kebomas

spots.name: Pari Temple
spots.desc: This temple was built in 1293 Saka (1371 AD). This stone is a relic of the Majapahit era during the reign of King Hayam Wuruk (1350-1389 AD).

spots.name: Yosowilangun Railway Station
spots.desc: An inactive station was opened in 1927 by Staatsspoorwegen and closed in 1986.

spots.name: Kong Miao Confucian Temple
spots.desc: This temple consisting of three buildings, namely the blessing temple (Qi Fu Dian), the great prophet (Da Cheng Dian), and the sacred altar (Tian Tan). Da Cheng Dian is a rectangular building consisting of two floors with a Chinese-style design, the ground floor is used as an office and also a library, while the upper floor is used as a place for worship. Qi Fu Dian is an square building…

spots.name: Bird Park
spots.local: Taman Burung Taman Mini Indonesia Indah
spots.desc: For bird lovers, there is a Bird Park which has more than 1,500 species. Visitors can also learn about various types of birds.

spots.name: The Flame of Pancasila Monument
spots.desc: This monument commemorates the declaration of the five basic principles (pancasila) of Indonesia on 1 June 1945.

spots.name: Contemporary Art Gallery
spots.desc: It hosts changeable thematic contemporary art exhibition. The building also houses the park's merchandise store

spots.name: The Archipelago Colossal Stage
spots.desc: A miniature of Indonesia country in a huge lake. It has artificial islands that mimics the actual big islands of Indonesia: i.e. Sumatra, Java, Kalimantan, Sulawesi, and Papua. The lake has a dancing fountain attraction named Tirta Menari (dancing waters). When the night comes, the fountain is combined by a water screen that projects nine selected Indonesian folklores, thus making the combination…

spots.name: Saudjana Viewing Tower
spots.desc: It's an observation tower at the west of the archipelago lake. You can easily look at the replicas of the Indonesian archipelago on the lake from on top of the tower, or you can also see other parts of the park around you.

spots.name: Walahar Dam
spots.desc: The Walahar Dam construction project was started in 1923 by the Dutch with the supervision of a water expert from the Netherlands named C. Swaan Koopman. Walahar Dam was put into use on November 30, 1925. It is the dam of the Citarum River.

spots.name: Munduk Waterfall
spots.desc: These falls are impressive and really roar in the wet season. A spot that is little visited, despite being perhaps the most impressive accessible falls on the whole island. You will have to park your car or motorbike somewhere on the side of the road and then walk down something like 500 meters through a narrow path. You will not see the waterfalls from the road. Next to the waterfalls you will…

spots.name: Bali Handara Kosaido Golf and Country Club
spots.desc: At an altitude of 1,142 metres and surrounded by green mountains, crater lakes and ancient forest, this Peter Thompson designed course is considered one of the very best in Asia.

spots.name: Bali Treetop Adventure Park
spots.desc: The park includes six main circuits that stretch from tree to tree, as well as nets, Tarzan Jumps, and bridges. Each run also features "Flying Fox" zip-lines of up to 160 metres, providing heart-pounding thrills to guests as they fly through the air. Two circuits are designed for young children from 4 years old.

spots.name: Bedugul Traditional Market
spots.desc: Bedugul is the highland garden of Bali, producing lots of cool climate fruits and vegetables. In the market here you can find strawberries plus a myriad of tropical fruits, vegetables, corn and orchids. This is a great place to buy exotic spices, with mixed gift packs being especially popular. There is also an art section of the market with lots of handicrafts.

spots.name: Bedugul Lake View
spots.desc: An Indonesian restaurant on the way down from the market to Lake Bratan. Serves Ayam Taliwang and other tasty local dishes.

spots.name: Ulun Danu Restaurant
spots.desc: The main restaurant at Ulun Danu Beratan attraction. Established among the beautiful scenery of Beratan temples and close to Beratan Lake enable to giving you a wonderful panoramic view of garden, temples and the lake simultaneously. Serving Western, Indonesian also Chinese foods. A'la Carte and Buffet menus as your option. Fish, chicken duck, and vegetarian food on request.

spots.name: Ngiring Ngewedang
spots.desc: Very good value Indonesian food in a restaurant with views to die for. They also process local coffee beans here and will be happy to show the facility and sell you green or freshly roasted beans. An excellent option for lunch if you want to get away from the crowds in Bedugul.

spots.name: Restaurant Batukaru
spots.desc: Must-visit restaurant if you're driving the road around Jatiluwih. It has a stunning view over the rice terraces and also a close-view rice terrace right beside it. Expect big tourist coaches to stop here in the early afternoon, but you'll most likely be the only visitors between 3PM and 4PM. There's a buffet, but you can also just order from the menu. After eating, head up stairs through the…

spots.name: Roti Bedugul
spots.desc: Bakery in Candi Kuning famous for good quality bread, croissants and Danish pastries.
spots.price: small bakeries Rp 5,000, cookies bag Rp 50,000

spots.name: Strawberry Hill
spots.desc: Mountain roadside restaurant serving tasty Indonesian favourites and soups, salads, chicken and burgers - and strawberries. When the air is cool, cozy up beside a real log fire. Also comfortable mid-range accommodation here.
spots.addr: 5 minutes to the south of Bedugul at the KM48 marker

spots.name: Strawberry Stop
spots.desc: Stop by this strawberry farm for snacks, milkshakes and of course, strawberries. Unless you are brave, give the strawberry wine a very wide berth.

spots.name: Warung Anugerah
spots.desc: Simple and cheap rice, but nothing special. It's often the only restaurant open after 8PM on the main square in Candikuning.

spots.name: Warung Kopi Bukit Hexon
spots.desc: An organic food restaurant situated just north of Lake Buyan.

spots.name: Mini Zoo
spots.desc: Many kinds of birds (cockatoo, lory, hornbill), reptiles (python, tortoise, skink) and mammals (slow lori, palm civet, porcupine).

spots.name: Shell Museum
spots.desc: An odd little place and a very charming one to boot. Exactly as it says, shells.

spots.name: Coconut Yoga
spots.desc: A quiet shala in the forest, a little set back from the main road, at Kelapa Cottage. Daily yoga classes, retreats and yoga teacher trainings. Classes are accessible to all levels.

spots.name: Apneista Yoga and Freediving School
spots.desc: Beachside yoga sala and training in Jemaluk bay. Most days there is a 90-min Asana class in the evenings and often in the mornings. Workshops in pranayama and meditation.

spots.name: Adventure Divers Bali
spots.desc: PADI and SSI dive shop offering a full range of courses. Instructed by David, an Englishman who moved to Amed with Liselotte, his Belgian wife. Together they run the diving school and Geria Giri Shanti Bungalows. Great couple that makes you feel at home.

spots.name: Amed Dive Center
spots.desc: Full range of PADI courses, fun dives, diving and sailing trips. English, French and German speaking.

spots.name: Amed Fun Divers
spots.desc: SSI dive school offering dive courses and fun dives. The school is teaching every course level including dive master and instructor training courses.They have a variety of dive sites to choose from in Amed and Tulamben areas. They also offer night dives and dive safaris. The school is devoted to helping the young local people get into the diving industry and increase their environmental…
spots.price: Price for fun dives starts at €45 for 2 dives, depends on the entry methods and distance

spots.name: Amed Scuba
spots.desc: Offers diving tours around Bali, local Amed-based dive-safaris and yoga classes. Instruct all PADI courses from Open Water to Divemaster. German, English and French speaking. Instructed by a German biologist.

spots.name: Baliku Dive Center
spots.desc: PADI and SSI dive shop offering a full range of courses. Managed by a Belgian, courses and dives are available in French, English, German and Indonesian.

spots.name: Baruna Dive Bali
spots.desc: Founded in 2012. PADI and SSI dive centre. French management with professional and local staff, multilingual courses and dives. Courses are available in French, English and Spanish. Small groups of maximum 4 divers per instructor or guide.

spots.name: Ecodive Bali
spots.desc: Amed's oldest and largest dive centre, established in 1997 and run by a PADI Master Instructor/SSI Instructor Trainer with over 35 years professional experience. Daily dive trips and a full range of courses from Open Water to Instructor. Languages served: English, French, German, Dutch and Indonesian. Responsible and sustainable tourism policies; pledges US$1 from every dive and US$10 from every…

spots.name: Euro Dive
spots.desc: PADI dive centre established in 1999. English, French, German and Indonesian speaking. Associated with Hidden Paradise and Coral View cottages.

spots.name: Fusion Freedive and Yoga
spots.desc: Freediving school - offers freedive courses in AIDA, Pure Apnea and SSI systems, coaching, depth and pool trainings for all levels, monofin clinic, freedive and spearfishing gear rental, spearfishing courses and trips, fun-dives, manta trips, wreck diving, breath-hold clinic for surfers, freedive/spearfishing shop.

spots.name: Jukung Dive Bali
spots.desc: PADI 5-star Gold Palm Resort run by a Dutch family. They speak English, French and Dutch. The 2 swimming pools are used for instruction sessions but are also a place to relax. 3 bungalows with sea view available, A/C, hot water and a restaurant with very good food. Bali Dive Safaris is part of Jukung Dive and offers dive safaris to dive spots in Bali.

spots.name: La Bila Dive Resort
spots.desc: PADI dive centre that offers a range of dive courses from Discover Scuba Diving to Dive Master. The staff and instructors are very friendly, helpful and competent. They offer fun dives to a wide variety of dive sites around Amed and Tulamben. It has a great restaurant and accommodation with A/C and hot water available. Languages spoken: English, German, Indonesian and Spanish.

spots.name: Bali Reef divers
spots.desc: PADI dive shop managed by 2 Belgians, offering a full range of courses, in Amed & Tulamben with adjacent accommodation - Amed : Puri Wirata dive resort & Tulamben : Bali Reef divers Tulamben. Dives in the Amed, Tulamben and Kubu area and lessons in French, Dutch, German, Indonesian, Balinese and Chinese.

spots.name: Ocean Sun Dive Resort Tulamben
spots.desc: SSI Diamond Dive Resort with 10 bungalows and the restaurant "Chops and Hops". Daily dives, full range of dive course from Open Water Diver till Instructor and Technical Diving is offered by the Dive Resort.

spots.name: Aqua Dive Paradise
spots.desc: A small, locally-owned place with friendly, professional local staff and negotiable prices. They also have three new, clean, affordable, fan-cooled rooms available (a decent breakfast included).
spots.price: Rp 250,000 per dive or Rp 350,000 per night dive (Aug 2011)

spots.name: Dive Concepts, Bali
spots.desc: PADI dive centre offering local fun dives around Amed and on the USAT Liberty wreck. Day trips to Nusa Penida and Menjangan Island, multi-day dive safaris and courses from Discover Scuba Diving to Assistant Instructor. Foreign instructors and divemasters emphasis speaking French and English but also offer courses in Italian, Spanish and German. The shop has multiple locations; in addition to the…
spots.addr: Jl Raya, Amed & @ Pura Aries Hotel, Tulamben

spots.name: PLOUF Diving
spots.desc: SSI dive center driven by two French instructors within a family atmosphere. Full range of courses from Discover Scuba Diving to Instructor. Large swimming pool available for dive training and relaxing. English, French, Spanish and Indonesian speaking. Offering local fun dives and night dives around Amed and Tulamben (including USAT Liberty wreck) and multiple Macro spots for photography lovers.

spots.name: Warung Enak
spots.desc: Popular family-run warung serving Indonesian, Balinese and Western dishes, including fresh seafood. Good-value and frequently busy.

spots.name: Warung Bobo II
spots.desc: Fresh fish and local cuisine. Located at the edge of the waves, popular at sunset.

spots.name: Warung Pantai I
spots.desc: Small beachfront warung serving inexpensive Indonesian and Balinese dishes, including curries, nasi campur and fresh seafood.

spots.name: Warung Segara
spots.desc: Authentic atmosphere, tiny restaurant, one woman show, varied menu all items under Rp 20,000, locally made arak, take away half litre bottle Rp 15,000.

spots.name: Warung Sabar
spots.desc: Friendly family-run warung serving Balinese and Indonesian food, including fresh seafood, grilled fish, sate lilit and pork dishes. Good value.

spots.name: Warung Osin
spots.desc: Small warung specialising in Indonesian food and fresh seafood. Popular for grilled fish, fish curry and homemade sambal.

spots.name: Warung Ketut
spots.desc: Small family warung serving fresh seafood and Indonesian dishes, including grilled fish and pork satay. Excellent value.

spots.name: Warung Agung Amed
spots.desc: Friendly family-run restaurant serving Balinese, Indonesian and Western food, with fresh seafood including grilled mahi mahi and tuna.

spots.name: Green Melon Warung
spots.desc: Small family-run warung serving freshly prepared Balinese and Indonesian food, including curries, sate lilit, seafood and vegetarian dishes. Good food at reasonable prices.

spots.name: Chops & Hops Restaurant
spots.desc: The restaurant in the Ocean Sun Dive Resort is popular for the steaks and burgers, curries, Indonesian dishes, and home-made ice cream.

spots.name: Jukung Dive
spots.desc: Nice little restaurant operated by the diveshop. Very friendly and well trained staff. Excellent local and western food.

spots.name: Titi Sedana
spots.desc: Small family restaurant with 4 tables serves absolutely delicious food. They have 2 bungalows as well. Free WiFi.

spots.name: Wawa Wewe
spots.desc: Restaurant with bar serving cocktails, attached to Wawa Wewe I bungalows. On Tu and Sa a band is provided. On W and F traditional Legong Dance is performed.

spots.name: Garam Cafe
spots.desc: Part of Hotel Uyah Amed&Spa. Built behind the salt production fields and uses salt production as a theme aiming to preserve traditional salt production and explaining the production process to visitors. Souvenir shop, billiard tables, table tennis and salt panning. Western, Indonesian, Balinese and regional Asian style menu. Free Wifi

spots.name: Amed Cafe
spots.desc: A cafe attached to the 23 bungalows of the same name. Serves fresh seafood, Balinese food and international style food. Public internet access is available.

spots.name: Galanga
spots.desc: Popular Asian-fusion restaurant with a varied menu and attractive setting. Good choice when you want something beyond the usual Indonesian and Western fare.

spots.name: Restaurant Bukit Segara
spots.desc: Elegant restaurant overlooking the sea, serving seafood, Indonesian and international dishes. Known for its slow-cooked duck and attractive oceanfront setting.

spots.name: Barong Cafe and Restaurant
spots.desc: Balinese, Indonesian and international cuisine. Provides free pick up and drop-off around Amed area.

spots.name: Sails
spots.desc: A very good, more upscale restaurant in great headland setting. Modern and clean with an extensive well thought out menu. The restaurant specialises in Western food but includes Indonesian favourites. Offers a free pick up and drop off service anywhere in the Amed area.

spots.name: Rasta Bar
spots.desc: A chill-out shack that fronts the beach with a reggae atmosphere, live music every night and a large selection of cheap, delicious and fast-served dishes and drinks. Free wifi. Owner Rusthi can provide various services.

spots.name: Bukit Komala Sunrise Point
spots.desc: Check out the sunrise from hill, north side of the village. At night, you can see the view of the town of Amlapura and the sea activities from the Lombok Strait from the top of the hill.

spots.name: Budakeling Terraced rice fields
spots.desc: View of the terraced rice fields, with the best point on the north side of the village.

spots.name: Pande Mas
spots.desc: The activity of making traditional rings and necklaces with Balinese characteristics in the Pande Mas community.

spots.name: Pura Dalem Budakeling
spots.desc: At certain times from March to April you can see a wide variety of cultures staged at the temple.

spots.name: Pura Dalem Saren
spots.desc: Once every two years can see the activities of the fire war on the south side of the village.

spots.name: Samsara Living Museum
spots.desc: A place to study and see the life and activities of Balinese people in the past.

spots.name: Warung Cemara Cader
spots.desc: Chinese fusion food, Capcay, Nasi Goreng, Rica-rica chicken.

spots.name: Blue Lagoon Beach
spots.desc: A great beach for snorkeling, despite the narrow one hundred meters length. The beach is unique in color; the sandy beach is not always white, but sometimes changes to rather black. If the current comes from the west, the beach will be white, but if the current comes from the east, it will be black and white. The coral reef goes right up to the shore and is very pretty with clown fishes and small…

spots.name: Bias Tugal Beach
spots.desc: A beautiful white sandy beach and the best beach in Padang Bai. It's wider than Blue Lagoon Beach and good for swimming, though the currents can be strong. There are about five warungs, serving simple Indonesian dishes, juices and beer. From the path to the beach, you should be able to see the largest mountain on Bali, Mount Agung — a powerful sight.

spots.name: Pura Silayukti
spots.desc: Once the home of the great Hindu sage Empu Kuturan and dating back to the 11th century, making it one of the oldest extant temples on the island.

spots.name: Absolute Scuba
spots.desc: Teaches both PADI and SSI up to and including instructor course, in English, German, Italian, Russian and Indonesian. 3-m deep training pool, classroom, 22 air conditioned rooms, 1 speedboat, 1 small boat.

spots.name: Geko Dive Bali
spots.desc: Five star PADI dive resort and TecRec dive center. Offers a wide range of courses and fun dives. Active in the community and with environmental projects. Maximum of four divers to each divemaster. This ratio is reduced if requested or needed. Dive groups are welcome. Courses taught in English, French, German, Spanish and Indonesian. 2 speedboats, 1 large outrigger boat and a variety of smaller…

spots.name: Paradise Diving Bali
spots.desc: German dive center offering daily dive safaris and PADI courses.

spots.name: Spiral Spa @ Bloo
spots.desc: Padang Bai's only spa facility. A wide range of massages, also facial & body care, hair treatments and organic spa products. Shuttle service within Padang Bai to pick up guests.

spots.name: Cafe Kerti
spots.desc: Kerti is a not so good budget place to stay, but serves good food in their restaurant. Nice views from the second floor.

spots.name: Martini's Warung
spots.desc: Set in the corner of the main square (where buses drop off), Martini's Warung is a great little local treat. With budget prices Martini's offers authentic local food, often cooked by Martini herself. Tourists come to chat to Martini and each-other over beers and home cooked meals. Mie Goreng is highly recommended.

spots.name: Omang Omang Cafe
spots.desc: Opposite the reggae bars, Omang Omang Cafe is one of the best restaurants in town. Serves Western and Indonesian cuisine, very good BBQ selection and various cocktails. Many home grown organic ingredients, home made cakes and ice cream. Also a regular venue for live music.

spots.name: Puri Rai Restaurant
spots.desc: A decent restaurant serving Indonesian food including locally caught fresh sea food.

spots.name: Babylon Reggae Bar
spots.desc: A tiny reggae bar with very friendly staff. They will make you feel this is your place, and you can enjoy live music with everyone in the bar.

spots.name: Kinky Reggae Bar
spots.desc: A tiny reggae bar with extremely friendly staff. Their Long Island Ice Teas are good value.

spots.name: Ozone Café
spots.desc: A long established institution in Padang Bai, the food is good, especially the pizzas. It is a lively place for a drink and a good place to swap information with fellow backpackers.

spots.name: Sunshine Bar
spots.desc: Another friendly music bar. The owners are almost too friendly and will sit and chat with you about life for hours. Instruments are available and they love nothing more than getting the whole bar singing, playing guitar and bongos.

spots.name: Nuanu Creative City
spots.desc: A large space featuring art installations, a restaurant, a beach club, an event hall, an alpaca petting zoo, and more. As of December 2024, entrance is free. Free shuttle buses operate within the premises.

spots.name: SAKA Museum
spots.desc: A major new museum devoted to Bali’s living cultural heritage, with immersive exhibitions on Nyepi, the Saka calendar, the subak irrigation system and the philosophy of Tri Hita Karana. Large ogoh-ogoh figures, ritual objects, multimedia displays and the SAKA Dome make this the Bukit Peninsula’s best rainy-day cultural attraction. Book online or check current ticket prices before visiting.

spots.name: Balangan
spots.desc: A broad, scenic beach beneath low cliffs on the Bukit’s west coast, known for its long left-hand surf break and sunset views. It remains more relaxed than some of the peninsula’s main resort beaches, but is no longer a little-known escape; expect surf visitors, beach warungs and limited parking in busy periods. Swimming can be hazardous when the surf is up.

spots.name: Dreamland
spots.desc: A developed resort beach on the Pecatu coast with pale sand, surf breaks and a range of commercial facilities nearby. It is popular with surfers and day visitors, though the surrounding development means it has a very different character from the Bukit’s more isolated coves.

spots.name: Padang-Padang
spots.desc: A truly lovely beach with a big surf break offshore. Accessed from a stepped pathway on the north side of the obvious bridge 3 km north of Uluwatu Temple heading back towards Pecatu. The white sand beach here is a little bit narrow at the highest of tides but is otherwise very nice indeed.

spots.name: Suluban Beach
spots.desc: West of Padang Padang, Suluban is a dramatic reef-and-cave beach reached by descending through cafés, shops and narrow limestone passages below the cliffs. It is less open and more tucked away than Padang Padang, though no longer reliably quiet, especially around sunset and during peak surf season. At lower tide, the beach extends among rocks, coral and seaweed, making it an interesting place to…

spots.name: Gunung Payung Beach
spots.desc: Accessed by descending a long flight of concrete steps from the hilltop Gunung Payung Temple, this secluded beach rewards adventurous visitors with soft white sand, dramatic rock formations, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Unlike the more developed beaches nearby, Gunung Payung remains relatively untouched—there are no beach clubs or major facilities, just the sound of waves and the…

spots.name: Tirtha Wedding Chapel
spots.desc: This impressive chapel was designed by leading architect Glen Parker and is stunningly located on the cliff top above Nyang Nyang Beach. The architecture is very modern and the chapel is essentially a series of glass-walled triangular pavilions surrounded by reflection pools. Full wedding planning services offered.
spots.addr: Jl Raya Uluwatu,Banjar Dinas Karang Boma, Pecatu

spots.name: New Kuta Golf Course
spots.desc: This golf course is stunningly located on top of the cliffs above Dreamland beach and is a top class venue. It is part of the highly controversial Pecatu Graha Indah development that was the brainchild of former dictator Soeharto's son Tommy. The dubious acquisition methods of the land here by his development company from the traditional landowners is still a huge bone of contention in Bali.…
spots.addr: Kawasan Pecatu Indah, Jl Uluwatu, Pecatu

spots.name: Ayutaya Spa Bali
spots.desc: Located with a view of Garuda Wisnu Kencana Culture Park. All treatment rooms have are equipped with a locker, large bathtub with hot shower and two jacuzzis.
spots.addr: Jl. Bingin Sari, Pondok Belong Jimbaran

spots.name: Yoga Searcher Bali - Organic Spa
spots.desc: Offer 100% organic products for their spa menu (lulur full body scrub, manicure, pedicure, nail color, organic body waxing, traditional Balinese massage, wheat grass facial, and yogi surf burn relief. They also offer an infra red sauna and an herbal steam sauna.

spots.name: Cafe Moka
spots.desc: Excellent coffee shop and cafe in Ungusan village close to the main Nirmala Supermarket. Bread and pastries are fresh daily and salads are excellent. Free wireless internet for customers.

spots.name: Jiwa Juice Internet Cafe
spots.desc: A full service internet cafe and wireless hotspot. Serves breakfast, sandwiches, salads and smoothies. Also acts as a business centre, has a bulletin board and is a well known local surfies meeting spot. Jiwa means soul in Indonesian.

spots.name: Yeye's
spots.desc: Pizzas and other reliable fare is served at this simple cafe close between Padang-Padang and Suluban. Beware that it is sometimes closed all day in the off season.

spots.name: Single Fin
spots.desc: Sprawling multi-level bar/club with postcard sunset views high above the surf at Uluwatu beach. Trendy, with prices and patrons to match.

spots.name: Serenity Yoga Canggu Bali
spots.desc: Beginner, intermediate and advanced yoga classes. No reservation required, bring towel.

spots.name: OM Beach Lounge Restaurant
spots.desc: International style food in a large bamboo construction, nice sunset views. Organic market on Sundays, child friendly environment.

spots.name: CRATE Cafe
spots.desc: A space where good music, good food, good coffee and good people meet, and create good vibes.

spots.name: Gypsy Kitchen+Bar
spots.desc: Gypsy Kitchen and Bar serves fresh cocktails and food from famous Canadian chef Robin Filteau-Boucher.

spots.name: Te’Amo Gastro-Bistro
spots.desc: Contemporary European restaurant in Canggu serving wood-fired pizzas, fresh handmade pasta, seafood, and Mediterranean-inspired dishes. The bar offers cocktails, mocktails, craft beers, and more than 30 wines by the glass. Indoor and outdoor seating available.

spots.name: HUBBLE Restaurant Canggu
spots.desc: Multi-level restaurant and lounge in Berawa serving international and Ukrainian dishes, cocktails, pastries and shisha, with a rooftop area.
spots.addr: Jl. Subak Sari, Berawa, Tibubeneng, Kuta Utara, Badung, Bali, Indonesia

spots.name: Hookah Place Canggu
spots.desc: Restaurant and lounge in Canggu serving Japanese and international dishes, cocktails and shisha, with comfortable seating and a PS5 gaming area. Copy
spots.price: Around Rp 250,000 per person; varies by order
spots.addr: Jl. Batu Mejan No.108, Canggu, Kuta Utara, Badung, Bali 80363, Indonesia

spots.name: Alkaline Restaurant
spots.desc: Vegan raw western Indonesian cafe and juice bar. Offers healthy snacks and meals.

spots.name: People's
spots.desc: Probably the best sushi and tapas in Canggu. Nice selection of cocktails and gorgoous view over the rice paddy. Live jazz band every Saturday.

spots.name: The Beach House
spots.desc: Popular with local expats and visitors. Sunset views and a variety of eating areas. Tables spill out onto a beach side area, live music, seafood barbecues.

spots.name: Sukerti's Garden Restaurant
spots.desc: A garden restaurant in the Pantai Berawa Area close to the surf spot. Western and Asian food for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Free WiFi, surfer shower and a garden.

spots.name: Finns Beach Club
spots.desc: A beachfront venue, featuring 4 pools, 9 bars, 6 restaurants and amazing sunsets.

spots.name: The Lawn
spots.desc: Opening directly onto the black sanded beach of Canggu, with the soundtrack of the waves rolling in, a beach lounge for guests to share eats and drinks, relax and dance.

spots.name: Museum Situs Purbakala
spots.desc: Architectural excavations in the Gilimanuk area have revealed the earliest evidence of human habitation in Bali. This small museum houses a collection of skeletons and artifacts found near Cekik, which are thought to be 3,000-4,000 years old. Worth a visit if you have an hour to kill before jumping on a ferry.

spots.name: Hatten winery
spots.desc: The area around Pulaki village just east of Pemuteran is full of vineyards and is the centre of the grape growing industry in Bali. The local Hatten winery produces a variety of white and red wines. There is a visitor and tasting centre.

spots.name: Easy Divers
spots.desc: A PADI dive resort with more than 10 years' history in Pemuteran.

spots.name: Reef Seen Aquatics
spots.desc: First established dive operator that offers guided dives and PADI courses from absolute beginner upwards. Very active in marine conservation: runs their own turtle breeding and release programme, for example. Attractive beach-side divers' accommodation.

spots.name: Sea Rovers
spots.desc: Offer a full range of fun dives and courses. PADI accredited.

spots.name: Pataba Library
spots.desc: A private library and a small museum of Pramoedya Ananta Toer, a Nobel Prize nominee for literature, an Indonesian author of novels, short stories, essays, polemics, and histories of his homeland and its people. He got many awards including UNESCO Madanjeet Singh Prize, PEN/Barbara Goldsmith Freedom to Write Award, and many more.

spots.name: Replika Gajah Purba Blora
spots.desc: Ancient elephant fossil replica museum. There is a replica of Elephas hysudrindicus that was found in Sunggun village, Kradenan district of Blora in 2009. The ancient elephant died mired in the sediment of Bengawan Solo river, 200,000–300,000 years ago.

spots.name: Jipang Palace
spots.desc: In this palace, you can learn a lot about the history of the palace and the story of Arya Penangsang.

spots.name: MC Edupark
spots.desc: A water playground, facilities for sports, ATV, paintball, and archery. Near the park, there is also a golf course.

spots.name: Warung Makan Bu Nur Spesial Ikan Jendil
spots.desc: Serves fried ikan jendil (shark catfish) with lalap (boiled veggies) and sambal. The fish is taken from Bengawan Solo river.

spots.name: Troso village
spots.desc: Known for its loom weaving: jacquard and copies of East Nusa Tenggara styles. There are showrooms along the main street, some of which have workshops. There are also small workshops in some of the houses. Some batiking is also done.

spots.name: Kartini Beach
spots.desc: There are boats to Karimunjawa and Panjang Island. It also has the Kura-Kura Ocean Park, a turtle-shaped building that contains a large aquarium, fish spa, and educational attractions for children.
spots.price: Rp5,000–Rp 7,500 entry, Rp12,500–Rp17,500 for Kura-Kura Ocean Park

spots.name: Panjang Island
spots.desc: White sand beach and clear, shallow water. It is the location of the grave of Waliyullah Al Habib Abubakar bin Ahmad bin Syekh bin Yahya Ba'alawi, also known as Syekh Abubakar, who is said to be one of Prophet Muhammad's descendants.

spots.name: Arty's Design Collection
spots.desc: Furniture and homewares. Retail and trade. Worldwide shipping. Some imported Turkish items.

spots.name: Woven and batik textiles
spots.desc: Various showrooms along the main street of the village. Some have looms and some households are weaving at home.

spots.name: Furniture and wooden homewares
spots.desc: Many of Jepara's streets are lined with showrooms of furniture and wooden homewares, appealing to both domestic and international tastes. The showrooms serving the international export market will be mainly focussed on showcasing their products for wholesale buyers, but some of them do sell retail, so go ahead and ask. Most will be able to take orders, especially for larger quantities, and can…

spots.name: Yam Yam Resto
spots.desc: Thai and Western. Oceanside, good for sunsets but no beach. Swimming pool. Serves beer. A little hidden away. If you enjoy it, there's a branch in Jogja.

spots.name: Cipto Roso
spots.desc: Famous for the Jepara specialty called pindang serani, a clear, fresh, spicy fish soup.

spots.name: Es Gempol Pleret Panggang
spots.desc: Es gempol is a specialty cold beverage from Jepara. It is a rice flour dough with coconut milk soup, sugar, and ice.

spots.name: Joglo Pencu Kudus
spots.desc: A building made of teak wood with a tile roof called atap pencu, decorated with simple carvings typical of Kudus Regency, a blend of styles from Javanese (Hindu), Persian (Islam), Chinese, and European (Dutch) cultures.

spots.name: Lentog Tanjung
spots.desc: Serves lentog, a rice cake with sayur lodeh (veggies soup) and tofu.

spots.name: Opor Sunggingan
spots.desc: Serves opor bakar, a specialty chicken dish from Kudus. It is eaten with a spoon made from banana leaves called suru.

spots.name: Pindang Kudus Pak Sulichan
spots.desc: Nasi pindang is one of the local specialties, like most food in Kudus, it contains no bovine meat (which is considered sacred). It is rice with chicken or water buffalo served with godhong so/melinjo (gnetum leaves).

spots.name: Ratanavana Arama Temple
spots.desc: There is a Gold-plated reclining Buddha statue in this Buddhist temple.

spots.name: Montel Waterfall
spots.desc: A single waterfall with a height of about 50 m. The water flow is very clear and clean, out between the towering cliffs.

spots.name: Waduk Gunung Rowo
spots.desc: Fishing using a bamboo raft. There is mujair fish (Oreochromis mossambicus), carp, tilapia, and other freshwater fish.

spots.name: Waroeng Keboen Iboe
spots.desc: A garden restaurant which is a pleasant escape from the heat of the lowland plains.

spots.name: Ancient Boat Punjulharjo
spots.desc: The Punjulharjo boat has a length of 17.9 meters with a remaining width of 4.6 meters. Estimated from the year 660-780 AD. It was discovered in July 2008 by local residents.

spots.name: Roemah Martha Tilaar
spots.desc: Museum in a colonial-style building from 1920. It was Marta Tilaar's house. The home of a nationally-famous beautician.

spots.name: Waduk Sempor Gombong
spots.desc: Large reservoir dam surrounded by forested hills, popular for boat trips, biking & running trails.

spots.name: Sempor Dam
spots.desc: An embankment dam on the Sempor River. It is used for irrigating paddy fields, flood control, and hydroelectric power, generating 1MW of electricity. It was built in 1967, but was breached in the same year, causing a flood that killed a thousand people. It was rebuilt in 1978. It is possible to go fishing and to explore the dam by boat.

spots.name: Alun-alun Kebumen
spots.desc: The large grassed square found in the centre of all Javanese towns, the focus of local government and always popular for recreation.

spots.name: Loano Mosque
spots.desc: The mosque was founded by Sunan Geseng, a student of Sunan Kalijaga, in 1472. As is typical of mosques in Java, Loano Mosque uses wooden pillars as building supports. The main pillar in the main part of the mosque is more than 500 years old. While the terrace was built around 1872.

spots.name: Pasar Baledono Purworejo
spots.desc: Food, snacks, fresh fruits, and vegetables, also household and kitchen utensils.

spots.name: Kajen Market
spots.desc: the largest traditional and semi-modern market in Kajen city.

spots.name: Prambanan Museum
spots.desc: North of Candi Lara Jonggrang is a poorly displayed museum laid out in a series of small houses connected by walkways. Explanations are minimal, mostly only Indonesian text, but entry is free so you might as well take a look.

spots.name: Ramayana Resto
spots.desc: Serving Indonesian food buffet with Rp75,000 per pax. Usually visited in late afternoon to nightfall for a stop over dinner while waiting for Prambanan Ramayana Ballet performance next door at 19:30. The restaurant is set against the majestic flood-lit Prambanan temple as the background which make a romantic setting for dinner while waiting for the Javanese dance performance.

spots.name: Eling Bening
spots.desc: A resort on a hilltop at Bawen, with a stunning view of the Mount Telomoyo, Merbabu, Lake Rawapening and Ambarawa.

spots.name: Banaran Agrotourism Park
spots.desc: Operated by state-owned PTPN 9. You can do camping, horse-riding, swimming, and riding an ATV or Jip (off-road vehicle) around the coffee plantation.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Bawen - Solo Km 1.5, Bawen

spots.name: Nature Gumuk Reco
spots.desc: Do flying fox, walk beside the cliff and try the giant swing.

spots.name: Gecok Tlogo
spots.desc: Originating from Tuntang, a district on the east side of Rawa Pening Lake. Gecok kambing is the lamb in a spicy soup.

spots.name: Serabi Ambarawa
spots.desc: Serabi Ngampin is an Ambarawa pancake in sweet coconut milk soup.

spots.name: Warung Makan Mbak Toen
spots.desc: Try Pecel keong, Javanese salad in peanut sauce with cooked freshwater snail, and Kripik belut (Swamp-eel chips).

spots.name: Eva Coffee House
spots.desc: A coffee shop whose coffee comes from a local farm of the same owner. They also sell gudeg manggar (young coconut flowers stewed with coconut milk and some herbs).

spots.name: Makam Sunan Kalijaga
spots.desc: Sunan Kalijaga was one of the Wali Songo (Nine Saints) who helped spread Islam throughout Java.

spots.name: Api Abadi Mrapen
spots.desc: An eternal flame monument. A constantly burning flame is used to light torches for religious & sporting ceremonies.

spots.name: Gedung Papak
spots.desc: Gedung Papak is a building that was built in 1919 as the headquarters of the Dutch army.

spots.name: Kedung Ombo Reservoir
spots.desc: Kedung Ombo Reservoir is one of the major reservoirs in Indonesia. It is on the border of three regencies in Central Java Province, namely Grobogan Regency, Sragen Regency, and Boyolali Regency.

spots.name: Pecel Gambringan Mbak Yayuk
spots.desc: Serves pecel Gambringan. Also, some side dishes like peyek (Indonesian cracker) and gorengan (fritter).

spots.name: Warung Makan Farchat
spots.desc: Try Momoh, a delicacy beef dish of Kaliwungu district, Kendal.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Timur Kaliwungu, Pandean, Krajan Kulon, Kaliwungu

spots.name: Curug Lawe
spots.desc: Actually two waterfalls close by each, Curug Lawe and Curug Benowo (curug is Javanese for waterfall). The first part of the hike is along the side of an irrigation canal, followed by a section across the fairly rocky ground. There is the chance to see black Javanese leaf monkeys. They are usually active in the early morning.

spots.name: Curug Semirang
spots.desc: A couple of hours hike through nutmeg plantations and natural forest. There is a pool so you can swim there. Some small food stalls have been set up near the waterfall.
spots.addr: Gintungan hamlet, Gogik village, Ungaran Barat district

spots.name: Umbul Sidomukti
spots.desc: There is a swimming pool that offers beautiful views of the mountains since it is 1,200 m above sea level. You can do flying fox, rappelling down the valley, ATV, trekking, and horseback riding.

spots.name: Mawar Camp
spots.desc: One of the gateways to reach Mount Ungaran peak (2,050 masl).

spots.name: Medini tea plantation
spots.desc: Located on the slope of Mount Ungaran. You also may trail to the waterfall Curug Lawe Secepit.

spots.name: Pasar Bandungan
spots.desc: The traditional market of Bandungan. It is clean and neat, unlike dirty markets in other parts of Indonesia. Primarily sells vegetables, fruits, and local foods.

spots.name: Kampoeng Djowo Sekatul
spots.desc: Serves Javanese cuisine. The restaurant uses the Javanese traditional house, Joglo.
spots.addr: Jl. Sunan Katon No.99, Sekutis, Margosari, Limbangan

spots.name: Pemancingan Suharno 1
spots.desc: Eat grilled or fried freshwater fish taken freshly from fishing in their ponds. It is served with sambal and lalapan (raw fresh veggies).

spots.name: Tahu Bandungan Oom Shin
spots.desc: Eat Bandungan fried tofu call Tahu serasi. Also, try their Susu kedelai (Soy milk).

spots.name: Warung Sate Kelinci Pak Kenthus
spots.desc: Eat a specialty of Bandungan district, Sate kelinci (Rabbit satay).

spots.name: Kolam Renang Tirto Argo Siwarak
spots.desc: Public swimming pool with refreshing water from Mt. Ungaran.
spots.addr: Jl. Tirto Argo, Blanten, Nyatnyono, West Ungaran

spots.name: Tahu Baxo Ibu Pudji
spots.desc: Tahu bakso is tofu with beef or fish dough inside. It is specialty of Ungaran, Semarang Regency.
spots.addr: Jl. Jend. Sudirman No.156, Setiggen, Langensari, West Ungaran

spots.name: Mie Ayam dan Bakso Bang Krebo
spots.desc: Serve mie ayam (chicken noodles soup) and bakso (meatball soup). Also, they have lemonade and iced tea for drink.
spots.addr: Jl. Ahmad Yani, Sidomulyo, East Ungaran

spots.name: Soto Gudangan Bu Kusnin
spots.desc: Soto gudangan or abbreviated as Sogud is Ungaran type of soto (traditional Indonesian soup). It is a beef soup rice with veggies and grated coconut.
spots.addr: Jl. MT Hariyono, Sidomulyo, East Ungaran

spots.name: Virgin Cake & Bakery Ungaran
spots.desc: There are various breads and cakes. Also, they have some traditional Javanese snacks.

spots.name: Kopi Klothok Sadar
spots.desc: Serve arabica and robusta coffee. Also, they have hot ginger drinks, tea, and hot chocolate.

spots.name: Delingan Dam
spots.desc: Do jogging or cycling around the dam. The view is Mount Lawu.

spots.name: Umbul Manten
spots.desc: A verdant natural spring. Set amid towering trees, this natural pool with clear water is a popular spot for swimming.
spots.addr: Jalan Janti Boto, Boto, Wunut, Tulung

spots.name: Soto Bebek Bu Heri
spots.desc: Klaten specialty dish, soto bebek (duck meat soto) and soto kering (dry soto).
spots.addr: Jl. Jend. Ahmad Yani No.65, Senden, Danguran, Wedi

spots.name: Tumpang Lethok Mbak Riyanti
spots.desc: Serves nasi tumpang lethok, white rice, vegetables, boiled eggs and doused with a sauce made from a mixture of tempeh, chili, coconut milk, and spices.

spots.name: Taman Edukasi Ndayu Park
spots.desc: Kid-oriented recreational complex with a compact zoo, a waterpark, and a natural green space.

spots.name: WM. Botok Mercon Mbah Wiro
spots.desc: Serves botok mercon, a spicy shark catfish wrapped in banana leaves.
spots.addr: Jl. Gemolong-Sragen, RT.03/RW.02, Nglombo, Tenggak, Sidoharjo

spots.name: Lesehan Mbah Pine
spots.desc: Serves Javanese food such as trancam (raw veggies with grated coconut), bubur gurih (savory porridge), sate gembus (Javanese okara/tofu dregs satay), etc.
spots.addr: Jl. Ahmad Yani, Kutorejo, Sragen Tengah

spots.name: Hastana Mosque
spots.desc: A mosque that was built in Kartasura palace, the capital of Mataram Sultanate in 1680–1745. There is also a fortress near the mosque.
spots.addr: Jl. Krapyak Raya, RT.01/RW.10, Dusun II, Kartasura

spots.name: Cagar Budaya Bangunan Pabrik Gula Gembongan Kartasura
spots.desc: Art deco style building of inactive sugar factory was built in 1899.

spots.name: Taman Pakujoyo
spots.desc: Small park with a children's play area and a pond for boat rentals, plus kiosks selling cold drinks.

spots.name: Pandawa Water World
spots.desc: This kid-friendly waterpark has swimming pools, slides & playgrounds, plus artificial waves.
spots.addr: Komplek Pandawa Jl. Cemara Raya Gedangan, Dusun 2, Grogol

spots.name: Pasar Ir. Soekarno Sukoharjo
spots.desc: A traditional market serves daily necessities, spices, and food ingredients.
spots.addr: Jl. Jend. Sudirman, Sukoharjo, Larangan Kulon

spots.name: Imogiri royal graves
spots.desc: Graveyard of the Sultan Agung and his descendants, the Yogyakarta and Surakarta royal families. It was damaged during an earthquake in 2006 but has been reopened.

spots.name: Leksa Ganesha Batik Gallery
spots.desc: This gallery just outside Yogyakarta offers something a little different to batik collectors: a chance to visit the studios of renowned batik artists and villagers and meet them as they work. Social entrepreneur Tatang Wibowo started this project in 2011 as a way to continue supporting local artists in an innovative tourism model. It's a rare opportunity to make a connection with the people who…
spots.addr: Jl Parangtritis 8.5 km, Tembi, Timbulharjo, Sewon

spots.name: Tabubu Ethnic Music Shop
spots.desc: They make and sell traditional musical instruments (flutes, drums, stringed instruments, etc.) from various parts of Indonesia. The shop is in the owner's house, and he is very friendly - just drop by and you can see and try the instruments he has on display. If you want to buy, however, you will have to make a custom order, as the instruments on display are not for sale. The prices are pretty…
spots.addr: Jl Saman, Block 2, no. 167, Rt. 06, Bangunharjo

spots.name: Bakmi Jawa Mbah Giman
spots.desc: Serves mie jawa (Javanese noodle soup or stir-fried) also nasi goreng, nasi godog (soupy rice), and magelangan (fried rice mixed with noodle).

spots.name: Mie Lethek Mbah Jumal
spots.desc: Serves mie lethek, noodles made from gaplek (dried cassava).

spots.name: Mie Pentil dan Mie Iris Bu Nur
spots.desc: Serves yellowish mie pentil, made from tapioca. It has chewy texture. Also mie iris, also made from tapioca but the dough is sliced ​​using a knife.

spots.name: Soto Pak Marto
spots.desc: A local delicacy - usually eaten for breakfast - of beef-based soup served with rice (mixed in or separate). Offal is included unless you specifically ask for beef only. Fried offal, to be eaten with kecap manis, is delicious.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Janti No.336, Modalan, Banguntapan

spots.name: Warung Bumi
spots.desc: Part of the Bumi Langit Institute, a charitable community-based permaculture foundation. The café is part of their outreach, offering mostly local dishes made with locally-grown and organic produce. In a beautiful open joglo building perched high on an escarpment overlooking Jogja in the distance. Farms tours available. Some local produce - jams and syrups - available to buy.
spots.price: From around Rp60,000 for a plate of nasi campur and a fruit juice
spots.addr: Jl Imogiri Mangunan Km. 3, Desa Giriloyo, Wukirsari

spots.name: Jiwajawi Jogja
spots.desc: Serene restaurant in the middle of greenery and villages, serving unique local cuisine.
spots.addr: Jl. Tugu Gentong Jl. Fasco Village, Salakan, Bangunjiwo, Kec. Kasihan, Kabupaten Bantul

spots.name: Kedai Rukun
spots.desc: Indonesian-Javanese authentic warung experience. Access only by bike and walk (no car).
spots.addr: Gg. Darussalam, Kadipiro, Ngestiharjo, Kec. Kasihan, Kabupaten Bantul

spots.name: Haia Space
spots.desc: Small coffee shop with artisan bakery. One of local favourite to work from cafe.
spots.addr: Jl. Jend. Sudirman No.38, Bantul Wr., Bantul, Kec. Bantul, Kabupaten Bantul

spots.name: Ngrenehan Beach
spots.desc: A small bay surrounded by rocky hills that has fascinating panorama and swirling waves hitting white sandy beach and rocky edge of the hills. The local fishermen can prepare fresh or grilled fish for visitors.

spots.name: Krakal Beach
spots.desc: Krakal has sandy beaches, which attracts with white beaches, jagged rocks and high waves. But, you have to cut back on the facilities and the swimming facilities, since the full force of the Indian Ocean usually does not allow more than splashing around on the beaches.

spots.name: Jogan Beach
spots.desc: Oceanfront destination featuring a viewing platform by a waterfall flowing onto a rocky shoreline.

spots.name: Tanding Cave
spots.desc: Cave known for striking rock formations, with raft rides available on an underground river.

spots.name: Pindul Cave
spots.desc: Pindul Cave is a cave formed by karst with an underground river located about 7 kilometres south of the city centre Wonosari, Gunung Kidul. It is known for the cave tubing that visitors can do and is done with tires that float above the underground river inside the cave, this activity is known as cave tubing.
spots.addr: Jalan Goa Pindul Gelaran 2, RT.3/RW.16, Bejiharjo, Karangmojo

spots.name: Gondola Pantai Timang
spots.desc: Crossing the sea to a rock where the local fisherman looks for the lobster.

spots.name: Saptohoedojo Art Gallery
spots.desc: This sprawling complex houses an utterly eclectic collection of Indonesian art, ranging from abstract modern paintings and batik shirts through gamelan instruments and stuffed tigers to Papuan tribal totems complete with the skulls of vanquished enemies. Everything is for sale and previous customers, pictures of whom are proudly pasted on the walls, include Pope John Paul II and the Dalai Lama.…

spots.name: Ayam Geprek Bu Rum
spots.desc: The pioneer of ayam geprek (smashed fried chicken with spicy sambal).

spots.name: Jejamuran
spots.desc: Spacious restaurant & shop with a leafy terrace. All dishes are mainly made from mushrooms.

spots.name: Kindai
spots.desc: This breakfast place serves delicious soto Banjar (a chicken soup from Banjarmasin, South Kalimantan) with a choice of chicken wing and/or egg. They also have nasi kuning (yellow rice) and sate ayam (chicken satay).

spots.name: Mie Ayam & Soto Pak Mus
spots.desc: Try special Jogja style of mie ayam, called mieyago which stands for mie ayam goreng (stir-fried chicken noodles).

spots.name: Pecel Solo
spots.desc: Offers a large selection of Solo style foods like Pecel Solo (vegetables with peanut sauce), Sego Liwet (steamed rice with sweet curry sauce), Nasi Kebuli (pungent rice with roasted lamb), and Bebek Goreng (fried duck Solo style). Rp10,000-30,000.

spots.name: Soto Sawah Pak Slamet
spots.desc: A local chicken soup outlet 5 km west of Jogja, open morning-afternoon.

spots.name: Warung Vegetarian Somayoga
spots.desc: Vegetarian/vegan organic food. Typical Indonesian food. Very tasty.

spots.name: Kopi Klotok
spots.desc: Known for authentic Javanese home-cooked breakfast, especially for its pisang goreng (banana fritters) and black coffee.
spots.addr: Jalan Kaliurang No.KM.16, Area Sawah, Pakembinangun, Kec. Pakem

spots.name: Ayam Goreng Suharti
spots.desc: A very popular Javanese fried chicken restaurant, the recipe remains a secret.

spots.name: Androwino Bistro
spots.desc: The all-day dining restaurant offering Continental and Asian cuisine in a relaxed modern Javanese setting. On the top floor of Sheraton Mustika Yogyakarta Resort & Spa where at the entrance of the restaurant guests will be welcomed with a big painting of the grandfather of the hotel’s owner named Sampean Dalem Ingkang Sinuhun Kandjeng Susuhunan Pakoe Boewono X, 1896 – 1939 (King of Solo) and…

spots.name: Gadjah Wong
spots.desc: Serves French, Italian, Indian, Chinese and Indonesian. Divided into 3 zones: Country, Javanese and Colonial, each is lavishly decorated and themed with live music. In the Javanese zone, you can hear Javanese gamelan music, while the Colonial zone has a live jazz band.

spots.name: Boshe VVIP Club
spots.desc: Packed every night. Free entry for girls. Live music and DJs.

spots.name: Liquid
spots.desc: Packed every night and free entry for ladies. Unclear If the drinks are fake or genuine, but they are cheap. Live music and DJs.

spots.name: Filosofi Kopi Jogja
spots.desc: Popular cafe shop based on an Indonesian renowned fiction book which later adapted into movies.
spots.addr: Jl. Pandhawa No.001/17, Tegal Rejo, Sariharjo, Kec. Ngaglik

spots.name: Couvee
spots.desc: Local favourite to-go coffee, serving kopi susu gula aren (Indonesian style milk coffee with palm sugar).
spots.addr: Jl. Kaliurang No.Km 5.2, Manggung, Caturtunggal, Kec. Depok

spots.name: Kayangan Api
spots.desc: It is an eternal flame spot nestled among the teak forest, 21 km south of Bojonegoro. In the west side of Kayangan Api, there is a mud pond containing sulphur which in the past was used by Mpu Kriyo Kusumo to make and craft Keris (daggers - often with a curved blade and highly ornamented). Local people still believe that the fire is sacred and use it for important ceremonies.

spots.name: Hok Swie Bio Confucian Temple
spots.desc: It is the only Confucian temple in Bojonegoro and famous for its Dragon Head design. Many Confucians visit the temple during Chinese new year celebration and other religious ceremonies.

spots.name: Bojonegoro Town Square
spots.desc: Alun-alun Bojonegoro is the heart of Bojonegoro with greenery, field, fountains, jogging track, and many sport facilities. The iconic giant stone called Watu Semar sits on the east side of the square. The great mosque and government offices are located nearby.

spots.name: Wana Wisata Dander
spots.desc: Do forest trekking, camping, and many activities in outbound park also swimming in the waterpark.

spots.name: Pawon Seafood & Resto
spots.desc: Serves mainly seafood and other cuisines as well with a good vibe at low prices. The main dishes are about Rp13,900-Rp69,900.

spots.name: Pacal Reservoir
spots.desc: A reservoir is surrounded by trees, farmland, and features boating. It was inaugurated in 1933.

spots.name: Teksas Wonocolo
spots.desc: Traditional oil drilling. More than a century old. Using teak wood rig.

spots.name: Tirta Wisata
spots.desc: A park and recreation center with a swimming pool and a tennis court.

spots.name: Pujasera Kebonrojo
spots.desc: A local open-air food court featuring various stalls. Great for families as it includes a playground. Ayam Geprek to local noodles and snacks.

spots.name: Nasi Pecel Bu Djiah
spots.desc: A legendary breakfast and lunch spot serving "Nasi Pecel" (traditional vegetable salad with spicy peanut sauce). It is famous for its vast array of side dishes, including fried empal (sweet beef), lungs (paru), and beef tongue.

spots.name: Sate Kampret Jula-Juli
spots.desc: A famous night-time culinary icon. "Kampret" (bat) refers to its late operating hours. It serves very spicy beef satay accompanied by savory lodeh (vegetable curry) or rawon soup. A must-visit for spice enthusiasts.

spots.name: Nasi Kikil Redjo Agung
spots.desc: It features tender beef tendon (kikil) in a rich coconut milk soup, served on a traditional banana leaf (pincuk).
spots.addr: Jl. KH. Hasyim Asy'ari No.144, Diwek

spots.name: Rawon Rosobo
spots.desc: Renowned for having the best Rawon (black beef soup) in East Java. The signature feature is the thick and tender chunks of "Empal" (fried beef) served with the soup.

spots.name: Soto Dok Seger
spots.desc: A Javanese beef soup experience where the vendor bangs the soy sauce bottle against the table, creating a loud "Dok!" sound. It offers a savory clear broth with bean sprouts and tender beef.

spots.name: Tahu Pong Gloria
spots.desc: A popular spot for "Tahu Pong" (hollow fried tofu). Served crispy with a signature spicy dipping sauce.

spots.name: Essemu Coffee & Kitchen
spots.desc: Lifestyle cafe. It offers a cozy interior, outdoor seating on the second floor, and a wide variety of espresso-based drinks and refreshments. Good Wi-Fi and plenty of power outlets.

spots.name: TJ Coffee Lab
spots.desc: A 24-hour coffee shop in an old colonial-style building, a former sugar mill staff house. Known for its affordable prices and historical "vintage" atmosphere.

spots.name: Narastory Coffee
spots.desc: Another reliable 24-hour spot with a spacious outdoor area. It is very popular with local students and is often crowded during weekend nights. The service is fast, even when it is busy.

spots.name: STMJ & ITB Simpang 3
spots.desc: A local night spot serving STMJ (Milk, Egg, Honey, and Ginger). The "ITB" in the name refers to "Ika Teki Bakar" (grilled snacks). It is a traditional way to enjoy the night air while staying warm with ginger-infused drinks.

spots.name: Kuliner Malam Jombang
spots.desc: This street becomes a lively night market after 5 PM. While mainly for food, it's the best place to find local drinks like "Es Teler", "Susu Segar" (fresh milk), and "Kopi Ijo" from various street vendors at very low prices.

spots.name: Museum Koes Plus
spots.desc: Koes Plus is a legendary Indonesian band from Tuban. The collection of Koes Plus tapes and photos is very complete there.

spots.name: Warunge Mak Dah
spots.desc: Serves kare rajungan and other Javanese seafood dishes. There is also a beef dish called becek sapi (beef in spicy coconut milk soup) and a chicken dish kare ayam (chicken in curry soup). The other menu are pepes (steamed meat in banana leaves) using squid eggs pepes telur cumi, ariid catfish eggs pepes telur manyung and blue swimmer crab eggs pepes telur rajungan.
spots.price: Rp60,000 for kare rajungan, Others around Rp20,000
spots.addr: Pasar Baru Tuban, Jl. Gajahmada No.5, Kebonsari, Sidorejo

spots.name: Warung Sate Menthok Sor Sawo
spots.desc: Serves sate menthok, also becek menthok (muscocy duck in coconut milk soup). Eaten with carbs, rice, or sego jagung (mashed maize).
spots.addr: Jl. Mojopahit Gg. Buyung No.180, RT.01/RW.03, Krajan, Karang, Semanding

spots.name: Benteng Panaroekan
spots.desc: The ruins of a 19th century fort built by the Dutch. There is not much left, only some walls 1-5 meters high. It is located near a cemetery.

spots.name: Tugu Portugis
spots.desc: A 3-meter-tall monument which is the last remnant of Portuguese presence in the area. It is located in the middle of rice fields. The Portuguese came and built a trading post on the eastern bank of Sampeyan River in the 16th century.

spots.name: Sukarno Museum
spots.desc: This quite well-maintained and well-known museum and library (known locally as Istana Gebang) is in the house where Sukarno lived as a young boy. It is full of Sukarno memorabilia, papers, photographs etc and is useful to visit in conjunction with a call to the grave (makam) site. (Price of entry: by contribution.)
spots.addr: Jl Sultan Agung 69, Blitar, East Java

spots.name: Tambakrejo Beach
spots.desc: This is an extensive and attractive 10 km stretch of white sand beach that is more often than not virtually deserted. It is not safe for swimming though.

spots.name: Ngulungwetan Beach
spots.desc: The combination of beaches, meadows, coconut trees, and buffaloes. It is also good for picnics and camping.

spots.name: Senden Ngerit Cave
spots.desc: A cave with natural rock formations and a small waterfall. You may feel the environment like in the Flintstone cartoon series.

spots.name: Pelang Beach
spots.desc: A beach that offers two natural beauties at once, those are a beach and a waterfall.

spots.name: Niyama Dam
spots.desc: The dam was built during the Japanese occupation in Indonesia.

spots.name: Dadi Temple
spots.desc: Dadi Temple is one of the architectural works of the Majapahit era, built around the end of the 14 century to the end of the 15 century, during the last reign of King Hayam Wuruk.

spots.name: Wonorejo Dam
spots.desc: A reservoir surrounded by woods, trails, and viewing platforms on trees.

spots.name: Wajakensis Museum
spots.desc: The Nandi statue, the Agastya statue, the Garudeya statue, and a replica of the ancient human skull fossil of Wajak Man (Homo Wajakensis), the two fossil human skulls discovered near Wajak, a village in Tulungagung, Indonesia (then Dutch East Indies) in 1888/90. The first was found on 24 October 1888 by mining engineer B.D. van Rietschoten who sent it to paleontologist Eugène Dubois who…
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Boyolangu No.km 4, Gedang Sewu Selatan, Gedangsewu, Boyolangu

spots.name: Nangkula Park
spots.desc: Large park with flower gardens, food stalls, plus views of rice paddies.

spots.name: Warung Surockboyo Bakso Lobster
spots.desc: Serves bakso lobster, meatball soup with boiled fresh lobster.

spots.name: Padang Golf Petrokimia Gresik
spots.desc: A golf course. There are also a tennis court and a swimming pool.

spots.name: Alun-Alun Lamongan
spots.desc: A city square with a park, Ferris wheel, grounded GAF Nomad aircraft, and also a kid's playground. You may see Masjid Agung Lamongan (Great Mosque of Lamongan) which was built in 1908.

spots.name: Museum Mpu Tantular
spots.desc: It was opened in 1937. The collection is about historical and geological stuff, numismatics, arts, archaeology, and many others.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Buduran - Jembatan Layang, Bedrek, Siwalanpanji, Buduran

spots.name: Delta Fishing
spots.desc: Family recreation complex with ponds for fishing, kids' swimming pools, and food stalls.
spots.addr: Jl. Mbah Sholeh No.1, Prasungtambak, Prasung, Buduran

spots.name: JFC (Jember Fashion Carnaval)
spots.desc: A spectacular event fashion carnival on the street. Usually taking place in August or September yearly, it lasts 3 days, with the peak on Sunday. Followed by around 600 participants witnessed by hundreds of thousands of spectators, it has been recorded in the MURI (Indonesia Museum Record) as a demonstration with the longest catwalk 3.6 km.

spots.name: Gudeg dan Pecel Lumintu Jember
spots.desc: In Jember, gudeg is mixed with pecel, the combination is called gudeg pecel.

spots.name: Sari Utama
spots.desc: The best Chinese restaurant in Jember. Brash, bright and noisy as you would expect but excellent food.

spots.name: Warung Bu Katun
spots.desc: Rawon with rice, beef empal (flattened beef), special brown sauce/sambal, and bumbu Bali (Bali spices).
spots.addr: Jl. Ade Irma Suryani No.13, Rogotrunan

spots.name: Markas Coffee
spots.desc: A coffee shop by the lake Ranu Klakah and you may see the view of Mount Lemongan.

spots.name: Rawon Sakinah
spots.desc: Javanese food, rawon (beef soup) and sate komo (beef satay).

spots.name: Rumah Makan Ikan Bakar Tanjung Pinang
spots.desc: Cheap local eatery with fresh fish and seafood, as well as Indonesian classics as nasi goreng.

spots.name: Surosowan sultan palace
spots.desc: Located in the once-prosperous kingdom of Banten, this royal palace was designed by a Muslim Dutchman Hendrick Lucas Cardeel and completed during the reign of the first sultan. Surrounded by a high brick wall, it served as a glorious residence from 1526 to 1808 and was equipped with an aqueduct connected to a reservoir. A major excavation in 1984 divulged the greatness of this exuberant palace.…

spots.name: Great Mosque of Banten
spots.desc: 16th century mosque, one of the few surviving buildings of the old Banten town. The minaret tower was built in 1632.

spots.name: Old Banten Archaeological Museum
spots.desc: Museum on the history of the town and the sultanate of Bandung, as well as Southeast Asian ceramics.

spots.name: Vihara Avalokitesvara
spots.desc: Buddhist monastery, and one of the oldest Chinese temples in Indonesia.

spots.name: Fort Speelwijk
spots.desc: Dutch fort built in 1682. The square-shaped fort is in good shape. Outside of the fort there is a Dutch cemetery.

spots.name: Labuan Fish Auction
spots.desc: The Labuan fish auction and fish market is one of the largest in the region, as Labuan has a large fishing port. It is of course possible to buy fish and seafood, but it is also interesting to see the trading on the market and the auction.

spots.name: Rumah Makan Bu Entin
spots.desc: Seafood and barbecue restaurant, also known for 'otak-otak' (grilled fish cake).

spots.name: Alun-Alun Pandeglang
spots.desc: The central town square of Pandeglang. It is one of the largest and most beautiful city squares in the province. The square features extensive grass fields, play areas for children, a lot of streetfood stalls, and a statue of a Javan rhinoceros. The Ujung Kulon National Park, in the regency of Pandeglang, is the only place where this endangered species can still be found.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Labuan / Jl. Mayor Widagdo

spots.name: Dapoer Iboe
spots.desc: Well-known restaurant and bakery with a wide range of Indonesian dishes. The specialty is gurame goreng cobek, or fried giant gourami fish with chili peppers.
spots.addr: Jl. Kyai Haji Mohammad Idrus No. 2

spots.name: Alun-Alun Rangkasbitung
spots.desc: The town square of Rangkasbitung. You can relax at tree-covered areas of the square or buy snacks from street vendors.

spots.name: Rangkasbitung Indah Plaza
spots.desc: Shopping centre with a large supermarket and several other shops, banks, and cafés.

spots.name: Rumah Makan Aqaba
spots.desc: Sundanese-style restaurant a bit out of town, with a beautiful garden.

spots.name: Mega Wisata Indonesia Icakan
spots.desc: The largest recreation park of the East Parahyangan region, with an extensive water park and other attractions, such as flying fox, pedalo, 3D cinema, horse-riding, tourist trains, etc.
spots.price: Entrance Rp5,000, additional fees per attraction

spots.name: Bebek Goreng H. Slamet
