spots.desc: Simple restaurant along the main road, serving fried duck as a specialty. Other dishes include fried chicken, tofu and tempeh, and various types of duck and chicken offals.

spots.name: Rumah Makan Pujaseda
spots.desc: Pujaseda Restaurant is one of the Sundanese food restaurants in Ciamis Regency, the exact location is on the Ciamis - Banjar highway. usually used as a resting location for car travel.A restaurant with a menu of Sundanese specialties which is quite a legend in the town centre of Ciamis, West Java. With a fairly large place and also a large parking area, this place can be an option for eating when…

spots.name: I'm You Cafe
spots.desc: Serves main course, beef, snack, pasta, and also hot/iced drinks.

spots.name: The Mountain Recreation Park
spots.desc: Water recreation park with several swimming pools and water slides.
spots.addr: Perumahan Pesona Alam Kuningan, Jalan Raya Cirendang

spots.name: Curug Muara Jaya
spots.desc: A waterfall of 73 metres high, near the western side of the Mount Ciremai National Park, surrounded by centuries old trees.

spots.name: Pananjung Pangandaran Nature Reserve
spots.desc: This natural reserva is nearby on a peninsula connected to the mainland by a narrow neck of land, so you can see sunrise at east of Peninsula (Pantai Timur or East Beach) and sunset at west of Peninsula (Pantai Barat or West Beach). About 80% of the nature reserve is secondary rainforest. A few hours can be spent here without the need for a guide, however, guides are available and can obviously…
spots.price: Rp20,000 for locals, Rp210,000 for foreigners (Rp310,000 on sundays+holidays)

spots.name: Green Canyon
spots.desc: Journey through some truly wondrous jungle - rich in massive teak trees, palms, various hanging vinery and the shrill sounds of extensive bird-life. The canyon is apparently a couple of hundred metres long, but it is only safe for visitors to venture the first hundred. At the end of the passable section, the opportunity arises to jump from a 5 metre high stalagmite formation rising from the…

spots.name: Learn to surf
spots.desc: A friendly surf school with low negotiable prices but safe practices. An instructor is always watching you while you surf. Surf lessons schedules depend on the tide, so book your course the day before so you don’t miss it. Tours to the Green Canyon and/or treks to local tribal communities are eagerly offered. They average about 150,000 per day.
spots.price: Surf lesson (2 hours) Rp 150,000, board rental Rp 50,000-75,000

spots.name: Mungil Steak House
spots.desc: Offers the same sort of menu as Bamboo, plus — not surprisingly — a steak menu.

spots.name: Relax Restaurant
spots.desc: offers European, Chinese and Indonesian food, plus - recommended menu; homemade brown bread and ice cream. Offers also yoghurt and muesli/cereals. Price for Indonesian food 35,000. Western food from 40,000 -

spots.name: D.E. Coffee
spots.desc: serves espresso coffee (although pricey) and tasty sandwiches as their speciality, but really it's recommended for its proximity to Steak House and wifi enabled internet cafe (Rp250 /minute). A perfect day well spent.

spots.name: Saung Miring coffee shop
spots.desc: 24 hours free internet access / free wi-fi, coffee and tea, pancake, sandwich and toast

spots.name: Bintang Timur
spots.desc: Fresh seafood and other. Small restaurant along the beach in front of the Futsal (boulevard turn right)the food is different and delicious. If you are in mood you can sing karaoke or eat under the moon.

spots.name: Fish market
spots.desc: There are many restaurants in the fish market. You choose the seafood which is then cooked for you.

spots.name: Jacko Bar
spots.desc: along the west beach near the other cafés and restaurants. Often has offers live music and DJ parties.

spots.name: Silent Bar or Diam Cafe
spots.desc: Next to Jacko bar. The owner cannot hear or speak but he speaks a lot in his own language and can be understood by all foreigners :)

spots.name: Mungil Cafe
spots.desc: or Steak House. Nice place to drink and listen to the live music

spots.name: Cactus Garden
spots.desc: A plant conservation area in the form of a greenhouse with a round roof resembling a cactus tree. The cactus park has a collection of 32 cacti and succulents from all around the world, such as Gimnogayumus Hibotan and Avage Parasana from Belgium, Melocactus and Echimocatus Grusonii from Japan, Cleistocatus stausil and Opuntia Microdasys from Mexico, and many other rare cactus plants.

spots.name: Jasmine Garden
spots.desc: After the designation of jasmine (Jasminum Sambac) as the national flower of Indonesia in 1994, the Jasmine Garden was built. This garden with an area of cultivates various kind of jasmine, and several other ornamental plants.

spots.name: Bekisar Park
spots.desc: A place for various activities with bekisar chickens. Starting from cultivation, training, captive breeding, and incubating. Sometimes, national or international bekisar chicken competition was held in this area.

spots.name: Fresh Water Aquarium
spots.desc: Fresh Water Aquarium is the second largest freshwater and brackish themed aquarium in Asia. The aquarium has over 6000 animals from 126 species, including reptiles, amphibian, crustaceans, and fish.

spots.name: APEC inscription
spots.desc: The inscription contains the signatures from ten first ladies who accompanied them at a friendly meeting of leaders of countries following the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) conference in November 1994.

spots.name: Skyworld Indonesia
spots.desc: This place is a place to learn about space and astronomy, with some recreation in its main facilities, such as Planetariun, Space/Astronomy Tours, 5D Cinema, Laser Tag, Children Water Play, and Playground called Taman Among Putro.
spots.hours: Mon to Fri 09:00 to 17.00; weekend & holiday 08:00 to 17:00
spots.price: Monday to Friday Rp 70,000; weekend & holiday Rp 70,000

spots.name: Pondok Pecel Madiun
spots.desc: Madiun-style Pecel offered here has a sweet taste. For side dishes, you can choose from empal, tempe bacem, rujak cingur, ayam penyet, rawon, and empal goreng.

spots.name: Rumah Makan Bahari 354
spots.desc: This restaurant offers a variety of food menus such as meatballs, chicken noodles, chicken soup, beef soup, fried or grilled chicken. Fresh coconut ice is also available here.

spots.name: Ayam Kremes Cak Wandi
spots.desc: If you want chicken menu, you can stop here. The Ayam Kremes here is the main menu. In addition to the Ayam Kremes, this shop also offers a variety of other menus. It's delicious to eat here while sipping young coconut ice which is served directly from the coconut shell.

spots.name: Pasar Nusantara Sarinah TMII
spots.desc: It's a newly-opened food court that offers a variety of Indonesian cuisines from whole over the country. You can also enjoy delightful traditional drinks and beverages.

spots.name: Gama Ikan Bakar & Seafood
spots.desc: The dining area is very spacious and very suitable for family gathering. Various types of fish can be grilled here, such as carp, white snapper, rabbitfish, and groupers. In addition to fish, other seafood menus are also delicious, there are salted egg prawns, scallop with oyster sauce, and tarakan crab which can be cooked with butter sauce and black pepper. If you don't like seafood, there are…

spots.name: Rumah Kopi Nusantara
spots.desc: A coffee 'museum'. Take a sip of coffee while studying their history at the same time.

spots.name: Candi Blandongan
spots.desc: One of the other temple buildings that has been recovered and partly restored. The original function of the Candi Blandongan temple building remains unknown. In contrast to the Candi Jiwa, the Blandongan structure has stairs on all four sides.

spots.name: Situ Kamojing
spots.desc: Small man-made lake, a popular place to hang out or go fishing for locals.
spots.addr: Kamojing, off Jl. Kota Bukit Indah Raya

spots.name: Mal Cikampek
spots.desc: Largest shopping centre in Cikampek with a variety of shops and cafés, and a large supermarket.

spots.name: Karangsong beach
spots.desc: The nearest beach to Indramayu city. Many fishermen bring their fish and shrimp to the shore here. There is also a mangrove forest, that can be reached easily from the beach by joining the boat of a fisherman.

spots.name: Tirtamaya beach
spots.desc: This beach, about 15 km from the city, is popular among locals.

spots.name: El Shaddai Seafood Restaurant
spots.desc: A variety of fish and seafood dishes, as well as Indonesian classics such as nasi goreng fried rice.

spots.name: Tugu Rawagede
spots.desc: Commemorative monument with several sculptures, as well as the 'cemetery for the heroes of Rawagede' (Taman Makan Pahlawan Rawagede).

spots.name: Wonderland Adventure Waterpark
spots.desc: Water theme park with various water slides, swimming pools, etc.

spots.name: Monumen Kebulatan Tekad
spots.desc: Monument for the Rengasdengklok Affair and Indonesian independence.

spots.name: Rumah Sejarah
spots.desc: The house that was owned by Djiaw Kie Siong, where Soekarno was brought on 16 August 1945 after he was kidnapped. The house is now like a small memorial/museum, with old pictures, and furniture that was already there in 1945. The house has been moved about 150 metres to the east in 1957, because it was prone to flooding because of the nearby Citarum river.

spots.name: Rengasdengklok Market
spots.desc: Just like a conventional traditional market, groceries in the market building are selling foodstuff. But along the Rengasdengklok Market street, there are lots of store that sell various stuff such as medical supply and mobile phone.

spots.name: Serabi Hijau
spots.desc: The famous seller of Serabi Hijau in Rengasdengklok. On the sign outside the place it is indicated that no other brances will be opened, so if you want to try, you will have to go to Rengasdengklok.

spots.name: Zumartour Outbound & Gathering
spots.desc: Professional event organizer specializing in group activities, corporate gathering, and team-building packages. They offer adrenaline-pumping fun offroad tracks using Land Rover, refreshing tea walks, paintball, and scenic rafting trips along the natural rapids of the Ciwidey River. Complete packages include professional facilitators, safety gear, meals, and documentation.
spots.price: Packages from Rp120,000 to Rp250,000 per person

spots.name: De Foret
spots.desc: Restaurant/café with a nice garden, with various types of Indonesian food and fresh fruit juices. Along the main road near the entrance of the Kawah Putih.

spots.name: Picnic Dodol Garut
spots.desc: One of the most famous sellers of dodol Garut. You can buy many types of dodol. It is also possible to visit the factory, but then it is advisable to send an email beforehand.

spots.name: Kebun Begonia
spots.desc: Resembles Keukenhof, the tulip park in Lisse, the Netherlands, with many colourful flowers.

spots.name: Terminal Wisata Grafika Cikole
spots.desc: Do outbund activities such as riding flying fox, rope bridge walking, and playing paintball.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Tangkuban Parahu No.Km.8, Cikole

spots.name: The Lodge Maribaya
spots.desc: Ride on hot air balloon, zip bike, hang glider, sky swing, and sky tree.
spots.addr: Jl. Maribaya No. 149/252 RT. 03 / RW. 15 Babakan, Gentong, Cibodas

spots.name: Kampung Daun
spots.desc: Sundanese food. You eat at a hut in the middle of valley near a small waterfall and river. At night it's really amazing to walk along candlelit pathways. Eating out really means eating out here. The atmosphere here is enchanting and magical. Lots of trees, bushes and secluded "pondok" small huts for relaxing and food, cool as it is set in a valley with the sound of running water from the…
spots.price: About Rp50,000-100,000 for a main course
spots.addr: Villa Triniti complex, Jalan Sersan Bajuri KM. 4,7

spots.name: Warung Sate Kelinci Pa Sapri
spots.desc: Known for the sate kelinci or rabbit satay (skewers), the restaurant also has a few other dishes including chicken satay and goat satay, as well as fried noodles and rice.

spots.name: Serba Susu Lembang
spots.desc: One of the famous milk cafés in Lembang, selling also yoghurt, ice cream, pastries, etc.

spots.name: Museum Wisma Karya
spots.desc: Literally the 'Home of Creations' museum, in the city centre of Subang. The museum shows the history of the region from prehistoric times to the present, including the spread of Buddhism, Hinduism, and Islam in Java, the colonial time. The museum is in a 19th century Dutch colonial building.
spots.addr: Jalan Ade Irma Suryani Nasution No. 2

spots.name: Fort Hollandia
spots.desc: Initially, Fort Hollandia was founded in 1642 under the name Fort Lonthoir. Later it was renamed Fort Hollandia by Pieter Vlak. Fort Hollandia was established with the aim of monitoring the movement of the Banda people, and monitoring sea traffic, especially the nutmeg trade in the Lonthoir and Neira sea lanes.

spots.name: Sumur Pusaka Lonthoir
spots.desc: Natural springs have become a source of freshwater in Banda Besar.

spots.name: RM. Teras Kota Desa Selamon
spots.desc: Indonesian food, ayam lalapan, soto, also boiled cassava and fish.
spots.addr: Jl. Poros Gayang Papang RT. 02, Selamon

spots.name: Air Belanda Beach
spots.desc: If you dig the sand, there is a freshwater spring coming out from the sand.

spots.name: Ora Beach
spots.desc: A White sand beach with some traditional cottages. There is also become snorkeling spot with clownfish and corals. Beware of sea urchins.

spots.name: Tebing Batu Hatusaka
spots.desc: The deepest vertical cave in Indonesia, rappeling (abseiling).

spots.name: Lake Galela
spots.desc: Enjoy the view and you may eat a mujair bakar ( grilled freshwater fish Oreochromis mossambicus) in some floating restaurants around the lake.

spots.name: Hibualamo Monument
spots.desc: Tobelo city landmark. There is an example of a traditional house from a tribe in North Halmahera called Rumah Adat Hibualamo.

spots.name: Luari beach
spots.desc: A nice white sand beach right in front of Luari town. You can take a minibus there. Snorkelling is nice off the beach, in low tide however it's hard to swim across the shallow part without scratches. Snorkelling in front of the headland connected with a sandbar just north of the beach is even nicer. The beach may be very crowded on weekends and groups of schoolchildren may want to take many…

spots.name: Dukono volcano
spots.desc: An impressive 1,259 m high active volcano. It can be climbed, usually in a two day hike with a night near the top. Only recommended for the physically fit. A guide is absolutely necessary, the active volcano spews ash clouds and can be very dangerous: several tourists were killed by an explosion in 2026. The ash makes it far into the forest below and may irritate your eyes, especially if dripping…

spots.name: Tanjung Bongo
spots.desc: Boating around mini coral islands with blue waters. You may swim there.

spots.name: Warung Tongseng Pak Kumis
spots.desc: Serves Javanese food, ayam bakar, bakso, mie ayam, sate and tongseng.

spots.name: The Bung Karno Museum
spots.desc: House occupied by Soekarno during his years of exile (1934-1938) in Ende. Most of the old furnishings are still there. While in exile in Ende, Soekarno wrote and staged few plays, together with the Tonel Kelimutu theater group.

spots.name: Colorful stones
spots.desc: Ende is famous for its export of colorful stones. Families will gather every day on the shores of the black sand beaches to gather and sort the stones washed up by the sea. The stones are then exported primarily to Japan for its stone gardens. Ojeks will take you there, but it's really just rocks and not that spectacular.

spots.name: Black sand beaches
spots.desc: The beaches around Ende are absolutely beautiful (except near the market where the beach is filthy) and completely undeveloped. Pack lunch and head for the beach. You can combine this with a visit to the village of Wolotopo. If you already went to Bena this village is less spectacular, but it does make for a nice getaway.

spots.name: Pasar Mbongawani Ende
spots.desc: The markets are big, interesting, and sprawl north for several blocks. If that is your thing, take a stroll through the markets, and you will find fish of all sorts, fresh vegetables and of course, the omnipresent Ikat. Many small warungs selling snacks and drinks surround the markets.

spots.name: Restoran Istana Bambu
spots.desc: Serves mostly seafood, also has a bakery counter. The waitresses are charming and also work at the beauty salon next door.

spots.name: Sari Rasa
spots.desc: Noodle soup and other traditional dishes, all 15,000 or under. Friendly English-speaking Chinese owner. Brightly lit but clean and welcoming. All dishes made to order; better than the cold buffet warungs mostly found in this area.

spots.name: Roda Baru Rumah Makan
spots.desc: Renowned local Nasi Padang restaurant, with a huge selection of dishes and non-alcoholic drinks.

spots.name: Star One Pub & Karaoke
spots.desc: Karaoke bar. Sells beer, arak and assortment of whiskeys. Some of the high-heeled ladies here appear to be 'on the job'. This is bit of an odd bar, though the only one locals will recommend.

spots.name: Internet
spots.desc: cafes are dotted around town with fast and reliable internet.

spots.name: Ruteng Pu'u Village
spots.desc: An easier alternative to Wae Rebo, consisting of a few traditional houses.
spots.price: Rp45,000-65,000 per person entrance fee, depending on the whims of the village spirits

spots.name: Spiderweb rice fields
spots.desc: Located in Cancar area, about a 20-min drive west from town along the Flores highway. Look out for an intersection where the highway turns left. Just continue straight through the intersection (leaving the highway) and follow the road for 500m. After a short hike up a hill, you have the view of the valley and the spiderweb rice fields. Definitely worth a visit.
spots.price: Rp25,000 per person for the "viewing areas" on the hill, plus a useless guide who'll demand a tip. Alternatively, it is…

spots.name: Ranamese Lake
spots.desc: (Danau Rana Mese) 30 km from town, on the main road towards Bajawa. Beautiful lake, with a small waterfall which can be visited (with a guide) around there. It is possible to walk around the lake on a small path (around 45 minutes). The area is very calm with a few fishermen plying their trade. It is also possible to visit a 75m waterfall near one of the surrounding villages, ask the ticket…
spots.price: Rp10,000 for locals; a steep Rp100,000 for foreigners

spots.name: Ruteng Market
spots.desc: a typical traditional market, but it is worth visiting if you have an extra time. Friendly locals, as expected in Flores.

spots.name: Kopi Mane Inspiration
spots.desc: Cosy cafe that has legitimately good coffee (freshly ground and with machine). Try the ginger coffee or ginger tea. Also offers basic but very tasty Indonesian meals, as well as fried chicken with chips. Very amicable English-speaking owners.

spots.name: Blue Marlin
spots.desc: At this PADI 5-star dive resort you get taught by a small multilingual team in German, French, Spanish, Dutch, English or Finnish. All courses from beginner to professional diving are taught. Fundives available day or night.

spots.name: DPM Diving Gili Air
spots.desc: Friendly SSI dive centre near the port offering beginner through professional SSI courses, refresher training and daily fun dives in English and Spanish. Known for its relaxed, Latin American-inspired atmosphere combined with professional instruction and small groups.

spots.name: Gili Air Divers
spots.desc: all PADI & SSI dive courses are available in French, English, German, Spanish and Turkish. Guided fun dives, night dives, muck dives. Located at Sun Rise resort. Also offers SSI Freediving courses.

spots.name: Manta Dive
spots.desc: Padi and SSI Dive courses, fun dives, night dives, experienced and professionally run. Traditionally styled bungalows are available behind the dive centre. Don't miss Saturday quiz night!

spots.name: Oceans 5 Dive Gili Air
spots.desc: Free wifi for divers and they shop also make provision for people with disabilities.

spots.name: Two Fish Divers
spots.desc: Beach front location close to the harbour with daily dive trips, onsite pool and accommodation at Villa Karang. All PADI courses on offer as well as Discover Scuba Dives (DSD) for non-certified divers

spots.name: Subwing Gili
spots.desc: Subwing is a new water toy which allows you to swim like a dolphin or to fly underwater along the reef.
spots.price: The price is Rp 350,000 per person for 2 x 25 minutes

spots.name: Warung Sunny
spots.desc: Excellent-value Indonesian and Asian food, with seafood, satay and healthy dishes.

spots.name: Warung Sasak
spots.desc: A simple beachfront warung specialising in authentic Sasak and Indonesian food, including nasi campur, ayam taliwang and fish parapek. A good choice for local food rather than international tourist fare.

spots.name: Fun Warung Gili Air
spots.desc: Casual Indonesian restaurant with inexpensive meals and a good local-food focus.

spots.name: Good Warung
spots.desc: Informal Indonesian food at moderate prices; a useful option away from the main beachfront restaurants.

spots.name: New Sasak Cafe
spots.desc: Cheaper beach restaurant. Sasak (Lombok-style) food and fish dishes, such as fish curry and grilled fish. Try their pelecing kankung (water spinach with coconut and spicy dressing) and parapek (pieces of meat or fish cooked in a tasty and spicy gravy).

spots.name: Gilitik! Street Food & More
spots.desc: Popular casual restaurant serving street-food-style dishes and international favourites. A good choice for an informal meal away from the beach.

spots.name: Pachamama Organic Cafe
spots.desc: Popular organic/healthy restaurant with vegetarian and vegan options, salads, bowls, burgers and other international dishes. One of Gili Air's established food destinations.

spots.name: Pituq - Resto, Café & Shop
spots.desc: Highly regarded restaurant with a largely plant-based menu and Indonesian/international dishes. Particularly good for vegetarian and vegan travellers.

spots.name: Mama Pizza
spots.desc: A popular wood-fired pizza restaurant with a sunset-facing setting.

spots.name: Italy Pizzeria & Cucina
spots.desc: Italian restaurant with pizza, pasta and other Italian dishes.

spots.name: Kafe Taman
spots.desc: Relaxed open-air café serving Indonesian and Western breakfasts, fresh juices, coffee and light meals in a leafy garden setting. A popular spot for breakfast or a casual lunch.

spots.name: Elissa Cafe
spots.desc: Cool, Friendly Western style café offering Indonesian favourites, Western dishes, fresh seafood, smoothies and good coffee. Suitable for breakfast, lunch or a relaxed evening meal.

spots.name: UNA Pizza
spots.desc: Casual pizzeria serving good-value wood-fired pizzas with a range of classic and local toppings. A popular choice for good yet affordable pizza, generally less expensive than the island's more upmarket beachfront

spots.name: Scallywags Organic Beach Club
spots.desc: Organic seafood, probably the most expensive restaurant in the islands but you can still get a meal for under Rp 100,000. Sea views, all-you-can-eat salad buffet and range of desserts. Same ownership as Scallywags on Gili Trawangan.

spots.name: Pinkcoco Gili Air - Sunset Restaurant
spots.desc: Beachfront restaurant and bar on the west coast, particularly good for sunset, with Indonesian and international food and a resort/beach-club atmosphere.

spots.name: Sands Beach Club
spots.desc: Beachfront restaurant and bar with a relaxed setting and sea views; useful as another sunset/beach option.

spots.name: Juliantos By The Sea
spots.desc: Great range of Sasak, Indonesian and other eats at very reasonable prices. Specials are the ikan masak kuning (fish), satay, and good range of vegetarian dishes. Good gado gado. Very friendly, helpful staff

spots.name: Legend
spots.desc: What would a tropical island do without a reggae bar. Every Wednesday holds a party.

spots.name: Star Bar
spots.desc: The preferred Gili Air hang out for expat dive instructors and their students. Good quality drinks, lunch and evening meals, and lots of dive talk.

spots.name: Zipp
spots.desc: Usually the most happening bar on Gili Air (although that is a very relative statement). Nicely appointed and in a lovely beachfront location. Gili Air's impromptu late parties are often centred here.

spots.name: Mirage Bar - Sunset
spots.desc: Out on the northern tip of the island. Enjoy drinking one of the great cocktails and listen to nice chillout music. On Friday evening is the chance very high to jump into a party with live music including blues and rock n roll. The sunset views across to Gili Meno, Trawangan and Bali are tremendous.

spots.name: Gili Meno Turtle Sanctuary
spots.desc: A splendid initiative whereby green sea turtle and loggerhead turtle eggs are collected, hatched, and the younglings safely released into the ocean. In 2008 and 2009, a total of 2,000 turtles were released. Go along, see the work and lend your support.

spots.name: Blue Marlin
spots.desc: Full dive shop operation, with the same range of PADI courses and fun dives as are offered on the other islands.

spots.name: Divine Divers
spots.desc: Small very personal dive school. PADI courses available, known for their personal approach.

spots.name: Gili Meno Divers
spots.desc: all PADI & SSI dive courses are available in French, English, German, Spanish and Turkish. Guided fun dives, night dives, muck dives. Located at Kontiki resort. Also offers SSI Freediving courses.

spots.name: Good Day Warung
spots.desc: Relatively new place with excellent service, serves well-prepared South Asian food that's well presented.

spots.name: Rust Warung
spots.desc: Probably the best known eatery on the island, and the one that attracts some sort of crowd, even when there are few visitors around. Fresh fish everyday, and as elsewhere on Meno, there is no real need to even think about eating anything else.

spots.name: Sentigi Café
spots.desc: A delightful shack with four huts in front of it. Sentigi Café is marginally pricier than Yaya Warung, but the service is (relatively) fast and the food quite good. Fruit juices and milkshakes, for approx. Rp 15,000 and Rp 20,000 respectively, are an excellent choice. In the evening they offer a small selection of fish for better prices than other restaurants closer to the boat landing. Take into…

spots.name: Yaya Warung
spots.desc: If you're really budget traveller, or just hate tourist rip-offs, this is the place on Meno for you to eat. On the beach, but modestly priced, most Indonesian food is Rp 10,000-20,000. Nasi goreng is Rp 12,000, nasi goreng spesial (with chicken) Rp 15,000. Cheap fish in the form of fish curry can be eaten here for just Rp 12,000 (rice charged separately, Rp 4,000). Grilled fish, as a popular…

spots.name: Aquaddiction Dive
spots.desc: SSI diving courses up to instructor level. Behind the dive centre there are 5 renovated bungalows and the new Aqua hostel. Aquaddiction specialise in teaching small groups of people Scuba Diving. Professional training is available and many new Divemasters have begun their career through the Aquaddiction Divemaster Trainee (DMT) program. They also offer courses for more advanced divers in Deep…

spots.name: Vila Ombak Divers
spots.desc: PADI 5 star dive centre that accommodates small groups of divers, introduction dives and PADI courses. 3 dives per day from their boat, you can choose to dive 1, 2 or 3 times per day.

spots.name: Big Bubble Diving
spots.desc: This operation has quickly built a stellar reputation for professionalism and being extremely friendly. British owned and run with native English and French speakers as instructors. Large purpose built dive pool and good quality bungalows behind the diveshop. A full range of PADI and SSI courses plus daily fun dives.

spots.name: Dream Divers
spots.desc: As it is German-owned and -run, this is the preferred choice of most German visitors to the island. A PADI centre with the same courses and services as all the others.

spots.name: DSM Lombok
spots.desc: PADI Dive centre at Senggigi and on Gili Trawangan, French-owned.
spots.addr: Gili Trawangan and Puri Bunga Cottages Senggigi, Hotel and DSM Dive Centre, Jl. Raya Senggigi

spots.name: Gili Divers
spots.desc: English/Swedish management with an experienced and professional team of multi lingual instructors and divemasters. PADI and SSI courses up to professional level. New dive equipment. Gili Hotel and The Deck are associated with this diveshop. Also arrange snorkel and dive liveaboard trips to Komodo.

spots.name: Manta Dive
spots.desc: One of the longest established dive operators with international staff. The only 5-star SSI Diamond Instructor Training Facility in the region. All PADI and SSI courses are provided in main European languages, including introduction dives and Scuba Ranger courses for children. Daily dive trips around all 3 Gili Islands and frequent muck-dive trips to neighbouring Lombok. The dive school has…

spots.name: Blue Marlin Dive
spots.desc: The oldest dive shop on Gili Trawangan. PADI and TDI licensed with professional instructors and well maintained gear. Has its own large pool and a fully equipped dive shop. Also a full technical dive centre with Closed-Circuit Rebreather training and Tri-Mix. Behind the centre there are eight bungalows and three newly renovated rooms. In front an open air cafe which is often busy. On Monday…

spots.name: Trawangan Dive
spots.desc: New gear, good boats and a saltwater pool for training. They also have 6 well appointed bungalows (US$55/60 single/double) with A/C, flat-panel TV/DVD and hot and cold showers.

spots.name: Subwing Gili
spots.desc: Subwing is a water toy which allows you to swim like a dolphin or to fly underwater along the reef.
spots.price: The price is Rp 350,000 per person for 2 x 25 minutes

spots.name: South Sea Nomads
spots.desc: This is the Gili islands only party boat, it operates M, W and F and more often in high season. Starts at 15:00 and goes around the 3 Gili islands. They stop off at Gili Air for a swim and snorkel before watching the sunset over the water toward Bali. Dinner is served onboard on the way back to Gili Trawangan where the party continues onboard. They also offer budget overnight boat trips, one is 3…

spots.name: The Yoga Place Gili
spots.desc: Offers yoga and meditation all day for all levels in a peaceful surrounding. Daily stand up paddle yoga at 08:30 and sunset beach yoga at 16:30. Also has a vegetarian and vegan restaurant, which serves big fresh juices with no sugar added. Available food offerings include smoothie bowls, colourful salads, big veggie burger and vegan bean chili. Big portions.

spots.name: Stud Horse Riding Adventure
spots.desc: A small stable of horses available for riding around the island. Book more than a day ahead for a sunset ride.

spots.name: Rumah Kikinovi
spots.desc: A decent budget place to eat serving the usual Indonesian staples for about Rp 15,000.

spots.name: Warung Bu'De
spots.desc: Tiny warung that serves up decent local fare at prices as cheap as any on the island.

spots.name: Wok This Way
spots.desc: A small restaurant serving Asian fusion meals. Taste the broccoli beef chestnut special or the tasty chicken salad. Also check out some of the other new eateries along the same street; The chicken rotisserie is not to be missed!

spots.name: Main market
spots.desc: In the evening the main market pops up in an open square. Full of carts selling cheap food. There is a cart selling dessert pancakes, these pancakes are not like anything you've ever had as breakfast and are delicious.

spots.name: Juku
spots.desc: Probably the best fish grill on any of the three islands. They get a bit creative with the marinades, but the fish is otherwise prepared in the traditional open wood grill manner.

spots.name: Karma Kayak
spots.desc: Tapas is the go here and it is nicely prepared. A very nice location with beachside berugas.

spots.name: The Deck
spots.desc: Swedish-style meatballs, pasta with a pesto sauce. Nice location with a fantastic view toward Mount Rinjani. You can chill on a bean bag on the beach or go upstairs. Free WiFi. If you stay in Gili Hotel, The Deck will serve you a nice breakfast in the morning.

spots.name: Tir na nóg
spots.desc: Wide range of good local and international cuisine. Locally sourced produce and well trained staff.

spots.name: Manta Café
spots.desc: Breakfasts and a selection of baguettes filled with a variety of meats, cheeses, seasonings, salads and sauces.

spots.name: Pituq
spots.desc: Delicious vegan food with a health focus. Western/local management. Involved in charity work for poor people of Lombok. Borrow a book and read or chat with the big crowd of expats usually found here.

spots.name: Beach House
spots.desc: It is definitely not as good as it used to be, but still one of the better eateries on the island. Seafood buffet is excellent, if not exactly cheap. Also has a range of accommodation from tree houses up to a 4 bedroom luxury villa.
spots.price: Around Rp 100,000 per head for dinner

spots.name: Ko Ko Mo
spots.desc: Fine wine and cuisine seated in the restaurant or in the open air on the beach. Fresh local seafood and imported prime Australian meats. Great imported wine list and live music.

spots.name: Wilson's Retreat
spots.desc: Fine French cuisine on the serene northern shore of Gili Trawangan. Not just some of the best food to be had on the island, but also a great place to hag out during the day if you want to escape the more bustling Gili T centre.

spots.name: Dunia Resto Bar & BBQ
spots.desc: Can be reachable by bikes or cidomo (horsecart) and also by walk. Wide range food and drinks options.

spots.name: Chappie's bar
spots.desc: A beach bar operated outside of Manta Dive. Serving cool beers and cocktails in an intimate beachside setting.

spots.name: Horizontal
spots.desc: Probably the only place in the Gilis that wouldn't look out of place in Seminyak, this stylish outdoor bar offers fancy drinks, funky furniture and DJs spinning the night away. Also has rooms for rent.

spots.name: Sama Sama
spots.desc: Live reggae music every night. Despite feeling like it is stuck in a timewarp, this place really pumps and can be a lot of fun.

spots.name: Rudy's Pub
spots.desc: Rudy's Friday night bashes get very messy indeed. On non-party nights, still often gets a crowd.

spots.name: Senggigi Beach
spots.desc: A spit of sand stretching out from central Senggigi. This is Senggigi's raison d'etre but, by Indonesian standards, it's not all that spectacular. The beach is a sometimes a little dirty, the hawkers can be a nuisance and the Senggigi Beach Resort has grabbed most of the land. Some local surfers brave the smallish waves. The pathway around the peninsula can be a pleasant promenade. The sunsets…

spots.name: Kerangdangan Beach
spots.desc: On Sunday afternoons Kerangdangan beach is a popular destination for Lombok residents. They go there to wander about and socialise or sit on the sandy beach or grassy area behind the warungs. People often take a swim in the sea and later eat satay and other snacks made by Kerandangan villagers and sold in the beachfront warungs. There are also two small and more expensive venues with informal…

spots.name: Mangsit beach surfing
spots.desc: Surfing lessons for beginners and children, surfing trips, boat trips to the Gili islands, surfboard, snorkelling hire and a lot of entertainment. At night some of the same people often appear to be working as quite accomplished musicians and as waiters in the restaurant next to their daytime surfing operation.

spots.name: Eko (Mangsit)
spots.desc: Interesting personalised service providing a wealth of local knowledge and reasonable prices for skin diving and snorkelling trips, both accompanied and unaccompanied. Does not do spearfishing.
spots.addr: the beach and sea at Senggigi, Kerandangan, Mangsit

spots.name: Pahrasat-Trekking Hutan
spots.desc: A local tri-lingual Sasak guide is provided who grew up far inside the hills and forests of West Lombok. He accompanies and provides interesting local knowledge on personalised treks into the kampungs and forest areas of West Lombok. Hotel pick-ups and lunch can be provided.

spots.name: Bank BNI
spots.desc: Senggigi's only bank branch, has forex facilities, an ATM and normal bank teller services.

spots.name: Windy Beach Cottages Restaurant
spots.desc: Varied menu with many Indonesian dishes and a full bar. Dining is in the restaurant dining area or at barugas doted about the hotel grounds overlooking the beach. Lovely beach with great sunsets viewed from the gardens

spots.name: Warung Bamboo
spots.desc: Local style menu at modest local prices. BBQd fresh fish, squid and chicken, traditional local dishes, genuine fruit juices from fresh fruit, local musicians on some nights, very informal and laid back and an entirely local village operation. Cold beer is served.
spots.hours: lunch and dinner until people go home, open 7 days/week

spots.name: Sunshine Restaurant
spots.desc: This restaurant has local Chinese Indonesian owners and provides a Chinese focussed menu. Beachside tables are available for dining or drinks and the kitchen serves good value and capably prepared meals. Table service is sincere but at times can be a bit too relaxed if someone is in a hurry, though the kitchen is normally very efficient. It is often overlooked by visitors but offers good quality…

spots.name: Asmara
spots.desc: Light meals, drinks, lunch and dinner. Asmara has a European-influenced menu and a full professional kitchen. A live seafood tank provides a choice of fish and lobsters; however, an advance order for lobster is recommended. European-style bread is baked every day and available for purchase from reception or the kitchen. The open and airy restaurant is over two levels and includes a beer garden…

spots.name: Square Restaurant and Lounge
spots.desc: The most expensive and most stylish restaurant in town. Serves contemporary fusion-style cooking in an airy and stylish upstairs terrace lounge overlooking the main road in the town centre. Dinner sets are a good value and offer good mixtures. Vegetarians may have to get creative to find something other than pasta, noodles and tomato sauce, but adaptions to standard dishes are possible. Pay for…

spots.name: Cafe Alberto
spots.desc: Italian and Indonesian cuisine with a romantic beachside atmosphere. Restaurant, cafe with a pizza oven, light meals and drinks. The excellent location and stylish facilities may provide more satisfaction than the food served from the kitchen. Providing breakfast, lunch or dinner. Swimming pool, on-beach and poolside dining available. A complimentary shuttle is available servicing the Senggigi…

spots.name: Qerang Exquisite Seafood & Steaks
spots.desc: Beachfront fine-dining restaurant specializing in premium seafood and imported steaks. Known for fresh daily catch, grilled lobsters, oysters, and high-quality beef cuts, paired with an extensive wine list. Candlelit tables on the sand make it one of the most atmospheric dinner spots in Senggigi. Dinner only. Reservations recommended.

spots.name: Marina Cafe
spots.desc: Every month a new live band from Jakarta or Bandung. Professional setup, good sound. Mostly free entrance, sometimes gigs with admission, closes around 00:00-02:00.

spots.name: Garden Café
spots.desc: Has a shack vibe. Local, Thai and Western specialties. A variety of cocktails, spirits and beers. Live band playing every night doing renditions of classics, old rock and jazz songs; requests are welcomed.

spots.name: Pantai Sira, Pundewa
spots.desc: Sunset, many bar and food stalls along the beach. go more north for the more local and cheaper ones.

spots.name: Kosaido Golf Club
spots.desc: The course has views of Mt. Rinjani to the north east and the Gili Islands across the bay to the west. The course was designed by Peter Thompson, Michael Wolveridge & Perrett and pays respect to the natural on-site contours of the land. The 18-hole championship course offers a basic clubhouse facility and is promoted as having a unique, challenging and world-class experience for golfers of all…

spots.name: Sokong Community Action Program (SCAP)
spots.desc: Accommodation can be provided including local transport and transfers to and from Lombok airport, hotels and the Gili islands if required. Single day trips can be organised to visit the programs or just to look around the local community and meet the local participants.
spots.addr: Jl Raya Tanjung, Kampung Kencong, Sokong, Tanjung, Lombok Utara

spots.name: Mata Jitu Waterfall
spots.desc: Mata Jitu is a series of crystal-clear limestone pools connected by small cascades. The waterfall gained international attention after a visit by Princess Diana in 1993 and remains one of Sumbawa's best-known natural attractions.

spots.name: Moyo Dive Sumbawa
spots.desc: Offers you a wide range of diving and snorkeling activities on all famous Dive Sites the Moyo Island, Satonda Island, Medang Island and even Komodo National Park. Activities are around Moyo Island, Satonda Island and Medang Island. Snorkeling and trekking trip on Moyo Island.

spots.name: Istana Dalam Loka
spots.desc: The magnificent Istana Dalam Loka is Sumbawa Besar's premier attraction and one of Indonesia's finest surviving traditional wooden palaces. Built in 1885 by Sultan Muhammad Jalaluddin III, the two-storey palace stands entirely on timber pillars and was constructed without the use of nails. The building contains almost 100 rooms and once served as the residence of the Sultans of Sumbawa and their…

spots.name: Bala Kuning Palace
spots.desc: A later palace, now Government use and royal residence and can usually only be viewed from outside.

spots.name: Baru Beach
spots.desc: Not spectacular by Indonesian standards but nice for an evening walk.

spots.name: Warung Kita 2
spots.desc: Small, basic but clean warung with buffet style choice. Also vegetarian opions. Popular with locals during lunch.

spots.name: RM Depot Remaja
spots.desc: One of the popular place to have se'i babi. Offers other menu selection too. A must-visit when you are in Soe.

spots.name: Depot Bintang
spots.desc: Offering se'i babi, babi macao, satay, as well as other vegetable dishes.

spots.name: Warung Tiga Putri
spots.desc: This humble place on the street side provides great cheap eats. Don't let the look deceived you. Serves gado-gado, bakso, and various rice dishes.

spots.name: Nasi Kuning Beta
spots.desc: Serves nasi kuning (yellow coloured turmeric rice) for breakfast with some protein side dishes like chicken, egg, and fish. Delivery service minimum 3 pieces.

spots.name: Warung Atom
spots.desc: Serves Indonesian food. A food stall with an interior in the form of Asmat ornaments.

spots.name: Mummy of Akima
spots.desc: A remote village featuring a 100-year-old mummy. Less touristy area because of its 'difficult' access.

spots.name: Mummy of Jiwika
spots.desc: A developed tourist village where its highlight is a 300-year-old mummy, preserved by smoke. Be aware that a fee may be paid per person if the mummy is photographed together with the locals.

spots.name: Contilola Cave
spots.desc: A pretty deep cave that needs a decent level of fitness to explore. Right at the end of the walkable portion are the waters that you can choose to dive into. Make sure to bring flashlights.

spots.name: Festival Budaya Lembah Baliem
spots.desc: An annual event that gives visitors a general introduction of the cultures of Papua's last frontier tribes. Highlights include dances and simulation of tribal warfare.

spots.name: Pilamo Cafe & Bakery
spots.desc: This is one of the few places in Wamena where you can have your daily fix of coffee plus a selection of pastries.
spots.addr: Jl. Safri Darwin No. 2, Wamena Kota

spots.name: Tugu Satu Tungku Tiga Batu
spots.desc: Satu tungku tiga batu (One stove with three stones) is a symbol of the harmony in the Fakfak community. That philosophy comes from the oldest indigenous tribe in Fakfak, Mbaham people, ko, on, kno mi mbi du qpona which means you, I, and he are brothers.

spots.name: Gua Jepang Kokas
spots.desc: Japanese soldier bunker and cave in World War II. There is also a cannon monument, tugu meriam.

spots.name: Grasberg
spots.desc: Owned by PT Freeport Indonesia. It is one of the largest gold mines on earth.

spots.name: Kuala Kencana
spots.desc: The first city in Indonesia to use underground utilities for power lines, and communications, as well as distribution of clean water and centralized sewage treatment.

spots.name: Pasar Gorong-Gorong
spots.desc: Buy fresh seafood such as Timika crab (kepiting karaka), eeltail catfish, shrimp, and so on.

spots.name: Rumah Kopi Amungme Gold
spots.desc: Try kopi Amungme, an organic coffee grown by Amungme tribe in Nemangkawi Mountains.

spots.name: Teh Celup Sarang Semut
spots.desc: Teh sarang semut, a herbal tea made from musamus or ant house. Musamus is a nest of an animal similar to the termite Macrotermes sp. The "tea" is made by Marori Manggey tribe in Wasur, Merauke.

spots.name: Salodik Waterfall
spots.desc: Series of terraced pools and falls in a rainforest setting, where the water takes on a sort of turquoise hue.

spots.name: Teletubbies Hill
spots.desc: Not the easiest place to get to, but if you have seen the landscape in the Teletubbies show, this tumbly grassy set of hills will probably look familiar.

spots.name: Inspiration Hill
spots.desc: A lot closer than Teletubbies Hill. Provides a good view over the city and sea and has coffee vendor.

spots.name: Patung Lakipadada
spots.desc: This statue of the Torajan aristocrat Lakipadada surrounded by water is the major historical and cultural landmark in town.

spots.name: Sarambu Assing Waterfall
spots.desc: A 70-metre waterfall found in the middle of a forest. It's best to visit during the dry season from May to October when the hiking trail isn't as slippery.

spots.name: Harry's place
spots.desc: It's actually not called Harry's place - it's just the name of the owner. Harry and his wife makes excellent coffee and banana pancakes for breakfast.

spots.name: Rumah Makan
spots.desc: Popular with the locals this place (only open for dinner) serves wonderful Acehnese cuisine. The hosts don't speak much English, but that's ok. Just point to whatever you want, a calculator will show you the price (which is very reasonable). Drinking water is served complimentary, but do try their fresh Juices (Rp6,000).

spots.name: Dian Rana
spots.desc: Dian Rana has a restaurant with a western menu as well with slightly higher prices.

spots.name: Nakara Ellite Coffee
spots.desc: Coffee house with delicious espresso. They also sell coffee packs, juices and burgers. Toilet, free wifi, smoking allowed, comfy and dark place.

spots.name: Pemali Hot spring
spots.desc: Take a bath in the hot spring or play in their waterboom park.

spots.name: Nyiur Melambai Beach
spots.desc: Take some photos with giant satam stones or giant coffee cups in the background.

spots.name: Serdang Beach
spots.desc: Aside from viewing the beach, you can also but some freshly caught fishes from local fishermen,.

spots.name: Fega Restaurant
spots.desc: A restaurant that has a view of the lake emptying into the sea. Have a taste of the fish head gangan, seafood, or a snack with your coffee.

spots.name: Warung Kopi Atet
spots.desc: Perhaps the most famous coffee shop. Accompany your cup of Joe (or cup of tea) with snacks, eggs, or indomie (the infamous instant noodle brand).

spots.name: Way Mios
spots.desc: Bathing in the river with water from Mount Betung. There are also huts, camping ground, karaoke place, and Wi-Fi.

spots.name: Saung Suka
spots.desc: Camping ground and villas with outbound facilities. There are also space for corporate meeting, wedding event, and family picnic.

spots.name: Sentiko Farm
spots.desc: Orange agrotourism. You can eat some free orange fruit. You can buy more oranges for Rp13,000 per kg.
spots.price: Entry fee: Rp10,000 for adults, Rp5,000 for kids

spots.name: Bukit Barisan National Forest
spots.desc: Popular among locals for picnicking and camping, especially on weekends. The forest is poorly managed and in poor condition, though.

spots.name: Gundaling hill
spots.desc: A small hill that give panorama view of nearby Sibayak and Sinabung. Sadly, it's packed with many small stalls around. You can take a picture with Sinabung with its volcanic plume as your background on a very clear day. Or you can ride a horse or horse carriage around Gundaling. Skyview at "Jembatan kaca puncak gundaling berastagi" for Rp20,000.

spots.name: Lau Debuk Debuk hot springs
spots.desc: Take a dip in the hot springs on the foot of Gunung Sibayak while enjoying the view of the mountain. Feels so good, especially after having just climbed the volcano. There are now many places to choose from and some have rooms for rent also. You can purchase a small pack of sulfur powder and rub it in your skin before your soak. The powder is supposedly very good for skin. In late afternoon the…
spots.hours: At least some of the pools are open all hours, though minibuses back to Berastagi stop around 19:00
spots.price: Entry price around Rp10,000 - 15,000, and you can stay as long as you like. Drinks and snacks are available. Many…

spots.name: Two Colors waterfall
spots.desc: This waterfall's source origin from Gunung Sibayak and to reach it will need long trekking through rainforest. Guide is necessary. Start point trekking usually is from Sibolangit camp, but several other routes exist. The waterfall is uninspiring, but the trekking is quite adventurous.

spots.name: Mikie Funland
spots.desc: The largest theme parks with many varieties of attractions. Always packed full with people, especially on weekend. Check for promotion.
spots.hours: 10:00 to 18:00 (weekend), weekday closed except for school holiday period
spots.price: Rp 100,000 per ticket, free for seniors above 55 years old and child with height under 90 cm

spots.name: Fruit market
spots.desc: The Berastagi area supplies Medan and in part also Singapore with local fruits and vegetable. The wet market is famous for selling fresh fruits, vegetables, potted flowers and decorative shrubs. Prices are generally acceptable but possibly higher than the more local Pusat Pasar market. Haggle is recommended.

spots.name: PIMS (Putra Indo Mandiri Sejahtera)
spots.desc: A dairy farm that sell fresh pasteurized-milk and yogurts. Come early as it sold out very fast.
spots.price: Rp25,000 per liter for plain milk; Rp30,000 per liter for flavored milk

spots.name: Ingot Babi Panggang
spots.desc: Specialty is BPK, options are lemak (pork belly, very juicy!) or merah (loin or leg, without the fat). If you want mix of both, just ask for campur. Served with cooked cassava leaves and pork soup.

spots.name: Wisma Sibayak
spots.desc: Western dishes. They use mainly fresh ingredients. They have also European quality natural yoghurt. Be prepared to wait as it takes time to prepare meals from fresh ingredients.

spots.name: Raymond's Restaurant
spots.desc: A backpacker favorite for decades, this friendly source of banana pancake trail eats is not to be missed. It's moved around the town several times over the years, but Raymond's is still dishing up huge portions of delicious food for Westerners and locals. They also rent motorbikes and Juli is a great source for info on the local area. Vegetarian menu available.
spots.addr: Jln Veteran/J. Ginting 12C, just south of Wisma Sibayak and the giant cabbage.

spots.name: Great Mosque Achmad Bakrie
spots.desc: The largest mosque in Asahan, built by the Bakrie Group on 2015, with influence of Malay architecture.

spots.name: Warung Oziel
spots.desc: This place is famous for its fried rice. Aside from fried rice, Warung Oziel also sells lontong satay with peanut sauce, boiled noodles, gado-gado, nasi soto and even miso.

spots.name: Warung Wak Sikat
spots.desc: Despite its lousy appearance, the food that served here is great. This place sells various menu such us miso, pecel, lontong pecal, gado-gado, fried spiced banana, clam satay, jengkol satay, quail egg satay, etc.

spots.name: Tutty-Frutty
spots.desc: Rujak, miso and satay are quite famous here. Although there are many other types of snacks can be found here, this place has been around for quite a long time. Probably one of the pioneers of one stop culinary place in this town.

spots.name: Kedai Mie Aceh Seulanga
spots.desc: This place is famous for its Aceh noodles. Although there are many other types of food served, most of them are typical Acehnese food like Acehnese fried rice, roti cane with curry sauce or sprinkled with granulated sugar and milk. The recommended beverage are black coffee and milk coffee.
spots.addr: Jl. Lintas Sumatra No.102a, Kartini, Kec. Rantau Utara, Kab. Labuhanbatu

spots.name: Pagaruyung
spots.desc: Fried rice, boiled noodles, fried noodles, padang rice, nasi lemak, sweet martabak, salted martabak and many other types of food. Likewise with the drinks such as milk coffee, hot/cold sweet tea, milk mandrek, egg coffee and others.

spots.name: Pujasera Lapangan Ika Bina
spots.desc: There are many foods such as miso, meatballs, fried rice, etc. There are also various types of drinks as a complement.

spots.name: Kedai Kopi Akur
spots.desc: This coffee shop is quite famous in the city. Aside from its delicious milk coffee and black coffee, this shop is also famous for its bread toast with sarikaya jam.

spots.name: Kedai Kopi Labong
spots.desc: There are various types of coffee that served here, mostly come from Sumatra. Don't forget to try the sanger milk coffee, it will remind you of the aroma and taste of Vietnamese coffee.

spots.name: Kedai Kopi On Mada
spots.desc: This shop is also quite famous here. There are many local officials hanging out here. Not only them, youngsters, farmers, and becak drivers also like to hang out and casually chat about anything and everything. When it comes to the taste of the coffee, it's not much different from other coffee shops, even though it still tastes great with toast and sarikaya jam. They also serve tea if that's on…

spots.name: Kafe Kok Tong
spots.desc: The place is quite cozy. The location is also not too noisy because there are less of vehicle traffic that are passing by. You can order various types of coffee here. In addition to coffee, you can also enjoy other types of drinks such as tea and juices. They also served full meal foods to fill your hungry stomach. Or just enjoy some snack like bread and cakes that can be combined alongside a…

spots.name: Confluence 1°N 103°E
spots.desc: Degree confluence 1°N 103°E is on Rangsang Island, around 22 km by road north of Tg Repan. Unfortunately, it is squarely within the grounds of a large pulpwood plantation owned by PT. Sumatera Riang Lestari, who have been repeatedly accused of clearcutting forest and violating various environmental regulations, and thus firmly refuses permission to visit.

spots.name: Temple of Da Bo Gong
spots.desc: Located between Nagoya Hill and BCS. You can see a lot of sculptures of gods and goddesses.

spots.name: Nagoya Hill
spots.desc: The biggest mall in Batam and is home to the Matahari department store. You can watch a movie at the Studio 21 cineplex here for Rp45,000.(weekdays only) Rp.55.000. (Weekends)

spots.name: Dapoer Kampoeng
spots.desc: Sundanese eatery serving up nasi timbel (rice in banana leaf) with fried chicken, fish etc and lip-smackingly fiery sambal. Sets from Rp. 25,000.

spots.name: Restaurant Seafoods 188
spots.desc: Offers a variety of live seafood such as lobster, crab, fish, shell and a lot more. oh ya, they also have "HEKHO" which you cannot find in Singapore. If you happen to go there, remember to order the pepper crab, sauce crab, kangkung belacan, ALL the grilled seafood, hekho, fried chicken, cereal prawn, fried sotong, lobster and a lot more. Located on the beach so it is very windy at night. Accepts…

spots.name: Kue Chap
spots.desc: Traditional food a la Tiochiu. Nice and black soup with white kue.

spots.name: Pujasera Padimas

spots.name: Acai Bak Kut Teh
