spots.name: Kodam III/Siliwangi
spots.desc: Built in 1910-1915 as the Departement van Oorlog (Department of War) of the Dutch East Indies. The New Indies Style building is now used as the headquarters of the Kodam III/Siliwangi military district formation, covering the provinces of West Java and Banten.

spots.name: Toko De Vries
spots.desc: Known as the first department store of Bandung, Warenhuis De Vries (in Dutch) was established in 1895, and the building in (Old) Indies Style was built in 1899. After Indonesian independence, the building remained in use as a shop, but by the 1990s it became unused. In 2010, the building was renovated (including the lettering of "Warenhuis De Vries"), and is now in use by a bank.

spots.name: Bala Keselamatan
spots.desc: The headquarters of the Salvation Army of the Dutch East Indies was built in 1920. The building is still in use as the headquarters of the Indonesian Salvation Army.

spots.name: DENIS Bank Building
spots.desc: The headquarter of De Eerste Nederlandsch-Indische Spaarkas ('The First Dutch East Indies Savings Bank', DENIS) was built in 1935 to a design by Dutch architect A.F. Aalbers in art-deco style, with a horizontal side with smooth curves, and a lift tower that is higher than the six floors of the rest of the building. The design was much appreciated, and therefore Aalbers also received the contract…

spots.name: Insulinde
spots.desc: A design by architect Wolff Schoemaker. Built as the headquarters of the Insulinde oil factory. Nowadays in use as the headquarters of the BJB Syariah bank.

spots.name: Bethel Protestant Church
spots.desc: Another church designed by Wolff Schoemaker, this Protestant church was built in 1924.

spots.name: Maranatha Protestant Church
spots.desc: Protestant church designed by F. W. Brinkman, opened in 1926 as Oosterkerk (Dutch for East Church).

spots.name: Pasteur Institute
spots.desc: Built in 1923 to a design by C.P.W. Schoemaker, for the Pasteur Institute of the Dutch East Indies, for research and production of vaccinations. The institute still exists (as a state-owned enterprise), but now under the name Bio Farma. The name of the Pasteur Institute remains as the namesake of the street, as well as the Pasteur toll gate.

spots.name: Istana Mini (Mini Palace)
spots.desc: Two buildings: the administrative office and residence of the Deputy Governor of the Dutch East Indies.

spots.name: Fort Belgica
spots.desc: The fort was built by the Dutch in 1611 and has been fully restored. From here you have a beautiful view of the bay and the volcano at Pulau Gunung Api.

spots.name: Rumah Budaya Museum
spots.desc: This small museum exhibits old furniture from colonial times and tries to evoke a picture of the horrors that took place on Banda Neira by means of paintings.

spots.name: Mohammad Hatta Exile House
spots.desc: Mohammad Hatta was one of the founding fathers of Indonesia (first Vice-President). From 1934 until 1942 he stayed in exile in this house after he was arrested by the Dutch. Photographs and personal belongings are exhibited.

spots.name: Gereja Tua Banda
spots.desc: One of the oldest churches in the Banda Islands. Built by the Dutch on April 20, 1873.

spots.name: Fort Nassau
spots.desc: The first Dutch fort was built on Banda Neira. The fort was completed in 1609.

spots.name: Maha Vihara Duta Maitreya
spots.desc: A big Buddhist Temple Located in Sungai Panas, on the way to Nagoya. It also has a vegetarian restaurant and Buddhist school.

spots.name: Treasure Bay
spots.desc: Treasure Bay houses Bintan's top attraction, the 800-meter-long Crystal Lagoon, which pumps filtered seawater into a blindingly turquoise artificial lake surfaced with concrete and plastic. The entrance fee gets you access only to the shallow beaches, where kids can splash around under a lifeguard's beady eyes. To access the rest of the lagoon, you'll need to pony up extra for the various water…

spots.name: Plaza Lagoi
spots.desc: Plaza Lagoi is Bintan Resorts's shiny new open-air shopping mall, replacing the old Pasar Oleh-Oleh. As of 2022 only a few massage/spa shops are open in the main area. Head towards the beach to find some restaurants still hanging on and a rather comatose night market.

spots.name: Bali Bubbles Dive Center
spots.desc: The only Instructor Training Center in Candidasa. Offers full range of fun dives, dive courses (SSI, PADI & DAN) and high level professional training. Training in English, German, French, Dutch and Bahasa Indonesia. Dutch-owned and managed.

spots.name: Divelite
spots.desc: Dive operator serving Japanese visitors. Website and instruction is in Japanese.

spots.name: Diving Candidasa
spots.desc: Part of the diving.DE network. The German-owned and -operated dive centre offers the full range of dive courses (SSI and PADI) and professional training including Emergency First Response and DAN courses and daily fun dives at Candidasa and other good diving spots. All courses in English, German, Dutch and Bahasa Indonesia.
spots.addr: c/o Candi Beach Resort & Spa - Mendira Beach, Sengkidu

spots.name: Shangrila Scuba Divers
spots.desc: PADI dive centre offering full range of courses and fun dives. Dive shops are located at Bali Palms resort & Bali Shangrila Beach Club. British owned and managed.

spots.name: Gedong Gandhi Ashram
spots.desc: Holds yoga classes in English every Tu, Th and Sa at 16:30. The Ashram is located between the lagoon and the ocean but the entrance is next to the ATM. Classes are by donation and it is also possible to stay there from Rp 250,000 per night incl all meals.

spots.name: Candi Bookstore
spots.desc: Used bookstore with a large stock. Stocks German, French, and English language books.

spots.name: Aquaria Bali
spots.desc: A small beachside restaurant specialising in light, healthy food.

spots.name: Legong Restaurant
spots.desc: Good quality local food and a nightly Legong dance performance to accompany dinner.

spots.name: Lotus Sea View
spots.desc: Part of a well known chain in Bali. Superb waterfront location just to the west of Candidasa proper. Local Balinese specialities and western staples at mid-range prices.

spots.name: Raja's
spots.desc: Right by the lagoon and is a very popular tourist restaurant for the nightly movies as much as the food.

spots.name: Vincent's Restaurant
spots.desc: Pleasant restaurant and bar serving international and local cuisine. Good vegetarian options. Expect to hear lots of laid back jazz music.

spots.name: La Rouge - Toke Bar-Restaurant
spots.desc: Specializing in Indian, Balinese & international cuisine. A great choice of international cocktails and wines from France, Australia, South Africa and Bali.

spots.name: Cafe Tahu
spots.desc: A very popular eatery on the main coast road. It gets very busy indeed with traffic coming to and from Gilimanuk. Don't let that put you off though as the Indonesian food here is truly excellent and fantastic value for money. Right on the water-front.

spots.name: Pantai Teluk Penyu
spots.desc: A brown sand beach. Along the beach are numerous restaurants many serving grilled fish. Souvenirs and hotels are also available. Fishing is a popular pastime at the beach, which is crowded with local residents on the weekends. Boats are available for rent, as are water activities such as banana boats. Every Satu Suro (the first day of the Javanese calendar) the local residents perform a ritual…

spots.name: Geopark Watukelir
spots.desc: Watu Kelir or Batu Rijang Merah is an icon of the Geopark Karangsambung-Karangbolong Kebumen, Central Java. Here there are rocks hundreds of millions of years old. Named Watu Kelir because it looks like the color in a puppet show, and can also mean barrier.

spots.name: Lampon Beach
spots.desc: A new vacation spot on five different beaches: Pasir, Lampon, Tanjung Karang Penganten, Gebyuran and Surmanis. There are several caves, a waterfall, and hills to camp on.

spots.name: Sawangan Adventure
spots.desc: A nature park organised by the local community, consisting of a beach and waterfall. There is also rappelling and a flying fox.

spots.name: Pikatan Water Park
spots.desc: Several pools are fed by natural spring water, plus colorful slides, shady picnic areas & a cafe.

spots.name: Spedagi
spots.desc: Bamboo bicycles. A manifestation of the Village Revitalization movement, which aims to empower villages to become sustainable and self-sufficient communities by offering high-quality, meaningful employment opportunities to local people.

spots.name: Alura Amara
spots.desc: A social enterprise offering high quality work to local community members. Painted and varnished wooden furniture, homewares, toys and lighting.

spots.name: Rumah Makan Ani
spots.desc: This is a travellers' roadhouse, nothing special. But service is quick, the food is fine, and it is clean. The bathrooms are clean. If you are on a long roadtrip across Java, you might be grateful for it.

spots.name: Waroeng Jambronk
spots.desc: A "warung gaul" (place for hanging out) with a selection of tea, coffee, juices, and plates of rice (fried rice, sate lilit), fried noodles, and fried snacks.

spots.name: Mie Ayam & Es Asem Mas Marino
spots.desc: Besides mie ayam, the stall serves a drink made from tamarind called es asem.

spots.name: Pak Glinding
spots.desc: Serves grilled freshwater fish, nila bakar. You may also try wader goreng, a local fish snack.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Wonogiri-Pracimantoro, Km. 7, Jajar, Sendang

spots.name: Rumah Makan Mbah Bhet
spots.desc: Serves lontong opor, shredded chicken and rice cake in a coconut milk soup. In this stall, the dish is added gudeg, sambal goreng kentang (potato sambal dish), telur bacem (Javanese boiled egg), and bubuk dele (soybean powder}.
spots.addr: Jl. Manyar II, RT.003/RW.001, Gerdu, Girikerto

spots.name: Filosofi Teh
spots.desc: Tea, herbal tea, coffee beer, and limun/sari temulawak (a drink made from Javanese ginger (Curcuma zanthorrhiza)).

spots.name: Mie Ayam Jamur Om Bum Bum
spots.desc: Serves mie ayam jamur (chicken noodles with oyster mushroom).
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Maospati - Magetan No.km. 4, Turus, Purwosari

spots.name: Warung Bubur Brongkos Kambing Bu Marsinah
spots.desc: Local Magetan food, bubur brongkos kambing, a rice porridge mixed with goat meat soup and veggies.

spots.name: Rabbit Park
spots.desc: A family-friendly educational park that allows children to interact with rabbits. It also has a cafe.
spots.price: Rp10,000 for kids, and Rp15,000 - Rp20,000 for adults

spots.name: Madiredo Lake
spots.desc: This lake isn't that big, but it's surrounded by lush trees, green rice fields, and a stunning, picturesque mountain as a background.

spots.name: Pujonkidul Ricefield Cafe
spots.desc: A cafe for dining, and for vegetable and fruit shopping. It has lots of photo spots.

spots.name: Pacet Mini Park
spots.desc: A place to relax on the way from Mojosari to Pacet, where you can see some passion fruit trees at the entrance and animal statues inside. This park also has a grilled fish "food court" with small pavilions/ bale area (warung lesehan). This tourist attraction also has some outbound and flying fox facilities.

spots.name: Pondok Lesehan 19
spots.desc: Simple Sundanese-style restaurant with fish and sea food, fried rice, noodles, etc.

spots.name: Pasar Panimbang
spots.desc: Many shops and stalls, selling groceries, clothes, streetfood, etc.
spots.addr: Jl. Raya Panimbang / Jl. Teluk Lada

spots.name: Karang Tanjung Layar
spots.desc: The rock of Tanjung Layar (Sail Cape) is the reason for the name of the cape, as it is shaped like a sail. It is the icon of Sawarna, and surrounded by beautiful beaches.

spots.name: Warung Makang Pak Kumis
spots.desc: Simple eatery at the beach, selling grilled fish and sea food.

spots.name: Taman Bunga Nusantara
spots.desc: Public park of over 23 hectares, with flower gardens from around the world, a maze, giant clock and a tower. There is also a leisure park called Alam Imajinasi next to the gardens, with many attractions especially for children. For an additional fee you can go around the flower gardens in the 'dotto train' or 'garden tram' each Rp50,000. The cheapest mass vehicle for explore the garden is…
spots.price: Rp40,000 entrance ticket, kids under 4 years old are free

spots.name: Wisata Agro Gunung Mas
spots.desc: See how tea is processed - get to the plantation early to see the factory actually in operation. Sit in the cafe and enjoy a cup of tea before walking or driving around the tracks to view the tea growing with the mountains as a backdrop. You can also go horse-riding around the tea plantations, but watch out for locals trying to rip you off.
spots.price: Rp6,000; Factory tour Rp7,500; Guide for tour Rp40,000 for a group up to 15 people

spots.name: Taman Wisata Matahari
spots.desc: There are water-play attractions: water slides, water giant bucket, water toys (aquabrella, aquacup, aquaslides, aquagate, aquaballs), wave pool, outbound area + rafting, foodcourt, souvenir shop, gazebo, guest house & vestibule. The view of Puncak while having fun at this waterpark can be a terrific and unforgettable experience.

spots.name: Puncak Pass Restaurant
spots.desc: The Hotel and Restaurant is on the highest point of Jl. Raya Puncak. Grab the sweet Poffertjes and hot ginger tea, in Dutch colonial style.

spots.name: Raffles Restaurant
spots.desc: Various types of food, including Sundanese, other Indonesian food, other Asian food, and European dishes.

spots.name: Green Canyon
spots.desc: Go by boat through beautiful jungle on a river of green-coloured brackish water. At the end of the navigable section of the river, there are beautiful waterfalls and rocks to jump off. In case of heavy rain, the water of the river turns brown for one or two days and the experience is not as nice.
spots.price: Entrance Rp12,500 per person; chartering a small boat (5 persons) about Rp100,000 per hour

spots.name: Warung Nasi Tin's
spots.desc: This small family run warung just opened in 2022 and offers great homecooked lunch and dinner. There are several vegan options that include tofu and tempeh. Chicken steamed in banana leafes is also delicious. When you enter the place you are warmly welcomed by the lady who runs the warung and are handed an empty plate. Help yourself and get rice from the rice cooker and serve yourself whatever…

spots.name: Linggajati Conference Museum
spots.desc: Dutch colonial residence built in 1918. The building was the main location of the negotiations between the Dutch administration and the Republic of Indonesia during the War of Independence in 1946 (although the agreement was finally signed in Central Jakarta). Linggajati was a compromise location, between the capital of the Dutch East Indies in Jakarta, and the centre of the revolution in…

spots.name: Rumah Makan Alinda
spots.desc: Traditional Sundanese restaurant, known for fried gurami fish with chili sauce.

spots.name: Supermal Karawaci
spots.desc: The largest shopping mall in Karawaci, featuring the Timezone indoor theme park.

spots.name: Pantai Kalapa Patimban
spots.desc: Popular beach that is easy to reach. There are various foodstalls around the beach area.

spots.name: Kilometre Zero
spots.desc: In 1808, the Great Post Road across Java was built (the section in Bandung's city centre is now called Jalan Asia Afrika). It is said that when Governor-General H.W. Daendels of the Dutch East Indies travelled along the route, he said at the place where the road crosses the Cikapundung river: "Make sure that a city has been built here, when I return." At that location, a 'Kilometre Zero'…

spots.name: Gedung Pakuan
spots.desc: Built 1864-1867 as the new residence of the resident of the residency of Parahyangan, as its capital was moved from Cianjur to Bandung. The Indies Empire style building is nowadays used as the official residence of the governor of West Java province.

spots.name: New Majestic
spots.desc: Cinema building designed by Wolff Schoemaker, built in 1924. Now the building is used as a restaurant, and sometimes as a concert venue.

spots.name: Santa Angela School
spots.desc: Private Catholic school, founded by Dutch Ursuline nuns in 1905, adjacent to the Ursuline convent. The building was constructed in 1922.

spots.name: "Ade Irma Suryani Nasution" Traffic Park
spots.desc: Recreation park in the heart of the city, for children to learn about traffic signs and rules. Children can ride around by mini-cars or bicycles. The park is located in a green garden space that used to be part of the command centre of the Dutch East Indies army.

spots.name: Braga City Walk
spots.desc: Small mall right in the heart of Bandung. The number of shops is limited, but there are various cafés and restaurants, and a cinema.

spots.name: Pasar Baru Trade Center
spots.desc: Very large shopping centre. One of the oldest shopping locations of Bandung, the Pasar Baru ('new market') was established in the 19th century. Nowadays, it is a centre with hundreds of small shops on 8 floors.

spots.name: Paskal Hyper Square
spots.desc: Open-air shopping centre with various shops, cafés, restaurants, a foodcourt, KTV, and the Amnesia night club.

spots.name: Toko Sin Sin
spots.desc: Sells various high quality handicraft and souvenirs, including wayang golek (wood puppet), wayang kulit (leather puppet), angklung, leather and crocodile skin handicraft (mostly bags, wallets, and belts), wood carvings, Indonesian traditional silverworks, paintings, and even Indonesian furniture. This is a shop with very long history, started even before Indonesia gained independence.

spots.name: Cupumanik
spots.desc: Centre for wayang golek (traditional Sundanese wooden doll puppets).

spots.name: Elizabeth
spots.desc: Leather handicrafts, including shoes, bags and other accessories. Elizabeth was founded in Bandung in 1963, and now has stores throughout Indonesia.

spots.name: Lotek Kalipah Apo 42
spots.desc: Established in the 1960s. Specialty is lotek, Bandung-style vegetable salad with peanut sauce.
spots.price: About Rp20,000 for a main course

spots.name: Sate Kardjan
spots.desc: Lamb satay speciality, since 1970. Try sate buntel (a grilled minced lamb meat), tongseng (lamb meat in a coconut milk soup), nasi goreng kambing (fried rice with lamb) or sate cempe (satay from 10 month old lamb).

spots.name: Soto Ojolali
spots.desc: Selling a variety of soups since the 1940s, specialties are Soto Bandung and Soto Jakarta.

spots.name: Warung Nasi Ampera
spots.desc: Ampera is a chain of Sundanese restaurants established in Bandung. Nowadays, there are dozens of branches across the city and Western Java.
spots.addr: Jl. Dalem Kaum Gg Kaum No 54/15A

spots.name: Kartika Sari
spots.desc: The primary brand for local Bandung pastries. A wide selection of pastries, but the most famous include its lapis cakes; the cheese sticks; keju bagelen; and the special pisang mollen, a round bread stuffed with banana that you can choose with or without choose. The main store is in Jalan H. Akbar near the main railway station, but there are several more branches throughout the city.

spots.name: Martabak Canada
spots.desc: A wide variety of martabak manis sweet stuffed pancakes and martabak asin salty stuffed pancakes.

spots.name: Rasa Bakery
spots.desc: One of the most well known ice cream parlors in Bandung. Home made for your sweet tooth.

spots.name: Soes Merdeka
spots.desc: The outlet has a legacy of its kue soes, a puff pastry with sweet fillings, but its specialty includes a rum filling.

spots.name: Sumber Hidangan
spots.desc: The bakery was opened as Het Snoephuis (The Candy House) in 1929. The interior is still pretty much the same as it was in earlier times. Breads and cookies' still retain their names on display in Dutch, such as zwieback, roomsoes, krentenbrood, saucijzenbrood, suiker hagelslaag. Its old-time ambience and original menu attracts tourists and long-time patrons. While the premise may look like a run…

spots.name: Amnesia Club
spots.desc: Large nightclub frequented by students as well as expats and tourists.

spots.name: North Sea Bar
spots.desc: Pub owned by a Dutchman that is popular among expats and bar-girls. Draught beers and Dutch snacks.

spots.name: BMC (Bandoengsche Melk Centrale)
spots.desc: In an old Dutch colonial house. They specialise in fresh milk beverages.

spots.name: Es Sekoteng Bungsu
spots.desc: Es sekoteng is a grated ice cube with avocado, young coconut and kolang-kaling (some local preserved fruit)

spots.name: Kopi Aroma Bandung
spots.desc: Good quality coffee store and factory, in an old district of town. The Robusta coffee beans are stored for 5 years and the Arabica beans for as long as 8 years and sourced from coffee plantations throughout Indonesia.

spots.name: Wiki Koffie
spots.desc: Probably the most crowded, jam-packed and the most popular coffee house in Braga vicinity. It is advisable to come as early as possible.

spots.name: Pasir Kunci
spots.desc: Village on the foothills on the northeastern side of Bandung. The village aims to retain elements of traditional Sundanese culture, arts, and cuisine, and is set in the middle of paddy fields.

spots.name: Saung Angklung Udjo
spots.desc: Angklung is a traditional Sundanese musical instrument, made by bamboo. Udjo Nalagena, a famous angklung artist, created an Angklung House in East Bandung, where angklung instruments are made, learned and played. You can enjoy an angklung concert played by the orchestra (which includes both adults and children), combined with a dance performance. The concert is interactive, with the spectators…

spots.name: Kedai Selasih
spots.desc: Somewhat hidden but rather large restaurant. A variety of dishes, from Sundanese to Chinese, and from Western to Japanese.

spots.name: Lomie Lombok
spots.desc: Serving a Bandung noodle dish, Lomie Bandung. A boiled noodle with brownish seafood sauce. It is served with Dorokdok crackers.

spots.name: Karnivor12
spots.desc: Steak (beef and chicken) restaurant, but cannot cook well of Korean steak, so BibimBeef is not recommended, but the other European and Indonesian steaks (such as chicken wings) are relatively Ok for the price.

spots.name: Parit 9 Seafood
spots.desc: Seafood restaurant with many types of fish and seafood for sale per 100 grams.

spots.name: Salam Sereh Resto
spots.desc: Sundanese restaurant. Also Chinese and Western dishes are available.

spots.name: Waroenk Nenek
spots.desc: Restaurant with a nice atmosphere. The menu includes chicken, duck, fried rice, and steak.

spots.name: Bawean Bakery
spots.desc: Established in 1946, the name was Sweetheart Bakery until they changed its name during the New Order regime. The new name is taken from the shop location at Jalan Bawean. Their specialties are cakes baked using rum; such as nougat rolls, brownies and similar. This alcoholic ingredient make their cakes taste a bit bitter but preservable for a week.

spots.name: Prima Rasa
spots.desc: The main contender of Kartika Sari, similar products but some of the pastries has an added modern touch. Its best-selling product includes the Picnic Roll, a box of assorted sweet and savory pastries.

spots.name: Two Cents - Brew Believer
spots.desc: Specialised in coffees from Bali, Dampit, Bajawa Flores, and Malabar. They also have their house blends such as Bewitched Blend and Awakening Blend.

spots.name: De Driekleur
spots.desc: Dutch Colonial house built in 1937 to a design by A.F. Albers, in modernist/Art Deco style. The building's name, De Driekleur, is Dutch for 'the tricolour' and refers to the Dutch flag. The building is now a branch of a bank.

spots.name: Dutch Cave
spots.desc: Cave built in 1918 as a water tunnel. During the Second World War and Indonesian War of Independence, it was used as an arms and ammunition storage, prison, communications centre, and shelter.

spots.name: Japanese Cave
spots.desc: Second cave, built during the Japanese occupation in 1942. The cave was built by using a forced-labour system, as a defence shelter for the Japanese.

spots.name: Gasibu Park
spots.desc: Large lawn square in front of Gedung Sate. It's a favourite spot for a walk around a park and all the way towards Monju (Monumen Perjuangan), some 500 metres away. The square is a fairground on Sunday mornings, with food stalls at the Monju Park. People's favourites include dim sum ceker (a chicken foot cooked dim sum style) and nasi liwet (rice cooked in coconut milk, with chicken and…

spots.name: Riau Junction
spots.desc: Relatively small shopping mall with a Yogya department store and various other shops and restaurants.

spots.name: Balubur Town Square
spots.desc: Shopping centre with mostly small independent shops, the large ACE Hardware store, and several cafés.

spots.name: Simpang Dago Market
spots.desc: Market near the Simpang Dago junction. Fresh meat, fish, produce, rice, etc., for low prices.

spots.name: ForMen
spots.desc: The dedicated factory outlet solely for men, from formal to casual wear.

spots.name: Heritage, The Factory Outlet
spots.desc: Colonial style exterior with humongous options of clothing. The outdoor café is very wide, has greenery, and a playing area. The top floor has a dedicated section for outwear or sweaters, as well as scrapbook making.

spots.name: The Secret Factory Outlet
spots.desc: A modern style outlet, the first outlet you'll encounter when you enter Jalan Riau. There is a huge section for kids at its back, but it is for generally all ages. Casual and smart casual options.

spots.name: Episode
spots.desc: International fashion. Also a specialised section of clothes, bags, etc. for hiking/trekking.

spots.name: UNKL347
spots.desc: Well-known local fashion brand, with the slogan "This is not made in China" to promote its local production.

spots.name: Screamous
spots.desc: Bandung distro that now has shops in multiple Indonesian cities.

spots.name: Warung Lela
spots.desc: On the hill side with a nice view to the city. Try yamien, a dried boiled noodle, mixed with soy sauce. There are sweet yamien and salt yamien. Try also chicken noodle and the strawberry juice as a dessert.
spots.price: About Rp20,000 for a main course

spots.name: Warung Pasta
spots.desc: A variety of Italian dishes for budget prices, popular among students of the nearby ITB university.

spots.name: Bakmi Jowo DU 67
spots.desc: Popular streetside warung serving varieties of Javanese noodles, originally from Gunung Kidul.

spots.name: Sop Kaki Kambing & Sapi 999
spots.desc: Very popular roadside food stall selling goat and beef soup, either with regular meat, with offal, or a combination. The stall is set up every evening around 17:00 and has seating for about 40 people.

spots.name: Bebek Ali Borromeus
spots.desc: Roadside food stall selling fried duck and chicken, along with a signature sambal (chilli sauce). It is a very popular place, and around dinner time there are often people waiting for seats.

spots.name: Hanamasa Dago
spots.desc: One of the two Bandung branches of the all-you-can-eat Japanese restaurant chain Hanamasa.

spots.name: Sindang Reret
spots.desc: Sundanese restaurant. Sindang Reret also has branches in Ciwidey, Lembang, and Karawang.

spots.name: Cafe Halaman
spots.desc: Café with nice garden, serving Indonesian, Chinese, and Western dishes.

spots.name: Fashion Pasta
spots.desc: International place for lunch and dining. Italian food: antipasti, pizza, salad, soup, pasta, main course, dessert.
spots.addr: Jl. Resort Dago Pakar No.18 A

spots.name: Sierra Café & Lounge
spots.desc: Located on the hill of Dago Pakar, Sierra has a relaxing and indulging ambience with a breathtaking view of Bandung's city lights. International cuisines include Western, Japanese and Thai.

spots.name: Thai Palace
spots.desc: The most well-known Thai restaurant of the city. There are two other branches at the Istana Plaza and Festival Citylink malls.

spots.name: Noah's Barn
spots.desc: Specialised in local variety of coffees such as Java, Bali, Toraja, and Papua.
spots.addr: Jl. Dayang Sumbi No. 2, Coblong, Bandung, West Java 40132

spots.name: Two Hands Full
spots.desc: Try the "Eggs in Hell" with chorizo, or a smoothie bowl. Some customers found the WiFi hard to connect or the signal quality is mediocre.

spots.name: One Eighty Coffee and Music
spots.desc: Spacious café on two floors. Shallow pool you can cool your feet in. Regular live music. Western and Asian brunch items.

spots.name: Yoghurt Cisangkuy
spots.desc: It has many flavours of fresh yogurt with fresh fruits. Very suitable as a resting place after walking in the hot weather.

spots.name: Villa Isola
spots.desc: Art-deco villa building designed by architect C.P.W. Schoemaker. It was built in 1932 for media tycoon D.W. Berretty. It lies in the northern part of Bandung, overlooking the city to south and the Tangkuban Perahu volcano to the north. Villa Isola and its 2 gardens have a magnificent design by its architect, combining the unique landscape and the Indo-European architectural style. The monumental…

spots.name: Cipaganti Mosque
spots.desc: Mosque designed by Dutch architect C.P.W. Schoemaker, built in 1933. It was the only mosque that was built in the European residential area in the northern part of Bandung. The central facade, using a mix of European and Javanese style elements, still has the original design, but the mosque has been expanded on both sides.

spots.name: Karang Setra Waterland
spots.desc: Water recreation park with many swimming pools, water slides, etc.

spots.name: ZEN Family Spa & Reflexology
spots.desc: One of the most popular massage/spa services in the city. The location on Jalan Sukajadi (near the PVJ shopping mall) is the original location, but nowadays they have more locations in Bandung and other Indonesian cities. Balinese relaxation massage, foot treatment, back and shoulder massage, face therapy, Thai massage, body scrub, and more.

spots.name: Punclut
spots.desc: Punclut, an abbreviation of Puncak Ciumbuleuit ("the peak of Ciumbuleuit") is an area in the northern foothills of Bandung. The area is known for its many cheap and traditional Sundanese restaurants, and for its natural surroundings. From Punclut, there are hiking trails through the mountains towards Lembang.

spots.name: Cihampelas Walk
spots.desc: After a drop from your outlet shopping at the strip, there are choices of restaurants to fill up, or rest at the outdoor park for a change of pace.

spots.name: Rumah Mode
spots.desc: Probably the most well-known factory outlet store in Bandung. The options are especially great for both girls and boys' formal wear, but may not be as cheap as the street outlets. If your feet are aching after the stroll, there are cafés with both indoor and outdoor sit-down areas. Rumah Mode gets very crowded on weekends.

spots.name: Jalan Cihampelas
spots.desc: Street known for its many clothing stores, and especially for the sale of jeans. A lot of denim shops are decorated with funky designs. Giant models of Superman, Goku, Rambo and others, stand guard over some of the shops. The Cihampelas Walk shopping mall is along the same street.

spots.name: Souvenir Shop 39
spots.desc: Very good quality and inexpensive local souvenirs. The shop in one of the many old Dutch colonial style buildings.

spots.name: D'COST Seafood BTC
spots.desc: Budget no-frill seafood restaurant that has several branches in Bandung, including one in the BTC Fashion Mall.

spots.name: Saung Punclut Teh Ita 3
spots.desc: Traditional Sundanese restaurant with a nice mountain view: sitting on the floor, eating using your hands. Like most of the restaurants in the Punclut area, the restaurant is known for its red rice.

spots.name: N Cafe
spots.desc: Balinese & European cuisines, with great scenery, try the balinese fried duck.
spots.addr: Jl. Setra Duta Kencana II No.11

spots.name: Miss Bee Providore
spots.desc: Popular place with a big selection of good, standard Western and Asian classics in a spacious, family-friendly setting.

spots.name: Wild Grass
spots.desc: Semi-open brick building with garden. Mostly western food with a modern twist, inventive desserts, big selection of non-alcoholic cocktails.

spots.name: Woodfired Pizza & Gelato Cremeria Di Dee
spots.desc: Tiny pizza place (limited selection, but wood fired oven) with Gelateria next door, in an open garden setting. Cozy to relax for a while in sunny weather.

spots.name: Vienna Cafe
spots.desc: Italian restaurant with pasta, pizza, fried chicken, salad, soup.

spots.name: Fame Station
spots.desc: Nightclub in the hills of northern Bandung. Regular live performances of local bands, followed by electric/dance music.

spots.name: Sobber's Bar
spots.desc: Popular bar/nightclub, with regular performances by famous Indonesian DJs.

spots.name: Festival Citylink
spots.desc: Shopping mall with a range of shops, restaurants, cafés, a cinema, KTV, and a hotel with convention centre.

spots.name: Miko Mall
spots.desc: Mall along the southern toll road (Kopo exit), with Blitz cinema, large supermarket, and various other shops, restaurants, and cafés.

spots.name: Cibaduyut shoes centre
spots.desc: The Cibaduyut neighbourhood in Southern Bandung is known for its leather shoes production. There are numerous shoes shops along Jalan Raya Cibaduyut and in its surroundings. In addition to shoes, also other leather products are sold.

spots.name: LORI Art Design
spots.desc: Ethnic contemporary styled jewellery and handicraft accessories for women and men. Product use natural, environment friendly materials such as stones, cowstone, woods, seeds and Rudrakash/Ganitrus Beads.

spots.name: OneJava Seni
spots.desc: Wayang golek (traditional Sundanese wooden doll puppets) and other local cultural handicrafts, including angklung musical instruments.

spots.name: Mie Kocok SKM
spots.desc: Mie Kocok is a noodle soup, served with beef foot, beef skin and tauge or mung bean sprout. If you don't fancy with these parts of beef, then you can ask not to have it and you can still taste its appetite.

spots.name: Rumah Makan Ibu Haji Ciganea
spots.desc: Sundanese restaurant. Originally from Purwakarta, now also with a branch in Bandung.

spots.name: Brownies Kukus Amanda
spots.desc: Amanda's highlight is its steamed (no-bake) chocolate soft brownies, enticing people to form a line at its outlets! The outlet at Jl. Rancabolang is its main outlet, but there are several more branches across the city, and in other Indonesian cities.

spots.name: Es Cendol Elizabeth
spots.desc: Cendol is an Indonesian drink made with coconut and coconut milk, served with ice cubes and sweet brown sugar.

spots.name: Sari Ater Natural Hot Spring
spots.desc: Hot spring pools with temperatures up to 42.5°C. There is a pool with terrace and restaurant, but also natural 'river' pools with waterfalls that have beautiful lights in the night. Sari Ater also has various other recreational facilities, such as archery, ATV riding, horse riding, and paintball.
spots.hours: Hot spring pools open 24 hours, other recreational facilities during daylight hours
spots.price: Entrance from Rp28,000 with additional charges for some of the pools

spots.name: Prabu Geusan Ulun Museum
spots.desc: Collection of traditional Sundanese weaponry, as well as the crown jewels and other finery.
spots.addr: Jl. Prabu Geusan Ulun No. 40 B

spots.name: R.M Joglo Sumedang
spots.desc: A Javanese (i.e. Central Java) style restaurant in West Java. The specialty is nasi liwet, rice dish cooked in coconut milk, chicken broth and spices originally from Solo, but there are also local Sundanese dishes, such as soto Bandung and tahu Sumedang.

spots.name: Danakan Dive Center
spots.desc: Dive center with a nearby lodge for divers Danakan Losmen. Offers dive courses, dive trips and introduction dives. Equipment is fine, dive masters are local and know where to find everything. A trip with 2 divers costs Rp350,000 each dive (Rp1,050,000 for 3 dives), but if you want to do them in another island and not in Derawan, you have to add Rp1,500,000 to charter a small boat for the day.…

spots.name: Masjid Besar Kampung Baru
spots.desc: The oldest mosque in Banda Neira. It was inaugurated in 1889.

spots.name: Luminocean
spots.desc: Sustainability-focussed social enterprise offering eco-diving training and courses in marine ecology.

spots.name: Toko Oleh-Oleh Khas Banda (Ibu Icha)
spots.desc: Nutmeg product, manisan pala (candied nutmeg), sirup pala (nutmeg syrup), and so on.

spots.name: Rumah Makan Nusantara
spots.desc: Indonesian food including nasi kuning ikan (yellow rice with fish), nasi goreng, etc.

spots.name: Kafe Calepo
spots.desc: Ikan bakar (grilled fish), jus gandaria (plum mango juice), kue manto (fish roll), and others.

spots.name: Nutmeg Cafe Juice & Pancake
spots.desc: Fruits juices, oranges, avocado, bananas, papaya, pineapple. Also, the specialty dish, pancake selai pala (pancake with nutmeg jam). You may try sirup pala (nutmeg syrup) drink too as well as the nutmeg fish soup sup ikan pala.

spots.name: Cafe DKRF
spots.desc: Fruits juices, dragon fruit, apple, tomato, mango, and so on.

spots.name: Fort Revengie
spots.desc: A fort built by Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie (VOC, "Dutch East India Company") on Pulau Ai in 1616.

spots.name: Traditional villages
spots.desc: The most famous villages are: Bena, Gurusina, and Tololela. Although clearly a tourist destination, the villages house regular people, doing everyday things. Some are weaving ikat, others are simply tending to their livestock. It is okay to be photograph the villagers, but of course ask first. Bring around Rp1,000,000 if you would like to get woven cloth. There is no ATM nearby.
spots.price: Rp20,000-Rp25,000, depending on the village (as of Nov 2018).

spots.name: Traditional fighting or dancing (not at the same time)
spots.desc: This is not a show put on for tourists. However, it is a show. People from the villages gather to fight. The rules seem to be that there are no rules, and so it is difficult to determine a winner. A fight continues for as long as the audience is entertained and the fighters are willing to continue. Ask at your hotel if there is something scheduled. This traditional fight called "sagi" is similar…

spots.name: Inerie volcano
spots.desc: The Mt Inerie volcano is an impressive volcano located close to Bajawa. It is possible to climb the volcano with a guide but this should not be taken lightly.

spots.name: Oggi Waterfalls
spots.desc: Based around Oggi village. It is possible to walk from the main road along the rice-fields till you get to the waterfall. There are also steps on the side of the waterfall that allows climbing up.

spots.name: Mangeruda Hot Spring
spots.desc: After a long day of traditional culture, it feels nice to plummet into the hot springs. There are 2 pools (as in man-made pools) with hot springs, and one that flows into a river mixing the water to a comfortable warm temperature. There is an overpriced shop there, so it's better to stop along the way for some ice cold Bintang to enjoy in the pools. The place is poorly maintained, but the spring…

spots.name: Malanage Hot Spring
spots.desc: The hot volcanic water flows in a river and mixes with cold mountain water creating a natural hot spring. By careful positioning yourself in the river it is possible to regulate the temperature. There are no tourist facilities apart from a changing-room/toilet pavilion. Snacks and beverages can be purchased from the small Warung besides the river.

spots.name: Wawomudha
spots.desc: After an easy one hour hike up with some nice views, you get to see two small volcanic ponds which apparently change color just like the Kelimutu lakes. This is in no way comparable to Kelimutu and can be disappointing in the dry season.

spots.name: Wolobobo Viewpoint
spots.desc: 9 km away from town center, this viewpoint overlooks Mt Inerie and the surrounding mountainous area. You can see the crater from the previous eruption long ago. No food & beverage facility (or anything of that sort).

spots.name: Dito's
spots.desc: Reasonably priced restaurant. It has the usual suspects of Indonesian cuisine and some western food as well. The pork satay comes highly recommended.

spots.name: Lucas Restaurant
spots.desc: Cosy place with decent food, a nice atmosphere and reasonable prices. Arak is available, although not of top quality. Also a hotel with four rooms available, choose between hot or cold shower. Otherwise, the rooms are the same, with one double and one single bed.

spots.name: Roda Baru Restaurant
spots.desc: Tasty Nasi Padang food and drinks with English speaking owner.

spots.name: Tetebatu Rice Terraces
spots.desc: The rice fields around Tetebatu are the area's principal attraction. Paths wind between irrigated paddies, villages, plantations and small streams, with views towards the heavily forested slopes of Rinjani. The landscape changes considerably with the agricultural cycle. Freshly planted fields can be an intense green, while mature rice gives the countryside a more golden appearance. Early morning…

spots.name: Tetebatu Monåkey Forest
spots.desc: This park is a gentle 4-km walk north of the town. Expect lots of macaques and some pleasant enough scenery and waterfalls. Again, ask at your hotel about a guide, and avoid any offers of motorised transport.

spots.name: Air Terjun Jukut
spots.desc: These falls are not as spectacular as those in the north of the national park around Senaru, but still very much worth the effort to see. You will need a guide to find Jukut and your hotel will certainly help with this. Expect to pay about Rp 100,000-150,000. The falls are reached via a really pleasant two hour walk from Tetebatu through charming rice paddies. Less recommended is to drive to the…

spots.name: Kotaraja
spots.desc: About 5 km south of Tetebatu, Kotaraja is a substantial Sasak village and one of the best places in the area to investigate traditional peresean. Peresean is a ceremonial form of stick fighting in which two men fight with rattan sticks and buffalo-hide shields. It has both competitive and ritual dimensions and forms part of broader Sasak cultural traditions. Fights are not necessarily held every…

spots.name: Air Terjun Sindang Gila
spots.desc: The best known and most spectacular of the three. The water cascades everywhere here breaking some 50 m above the main arrival point. From Senaru village walk about 20 minutes to the southeast. The path is pleasant and leads through some splendid tropical forest. Good to chill eat, few tables, else locals set on floor/path. Few stalls with basic stuff like instant noodles. Few shelters between…
spots.price: Foreigner Rp 20,000 (both Sindang Gila and Tiu Kelep)

spots.name: Air Terjun Tiu Kelep
spots.desc: Less spectacular but still very much worth it. Continue on uphill from Sindang Gila for about 30-60 minutes (depending on your fitness, this will involve a steep uphill climb and a creek crossing and several other obstacles). Tiu Kelep has a nice bathing pool below the falls with very cool invigorating water. Guide is not required if fit and experienced enough but better if kids and/or elderly.…
spots.price: Foreigner Rp 20,000 (both Sindang Gila and Tiu Kelep)

spots.name: Kampung Tradisiona - Desa Senaru
spots.desc: Next to the office of the national park is the traditional village of Senaru. You will see traditional houses and can watch the daily life of local people.

spots.name: View From Coffee Plantation To Waterfall
spots.desc: View from above on Tiu Kelep Waterfall. Drinks shop seems closed.

spots.name: Market in Ancak
spots.desc: Every Thursday morning is the local market in Ancak. Many people of the surrounding villages come there to buy vegetable, meat and fish, clothes, shoes, and everything they need for their daily life.

spots.name: Tanjung A'an
spots.desc: a beautiful area near the Kuta Beach. The sand is very unique that it looks like pepper. Beach guards are on the beach early. They prevent hawkers from hassling tourists, but normally the hawkers are mostly children and quiet villagers trying to make a living, and they are quite good natured. Often good quality sarongs and kalapa muda (young coconut) drinks are available from local people seeking…

spots.name: Mandalika Beach Park
spots.desc: landscaped beachfront area forming part of the Mandalika tourism development. Wide promenades, cycle paths, gardens and public beaches provide an attractive place for walking, relaxing and watching the sunset. Cafés, resorts and the nearby Pertamina Mandalika International Circuit have transformed the area into Lombok's premier resort district while retaining public beach access.

spots.name: Seger Hill
spots.desc: A short climb above Seger Beach rewards visitors with panoramic views over Kuta Bay, Mandalika, the international racing circuit and the surrounding coastline. The hill is particularly popular at sunrise and sunset, and is also the focal point of the annual Bau Nyale festival celebrating the legend of Princess Mandalika.

spots.name: Pantai Putri Nyale
spots.desc: This is where the Novotel Lombok is located. It's a beautiful beach, but at low tide it gets almost completely dry and is no longer suited for swimming.

spots.name: Mawun
spots.desc: Mawun beach is a secluded half-moon bay with crystal clear water and pristine sand. There's one big tree where people congregate in the shade. An awesome place for relaxing, safe swimming and surfing. The only facilities are a few drinks stalls.

spots.name: Lancing beach
spots.desc: A huge stretch of sand almost midway between Kuta and Selong Belanak. This beach is barely crowded and has only a couple of warungs serving food and drinks. It is easy to miss as it's a short ride off the main road. This is in complete contrast to other beaches and is so huge that it is divided into two parts on the main road.The backdrafts can be strong and not as good for swimming like Tanjung…

spots.name: Shore Thing Fishing Trips
spots.desc: Fishing & sightseeing trips from 3-9 hours. Choose between two boats: a traditional prahu or a new fiberglass speedboat. Trolling, popping, jigging and bottom fishing. Charters available, local pickup and drop off. All equipment bait and life jackets included. On the speedboat, Fish Finder, GPS and sonar are in use. No angling experience necessary. Call made on 081917 250699 or Oz on087865 268184.
spots.addr: Mimpi Manis Homestay, Desa Mong, Kuta

spots.name: Kuta Horses
spots.desc: Kuta Horses provides horse riders with horseback views of deserted beaches, bays, valleys, hills with breathtaking views and rice paddies, tobacco fields or little traditional fishing villages. Their 6 western-sized horses are tall and healthy, they have been selected for their endurance and personality, they are very well trained. Their equipment is only handmade comfortable leather brands as…

spots.name: Massage on the Hill
spots.desc: Professional therapist educated at Bisa Scholl (Bali). Organic oil only - 1 hr 30 min treatment. Appointment only.

spots.name: Warung Jawa I
spots.desc: Delicious local food. Very friendly staff. Even the "hawkers" are quite fun when you go there regularly. Popular place for expats and surfers. Always a bit crowded late afternoon. Probably the cheapest food in Kuta. Shakes also very cheap (Rp7,000).

spots.name: Warung Jawa 2
spots.desc: Good cheap local food and fruit juices such as Avocado for Rp7,000.

spots.name: Nuggets Corner
spots.desc: Great value restaurant serving local-style food and chicken nuggets.

spots.name: El Bazar Cafe & Restaurant
spots.desc: Well-known regionally for bold flavours of the Mediterranean, hearty service and top quality coffee made by their trained barista. They serve top class breakfast and for lunch and dinner they have vegetarian, fresh fish, pan seared yellow fin tuna, Mezze platter, kebab, tagines, lamb braised for hours. place gets very busy, so go early or make a reservation.

spots.name: Milk Espresso
spots.desc: Modern Australian-style café known for excellent coffee, generous breakfasts, sandwiches, smoothie bowls and rooftop bar. Popular with surfers and remote workers throughout the day.

spots.name: Bush Radio
spots.desc: Trendy speciality coffee shop serving excellent espresso, brunch dishes, sourdough, smoothie bowls and homemade pastries in a relaxed creative atmosphere. Particularly popular with surfers and digital nomads.

spots.name: Mama Pizza
spots.desc: Long-running pizzeria serving wood-fired pizzas, pasta and Italian favourites in a casual atmosphere. Popular with families and groups

spots.name: Drifters
spots.desc: Popular surf café and restaurant serving burgers, healthy bowls, breakfast and coffee alongside an attached surf shop.

spots.name: Keker Taliwang & Grilled Seafood
spots.desc: Local restaurant specialising in spicy Lombok ayam taliwang, grilled seafood and other Sasak specialities.

spots.name: Ashtari Cafe
spots.desc: On the hill with spectacular views of the south coast. You need transport to get there. Relax and enjoy the daily fresh menu. Delicious food. Vegetarian food.

spots.name: Dwiki's Cuisine
spots.desc: Serves a variety of European and Asian cuisines. The owners have a love for good food and for their customers. They may have the best pizza in town, but it is a little overpriced.

spots.name: The Breakery
spots.desc: French-inspired bakery and café serving artisan breads, pastries, cakes, coffee and light breakfasts.

spots.name: Family House Lombok - Hotel & Restaurant
spots.desc: A large restaurant with an Indonesian menu and some western dishes. Serves cocktails as well.

spots.name: Sonya's
spots.desc: Sonya's is a very reasonably-priced restaurant which is busy every night. It is on the main road that leads down to Kuta beach, on the left hand side if heading towards the beach, or on the right hand side if heading towards town, before the junction with the mini mart. Outside is a chalkboard saying "The Best Food in Town", and this isn't a false statement. It is a basic bamboo hut, look out the…

spots.name: Kenza
spots.desc: Contemporary restaurant combining tropical café by day with an elegant dinner venue in the evening. Serves creative international cuisine, excellent breakfasts, seafood, steaks, cocktails and an extensive wine list.

spots.name: Curfew
spots.desc: Lively restaurant and beer garden serving burgers, tacos, salads, craft beer and cocktails, with regular live music and DJs in the evenings.

spots.name: Terra
spots.desc: Contemporary café and restaurant serving modern international cuisine with an emphasis on fresh local ingredients, quality coffee and creative cocktails.

spots.name: Shore Bar & Restaurant
spots.desc: This beach bar is probably the only place that boosts somewhat of a night life in Kuta. Cold beers and cocktails. A local rock band playing covers will entertain you on a Saturday night, other nights disco DJ show. Happy hour from 16:00-19:00. Also serves lunch and dinner. BBQ fish and any kind of seafood.

spots.name: Pantai Seger
spots.desc: Beach suited for surfing, not for swimming because of the very strong currents. There are some drink stalls. Climb the hill here to watch the sunset.

spots.name: Merese Hill
spots.desc: This hill has stunning views of the open sea, especially during the day and on clear days. Not only that, you can also watch the sunrise and sunset from this hill while sitting comfortably amidst the expanse of green grass.
spots.addr: Jl. Kuta-Lombok, Pujut District, Central Lombok Regency

spots.name: Alangen Restaurant
spots.desc: Cafe on the beach with Beruga style seating in a small, open sitting area with grass roof.

spots.name: Dessert Point
spots.desc: Dessert Point is widely regarded as one of the world’s very best surf spots on its day and the fast-moving, barreling waves are not for the faint-hearted.

spots.name: Bunga Bunga Cafe
spots.desc: This is generally where the shuttle buses and taxis leave from. You can have breakfast here too.

spots.name: Ratenggaro Beach
spots.desc: Located just about 200 m from Ratenggaro Village, this is the original site of Ratenggaro Village before it relocated to the current site. You can find some megalithic tombs here, including one of the previous village chief's. Entrance fee is fixed at Rp20,000 per motorbike and Rp50,000 per car (as of Dec 2018).

spots.name: Warung Barokah
spots.desc: Nice clean Warung. Serves Bakso and Soto Ayam. Comes with a big plate of plain rice.

spots.name: Arema Sape
spots.desc: This place serves a lot of fish dishes, but also mie goreng and nasi goreng (not on the menu, just ask for it). There is also an internet café inside if you need to wait for the ferry.

spots.name: Wafsarak Waterfall
spots.desc: Jump from the top of the waterfall. There is also a waterfall cave.

spots.name: Permandian Malotong
spots.desc: Freshwater springs in built-up pool where people go swimming (and unfortunately bathe with soap sometimes).

spots.name: Deri
spots.desc: Several tombs in full nature (in particular a particularly impressive forest of giant bamboos). The site is much less interesting than other equivalent ones in Tana Toraja, but the road reaching Deri is very scenic, with many villages as beautiful as Kete Kesu but without any tourist (nor entrance fee) here.

spots.name: Ke'te Kesu'
spots.desc: Among the nominated sites, Ke'te' Kesu' is the most complete settlement. The site consists of a compound of houses and granaries, burial place, ceremonial ground, ricefields and water-buffalo pasture.

spots.name: Lemo
spots.desc: Lemo is also a cliff burial site with galleries of ancestor statues. One of the most interesting (and visited) sites.

spots.name: Londa
spots.desc: Londa is a grave site where two methods of burial are customary. One of the most interesting (and visited) sites.

spots.name: Bori Parinding
spots.desc: The site of Bori Parinding is a combination of ceremonial grounds and burials. The ceremonial ground is an open space used for traditional ceremonies, including rituals for the dead and thanksgiving.

spots.name: Pallawa
spots.desc: Pallawa site is also a compound of houses and granaries. There are 11 houses and 15 granaries.

spots.name: Todi Shop
spots.desc: A big museum-cum-shop, with demonstration looms and fabrics on display from all over Sulawesi.

spots.name: Café Aras
spots.desc: A café serving local food in a nice atmosphere. Decent prices. However, as in many places, the owners will try to have you hiring a "guide" at a too-expensive price.

spots.name: Warung Gian
spots.desc: Opened in early 2018, this place offers clean food, local dishes, and Wi-Fi.

spots.name: Poppies Toraja
spots.desc: Located inside the hotel of the same name, this restaurant serves excellent local food, always cooked on demand. Hence every dish must be ordered in advance (at least 45 min, up to 2 hr for the most famous specialties).

spots.name: Waroenk Gentong
spots.desc: A restaurant mixing the street food style restaurant and more elaborate hipsters-like restaurants (with wooden tables, and pictures of food and various music instruments on the wall).

spots.name: Lemon 84 Coffee
spots.desc: Nice café where the young inhabitants of Toraja come to have a drink. Electricity. Free Wi-Fi. Many mosquitos though.

spots.name: Tanjung Pendam Beach
spots.desc: So called the city beach of Tanjung Pandan. It's where the city locals typically go during the weekend to watch the sunset, play at the playground or dine at the seafood restaurants.

spots.name: Kaolin Lake
spots.desc: This is what is left of a kaolinite mine. A lake with blue water and white rocks around it deceives you as if you are near the Poles or a volcano crater.

spots.name: Kulong Keramik
spots.desc: A recreational spot that used tu ba a ceramic manufactury. Relax while watching the fish swim in the lake. There are also restaurants and places that selling souvenirs.
spots.addr: Jln. Ahmad Yani, Desa Lesung Batang

spots.name: Unique Bistro & Karaoke
spots.desc: Do karaoke in room or enjoy live music each night. They are serving common Indonesian food and to some extent, western food.

spots.name: Belitung Mangrove Park
spots.desc: A mangrove ecotourism park. If you want to enjoy food in the mangrove area, you can visit the floating restaurant in a Pinisi ship.

spots.name: Galeri KUMKM Belitung
spots.desc: This is the market where small designers sell their product to fame. The most complete collection of souvenirs, they have all of the above.

spots.name: Toko Oleh-oleh Keluarga OK
spots.desc: Locally produced bags, fashion, and shell arts. If you buy the crackers in bulks, they have a special wrapping box for your convenience.

spots.name: Kentucky Fried Chicken Tanjung Pandan Belitung
spots.desc: Want a temporary relief to Western food? Shift yourself to its fried chicken from this fast food restaurant.

spots.name: Dapur Sakato
spots.desc: Where there are Padang (Minangkabau) people, there is always a restaurant of their cuisine. Does not have the typical prominent roof, but a more premium feel.

spots.name: Mie Belitung Atep
spots.desc: Since 1973, this stall has attracted numerous national celebrities to stop by, even the former president Megawati. Specialties are the Mie Belitung, and the key lime juice. Cheap but you might need two to fill you up.

spots.name: Mie Yamin Achoi
spots.desc: If you want meat, that is their main ingredient for their noodle dish (bakmi), but they also have the Mie Belitung.

spots.name: RM Diva
spots.desc: Has seafood, but much more options if you are bored with it.

spots.name: RM Mutiara
spots.desc: Crowded, but has premium seafood options: crab, fish, and squid. They have the gangan, choose between whole fish or fish head.

spots.name: RM Belitong Tempo Duluk
spots.desc: Also a typical restaurant with local food, but with a more premium and hygienic feel. Knick knacks and recipes from the old days of the island.

spots.name: Sriwijaya Shop
spots.desc: There is actually no name for the shop but it houses a travel agent (the front display says they sell Sriwijaya Air tickets) and sells local snacks. On a hot day, as is always the case, sit here and enjoy a refreshing shaved ice (sekoteng) with jelly, red or green beans and other toppings, condensed milk and syrup.

spots.name: Markas Kodim Swimming Pool
spots.desc: A swimming area for kids in front of the District Military Command headquarter.
spots.price: Entrance fee: Rp5,000. Free for orphans

spots.name: DeMaja River
spots.desc: Playground, waterpark, and photo spot. Keep in mind that you will be fined Rp5,000 if you brought food from outside.

spots.name: Hill of Gibeon
spots.desc: Purple-roof complex of church popular for locals and the Christians to pray. The church only open on weekend. There's a small waterfall and swimming pool opened for public every day.

spots.name: Sidamanik Tea Plantation
spots.desc: This tea plantation is owned by PTPN IV and opened in the early 1900s. Sidamanik Tea Plantation can be reached in less than three hours from Medan City. Moreover, there is now a toll road connecting Medan to Tebing Tinggi City. The location of the tea plantation is also not far from Lake Toba.

spots.name: Asahan River
spots.desc: Rafting in Parhitean: Asahan River is a river in North Sumatra which flows from Lake Toba. This river passes Porsea, district Asahan, and ends at Nibung Gulf, the Strait of Malacca. The river is 150 km in length and passes through the valleys of the Barisan Mountains. The Asahan River, especially around the Tangga village, flows around 120 m/sec with grade IV-V + and has an average depth of 5 m…

spots.name: Aek Manik
spots.desc: Take a bath or swim at this natural spring. The water is clear and there are white sand at the bottom. Legend says that this is a bathing place for the King Damanik and his family.

spots.name: Parapat Saturday morning market
spots.desc: Early on Saturday morning there is food market: fruits, vegetables, fresh fish (or still alive). You can get everything very cheap (compared to western standards). It is packed with people and food. Go before 09:00 then there is still plenty of choice.

spots.name: RM Muslim Suroboyo
spots.desc: An alternative to Sitopsi if the latter is packed full. Offer more or less similar menu, price and services.

spots.name: Sitopsi
spots.desc: Offer fresh seafood with a very cheap price. You can choose either grilled or fried. Do try the lobster! Very packed with people around lunch time and serving time seems to take forever.

spots.name: Toga Aritonang Monument
spots.desc: A magnificent monument of Aritonang, one of the family in Batak Toba.

spots.name: Batu Maranak
spots.desc: Climb the most accessible highest hill to get a specatular view of Southern Samosir and southwest Lake Toba. There's a concrete path up to near summit, with an elevation gain about 100-200 metres (around 15-30 mins). Head right through a thick bush at the clearing after the concrete path to reach the summit.

spots.name: Montero Coffee & Resto
spots.desc: No pork restaurant with a spectacular view at Lake Toba and Muara town. Glamping is offered as well.

spots.name: Waterfront Pangururan
spots.desc: The lakeside Pangururan is converted into a park & walkway spanning from Tano Panggul bridge until Pangururan's market. Every weekend at 8 PM, there's fountain show that last about 20-30 minutes. Come early to get best front view as it's packed with lots of people.

spots.name: Dynasty Restaurant
spots.desc: For those who love to eat seafood. this restaurant will be the right place for you. They offer a variety of live seafood such as crab, fish, shellfish and a lot more. They also have "HEKHO" and "Spicy and sour Lome" which you cannot find in Singapore or Malaysia. If you happen to go there, try the pepper crab, sauce crab, kangkung belacan, ALL the grilled seafood, hekho, fried chicken, cereal…

spots.name: Asia Baru Restaurant
spots.desc: For those who love to eat Indonesian food (nasi Padang), this restaurant will be the right place for you. Four people eat much for less than RM 20 or S$8.

spots.name: Masjid Raya
spots.desc: This mosque has a beautiful 'pyramid' architecture. Quite good but already looks a bit old.

spots.name: Mega Wisata Ocarina Batam
spots.desc: This is a newly developed family-friendly theme park for fun and entertainment. You can also see Shio sculptures along the way. It is about 15 minutes from Batam Centre harbour. They have a beach, mini theme park, and a new water park. The large Ferris wheel and other carnival attractions are fun, there is a water park and 3D movie theater inside, along with several food-court style restaurants.…
spots.addr: Coastarina, near Batam Center Ferry Terminal

spots.name: Batam CableSki Park
spots.desc: Popular cable-pulled wakeboarding outfit. Has a pleasant little attached bar/cafe and offers day and overnight packages which include express immigration and your ferry tickets from Singapore.
spots.price: 1 hour S$25, half-day S$55 and full-day S$65, overnight from Singapore S$100, overnight from Singapore spectator S$60

spots.name: Tea Tree Spa
spots.desc: Well-regarded Balinese-style spa offering Javanese lulur scrubs, hot stone massage etc, set in a faux-Balinese temple courtyard. It's not cheap at S$60/hour, but there is a 20% discount before 3 PM and quite a few packages for couples, hotel guests, etc. No hanky-panky!

spots.name: Delima Seafood Restaurant
spots.desc: Easily spotted, Delima is the only restaurant here with a breezy kelong (platform on stilts) set up over the rocky beach, and they do a roaring trade on weekends. Everybody orders the chili crab (from Rp. 88,000) and with reason, but the rest of the menu is pretty good as well: try the kailan tahu jepung (Rp. 15000), Chinese broccoli with Japanese egg tofu.

spots.name: Dragon Inn
spots.desc: Within the Holiday Inn complex, this slick, upmarket Chinese seafood restaurant caters to both holidaymakers and demanding gourmets with dishes ranging from fried rice to abalone. Dim sum for lunch is popular.

spots.name: Queen's Restaurant & Café
spots.desc: Catering squarely to oil industry expats, Queen's has beer, pub grub and ladies of negotiable virtue.

spots.name: Aussie Bar
spots.desc: New bar opened by long term resident. 150m from ferry terminal has become the most popular watering hole in Waterfront. Cold beer, pizzas delivered, projector TV, free internet, pool table, good music, full range of drinks, friendly staff welcome many of the expats as well as weekend tourists. Has become the second office of several large company bosses.

spots.name: Laguna Golf Bintan
spots.desc: Bintan's best-known golf course that regularly shows up in lists of Indonesia's best. Offers promotional rates and packages for staying at nearby hotels.
spots.price: Weekday rates from Rp780,000/1,280,000 for 9/18 holes

spots.name: Pujasera Lagoi
spots.desc: The only place in Bintan that could reasonably be characterized as budget-friendly is this lackluster foodcourt offering local favorites, with nasi padang stall Lamak Basamo the best known of the bunch. Just don't expect frills like air-con or much attention to hygiene.

spots.name: Warung Yeah!
spots.desc: Don't be put off by the exclation mark, Yeah! serves tasty and reasonably priced Javanese classics: Madura-style sate ayam (chicken satay), many styles of nasi goreng and excellent ikan bakar (grilled fish). Even the enormous coconuts are fresh and tasty. Beware: the food here is geared towards local palates and can be very spicy! Head to the second floor Yeah! Lounge afterwards to recover with a…

spots.name: Kelong
spots.desc: A kelong is a Malay-style fishing platform on stilts, so true to the name, Kelong is an open-air seafood restaurant suspended on stilts above the sea. The food here is Chinese style, with local favorites including black pepper mud crab (tasty but pricey) and gong-gong (sea snails) prepared to order.

spots.name: The Patio
spots.desc: The menu at the Patio is exactly what you'd expect from a Marriott chain hotel, but the Indonesian dishes here are a cut above the norm and, most importantly, it's the only restaurant in the Treasure Bay area to offer air-conditioning.

spots.name: Treetops
spots.desc: The Banyan Tree's long-running all-day dining restaurant distinguishes itself at dinnertime with excellent Indonesian-style degustation courses from Rp. 510,000/person.

spots.name: Sun Moon Restaurant
spots.desc: Set out on a little island off the resort's beach and connected to the mainland by a pier, this popular seafood eatery keeps the day's catch swimming in nets at the back and cooks it to order. The food is good, alcohol is served, and if you get there early enough you might even avoid the karaoke. Pricy by Bintan standards (Rp 50,000 and up for most fish dishes), but quite cheap compared to…
spots.hours: Open for lunch and dinner daily

spots.name: Cetiya Sasana Kitri
spots.desc: Unique red calabash in front of the temple that differentiate it from other temples.

spots.name: Vihara Dharma Shanti Kundur
spots.desc: have a stroll and enjoy the breeze in the late evening. Spacious, with tables and chairs. The door is painted with guardian deities, probably one of the great spot in the town.

spots.name: Ah Kun's brother Restaurant
spots.desc: The ikan bakar (Rp 10,000) and ayam panggang can be sold out as early as 17:30.

spots.name: Toko abadi
spots.desc: A bakery that sells a wide variety of cakes, and pastries. On top of these modern products, it also produces traditional ones, for example "la pia" (pie made of lark) and of course the moon cake during the mid-autumnfestival. In addition, they do sell materials and ingredients for cake-making.
